questions.stem: The following experiment is used for the following question. A researcher discovered a species of moth that lays its eggs on oak trees. Eggs are laid at two distinct times of the year: early in spring when the oak trees are flowering and in midsummer when flowering is past. Caterpillars from eggs that hatch in spring feed on oak flowers and look like oak flowers, but caterpillars that hatch in summer feed on oak leaves and look like oak twigs. How does the same population of moths produce such different-looking caterpillars on the same trees? To answer this question, the biologist caught many female moths from the same population and collected their eggs. He put at least one egg from each female into eight identical cups. The eggs hatched, and at least two larvae from each female were maintained in one of the four temperature and light conditions listed below. Temperature Day Length Springlike Springlike Springlike Summerlike Summerlike springlike Summerlike summerlike In each of the four environments, one of the caterpillars was fed oak flowers, the other oak leaves. Thus, there were a total of eight treatment groups (4 environments × 2 diets). Which one of the following is not a plausible hypothesis that can be tested in this experiment?

choices.A: The longer day lengths of summer trigger the development of twig-like caterpillars.
choices.B: The cooler temperatures of spring trigger the development of flowerlike caterpillars.
choices.C: Differences in air pressure, due to differences in elevation, trigger the development of different types of caterpillars.
choices.D: Differences in diet trigger the development of different types of caterpillars.

questions.answer_text: Differences in air pressure, due to differences in elevation, trigger the development of different types of caterpillars.

questions.stem: The following experiment is used for the following question. A researcher discovered a species of moth that lays its eggs on oak trees. Eggs are laid at two distinct times of the year: early in spring when the oak trees are flowering and in midsummer when flowering is past. Caterpillars from eggs that hatch in spring feed on oak flowers and look like oak flowers, but caterpillars that hatch in summer feed on oak leaves and look like oak twigs. How does the same population of moths produce such different-looking caterpillars on the same trees? To answer this question, the biologist caught many female moths from the same population and collected their eggs. He put at least one egg from each female into eight identical cups. The eggs hatched, and at least two larvae from each female were maintained in one of the four temperature and light conditions listed below. Temperature Day Length Springlike Springlike Springlike Summerlike Summerlike springlike Summerlike summerlike In each of the four environments, one of the caterpillars was fed oak flowers, the other oak leaves. Thus, there were a total of eight treatment groups (4 environments × 2 diets). Recall that in the experiment, caterpillars born in the spring looked like flowers, and caterpillars born in the summer looked like twigs. What is the most likely selective advantage for this difference in body shape?

choices.A: Looking like their food sources allows the caterpillars to move through their environment more efficiently.
choices.B: Development into the adult moth form is faster for caterpillars shaped like twigs than like flowers.
choices.C: Looking like their food source lets the caterpillars blend into their surroundings, reducing predation.

questions.stem: Use the following information when answering the following question. In 1668, Francesco Redi performed a series of experiments on spontaneous generation. He began by putting similar pieces of meat into eight identical jars. Four jars were left open to the air, and four were sealed. He then did the same experiment with one variation: Instead of sealing four of the jars completely, he covered them with gauze (the gauze excluded the flies while allowing the meat to be exposed to air). In both experiments, he monitored the jars and recorded whether or not maggots (young flies) appeared in the meat. What hypothesis was being tested in the initial experiment with open versus sealed jars?

choices.A: Spontaneous generation is more likely during the long days of summer.
choices.B: The type of meat used affects the likelihood of spontaneous generation.
choices.C: Maggots do not arise spontaneously, but from eggs laid by adult flies.
choices.D: Spontaneous generation can occur only if meat is exposed to air.

questions.answer_text: Maggots do not arise spontaneously, but from eggs laid by adult flies.

choices.C: the structure and function of DNA
choices.D: natural selection

questions.answer_text: the structure and function of DNA

chapter.title: Evolution, the Themes of Biology, and Scientific Inquiry

questions.stem: A controlled experiment is one that

choices.A: proceeds slowly enough that a scientist can make careful records of the results.
choices.B: tests experimental and control groups in parallel.
choices.C: is repeated many times to make sure the results are accurate.
choices.D: keeps all variables constant.

questions.answer_text: tests experimental and control groups in parallel.

chapter.title: Evolution, the Themes of Biology, and Scientific Inquiry

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best distinguishes hypotheses from theories in science?

choices.A: Theories are hypotheses that have been proved.
choices.B: Hypotheses are guesses; theories are correct answers.
choices.C: Hypotheses usually are relatively narrow in scope; theories have broad explanatory power.
choices.D: Theories are proved true; hypotheses are often contradicted by experimental results.

questions.answer_text: Hypotheses usually are relatively narrow in scope; theories have broad explanatory power.

chapter.title: Evolution, the Themes of Biology, and Scientific Inquiry

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of qualitative data?

choices.A: The fish swam in a zigzag motion.
choices.B: The contents of the stomach are mixed every 20 seconds.
choices.C: The temperature decreased from 20°C to 15°C.
choices.D: The six pairs of robins hatched an average of three chicks each.

questions.answer_text: The fish swam in a zigzag motion.

chapter.title: Evolution, the Themes of Biology, and Scientific Inquiry

questions.stem: Which sentence best describes the logic of scientific inquiry?

choices.A: If I generate a testable hypothesis, tests and observations will support it.
choices.B: If my prediction is correct, it will lead to a testable hypothesis.
choices.C: If my observations are accurate, they will support my hypothesis.
choices.D: If my hypothesis is correct, I can expect certain test results.

questions.answer_text: If my hypothesis is correct, I can expect certain test results.

questions.stem: About 25 of the 92 natural elements are known to be essential to life. Which 4 of these 25 elements make up approximately 96% of living matter?

choices.C: oxygen, hydrogen, calcium, nitrogen
choices.D: carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen

questions.answer_text: carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen

questions.stem: Trace elements are those required by an organism in only minute quantities. Which of the following is a trace element that is required by humans and other vertebrates, but not by other organisms such as bacteria or plants?

choices.C: sodium
choices.D: phosphorus

questions.answer_text: iodine

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE?

choices.A: Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and calcium are the most abundant elements of living matter.
choices.B: Some naturally occurring elements are toxic to organisms.
choices.C: All life requires the same essential elements.
choices.D: A patient suffering from a goiter should not consume seafood.

questions.answer_text: Some naturally occurring elements are toxic to organisms.

questions.stem: Which of the following are compounds?

choices.C: O2 and CH4
choices.D: H2O and CH4, but not O2

questions.answer_text: H2O and CH4, but not O2

questions.stem: Atoms have no electric charge because they have ________.

choices.B: an equal number of protons and neutrons
choices.C: an equal number of protons and electrons
choices.D: an equal number of charged and uncharged subatomic particles

questions.answer_text: an equal number of protons and electrons

questions.stem: An ion with six protons, seven neutrons, and a charge of 2+ has an atomic number of ________.

choices.C: six
choices.D: seven

questions.answer_text: six

questions.stem: Molybdenum has an atomic number of 42. Several common isotopes exist, with mass numbers from 92-100. Which of the following can be true?

choices.A: Molybdenum atoms can have between 50 and 58 neutrons.
choices.B: Molybdenum atoms can have between 50 and 58 protons.
choices.C: Molybdenum atoms can have between 50 and 58 electrons.
choices.D: Isotopes of molybdenum have different numbers of electrons.

questions.answer_text: Molybdenum atoms can have between 50 and 58 neutrons.

questions.stem: Carbon-14 has the same ________.

choices.A: atomic number and atomic mass as carbon-12
choices.B: atomic number and thus number of neutrons as carbon-13
choices.C: atomic mass as both carbon-12 and carbon-13
choices.D: number of protons but more neutrons than carbon-12

questions.answer_text: number of protons but more neutrons than carbon-12

questions.stem: A(n) ________ has charge but negligible mass, whereas a(n) ________ has mass but no charge.

choices.C: neutron; electron
choices.D: electron; neutron

questions.answer_text: electron; neutron

questions.stem: The atomic number of nitrogen is 7. Nitrogen-15 has a greater mass number than nitrogen-14 because the atomic nucleus of nitrogen-15 contains ________.

choices.C: 8 protons
choices.D: 15 protons

questions.answer_text: 8 neutrons

questions.stem: The left to right order of elements in the periodic table is based on their ________.

choices.C: electric charge of the atom
choices.D: the number of neutrons

questions.answer_text: atomic number

questions.stem: A neutral atom has two, eight, eight electrons in its first, second, and third energy levels. This information ________.

choices.A: does not tell us about the atomic number of the element
choices.B: does not tell us about the chemical properties of the element
choices.C: does not tell us about the atomic mass of the element
choices.D: does not tell us about the size of the element

questions.answer_text: does not tell us about the atomic mass of the element

questions.stem: In a chemical reaction, the element 13Al will most preferably ________.

choices.A: lose three electrons and become positively charged
choices.B: gain five electrons and become negatively charged
choices.C: lose five electrons and become positively charged
choices.D: gain three electrons and become positively charged

questions.answer_text: lose three electrons and become positively charged

questions.stem: What element does not prefer to react with other elements?

choices.C: beryllium
choices.D: both hydrogen and beryllium

questions.answer_text: helium

questions.stem: Which pair of elements would likely have similar valency and thus similar chemical behavior?

choices.C: sodium and chlorine
choices.D: hydrogen and helium

questions.answer_text: nitrogen and phosphorus

questions.stem: How many electrons are present in a Phosphorus 3+ atom?
How many electrons will a single atom of sulfur with no charge and no bonds have in its valence shell?
Oxygen has an atomic number of 8 and, most commonly, a mass number of 16. Thus, what is the atomic mass of an oxygen atom?

choices.C: approximately 16 grams
choices.D: approximately 16 daltons

questions.answer_text: approximately 16 daltons

questions.stem: Elements 72Zn, 75As, and 74Ge have the ________.

choices.B: same number of protons and electrons
choices.C: same number of neutrons
choices.D: same number of neutrons and electrons

questions.answer_text: same number of neutrons

questions.stem: Can the atomic mass of an element vary?

choices.A: No, it is fixed; otherwise a new element will be formed.
choices.B: Yes. Adding or losing electrons will substantially change the atomic mass.
choices.C: Yes. Adding or losing protons will change the atomic mass without forming a different element.
choices.D: Yes. Adding or losing neutrons will change the atomic mass without forming a different element.

questions.answer_text: Yes. Adding or losing neutrons will change the atomic mass without forming a different element.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best description of an atom's physical structure?

choices.A: An atom is a solid mass of material.
choices.B: The particles that form an atom are equidistant from each other.
choices.C: Atoms are little bubbles of space with mass concentrated at the center of the bubble.
choices.D: Atoms are little bubbles of space with mass concentrated on the outside surface of the bubble.

questions.answer_text: Atoms are little bubbles of space with mass concentrated at the center of the bubble.

questions.stem: When are atoms most stable?

choices.A: when they have the fewest possible valence electrons
choices.B: when they have the maximum number of unpaired electrons
choices.C: when all of the electron orbitals in the valence shell are filled
choices.D: when all electrons are paired

questions.answer_text: when all of the electron orbitals in the valence shell are filled

questions.stem: A salamander relies on hydrogen bonding to stick to various surfaces. Therefore, a salamander would have the greatest difficulty clinging to a ________.

choices.C: surface of mostly carbon-oxygen bonds
choices.D: surface of mostly carbon-nitrogen bonds

questions.answer_text: surface of hydrocarbons

questions.stem: Which one of the atoms shown would be most likely to form a cation with a charge of +1?
Which one of the atoms shown would be most likely to form an anion with a charge of -1?
A covalent chemical bond is one in which ________.

choices.A: electrons are removed from one atom and transferred to another atom so that the two atoms become oppositely charged
choices.B: protons and neutrons are shared by two atoms so as to satisfy the requirements of both atoms
choices.C: outer-shell electrons of two atoms are shared so as to satisfactorily fill their respective orbitals
choices.D: outer-shell electrons of one atom are transferred to fill the inner electron shell of another atom

questions.answer_text: outer-shell electrons of two atoms are shared so as to satisfactorily fill their respective orbitals

questions.stem: What is the maximum number of covalent bonds that an oxygen atom with atomic number 8 can make with hydrogen?
Nitrogen (N) is more electronegative than hydrogen (H). Which of the following is a correct statement about the atoms in ammonia (NH3)?

choices.A: Each hydrogen atom has a partial positive charge; the nitrogen atom has a partial negative charge.
choices.B: Ammonia has an overall positive charge.
choices.C: Ammonia has an overall negative charge.
choices.D: The nitrogen atom has a partial positive charge; each hydrogen atom has a partial negative charge.

questions.answer_text: Each hydrogen atom has a partial positive charge; the nitrogen atom has a partial negative charge.

questions.stem: Bonds between two atoms that are equally electronegative are ________.

choices.C: nonpolar covalent bonds
choices.D: ionic bonds

questions.answer_text: nonpolar covalent bonds

questions.stem: In the following structure where A and B represent two different elements, the valency of A is ________ and B is ________.

choices.C: three; five
choices.D: eight; eight

questions.answer_text: one; three

questions.stem: A covalent bond is likely to be polar when ________.

choices.A: one of the atoms sharing electrons is more electronegative than the other atom
choices.B: the two atoms sharing electrons are equally electronegative
choices.C: carbon is one of the two atoms sharing electrons
choices.D: the two atoms sharing electrons are of the same elements

questions.answer_text: one of the atoms sharing electrons is more electronegative than the other atom

questions.stem: What is the difference between covalent bonds and ionic bonds?

choices.A: Covalent bonds involve the sharing of pairs of electrons between atoms; ionic bonds involve the sharing of single electrons between atoms.
choices.B: Covalent bonds involve the sharing of electrons between atoms; ionic bonds involve the electrical attraction between charged atoms.
choices.C: Covalent bonds involve the sharing of electrons between atoms; ionic bonds involve the sharing of protons between charged atoms.
choices.D: Covalent bonds involve the transfer of electrons between charged atoms; ionic bonds involve the sharing of electrons between atoms.

questions.answer_text: Covalent bonds involve the sharing of electrons between atoms; ionic bonds involve the electrical attraction between charged atoms.

questions.stem: The atomic number of chlorine is 17. The atomic number of magnesium is 12. What is the formula for magnesium chloride?

choices.C: Mg2Cl
choices.D: MgCl3

questions.answer_text: MgCl2

questions.stem: How many electron pairs are shared between carbon atoms in a molecule that has the formula C2H4?

choices.C: three
choices.D: four

questions.answer_text: two

questions.stem: Which bond or interaction would be difficult to disrupt when compounds are put into water?

choices.C: ionic bonds
choices.D: ionic and hydrogen bonds

questions.answer_text: covalent bonds between carbon atoms

questions.stem: Which of the following is broken when water evaporates?

choices.C: hydrogen bonds
choices.D: polar covalent bonds

questions.answer_text: hydrogen bonds

questions.stem: Van der Waals interactions may result when ________.

choices.A: electrons are not symmetrically distributed in a molecule
choices.B: molecules held by ionic bonds react with water
choices.C: two polar covalent bonds react
choices.D: a hydrogen atom loses an electron

questions.answer_text: electrons are not symmetrically distributed in a molecule

questions.stem: What is the maximum number of hydrogen atoms that can be covalently bonded in a molecule containing two carbon atoms?

choices.C: six
choices.D: eight

questions.answer_text: six

questions.stem: What results from the chemical reaction in the illustration? The reactants have no charge.

choices.A: a cation with a net charge of +1 and an anion with a net charge of +1
choices.B: a cation with a net charge of -1 and an anion with a net charge of -1
choices.C: a cation with a net charge of -1 and an anion with a net charge of +1
choices.D: a cation with a net charge of +1 and an anion with a net charge of -1

questions.answer_text: a cation with a net charge of +1 and an anion with a net charge of -1

questions.stem: What is the atomic number of the cation formed in the reaction in the illustration?
What causes the shape of the molecule shown?

choices.A: the shape of the two p orbitals in the carbon atom
choices.B: the shape of the one s orbital in the carbon atom
choices.C: the shape of the sp3 hybrid orbitals of the electrons shared between the carbon and hydrogen atoms
choices.D: hydrogen bonding configurations between the carbon and hydrogen atoms

questions.answer_text: the shape of the sp3 hybrid orbitals of the electrons shared between the carbon and hydrogen atoms

questions.stem: How many electrons are involved in a triple covalent bond?
Based on electron configuration, which of the elements in the figure would exhibit a chemical behavior most like that of oxygen?

choices.C: sulfur
choices.D: phosphorus

questions.answer_text: sulfur

questions.stem: If an atom has a charge of +1, which of the following must be true?

choices.A: It has two more protons than neutrons.
choices.B: It has the same number of protons as electrons.
choices.C: It has one more electron than it does protons.
choices.D: It has one more proton than it does electrons.

questions.answer_text: It has one more proton than it does electrons.

questions.stem: Elements found on the left side of the periodic table contain outer shells that are ________; these elements tend to form ________ in solution.

choices.C: almost full; cations
choices.D: almost full; anions

questions.answer_text: almost empty; cations

questions.stem: An atom has four electrons in its valence shell. What types of covalent bonds is it capable of forming?

choices.C: single bonds only
choices.D: double bonds only

questions.answer_text: single, double, or triple

questions.stem: When the atoms involved in a covalent bond have the same electronegativity, what type of bond results?

choices.C: a nonpolar covalent bond
choices.D: a polar covalent bond

questions.answer_text: a nonpolar covalent bond

questions.stem: Nitrogen (N) normally forms three covalent bonds with a valence of five. However, ammonium has four covalent bonds, each to a different hydrogen (H) atom (H has a valence of one). What do you predict to be the charge on ammonium?
You are asked to indicate the type and number of atoms in a molecule. Which representation would work best?

choices.C: ball-and-stick model
choices.D: space-filling model

questions.answer_text: molecular formula

questions.stem: How is a single covalent bond formed?

choices.A: Two atoms share two pairs of electrons.
choices.C: Two atoms share one electron.
choices.D: One atom loses a pair of electrons to the other.

questions.answer_text: Two atoms share two electrons.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true for the reaction?

choices.B: Hydrogen and nitrogen are the reactants of the reverse reaction.
choices.C: Ammonia is being formed and decomposed simultaneously.
choices.D: Only the forward or reverse reactions can occur at one time.

questions.answer_text: Ammonia is being formed and decomposed simultaneously.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors will increase the rate of reaction in the forward direction?

choices.C: addition of hydrogen
choices.D: addition of both nitrogen and hydrogen

questions.answer_text: addition of both nitrogen and hydrogen

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes chemical equilibrium?

choices.A: Forward and reverse reactions continue with no net effect on the concentrations of the reactants and products.
choices.B: Concentrations of products are higher than the concentrations of the reactants.
choices.C: There are equal concentrations of products and reactants while forward and reverse reactions continue.
choices.D: There are equal concentrations of reactants and products, and the reactions have stopped.

questions.answer_text: Forward and reverse reactions continue with no net effect on the concentrations of the reactants and products.

questions.stem: In the term trace element, the adjective trace means that

choices.A: the element is required in very small amounts.
choices.B: the element can be used as a label to trace atoms through an organism's metabolism.
choices.C: the element is very rare on Earth.
choices.D: the element enhances health but is not essential for the organism's long-term survival.

questions.answer_text: the element is required in very small amounts.

questions.stem: Compared with 31P, the radioactive isotope 32P has

choices.C: one more electron.
choices.D: one more neutron.

questions.answer_text: one more neutron.

questions.stem: The reactivity of an atom arises from

choices.A: the average distance of the outermost electron shell from the nucleus.
choices.B: the existence of unpaired electrons in the valence shell.
choices.C: the sum of the potential energies of all the electron shells.
choices.D: the potential energy of the valence shell.

questions.answer_text: the existence of unpaired electrons in the valence shell.

questions.stem: Which statement is true of all atoms that are anions?

choices.A: The atom has more electrons than protons.
choices.B: The atom has more protons than electrons.
choices.C: The atom has fewer protons than does a neutral atom of the same element.
choices.D: The atom has more neutrons than protons.

questions.answer_text: The atom has more electrons than protons.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes any chemical reaction that has reached equilibrium?

choices.A: The concentrations of products and reactants are equal.
choices.C: Both forward and reverse reactions have halted.
choices.D: The rates of the forward and reverse reactions are equal.

questions.answer_text: The rates of the forward and reverse reactions are equal.

questions.stem: We can represent atoms by listing the number of protons, neutrons, and electrons—for example, 2p+, 2n0, 2e- for helium. Which of the following represents the 18O isotope of oxygen?

The atomic number of sulfur is 16. Sulfur combines with hydrogen by covalent bonding to form a compound, hydrogen sulfide. Based on the number of valence electrons in a sulfur atom, predict the molecular formula of the compound.

choices.C: H2S
choices.D: H4S

questions.answer_text: H2S

questions.stem: What coefficients must be placed in the following blanks so that all atoms are accounted for in the products? C6H12O6 → ________ C2H6O + ________ CO2
In a single molecule of water, two hydrogen atoms are bonded to a single oxygen atom by ________.

choices.C: polar covalent bonds
choices.D: ionic bonds

questions.answer_text: polar covalent bonds

questions.stem: The partial negative charge at one end of a water molecule is attracted to the partial positive charge of another water molecule. What is this attraction called?

choices.C: an ionic bond
choices.D: a van der Waals interaction

questions.answer_text: a hydrogen bond

questions.stem: The partial negative charge in a molecule of water occurs because ________.

choices.A: the oxygen atom donates an electron to each of the hydrogen atoms
choices.B: the electrons shared between the oxygen and hydrogen atoms spend more time around the oxygen atom nucleus than around the hydrogen atom nucleus
choices.C: the oxygen atom has two pairs of electrons in its valence shell that are not neutralized by hydrogen atoms
choices.D: one of the hydrogen atoms donates an electron to the oxygen atom

questions.answer_text: the electrons shared between the oxygen and hydrogen atoms spend more time around the oxygen atom nucleus than around the hydrogen atom nucleus

questions.stem: Sulfur is in the same column of the periodic table as oxygen, but has electronegativity similar to carbon. Compared to water molecules, molecules of H2S will ________.

choices.A: have greater cohesion to other molecules of H2S
choices.B: have a greater tendency to form hydrogen bonds with each other
choices.C: have a higher capacity to absorb heat for the same change in temperature
choices.D: not form hydrogen bonds with each other

questions.answer_text: not form hydrogen bonds with each other

questions.stem: Water molecules can form hydrogen bonds with ________.

choices.A: compounds that have polar covalent bonds
choices.C: oxygen gas (O2) molecules
choices.D: chloride ions

questions.answer_text: compounds that have polar covalent bonds

questions.stem: Cohesion, surface tension, and adhesion are the properties of water molecules that ________.

choices.C: are a result of hydrogen bonding
choices.D: are a result of polar covalent bonding

questions.answer_text: are a result of hydrogen bonding

questions.stem: Liquid water ________.

choices.B: has a specific heat lower than that of most other substances
choices.C: has a heat of vaporization higher than that of most other substances
choices.D: is nonpolar

questions.answer_text: has a heat of vaporization higher than that of most other substances

questions.stem: Which of the following can be attributed to water's high specific heat?

choices.A: Oil and water do not mix well.
choices.B: A lake heats up more slowly than the air around it.
choices.C: Ice floats on water.
choices.D: Sugar dissolves in hot tea faster than in iced tea.

questions.answer_text: A lake heats up more slowly than the air around it.

questions.stem: The cities of Portland, Oregon, and Minneapolis, Minnesota, are at about the same latitude, but Minneapolis has much hotter summers and much colder winters than Portland. Why?

choices.A: They are not at the same exact latitude.
choices.B: The ocean near Portland moderates the temperature.
choices.C: Fresh water is more likely to freeze than salt water.
choices.D: Minneapolis is much windier, due to its location in the middle of North America.

questions.answer_text: The ocean near Portland moderates the temperature.

questions.stem: To act as an effective coolant in a car's radiator, a substance has to have the capacity to absorb a great deal of heat. You have a reference book with tables listing the physical properties of many liquids. In choosing a coolant for your car, which table would you check first?

choices.C: heat of vaporization
choices.D: specific heat

questions.answer_text: specific heat

questions.stem: Water has many exceptional and useful properties. Which is the rarest property among compounds?

choices.B: Solid water is less dense than liquid water.
choices.C: Water has a high heat capacity.
choices.D: Water has surface tension.

questions.answer_text: Solid water is less dense than liquid water.

questions.stem: Which of the following effects can occur because of the high surface tension of water?

choices.A: Lakes cannot freeze solid in winter, despite low temperatures.
choices.B: A raft spider can walk across the surface of a small pond.
choices.C: Organisms can resist temperature changes, although they give off heat due to chemical reactions.
choices.D: Sweat can evaporate from the skin, helping to keep people from overheating.

questions.answer_text: A raft spider can walk across the surface of a small pond.

questions.stem: Thermal energy of the water in a bathtub is ________ than in a freshly brewed coffee pot because of its ________.

choices.C: lower; low temperature
choices.D: lower; low density

questions.answer_text: higher; greater volume

questions.stem: Low humidity in the atmosphere on a hot day ________.

choices.A: helps in cooling because skin absorbs water from the atmosphere
choices.B: does not help in cooling because water evaporates from the skin faster
choices.C: helps in cooling because water evaporates from the skin faster
choices.D: does not help in cooling because skin absorbs water from the atmosphere

questions.answer_text: helps in cooling because water evaporates from the skin faster

questions.stem: A dietary Calorie equals 1 kilocalorie. One kilocalorie equals ________.

choices.A: 1000 calories, or the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 g of water by 1°C
choices.B: 10,000 calories, or the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of water by 1°F
choices.C: 1000 calories, or the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of water by 1°C
choices.D: 1000 calories, or the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 100 g of water by 100°C

questions.answer_text: 1000 calories, or the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of water by 1°C

questions.stem: Why does ice float in liquid water?

choices.A: The high surface tension of liquid water keeps the ice on top.
choices.B: The ionic bonds between the molecules in ice prevent the ice from sinking.
choices.C: Stable hydrogen bonds keep water molecules of ice farther apart than water molecules of liquid water.
choices.D: The crystalline lattice of ice causes it to be denser than liquid water.

questions.answer_text: Stable hydrogen bonds keep water molecules of ice farther apart than water molecules of liquid water.

questions.stem: Hydrophobic substances such as vegetable oil are ________.

choices.A: nonpolar substances that repel water molecules
choices.B: nonpolar substances that have an attraction for water molecules
choices.C: polar substances that repel water molecules
choices.D: polar substances that have an affinity for water

questions.answer_text: nonpolar substances that repel water molecules

questions.stem: Why is a steam burn more severe than a hot water burn?

choices.A: Burns caused by liquids are always milder.
choices.B: Steam can penetrate into the skin.
choices.C: Steam contains more energy than water.
choices.D: Water evaporates and leaves the surface faster and helps in cooling.

questions.answer_text: Steam contains more energy than water.

questions.stem: Melting of ice and thus reduced feeding opportunities for polar bears is occurring because of the ________.

choices.B: drying up of lakes and streams
choices.C: constant breaking and reforming of hydrogen bonds in water
choices.D: increase in CO2 and other greenhouse gases in the atmosphere

questions.answer_text: increase in CO2 and other greenhouse gases in the atmosphere

questions.stem: One mole (mol) of glucose (molecular mass = 180 daltons) is ________.

choices.B: 1 kilogram of glucose dissolved in 1 liter of solution
choices.C: 180 mL of dissolved glucose
choices.D: 180 grams of glucose

questions.answer_text: 180 grams of glucose

questions.stem: When an ionic compound such as sodium chloride (NaCl) is placed in water, the component atoms of the NaCl crystal dissociate into individual sodium ions (Na+) and chloride ions (Cl-). In contrast, the atoms of covalently bonded molecules (e.g., glucose, sucrose, glycerol) do not generally dissociate when placed in aqueous solution. Which of the following solutions would be expected to contain the greatest number of solute particles (molecules or ions)?

choices.C: 1 liter of 1.0 M glucose
choices.D: 1 liter of 1.0 M NaCl and 1 liter of 1.0 M glucose will contain equal numbers of solute particles.

questions.answer_text: 1 liter of 1.0 M NaCl

questions.stem: The molar mass of glucose is 180 grams per mole (g/mol). Which of the following procedures should you carry out to make a 1 M solution of glucose? In 0.8 liter (L) of water, dissolve ________.

choices.A: 1 g of glucose, and then add more water until the total volume of the solution is 1 L
choices.B: 18 g of glucose, and then add more water until the total volume of the solution is 1 L
choices.C: 180 g of glucose, and then add 0.2 L more of water
choices.D: 180 g of glucose, and then add more water until the total volume of the solution is 1 L

questions.answer_text: 180 g of glucose, and then add more water until the total volume of the solution is 1 L

questions.stem: You have a freshly prepared 0.1 M sucrose (molecular mass 342) solution, which means ________.

choices.A: 6.02 × 1023 of sucrose molecules are present in the solution
choices.B: 6.02 × 1022 of sucrose molecules are present in the solution
choices.C: 34.2 g of sucrose is present in the solution
choices.D: 6.02 × 1022 of sucrose molecules or 34.2 g of sucrose is present in the solution

questions.answer_text: 6.02 × 1022 of sucrose molecules or 34.2 g of sucrose is present in the solution

questions.stem: How does 0.5 M sucrose (molecular mass 342) solution compare to 0.5 M glucose (molecular mass 180) solution?

choices.B: Sucrose has 171 molecules, whereas glucose has 90.
choices.C: Both have 3.01 × 1023 molecules.
choices.D: Sucrose has 171 mg/L, whereas glucose has 90 mg/L.

questions.answer_text: Both have 3.01 × 1023 molecules.

questions.stem: Use the following figure to answer the question. Based on your knowledge of the polarity of water molecules, the solute molecule depicted is most likely ________.

choices.C: without charge
choices.D: nonpolar

questions.answer_text: positively charged

questions.stem: Use the following figure to answer the question. Two moles of the compound in the figure would weigh how many grams? (Note: The atomic masses, in daltons, are approximately 12 for carbon, 1 for hydrogen, and 16 for oxygen.)

questions.stem: Which of the following are found in plant, animal, and bacterial cells?

choices.C: chloroplasts
choices.D: endoplasmic reticulum

questions.answer_text: ribosomes

questions.stem: In bacteria, DNA will be found in ________.

choices.C: the nucleoid
choices.D: ribosomes

questions.answer_text: the nucleoid

questions.stem: What is the function of the nuclear pore complex found in eukaryotes?

choices.A: It regulates the movement of proteins and RNAs into and out of the nucleus.
choices.B: It synthesizes the proteins required to copy DNA and make mRNA.
choices.C: It synthesizes secreted proteins.
choices.D: It assembles ribosomes from raw materials that are synthesized in the nucleus.

questions.answer_text: It regulates the movement of proteins and RNAs into and out of the nucleus.

questions.stem: Which of the following macromolecules leave the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell through pores in the nuclear membrane?

choices.C: mRNA
choices.D: phospholipids

questions.answer_text: mRNA

questions.stem: Which of the following macromolecules enter the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell through pores in the nuclear membrane?

choices.C: rRNA
choices.D: phospholipids

questions.answer_text: ribosomal proteins

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes some aspect of protein secretion from prokaryotic cells?

choices.A: Prokaryotes cannot secrete proteins because they lack an endomembrane system.
choices.B: Proteins secreted by prokaryotes are likely synthesized on ribosomes bound to the cytoplasmic surface of the plasma membrane.
choices.C: The mechanism of protein secretion in prokaryotes is probably the same as that in eukaryotes.
choices.D: Prokaryotes cannot secrete proteins because they lack rough endoplasmic reticulum.

questions.answer_text: Proteins secreted by prokaryotes are likely synthesized on ribosomes bound to the cytoplasmic surface of the plasma membrane.

questions.stem: Examination of a cell by transmission electron microscopy reveals a high density of ribosomes in the cytoplasm. This observation suggests that this cell is actively producing large amounts of which of the following molecules?

choices.C: lipids
choices.D: nucleic acids

questions.answer_text: proteins

questions.stem: The nuclear lamina is an array of intermediate filaments that line the inner side of the nuclear membrane. If a chemical treatment caused the lamina to disassemble, what would you expect to be the most likely immediate consequence?

choices.B: the inability of the nucleus to divide during cell division
choices.C: a loss of genetic information from chromosomes
choices.D: a change in the shape of the nucleus

questions.answer_text: a change in the shape of the nucleus

questions.stem: A cell with a predominance of rough endoplasmic reticulum is most likely ________.

choices.A: producing large quantities of proteins for secretion
choices.B: producing large quantities of proteins in the cytosol
choices.C: producing large quantities of carbohydrates to assemble an extensive cell wall matrix
choices.D: producing large quantities of carbohydrates for storage in the vacuole

questions.answer_text: producing large quantities of proteins for secretion

questions.stem: Which organelle often takes up much of the volume of a plant cell?

choices.C: Golgi apparatus
choices.D: chloroplast

questions.answer_text: central vacuole

questions.stem: A cell with a predominance of smooth endoplasmic reticulum is likely specialized to ________.

choices.B: import and export large quantities of protein
choices.C: actively secrete large quantities of protein
choices.D: synthesize large quantities of lipids

questions.answer_text: synthesize large quantities of lipids

questions.stem: Which structure below is independent of the endomembrane system?

choices.C: Golgi apparatus
choices.D: plasma membrane

questions.answer_text: chloroplast

questions.stem: Tay-Sachs disease is a human genetic abnormality that results in cells accumulating and becoming clogged with very large, complex, undigested lipids. Which cellular organelle is most likely defective in this condition?

choices.C: the smooth endoplasmic reticulum
choices.D: the rough endoplasmic reticulum

questions.answer_text: the lysosome

questions.stem: The liver is involved in detoxification of many poisons and drugs. Which of the following structures is primarily involved in this process and, therefore, abundant in liver cells?

choices.C: Golgi apparatus
choices.D: nuclear envelope

questions.answer_text: smooth endoplasmic reticulum

questions.stem: Which of the following organelles produces and modifies polysaccharides that will be secreted?

choices.C: Golgi apparatus
choices.D: peroxisome

questions.answer_text: Golgi apparatus

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common pathway taken by a newly synthesized protein that will be secreted by a cell?

choices.A: rough ER → Golgi → transport vesicle → nucleus
choices.B: Golgi → rough ER → lysosome → transport vesicle → plasma membrane
choices.C: rough ER → Golgi → transport vesicle → plasma membrane
choices.D: rough ER → lysosome → transport vesicle → plasma membrane

questions.answer_text: rough ER → Golgi → transport vesicle → plasma membrane

questions.stem: Asbestos is a material that was once used extensively in construction. One risk from working in a building that contains asbestos is the development of asbestosis caused by the inhalation of asbestos fibers. Cells will take up asbestos by phagocytosis, but are not able to degrade it. As a result, asbestos fibers accumulate in ________.

choices.C: peroxisomes
choices.D: lysosomes

questions.answer_text: lysosomes

questions.stem: Which organelle is the primary site of ATP synthesis in eukaryotic cells?

choices.C: Golgi apparatus
choices.D: peroxisome

questions.answer_text: mitochondrion

questions.stem: Thylakoids, DNA, and ribosomes are all components found in ________.

choices.C: lysosomes
choices.D: nuclei

questions.answer_text: chloroplasts

questions.stem: If plant cells are grown on media containing radioactively labeled thymine for one generation, radioactively labeled macromolecules will be detected in which of the following?

choices.B: only in the nucleus and mitochondria
choices.C: only in the nucleus and chloroplasts
choices.D: in the nucleus, mitochondria, and chloroplasts

questions.answer_text: in the nucleus, mitochondria, and chloroplasts

questions.stem: In a liver cell detoxifying alcohol and some other poisons, the enzymes of the peroxisome remove hydrogen from these molecules and ________.

choices.A: combine the hydrogen with water molecules to generate hydrogen peroxide
choices.B: combine the hydrogen with oxygen molecules to generate hydrogen peroxide
choices.C: combine the hydrogen with hydrogen peroxide to generate oxygen
choices.D: combine the hydrogen with hydrogen peroxide to generate oxygen and water

questions.answer_text: combine the hydrogen with oxygen molecules to generate hydrogen peroxide

questions.stem: The evolution of eukaryotic cells most likely involved ________.

choices.A: endosymbiosis of an oxygen-using bacterium in a larger bacterial host cell-the endosymbiont evolved into chloroplasts
choices.B: endosymbiosis of a photosynthetic archaeal cell in a larger bacterial host cell to escape toxic oxygen—the anaerobic archaea evolved into chloroplasts
choices.C: endosymbiosis of an oxygen-using bacterium in a larger bacterial host cell-the endosymbiont evolved into mitochondria
choices.D: evolution of an endomembrane system and subsequent evolution of mitochondria from a portion of the smooth endoplasmic reticulum

questions.answer_text: endosymbiosis of an oxygen-using bacterium in a larger bacterial host cell-the endosymbiont evolved into mitochondria

questions.stem: Where are proteins produced other than on ribosomes free in the cytosol or ribosomes attached to the endoplasmic reticulum?

choices.C: in the nucleolus
choices.D: in mitochondria

questions.answer_text: in mitochondria

questions.stem: Suppose a cell has the following molecules and structures: enzymes, DNA, ribosomes, plasma membrane, and mitochondria. It could be a cell from ________.

choices.A: a bacterium, but not a eukaryote
choices.B: an animal, but not a plant
choices.C: nearly any eukaryotic organism
choices.D: a plant, but not an animal

questions.answer_text: nearly any eukaryotic organism

questions.stem: Cyanide binds with at least one molecule involved in producing ATP. If a cell is exposed to cyanide, most of the bound cyanide is likely to be localized within the ________.

choices.C: lysosomes
choices.D: smooth endoplasmic reticulum

questions.answer_text: mitochondria

questions.stem: Suppose a young boy is always tired and fatigued, suffering from a metabolic disease. Which of the following organelles is most likely malfunctioning in this disease?

choices.C: mitochondria
choices.D: smooth endoplasmic reticulum

questions.answer_text: mitochondria

questions.stem: Motor proteins provide for molecular motion in cells by interacting with what types of cellular structures?

choices.A: membrane proteins of the inner nuclear envelope
choices.B: free ribosomes and ribosomes attached to the ER
choices.C: components of the cytoskeleton
choices.D: cellulose fibers in the cell wall

questions.answer_text: components of the cytoskeleton

questions.stem: A characteristic 9 + 2 arrangement of microtubules, consisting of nine doublets of microtubules surrounding a pair of single microtubules is associated with ________.

choices.C: eukaryotic flagella, motile cilia, and nonmotile cilia
choices.D: centrioles and basal bodies

questions.answer_text: eukaryotic flagella and motile cilia

questions.stem: Vinblastine, a drug that inhibits microtubule polymerization, is used to treat some forms of cancer. Cancer cells given vinblastine would be unable to ________.

choices.A: form cleavage furrows during cell division
choices.C: separate chromosomes during cell division
choices.D: maintain the shape of the nucleus

questions.answer_text: separate chromosomes during cell division

questions.stem: Amoebae move by crawling over a surface (cell crawling), which involves ________.

choices.A: growth of actin filaments to form bulges in the plasma membrane
choices.B: assembly of microtubule extensions that vesicles can follow in the direction of movement
choices.C: reinforcement of the pseudopod with intermediate filaments
choices.D: localized contractions driven by myosin and microtubules

questions.answer_text: growth of actin filaments to form bulges in the plasma membrane

questions.stem: Researchers investigating the mechanism of vesicular transport assembled a cell-free system that included microtubule tracks, vesicles, and ATP. However, they observed no movement of transport of vesicles in this system. What were they missing?

choices.C: intermediate filaments
choices.D: motor proteins

questions.answer_text: motor proteins

questions.stem: Cilia and flagella bend because of ________.

choices.A: conformational changes in ATP that thrust microtubules laterally
choices.B: a motor protein called radial spokes
choices.C: contraction by myosin
choices.D: a motor protein called dynein

questions.answer_text: a motor protein called dynein

questions.stem: Spherocytosis is a human blood disorder associated with a defective cytoskeletal protein in the red blood cells (RBCs). What do you suspect is the consequence of such a defect?

choices.B: an insufficient supply of ATP in the RBCs
choices.C: an insufficient supply of oxygen-transporting proteins in the RBCs
choices.D: adherence of RBCs to blood vessel walls, causing plaque formation

questions.answer_text: abnormally shaped RBCs

questions.stem: Cytochalasin D is a drug that prevents actin polymerization. A cell treated with cytochalasin D will still be able to carry out which of the following processes?

choices.C: extend pseudopodia
choices.D: move vesicles within a cell

questions.answer_text: move vesicles within a cell

questions.stem: Cells require which of the following to form cilia or flagella?

choices.C: actin
choices.D: intermediate filaments

questions.answer_text: tubulin

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the cytoskeleton is true?

choices.A: The cytoskeleton of eukaryotes is a static structure most resembling scaffolding used at construction sites.
choices.B: Although microtubules are common within a cell, actin filaments are rarely found outside of the nucleus.
choices.C: Movement of cilia and flagella is the result of motor proteins causing microtubules to move relative to each other.
choices.D: Chemicals that block the assembly of the cytoskeleton would have little effect on a cell's response to external stimuli.

questions.answer_text: Movement of cilia and flagella is the result of motor proteins causing microtubules to move relative to each other.

questions.stem: The cell walls of bacteria, fungi, and plant cells, and the extracellular matrix of animal cells are all external to the plasma membrane. Which of the following characteristics are common to all of these extracellular structures?

choices.A: They must block water and small molecules to regulate the exchange of matter and energy with their environment.
choices.B: They must provide a rigid structure that maintains an appropriate ratio of cell surface area to volume.
choices.C: They are constructed of materials that are synthesized in the cytoplasm and then transported out of the cell for assembly.
choices.D: They are composed of a mixture of lipids and nucleotides.

questions.answer_text: They are constructed of materials that are synthesized in the cytoplasm and then transported out of the cell for assembly.

questions.stem: A mutation that disrupts the ability of an animal cell to add polysaccharide modifications to proteins would most likely cause defects in which of the following organelles or structures?

choices.C: Golgi apparatus and extracellular matrix
choices.D: nuclear pores and secretory vesicles

questions.answer_text: Golgi apparatus and extracellular matrix

questions.stem: What is a primary function of integrins?

choices.A: connecting intermediate filaments to microtubules involved in vesicular transport
choices.B: linking the primary and secondary cell walls in plants
choices.C: transmitting signals from the extracellular matrix to the cytoskeleton
choices.D: transmitting chemical signals from the Golgi apparatus to the plasma membrane

questions.answer_text: transmitting signals from the extracellular matrix to the cytoskeleton

questions.stem: Which of the following structures form cytoplasmic channels that connect adjacent plant cells through the cell walls?

choices.C: plasmodesmata
choices.D: tight junctions

questions.answer_text: plasmodesmata

questions.stem: Ions can travel directly from the cytoplasm of one animal cell to the cytoplasm of an adjacent cell through ________.

choices.C: desmosomes
choices.D: gap junctions

questions.answer_text: gap junctions

questions.stem: In plant cells, the middle lamella ________.

choices.C: connects the cytoplasm of adjacent cells
choices.D: prevents excessive uptake of water by plant cells

questions.answer_text: glues adjacent cells together

questions.stem: A defect in which of the following intercellular junctions would allow partially digested material to leak passively between the cells of the small intestine into the abdominal cavity?

choices.C: plasmodesmata
choices.D: tight junctions

questions.answer_text: tight junctions

questions.stem: H. V. Wilson worked with sponges to gain some insight into exactly what was responsible for holding adjacent cells together. He exposed two species of differently pigmented sponges to a chemical that disrupted intercellular junctions, and the cells of the sponges dissociated. Wilson then mixed the cells of the two species and removed the chemical that caused the cells to dissociate. Wilson found that the sponges reassembled into two separate species. The cells from one species did not interact or form associations with the cells of the other species. How do you explain the results of Wilson's experiments?

choices.A: The two species of sponge had different enzymes that functioned in the reassembly process.
choices.B: The molecules responsible for cell-cell adhesion (cell junctions) were irreversibly destroyed during the experiment.
choices.C: The molecules responsible for cell-cell adhesion (cell junctions) differed between the two species of sponge.
choices.D: One cell functioned as an organizer for each organism, thereby attracting only cells of the same species.

questions.answer_text: The molecules responsible for cell-cell adhesion (cell junctions) differed between the two species of sponge.

questions.stem: Gaucher disease is the most common of lipid storage diseases in humans. It is caused by a deficiency of an enzyme necessary for the breakdown of lipids. This leads to the accumulation of fatty material in organs of the body including the spleen, liver, kidneys, lungs, brain, and bone marrow. Using your knowledge of the structure of eukaryotic cells, identify the statement below that best explains how internal membranes and the organelles of cells may be involved in Gaucher disease.

choices.A: The mitochondria are most likely defective and do not produce adequate amounts of ATP needed for cellular energy.
choices.B: The rough endoplasmic reticulum contains too many ribosomes, which results in an overproduction of the enzyme involved in lipid breakdown.
choices.C: The lysosomes lack sufficient amounts of enzymes necessary for the metabolism of lipids.
choices.D: The Golgi apparatus produces vesicles with faulty membranes, which fail to be transported to the plasma membrane for secretion.

questions.answer_text: The lysosomes lack sufficient amounts of enzymes necessary for the metabolism of lipids.

questions.stem: Both the volume and the surface area for three different cells were measured. These values are listed in the following table: Volume Surface Area Cell 1 9.3 μm3 26.5 μm2 Cell 2 12.2 μm3 37.1 μm2 Cell 3 17.6 μm3 40.6 μm2 Using data from the table above, select the best explanation for why that cell will be able to eliminate waste most efficiently?

choices.A: Cell 1, since it has the smallest volume and will not produce as much waste as the other cells.
choices.B: Cell 2, since it has the highest ratio of surface area to volume, which facilitates the exchange of materials between a cell and its environment.
choices.C: Cell 3, since it has the largest surface area, which will enable it to eliminate all of its wastes efficiently.
choices.D: Cell 3, because it is big enough to allow wastes to easily diffuse through the plasma membrane.

questions.answer_text: Cell 2, since it has the highest ratio of surface area to volume, which facilitates the exchange of materials between a cell and its environment.

questions.stem: Which structure is not part of the endomembrane system?

choices.C: Golgi apparatus
choices.D: plasma membrane

questions.answer_text: chloroplast

questions.stem: Which structure is common to plant and animal cells?

choices.C: mitochondrion
choices.D: centriole

questions.answer_text: mitochondrion

questions.stem: Which of the following is present in a prokaryotic cell?

choices.C: nuclear envelope
choices.D: chloroplast

questions.answer_text: ribosome

questions.stem: Cyanide binds to at least one molecule involved in producing ATP. If a cell is exposed to cyanide, most of the cyanide will be found within the

choices.C: peroxisomes.
choices.D: lysosomes.

questions.answer_text: mitochondria.

questions.stem: Which cell would be best for studying lysosomes?

choices.C: bacterial cell
choices.D: phagocytic white blood cell

questions.answer_text: phagocytic white blood cell

questions.stem: For a protein to be an integral membrane protein, it would have to be ________.

choices.C: amphipathic, with at least one hydrophobic region
choices.D: exposed on only one surface of the membrane

questions.answer_text: amphipathic, with at least one hydrophobic region

questions.stem: A phospholipid bilayer with equal amounts of saturated and unsaturated fatty acids displays a specific permeability to glucose. What effect will increasing the proportion of unsaturated fatty acids in the bilayer have on the membrane's permeability to glucose?

choices.C: Permeability to glucose will stay the same.
choices.D: Permeability will decrease initially then increase as the bilayer fills with glucose.

questions.answer_text: Permeability to glucose will increase.

questions.stem: According to the fluid mosaic model of cell membranes, phospholipids ________.

choices.A: can move laterally along the plane of the membrane
choices.B: frequently flip-flop from one side of the membrane to the other
choices.C: occur in an uninterrupted bilayer, with membrane proteins restricted to the surface of the membrane
choices.D: have hydrophilic tails in the interior of the membrane

questions.answer_text: can move laterally along the plane of the membrane

questions.stem: The membranes of winter wheat are able to remain fluid when it is extremely cold by ________.

choices.A: increasing the proportion of unsaturated phospholipids in the membrane
choices.B: decreasing the percentage of cholesterol molecules in the membrane
choices.C: decreasing the number of hydrophobic proteins in the membrane
choices.D: increasing the proportion of glycolipids in the membrane

questions.answer_text: increasing the proportion of unsaturated phospholipids in the membrane

questions.stem: According to the fluid mosaic model, a membrane ________.

choices.A: is composed of a fluid bilayer of phospholipids between two layers of hydrophilic proteins
choices.B: is composed of a single layer of fluid phospholipids between two layers of hydrophilic proteins
choices.C: is composed of a mosaic of fluid polysaccharides and amphipathic proteins
choices.D: is composed of a fluid bilayer of phospholipids with embedded amphipathic proteins

questions.answer_text: is composed of a fluid bilayer of phospholipids with embedded amphipathic proteins

questions.stem: An animal cell lacking carbohydrates on the external surface of its plasma membrane would likely be impaired in which function?

choices.A: transporting ions against an electrochemical gradient
choices.C: attaching the plasma membrane to the cytoskeleton
choices.D: establishing a diffusion barrier to charged molecules

questions.answer_text: cell-cell recognition

questions.stem: Which of the following types of molecules are hydrophilic and therefore excluded from the hydrophobic portion of the phospholipid bilayer?

choices.C: peripheral membrane proteins
choices.D: cholesterol

questions.answer_text: peripheral membrane proteins

questions.stem: Which of the following types of molecules lack hydrophilic domains?

choices.C: peripheral membrane proteins
choices.D: cholesterol

questions.answer_text: cholesterol

questions.stem: Why are lipids and proteins free to move laterally in membranes?

choices.A: The interior of the membrane is filled with liquid water.
choices.B: Lipids and proteins repulse each other in the membrane.
choices.C: Hydrophilic portions of the lipids are in the interior of the membrane.
choices.D: There are only weak hydrophobic interactions in the interior of the membrane.

questions.answer_text: There are only weak hydrophobic interactions in the interior of the membrane.

questions.stem: Which component in the accompanying figure is hydrophilic?

choices.C: C
choices.D: D

questions.answer_text: D

questions.stem: Which component in the accompanying figure is cholesterol?

choices.C: D
choices.D: E

questions.answer_text: E

questions.stem: Which component in the accompanying figure is a protein fiber of the extracellular matrix?

choices.C: C
choices.D: E

questions.answer_text: A

questions.stem: Which component in the accompanying figure is a microfilament (actin filament) of the cytoskeleton?

choices.C: C
choices.D: D

questions.answer_text: C

questions.stem: Which component in the accompanying figure plays a critical role in cell-cell recognition?

choices.C: C
choices.D: E

questions.answer_text: B

questions.stem: Cell membranes have distinct inside and outside faces. Which of the following statements is the most likely explanation for the membrane's asymmetrical nature?

choices.A: Since the cell membrane forms a border between one cell and another in tightly packed tissues such as epithelium, the membrane must be asymmetrical.
choices.B: Since cell membranes communicate signals from one organism to another, the cell membranes must be asymmetrical.
choices.C: The two sides of a cell membrane face different environments and carry out different functions.
choices.D: Proteins only function on the cytoplasmic side of the cell membrane, which results in the membrane's asymmetrical nature.

questions.answer_text: The two sides of a cell membrane face different environments and carry out different functions.

questions.stem: In what way do the membranes of a eukaryotic cell vary?

choices.A: Phospholipids are found only in certain membranes.
choices.B: Certain proteins are unique to each membrane.
choices.C: Only certain membranes of the cell are selectively permeable.
choices.D: Some membranes have hydrophobic surfaces exposed to the cytoplasm while others have hydrophilic surfaces facing the cytoplasm.

questions.answer_text: Certain proteins are unique to each membrane.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is a reasonable explanation for why unsaturated fatty acids help keep a membrane more fluid at lower temperatures?

choices.A: The double bonds form kinks in the fatty acid tails, preventing adjacent lipids from packing tightly.
choices.B: Unsaturated fatty acids have a higher cholesterol content, which prevents adjacent lipids from packing tightly.
choices.C: Unsaturated fatty acids are more nonpolar than saturated fatty acids.
choices.D: The double bonds block interaction among the hydrophilic head groups of the lipids.

questions.answer_text: The double bonds form kinks in the fatty acid tails, preventing adjacent lipids from packing tightly.

questions.stem: What kinds of molecules pass through a cell membrane most easily?

choices.C: large polar
choices.D: small and ionic

questions.answer_text: small and hydrophobic

questions.stem: Which of the following are least likely to diffuse through the phospholipid bilayer of a cell membrane?

choices.C: carbon dioxide
choices.D: small ions

questions.answer_text: small ions

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes a characteristic feature of a carrier protein in a plasma membrane?

choices.A: It exhibits specificity for a particular type of molecule.
choices.B: It requires the expenditure of cellular energy to function.
choices.C: It works against diffusion.
choices.D: It has no hydrophobic regions.

questions.answer_text: It exhibits specificity for a particular type of molecule.

questions.stem: Which of the following would likely diffuse through the lipid bilayer of a plasma membrane most rapidly?

choices.C: O2
choices.D: Na+

questions.answer_text: O2

questions.stem: Which of the following molecules dramatically increases the rate of diffusion of water across cell membranes?

choices.C: gated ion channels
choices.D: ATP

questions.answer_text: aquaporins

questions.stem: A research team is working on the design of a new drug for the treatment of lung cancer. To be most effective, this drug must specifically enter the cytoplasm of lung cells while not entering the cells of other tissues. Which of the following characteristics would likely enhance the specificity of this drug?

choices.A: the relative hydrophobicity of the drug molecule
choices.B: phospholipid composition of lung cell plasma membranes
choices.C: specificity of the drug molecule for binding to the extracellular matrix of lung cells
choices.D: similarity of the drug molecule to other molecules normally transported lung cells

questions.answer_text: similarity of the drug molecule to other molecules normally transported lung cells

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about diffusion is true?

choices.A: It is very rapid over long distances.
choices.B: It requires an expenditure of energy by the cell.
choices.C: It is an active process in which molecules move from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration.
choices.D: It is a passive process in which molecules move from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.

questions.answer_text: It is a passive process in which molecules move from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.

questions.stem: Which of the following processes includes all of the others?

choices.C: passive transport
choices.D: transport of an ion down its electrochemical gradient

questions.answer_text: passive transport

questions.stem: When a cell is in equilibrium with its environment, which of the following processes occurs for substances that can diffuse through the plasma membrane?

choices.A: There is directed movement of substances into and out of the cell.
choices.B: There is random movement of substances into and out of the cell.
choices.C: There is no movement of substances into or out of the cell.
choices.D: All movement of molecules across the plasma membrane occurs by active transport.

questions.answer_text: There is random movement of substances into and out of the cell.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes osmosis?

choices.A: Osmosis only takes place in red blood cells.
choices.B: Osmosis is an energy-demanding or "active" process.
choices.C: In osmosis, water moves across a membrane from areas of lower solute concentration to areas of higher solute concentration.
choices.D: In osmosis, solutes move across a membrane from areas of lower water concentration to areas of higher water concentration.

questions.answer_text: In osmosis, water moves across a membrane from areas of lower solute concentration to areas of higher solute concentration.

questions.stem: The solutions in the two arms of this U-tube are separated by a membrane that is permeable to water and glucose but not to sucrose. Side A is half-filled with a solution of 2 M sucrose and 1 M glucose. Side B is half-filled with 1 M sucrose and 2 M glucose. Initially, the liquid levels on both sides are equal. In the U-tube illustrated above, ________.

choices.A: side A is hypertonic to side B
choices.B: side A is hypotonic to side B
choices.C: side A is isotonic to side B
choices.D: side A is more turgid than side B

questions.answer_text: side A is isotonic to side B

questions.stem: The solutions in the two arms of this U-tube are separated by a membrane that is permeable to water and glucose but not to sucrose. Side A is half-filled with a solution of 2 M sucrose and 1 M glucose. Side B is half-filled with 1 M sucrose and 2 M glucose. Initially, the liquid levels on both sides are equal. Which of the following will be true when the system illustrated above reaches equilibrium?

choices.A: The concentration of sucrose on side A will be greater than the concentration of sucrose on side B.
choices.B: The water level will be higher in side A than in side B.
choices.C: The water levels will be unchanged.
choices.D: The water level will be higher in side B than in side A.

questions.answer_text: The water level will be higher in side A than in side B.

questions.stem: The solutions in the two arms of this U-tube are separated by a membrane that is permeable to water and glucose but not to sucrose. Side A is half-filled with a solution of 2 M sucrose and 1 M glucose. Side B is half-filled with 1 M sucrose and 2 M glucose. Initially, the liquid levels on both sides are equal. When the system illustrated above reaches equilibrium, the sugar concentrations on both sides of the U-tube will be ________.

choices.C: 1 M sucrose, 1 M glucose
choices.D: 1.5 M sucrose, 1.5 M glucose

questions.answer_text: 1.5 M sucrose, 1.5 M glucose

questions.stem: The solutions in the arms of a U-tube are separated at the bottom of the tube by a selectively permeable membrane. The membrane is permeable to sodium chloride but not to glucose. Side A is filled with a solution of 0.4 M glucose and 0.5 M sodium chloride (NaCl), and side B is filled with a solution containing 0.8 M glucose and 0.4 M sodium chloride. Initially, the volume in both arms is the same. At the beginning of the U-tube experiment illustrated above, which of the following statements is true?

choices.A: Side A is hypertonic to side B.
choices.B: Side A is hypotonic to side B.
choices.C: Side A is hypertonic to side B with respect to glucose.
choices.D: Side A is hypotonic to side B with respect to NaCl.

questions.answer_text: Side A is hypotonic to side B.

questions.stem: The solutions in the arms of a U-tube are separated at the bottom of the tube by a selectively permeable membrane. The membrane is permeable to sodium chloride but not to glucose. Side A is filled with a solution of 0.4 M glucose and 0.5 M sodium chloride (NaCl), and side B is filled with a solution containing 0.8 M glucose and 0.4 M sodium chloride. Initially, the volume in both arms is the same. In the U-tube experiment illustrated above, which of the following statements correctly describes side B at equilibrium?

choices.A: The concentration of NaCl and glucose will decrease, and the water level will increase.
choices.B: The concentration of NaCl will increase, the concentration of glucose will decrease, and the water level will increase.
choices.C: The concentration of NaCl will increase, the concentration of glucose will decrease, and the water level will decrease.
choices.D: The concentration of NaCl and glucose will increase, and the water level will decrease.

questions.answer_text: The concentration of NaCl will increase, the concentration of glucose will decrease, and the water level will increase.

questions.stem: Five dialysis bags, constructed of a type of membrane that is permeable to water and impermeable to sucrose, were filled with various concentrations of sucrose and then placed in separate beakers containing an initial concentration of 0.6 M sucrose solution. choices.C: C
choices.D: D

questions.answer_text: C

questions.stem: Five dialysis bags, constructed of a type of membrane that is permeable to water and impermeable to sucrose, were filled with various concentrations of sucrose and then placed in separate beakers containing an initial concentration of 0.6 M sucrose solution. At 10-minute intervals, the bags were massed (weighed), and the percent change in mass of each bag was graphed. questions.stem: Five dialysis bags, constructed of a type of membrane that is permeable to water and impermeable to sucrose, were filled with various concentrations of sucrose and then placed in separate beakers containing an initial concentration of 0.6 M sucrose solution. Which line or lines in the graph represent(s) bags that contain a solution that is hypertonic at 50 minutes?

choices.C: D
choices.D: D and E
