questions.stem: Celery stalks that are immersed in fresh water for several hours become stiff. Similar stalks left in a 0.15 M salt solution become limp. From this we can deduce that the fresh water ________.

choices.A: and the salt solution are both hypertonic to the cells of the celery stalks
choices.B: is hypotonic and the salt solution is hypertonic to the cells of the celery stalks
choices.C: is hypertonic and the salt solution is hypotonic to the cells of the celery stalks
choices.D: is isotonic and the salt solution is hypertonic to the cells of the celery stalks

questions.answer_text: is hypotonic and the salt solution is hypertonic to the cells of the celery stalks

questions.stem: What will happen to a red blood cell (RBC), which has an internal ion content of about 0.9%, if it is placed into a beaker of pure water?

choices.A: The cell would shrink because the water in the beaker is hypotonic relative to the cytoplasm of the RBC.
choices.B: The cell would shrink because the water in the beaker is hypertonic relative to the cytoplasm of the RBC.
choices.C: The cell would swell because the water in the beaker is hypotonic relative to the cytoplasm of the RBC.
choices.D: The cell will remain the same size because the solution outside the cell is isotonic.

questions.answer_text: The cell would swell because the water in the beaker is hypotonic relative to the cytoplasm of the RBC.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes the normal tonicity conditions for typical plant and animal cells? The animal cell is in ________.

choices.A: a hypotonic solution, and the plant cell is in an isotonic solution
choices.B: an isotonic solution, and the plant cell is in a hypertonic solution
choices.C: a hypertonic solution, and the plant cell is in an isotonic solution
choices.D: an isotonic solution, and the plant cell is in a hypotonic solution

questions.answer_text: an isotonic solution, and the plant cell is in a hypotonic solution

questions.stem: In which of the following environments would there be the greatest need for osmoregulation?

choices.A: an animal connective tissue cell bathed in isotonic body fluid
choices.B: a salmon moving from a river into an ocean
choices.C: a red blood cell surrounded by plasma
choices.D: a plant being grown hydroponically in a watery mixture of designated nutrients

questions.answer_text: a salmon moving from a river into an ocean

questions.stem: When a plant cell, such as one from a tulip leaf, is submerged in a hypertonic solution, what is likely to occur?

choices.B: Plasmolysis will shrink the interior of the cell.
choices.C: The cell will become flaccid.
choices.D: The cell will become turgid.

questions.answer_text: Plasmolysis will shrink the interior of the cell.

questions.stem: A sodium-potassium pump ________.

choices.A: moves three potassium ions out of a cell and two sodium ions into a cell while producing ATP for each cycle
choices.B: moves three sodium ions out of a cell and two potassium ions into a cell using energy from ATP hydrolysis
choices.C: moves three potassium ions out of a cell and two sodium ions into a cell using energy from ATP hydrolysis
choices.D: move three sodium ions out of a cell and two potassium ions into a cell and generates an ATP in each cycle

questions.answer_text: moves three sodium ions out of a cell and two potassium ions into a cell using energy from ATP hydrolysis

questions.stem: The sodium-potassium pump is called an electrogenic pump because it ________.

choices.A: pumps equal quantities of Na+ and K+ across the membrane in opposite directions
choices.B: is used to drive the transport of glucose against a concentration gradient
choices.C: decreases the voltage difference across the membrane
choices.D: generates voltage across the membrane

questions.answer_text: is used to drive the transport of glucose against a concentration gradient

questions.stem: Which of the following membrane activities requires energy from ATP hydrolysis?

choices.A: facilitated diffusion of chloride ions across the membrane through a chloride channel
choices.B: movement of Na+ ions from a lower concentration in a mammalian cell to a higher concentration in the extracellular fluid
choices.C: movement of glucose molecules into a bacterial cell from a medium containing a higher concentration of glucose than inside the cell
choices.D: movement of carbon dioxide out of a paramecium

questions.answer_text: movement of Na+ ions from a lower concentration in a mammalian cell to a higher concentration in the extracellular fluid

questions.stem: The voltage across a membrane is called the ________.

choices.C: osmotic potential
choices.D: electrochemical gradient

questions.answer_text: membrane potential

questions.stem: Diffusion of ions across membranes through specific ion channels is driven by ________.

choices.C: electrical gradients only
choices.D: ion electrochemical gradients

questions.answer_text: ion electrochemical gradients

questions.stem: Which of the following structures would decrease the electrochemical gradient across a membrane?

choices.C: a potassium channel
choices.D: both a proton pump and a sodium channel

questions.answer_text: a potassium channel

questions.stem: The phosphate transport system in bacteria imports phosphate into the cell even when the concentration of phosphate outside the cell is much lower than the cytoplasmic phosphate concentration. Phosphate import depends on a pH gradient across the membrane—more acidic outside the cell than inside the cell. In this bacterial cell, phosphate transport is an example of ________.

choices.C: active transport
choices.D: cotransport

questions.answer_text: cotransport

questions.stem: In some cells, there are many ion electrochemical gradients across the plasma membrane even though there are usually only one or two proton pumps present in the membrane. The gradients of the other ions are most likely accounted for by ________.

choices.C: pores in the plasma membrane
choices.D: passive diffusion across the plasma membrane

questions.answer_text: cotransport proteins

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is most likely true of a protein that cotransports glucose and sodium ions into the intestinal cells of an animal?

choices.A: Sodium and glucose compete for the same binding site in the cotransporter.
choices.B: Glucose entering the cell down its concentration gradient provides energy for uptake of sodium ions against the electrochemical gradient.
choices.C: Sodium ions can move down their electrochemical gradient through the cotransporter whether or not glucose is present outside the cell.
choices.D: A substance that blocks sodium ions from binding to the cotransport protein will also block the transport of glucose.

questions.answer_text: A substance that blocks sodium ions from binding to the cotransport protein will also block the transport of glucose.

questions.stem: Proton pumps are used in various ways by members of every domain of organisms: Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya. What does this fact most probably mean?

choices.A: Proton gradients across a membrane were used by cells that were the common ancestor of all three domains of life.
choices.B: The high concentration of protons in the ancient atmosphere must have necessitated a pump mechanism.
choices.C: Cells of each domain evolved proton pumps independently when oceans became more acidic.
choices.D: Proton pumps are necessary to all cell membranes.

questions.answer_text: Proton gradients across a membrane were used by cells that were the common ancestor of all three domains of life.

questions.stem: Several epidemic microbial diseases of earlier centuries incurred high death rates because they resulted in severe dehydration due to vomiting and diarrhea. Today they are usually not fatal because we have developed which of the following types of treatments?

choices.A: antiviral medications that are efficient and work well with most viruses
choices.C: medications to slow blood loss
choices.D: hydrating drinks with high concentrations of salt and glucose

questions.answer_text: hydrating drinks with high concentrations of salt and glucose

questions.stem: The force driving simple diffusion is ________, while the energy source for active transport is ________.

choices.C: transmembrane pumps; an electrochemical gradient
choices.D: phosphorylated carrier proteins; ATP

questions.answer_text: a concentration gradient; ATP hydrolysis

questions.stem: An organism with a cell wall would most likely be unable to take in materials through ________.

choices.C: phagocytosis
choices.D: facilitated diffusion

questions.answer_text: phagocytosis

questions.stem: White blood cells engulf bacteria using ________.

choices.C: osmosis
choices.D: receptor-mediated exocytosis

questions.answer_text: phagocytosis

questions.stem: Familial hypercholesterolemia is characterized by ________.

choices.A: defective LDL receptors on the cell membranes
choices.B: poor attachment of the cholesterol to the extracellular matrix of cells
choices.C: a poorly formed lipid bilayer that cannot incorporate cholesterol into cell membranes
choices.D: inhibition of the cholesterol active transport system in red blood cells

questions.answer_text: defective LDL receptors on the cell membranes

questions.stem: The difference between pinocytosis and receptor-mediated endocytosis is that ________.

choices.A: pinocytosis brings only water molecules into the cell, but receptor-mediated endocytosis brings in other molecules as well
choices.B: pinocytosis increases the surface area of the plasma membrane, whereas receptor-mediated endocytosis decreases the plasma membrane surface area
choices.C: pinocytosis is nonselective in the molecules it brings into the cell, whereas receptor-mediated endocytosis offers more selectivity
choices.D: pinocytosis can concentrate substances from the extracellular fluid, but receptor-mediated endocytosis cannot

questions.answer_text: pinocytosis is nonselective in the molecules it brings into the cell, whereas receptor-mediated endocytosis offers more selectivity

questions.stem: In receptor-mediated endocytosis, receptor molecules initially project to the outside of the cell. Where do they end up after endocytosis?

choices.B: on the inside surface of the cell membrane
choices.C: on the inside surface of the vesicle
choices.D: on the outer surface of the nucleus

questions.answer_text: on the inside surface of the vesicle

questions.stem: A bacterium engulfed by a white blood cell through phagocytosis will be digested by enzymes contained in ________.

choices.C: vacuoles
choices.D: secretory vesicles

questions.answer_text: lysosomes

questions.stem: A patient was involved a serious accident and lost a large quantity of blood. In an attempt to replenish body fluids, distilled water—equal to the volume of blood lost—is added to the blood directly via one of his veins. What will be the most probable result of this transfusion?

choices.A: The patient's red blood cells will shrivel up because the blood has become hypotonic compared to the cells.
choices.B: The patient's red blood cells will swell and possibly burst because the blood has become hypotonic compared to the cells.
choices.C: The patient's red blood cells will shrivel up because the blood has become hypertonic compared to the cells.
choices.D: The patient's red blood cells will burst because the blood has become hypertonic compared to the cells.

questions.answer_text: The patient's red blood cells will swell and possibly burst because the blood has become hypotonic compared to the cells.

questions.stem: In an HIV-infected cell producing HIV virus particles, the viral glycoprotein is expressed on the plasma membrane. How do the viral glycoproteins get to the plasma membrane? They are synthesized ________.

choices.A: on ribosomes on the plasma membrane
choices.B: by ribosomes in the rough ER and arrive at the plasma membrane in the membrane of secretory vesicles
choices.C: on free cytoplasmic ribosomes and then inserted into the plasma membrane
choices.D: by ribosomes in the rough ER, secreted from the cell, and inserted into the plasma membrane from the outside

questions.answer_text: by ribosomes in the rough ER and arrive at the plasma membrane in the membrane of secretory vesicles

questions.stem: What would be observed by live-cell fluorescence microscopy immediately after HIV entry if HIV is endocytosed first, and then later fuses with the endocytotic vesicle membrane?

choices.A: A spot of red fluorescence will be visible on the infected cell's plasma membrane, marking the site of membrane fusion and HIV entry.
choices.B: The red fluorescent dye-labeled lipids will appear in the infected cell's interior.
choices.C: A spot of red fluorescence will diffuse in the infected cell's cytoplasm.
choices.D: A spot of red fluorescence will remain outside the cell after delivering the viral capsid.

questions.answer_text: The red fluorescent dye-labeled lipids will appear in the infected cell's interior.

questions.stem: Three lab groups carried out an experiment to identify the concentration of sucrose in six solutions. choices.A: Unknown solution E contains the highest concentration of sucrose, and the change in mass is due to the active transport of sucrose out of the cell.

In what way do the membranes of a eukaryotic cell vary?

choices.A: Phospholipids are found only in certain membranes.
choices.B: Certain proteins are unique to each membrane.

choices.D: Only certain membranes are constructed from amphipathic molecules.

questions.stem: According to the fluid mosaic model of membrane structure, proteins of the membrane are mostly

choices.A: spread in a continuous layer over the inner and outer surfaces of the membrane.
choices.B: confined to the hydrophobic interior of the membrane.
choices.C: embedded in a lipid bilayer.
choices.D: randomly oriented in the membrane, with no fixed inside-outside polarity.

questions.answer_text: embedded in a lipid bilayer.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors would tend to increase membrane fluidity?

choices.A: a greater proportion of unsaturated phospholipids
choices.B: a greater proportion of saturated phospholipids
choices.C: a lower temperature
choices.D: a relatively high protein content in the membrane

questions.answer_text: a greater proportion of unsaturated phospholipids

questions.stem: Which of the following processes includes all the others?

choices.B: diffusion of a solute across a membrane
choices.C: passive transport
choices.D: transport of an ion down its electrochemical gradient

questions.answer_text: passive transport

questions.stem: Based on Figure 7.18, which of these experimental treatments would increase the rate of sucrose transport into a plant cell?

choices.C: decreasing cytoplasmic pH
choices.D: adding a substance that makes the membrane more permeable to hydrogen ions

questions.answer_text: decreasing extracellular pH

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true of metabolism in its entirety in all organisms?

choices.A: Metabolism depends on a constant supply of energy from food.
choices.B: Metabolism uses all of an organism's resources.
choices.C: Metabolism consists of all the energy transformation reactions in an organism.
choices.D: Metabolism manages the increase of entropy in an organism.

questions.answer_text: Metabolism consists of all the energy transformation reactions in an organism.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of potential rather than kinetic energy?

choices.B: light flashes emitted by a firefly
choices.C: a molecule of glucose
choices.D: a crawling beetle foraging for food

questions.answer_text: a molecule of glucose

questions.stem: Most cells cannot harness heat to perform work because ________.

choices.A: heat is not a form of energy
choices.B: temperature is usually uniform throughout a cell
choices.C: heat can never be used to do work
choices.D: heat must remain constant during work

questions.answer_text: temperature is usually uniform throughout a cell

questions.stem: A decrease in entropy is associated with which type of reaction?

choices.C: depolymerization
choices.D: hydrolysis

questions.answer_text: dehydration

questions.stem: Which of the following terms most precisely describes the cellular process of breaking down large molecules into smaller ones?

choices.C: anabolism (anabolic pathways)
choices.D: dehydration

questions.answer_text: catabolism (catabolic pathways)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about anabolic pathways is true?

choices.A: They are usually spontaneous chemical reactions.
choices.B: They consume energy to build up polymers from monomers.
choices.C: They release energy by degrading polymers to monomers.
choices.D: They decrease the entropy of the organism and its environment.

questions.answer_text: They consume energy to build up polymers from monomers.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes the first law of thermodynamics?

choices.A: Energy cannot be created or destroyed.
choices.B: The entropy of the universe is decreasing.
choices.C: The entropy of the universe is constant.
choices.D: Energy cannot be transferred or transformed.

questions.answer_text: Energy cannot be created or destroyed.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is an important consequence of the first law of thermodynamics for a living organism?

choices.A: The energy content of an organism is constant.
choices.B: An organism ultimately must obtain all of the necessary energy for life from its environment.
choices.C: The entropy of an organism decreases with time as the organism grows in complexity.
choices.D: Organisms grow by converting energy into organic matter.

questions.answer_text: An organism ultimately must obtain all of the necessary energy for life from its environment.

questions.stem: Living organisms increase in complexity as they grow, resulting in a decrease in the entropy of an organism. How does this relate to the second law of thermodynamics?

choices.A: Living organisms do not obey the second law of thermodynamics, which states that the entropy of an organism increases with each energy transformation.
choices.B: The decrease in entropy is associated with growth of an organism. As a consequence of growth, organisms cause a greater increase in entropy in their environment than the decrease in entropy associated with their increased complexity.
choices.C: As a consequence of growth, the decrease in entropy of the organism is associated with a corresponding decrease in the entropy of the universe.
choices.D: Living organisms are able to transform chemical energy into entropy.

questions.answer_text: The decrease in entropy is associated with growth of an organism. As a consequence of growth, organisms cause a greater increase in entropy in their environment than the decrease in entropy associated with their increased complexity.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is a logical consequence of the second law of thermodynamics?

choices.A: If the entropy of a system increases, there must be a corresponding decrease in the entropy of the universe.
choices.B: If the entropy of a system decreases, there must be a corresponding decrease in the entropy of the universe.
choices.C: If there is an increase in the energy of a system, there must be a corresponding decrease in the energy of the rest of the universe.
choices.D: Each chemical reaction in an organism must increase the total entropy of the universe.

questions.answer_text: Each chemical reaction in an organism must increase the total entropy of the universe.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is consistent with the second law of thermodynamics?

choices.A: A gain of free energy in a system is always associated with conversion of energy from one form to another.
choices.B: A constant input of energy is required to maintain the high level of cellular organization.
choices.C: Without an input of energy, the entropy of an organism would tend to decrease over time.
choices.D: Every energy transformation performed by an organism decreases the entropy of the universe.

questions.answer_text: A constant input of energy is required to maintain the high level of cellular organization.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of reactions would decrease the entropy within a cell?

choices.C: digestion
choices.D: catabolic reactions

questions.answer_text: anabolic reactions

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the evolution of life on Earth, from simple prokaryote-like cells to multicellular eukaryotic organisms, is true?

choices.A: By resulting in such diversity and complexity of life, it is an exception to the second law of thermodynamics.
choices.B: It has occurred in accordance with the laws of thermodynamics and resulted in a substantial increase in the entropy of the planet.
choices.C: It has occurred in accordance with the laws of thermodynamics and resulted in a substantial increase in the total energy in the universe.
choices.D: It has occurred in accordance with the laws of thermodynamics and resulted in a substantial decrease in the entropy of the planet.

questions.answer_text: It has occurred in accordance with the laws of thermodynamics and resulted in a substantial decrease in the entropy of the planet.

questions.stem: The mathematical expression for the change in free energy of a system is ΔG = ΔH - TΔS. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.A: ΔS is the change in enthalpy, a measure of randomness.
choices.B: ΔH is the change in entropy, the energy available to do work.
choices.C: ΔG is the change in free energy.
choices.D: T is the temperature in degrees Celsius.

questions.answer_text: ΔG is the change in free energy.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true for a system at chemical equilibrium?

choices.A: The system consumes energy at a steady rate.
choices.B: The system releases energy at a steady rate.
choices.C: The kinetic energy of the system is zero.
choices.D: The system can do no work.

questions.answer_text: The system can do no work.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true for all exergonic reactions?

choices.A: The products have more total energy than the reactants.
choices.B: The reaction proceeds with a net release of free energy.
choices.C: The reaction goes only in a forward direction: all reactants will be converted to products, but no products will be converted to reactants.
choices.D: A net input of energy from the surroundings is required for the reactions to proceed.

questions.answer_text: The reaction proceeds with a net release of free energy.

questions.stem: A chemical reaction that has a positive ΔG is best described as ________.

choices.C: spontaneous
choices.D: exergonic

questions.answer_text: endergonic

questions.stem: Chemical equilibrium is relatively rare in living cells because metabolic pathways are interconnected. Which of the following statements describes an example of a reaction that may be at chemical equilibrium in a cell?

choices.A: an exergonic reaction in which the free energy at equilibrium is higher than the energy content of the reaction at any point away from equilibrium
choices.B: an exergonic reaction in which the entropy change in the cell is precisely balanced by an opposite entropy change in the cell's surroundings
choices.C: a chemical reaction in which neither the reactants nor the products are being produced or consumed in any metabolic pathway at that time in the cell
choices.D: an endergonic reaction in an active metabolic pathway where the energy for that reaction is supplied only by heat from the environment

questions.answer_text: a chemical reaction in which neither the reactants nor the products are being produced or consumed in any metabolic pathway at that time in the cell

questions.stem: The relationship between catabolism and anabolism is most similar to the relationship between which of the following pairs of terms?

choices.C: free energy; entropy
choices.D: work; free energy

questions.answer_text: exergonic; endergonic

questions.stem: Why do hydrolysis reactions occur more readily in solution than dehydration reactions?

choices.A: Hydrolysis reactions increase G, or Gibbs free energy of the system.
choices.B: Hydrolysis reactions are endergonic and increase entropy of the system.
choices.C: Hydrolysis reactions are exergonic and decrease entropy of the system.
choices.D: Hydrolysis reactions are exergonic and increase entropy of the system.

questions.answer_text: Hydrolysis reactions are exergonic and increase entropy of the system.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes a central role that ATP plays in cellular metabolism?

choices.A: Hydrolysis of ATP provides an input of free energy for exergonic reactions.
choices.B: ATP provides energy coupling between exergonic and endergonic reactions.
choices.C: Hydrolysis of the terminal phosphate group stores free energy that is used for cellular work.
choices.D: Its terminal phosphate bond is stronger than most covalent bonds in other biological macromolecules.

questions.answer_text: ATP provides energy coupling between exergonic and endergonic reactions.

questions.stem: Why is the ΔG of ATP hydrolysis in the cell about twice as great as the ΔG of ATP hydrolysis in a test tube under standard conditions?

choices.A: A cell is an open system, whereas a test tube is a closed system.
choices.B: ATP hydrolysis in a test tube releases more heat than ATP hydrolysis associated with cellular metabolism.
choices.C: Reactant and product concentrations in the test tube are different from those in the cell.
choices.D: ATP hydrolysis in cells is catalyzed by enzymes, whereas the reaction in a test tube occurs spontaneously.

questions.answer_text: Reactant and product concentrations in the test tube are different from those in the cell.

questions.stem: Which of the following molecules is most similar in structure to ATP?

choices.C: an RNA nucleotide
choices.D: an amino acid with three phosphate groups attached

questions.answer_text: an RNA nucleotide

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes a common characteristic of catabolic pathways?

choices.A: They combine small molecules into larger, more energy-rich molecules.
choices.B: They require energy from ATP hydrolysis to break down polymers into monomers.
choices.C: They are endergonic and release energy that can be used for cellular work.
choices.D: They are exergonic and provide energy that can be used to produce ATP from ADP and i.

questions.answer_text: They are exergonic and provide energy that can be used to produce ATP from ADP and i.

questions.stem: When chemical, transport, or mechanical work is done by an organism, what happens to the heat generated?

choices.A: It is used to power yet more cellular work.
choices.B: It is captured to store energy as more ATP.
choices.C: It is used to generate ADP from nucleotide precursors.
choices.D: It is lost to the environment.

questions.answer_text: It is lost to the environment.

questions.stem: When ATP releases some energy, it also releases inorganic phosphate. What happens to the inorganic phosphate in the cell?

choices.B: It is used only to regenerate more ATP.
choices.C: It may be used to form a phosphorylated intermediate.
choices.D: It enters the nucleus to be incorporated in a nucleotide.

questions.answer_text: It may be used to form a phosphorylated intermediate.

questions.stem: A number of systems for pumping ions across membranes are powered by ATP. Such ATP- powered pumps are often called ATPases, although they do not often hydrolyze ATP unless they are simultaneously transporting ions. Because small increases in calcium ions in the cytosol can trigger a number of different intracellular reactions, cells keep the cytosolic calcium concentration quite low under normal conditions, using ATP-powered calcium pumps. For example, muscle cells transport calcium from the cytosol into the membranous system called the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR). If a resting muscle cell's cytosol has a free calcium ion concentration of 10-7 while the concentration in the SR is 10-2, then how is the ATPase acting?

choices.A: ATPase activity must be powering an inflow of calcium from the outside of the cell into the SR.
choices.B: ATPase activity must be transferring i to the SR to enable this to occur.
choices.C: ATPase activity must be pumping calcium from the cytosol to the SR against the concentration gradient.
choices.D: ATPase activity must be opening a channel for the calcium ions to diffuse back into the SR along the concentration gradient.

questions.answer_text: ATPase activity must be pumping calcium from the cytosol to the SR against the concentration gradient.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most correct interpretation of the figure?

choices.A: Energy from catabolism can be used directly for performing cellular work.
choices.B: ADP + i are a set of molecules that store energy for catabolism.
choices.C: ATP is a molecule that acts as an intermediary to store energy for cellular work.
choices.D: i acts as a shuttle molecule to move energy from ATP to ADP.

questions.answer_text: ATP is a molecule that acts as an intermediary to store energy for cellular work.

questions.stem: How do cells use the ATP cycle illustrated in the figure?

choices.A: Cells use the cycle to recycle ADP and phosphate.
choices.B: Cells use the cycle to recycle energy released by ATP hydrolysis.
choices.C: Cells use the cycle to recycle ADP, phosphate, and the energy released by ATP hydrolysis.
choices.D: Cells use the cycle primarily to generate heat.

questions.answer_text: Cells use the cycle to recycle ADP and phosphate.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about enzyme function is true?

choices.A: Enzyme function is generally increased if the three-dimensional structure or conformation of an enzyme is altered.
choices.B: Enzyme function is independent of physical and chemical environmental factors such as pH and temperature.
choices.C: Enzymes increase the rate of chemical reactions by lowering activation energy barriers.
choices.D: Enzymes increase the rate of chemical reactions by providing activation energy to the substrate.

questions.answer_text: Enzymes increase the rate of chemical reactions by lowering activation energy barriers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true when comparing an uncatalyzed reaction to the same reaction with a catalyst?

choices.A: The catalyzed reaction will be slower.
choices.B: The catalyzed reaction will have the same ∆G.
choices.C: The catalyzed reaction will have higher activation energy.
choices.D: The catalyzed reaction will consume all of the catalyst.

questions.answer_text: The catalyzed reaction will have the same ∆G.

questions.stem: Which of the following aspects of enzyme structure is best described by a clasping handshake analogy?

choices.A: the specific manner in which an enzyme folds to form secondary and tertiary structures
choices.B: the specific manner in which an enzyme interacts with water
choices.C: the specific manner in which an enzyme binds substrate
choices.D: the specific manner in which an enzyme is denatured by low pH

questions.answer_text: the specific manner in which an enzyme binds substrate

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics is most likely to be associated with an enzyme that catalyzes two different chemical reactions?

choices.A: The enzyme contains α-helices and β-pleated sheets.
choices.B: The enzyme is subject to competitive inhibition and allosteric regulation.
choices.C: The enzyme is composed of at least two subunits.
choices.D: Either the enzyme has two distinct active sites or the substrates involved in the two reactions have very similar structures.

questions.answer_text: Either the enzyme has two distinct active sites or the substrates involved in the two reactions have very similar structures.

questions.stem: What is the name of the thermodynamic barrier that must be overcome before products are formed in a spontaneous reaction?

choices.C: the equilibrium point
choices.D: free energy

questions.answer_text: activation energy

questions.stem: During a laboratory experiment, you discover that an enzyme-catalyzed reaction has a ∆G of -20 kcal/mol. If you double the amount of enzyme in the reaction, what will be the ∆G for the new reaction?

choices.C: -10 kcal/mol
choices.D: +20 kcal/mol

questions.answer_text: -20 kcal/mol

questions.stem: Which of the following is a primary function of the active site of an enzyme?

choices.A: It binds allosteric regulators of the enzyme.
choices.B: It binds noncompetitive inhibitors of the enzyme.
choices.C: It catalyzes the reaction associated with the enzyme.
choices.D: It is activated by the presence of the end product of the metabolic pathway in which the enzyme is involved.

questions.answer_text: It catalyzes the reaction associated with the enzyme.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes a key component of the induced fit hypothesis of enzyme catalysis?

choices.A: Substrate binds to an allosteric site rather than to the active site of an enzyme.
choices.B: Binding of an activator molecule changes the shape of the active site of an enzyme.
choices.C: The conformation of the active site is determined by the tertiary or quaternary structure of the enzyme.
choices.D: Binding of substrate to the active site changes the shape of the active site of an enzyme.

questions.answer_text: Binding of substrate to the active site changes the shape of the active site of an enzyme.

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions may be overcome by increasing the substrate concentration in an enzymatic reaction with a fixed amount of enzyme?

choices.C: noncompetitive inhibition
choices.D: competitive inhibition

questions.answer_text: competitive inhibition

questions.stem: Zinc, an essential trace element for most organisms, is present in the active site of the enzyme carboxypeptidase. The zinc most likely functions as ________.

choices.A: a noncompetitive inhibitor of the enzyme
choices.B: an allosteric activator of the enzyme
choices.C: a cofactor necessary for enzyme activity
choices.D: a coenzyme derived from a vitamin

questions.answer_text: a cofactor necessary for enzyme activity

questions.stem: How does a noncompetitive inhibitor decrease the rate of an enzyme-catalyzed reaction?

choices.A: by binding to the active site of the enzyme, thus preventing binding of the normal substrate
choices.B: by binding to an allosteric site, thus changing the shape of the active site of the enzyme
choices.C: by decreasing the free-energy change of the reaction catalyzed by the enzyme
choices.D: by binding to the substrate, thus changing its shape so that it no longer binds to the active site of the enzyme

questions.answer_text: by binding to an allosteric site, thus changing the shape of the active site of the enzyme

questions.stem: Which of the following graphs most likely describes the effect of pH on the function of the enzyme catalase in human cells? Note: The x-axis is pH and the y-axis is enzyme activity.
How might a change of one amino acid at a site, distant from the active site of an enzyme, alter the substrate specificity of an enzyme?

choices.A: by changing the stability of the enzyme
choices.B: by changing the three-dimensional conformation of the enzyme
choices.C: by changing the optimum pH for the enzyme
choices.D: by changing the binding site for a noncompetitive inhibitor

questions.answer_text: by changing the three-dimensional conformation of the enzyme

questions.stem: Rate of an enzyme-catalyzed reaction as a function of varying reactant concentration, with the concentration of enzyme constant. For the enzyme-catalyzed reaction shown in the figure, if the initial reactant concentration is 1.0 micromolar, which of these treatments will cause the greatest increase in the rate of the reaction?

choices.C: doubling the enzyme concentration
choices.D: increasing the concentration of reactants to 10.0 micromolar, while reducing the concentration of enzyme by 1/2

questions.answer_text: doubling the enzyme concentration

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question below. Rate of an enzyme-catalyzed reaction as a function of varying reactant concentration, with the concentration of enzyme constant In the figure, why does the reaction rate plateau at higher reactant concentrations?

choices.A: Feedback inhibition by product occurs at high reactant concentrations.
choices.B: Most enzyme molecules are occupied by substrate at high reactant concentrations.
choices.C: The reaction nears equilibrium at high reactant concentrations.
choices.D: The rate of the reverse reaction increases at high reactant concentrations.

questions.answer_text: Most enzyme molecules are occupied by substrate at high reactant concentrations.

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question below. Activity of various enzymes at various temperatures (a) and at various pH (b) Which curves on the graphs may represent the temperature and pH profiles of an enzyme taken from a bacterium that lives in a mildly alkaline hot springs at temperatures of 70°C or higher?

choices.C: curves 3 and 4
choices.D: curves 3 and 5

questions.answer_text: curves 3 and 5

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question below. Activity of various enzymes at various temperatures (a) and at various pH (b) Which temperature and pH profile curves on the graphs are most likely associated with an enzyme isolated from a human stomach where conditions are strongly acid?

choices.C: curves 2 and 4
choices.D: curves 3 and 4

questions.answer_text: curves 1 and 4

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question below. The figure illustrates the energy states associated with the reaction A + B ↔ C + D. Which of the following terms best describes the forward reaction in the figure?

choices.C: endergonic, ∆G < 0
choices.D: exergonic, ∆G > 0

questions.answer_text: exergonic, ∆G < 0

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question below. The figure illustrates the energy states associated with the reaction A + B ↔ C + D. Which of the following in the figure would be the same in either an enzyme-catalyzed or a noncatalyzed reaction?

choices.C: c
choices.D: d

questions.answer_text: d

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question below. The figure illustrates the energy states associated with the reaction A + B ↔ C + D. Which of the following represents the activation energy required for the enzyme-catalyzed reaction in the figure?

choices.C: c
choices.D: d

questions.answer_text: b

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question below. The figure illustrates the energy states associated with the reaction A + B ↔ C + D. Which of the following represents the activation energy required for the non-enzyme-catalyzed reaction in the figure?

choices.C: c
choices.D: d

questions.answer_text: c

questions.stem: In a metabolic pathway, succinate dehydrogenase catalyzes the conversion of succinate to fumarate. The reaction is inhibited by malonic acid, a substance that resembles succinate but cannot be acted upon by succinate dehydrogenase. Increasing the amount of succinate molecules to those of malonic acid reduces the inhibitory effect of malonic acid. Which of the following statements correctly describes the role played by molecules described in the reaction?

choices.A: Succinate dehydrogenase is the enzyme, and fumarate is the substrate in the reaction.
choices.B: Succinate dehydrogenase is the enzyme, and malonic acid is the substrate in the reaction.
choices.C: Succinate is the substrate, and fumarate is the product in the reaction.
choices.D: Fumarate is the product, and malonic acid is a noncompetitive inhibitor in the reaction.

questions.answer_text: Succinate is the substrate, and fumarate is the product in the reaction.

questions.stem: In a metabolic pathway, succinate dehydrogenase catalyzes the conversion of succinate to fumarate. The reaction is inhibited by malonic acid, a substance that resembles succinate but cannot be acted upon by succinate dehydrogenase. Increasing the amount of succinate molecules to those of malonic acid reduces the inhibitory effect of malonic acid. What role does malonic acid play with respect to succinate dehydrogenase?

choices.A: Malonic acid is a competitive inhibitor.
choices.B: Malonic acid blocks the binding of fumarate.
choices.C: Malonic acid is a noncompetitive inhibitor.
choices.D: Malonic acid is an allosteric regulator.

questions.answer_text: Malonic acid is a competitive inhibitor.

questions.stem: HIV is the virus that causes AIDS. In the mid-1990s, researchers discovered an enzyme in HIV called protease. Once the enzyme's structure was known, researchers began looking for drugs that would fit into the active site and block it. If this strategy for stopping HIV infections were successful, it would be an example of what phenomenon?

choices.C: allosteric regulation
choices.D: competitive inhibition

questions.answer_text: competitive inhibition

questions.stem: A series of enzymes catalyze the reactions in the metabolic pathway X → Y → Z → A. Product A binds to the enzyme that converts X to Y at a position remote from its active site. This binding decreases the activity of the enzyme. What is substance X?

choices.C: an intermediate
choices.D: the product

questions.answer_text: a substrate

questions.stem: A series of enzymes catalyze the reactions in the metabolic pathway X → Y → Z → A. Product A binds to the enzyme that converts X to Y at a position remote from its active site. This binding decreases the activity of the enzyme. With respect to the enzyme that converts X to Y, substance A functions as ________.

choices.C: an intermediate
choices.D: a competitive inhibitor

questions.answer_text: an allosteric inhibitor

questions.stem: ________ is a regulatory mechanism in which the end product of a metabolic pathway inhibits an enzyme that catalyzes an early step in the pathway.

choices.C: Feedback inhibition
choices.D: Metabolic inhibition

questions.answer_text: Feedback inhibition

questions.stem: Characterization of the complete three-dimensional structure of a newly purified protein suggests that it catalyzes the breakdown of a large substrate. The protein consists of a single polypeptide chain. It has a large pocket that appears to be the binding site for the substrate and a smaller indentation that appears to be the binding site for a regulatory molecule. What do these structural observations suggest about the mechanism by which the activity of this protein is likely regulated?

choices.A: It is probably an enzyme that is regulated by noncompetitive inhibition.
choices.B: It is probably a multi-subunit enzyme that is regulated by allosteric regulation.
choices.C: It is probably an enzyme that is regulated by competitive inhibition.
choices.D: It is probably an enzyme that is regulated by cooperativity.

questions.answer_text: It is probably an enzyme that is regulated by noncompetitive inhibition.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes an example of cooperativity associated with enzyme regulation?

choices.A: binding of the end product of a metabolic pathway to the first enzyme in the pathway to inhibit the enzyme
choices.B: one enzyme in a metabolic pathway passing its product to act as a substrate for the next enzyme in the pathway
choices.C: binding a substrate to one subunit of a tetramer stimulates faster binding of substrate to each of the other three subunits
choices.D: binding of an ATP molecule along with another substrate molecule in the active site of the enzyme

questions.answer_text: binding a substrate to one subunit of a tetramer stimulates faster binding of substrate to each of the other three subunits

questions.stem: In addition to activating or inhibiting enzymes through allosteric regulation, what other means does a cell use to control enzymatic activity?

choices.A: localization of enzymes into specific organelles or membranes
choices.B: secretion of enzymes out of the cell
choices.C: assembly of enzymes into large aggregates
choices.D: altering internal pH

questions.answer_text: localization of enzymes into specific organelles or membranes

questions.stem: Protein kinases are enzymes that transfer the terminal phosphate from ATP to an amino acid residue on the target protein. Many are located on the plasma membrane as integral membrane proteins or peripheral membrane proteins. What purpose may be served by their plasma membrane localization?

choices.A: ATP is more abundant near the plasma membrane.
choices.B: They can more readily encounter and phosphorylate other membrane proteins.
choices.C: Membrane localization lowers the activation energy of the phosphorylation reaction.
choices.D: They flip back and forth across the membrane to access target proteins on either side.

questions.answer_text: They can more readily encounter and phosphorylate other membrane proteins.

questions.stem: Biological systems use free energy based on empirical data that all organisms require a constant energy input. The first law of thermodynamics states that energy can be neither created nor destroyed. For living organisms, which of the following statements is an important consequence of this first law?

choices.A: The energy content of an organism is constant except for when its cells are dividing.
choices.B: The organism must ultimately obtain all the necessary energy for life from its environment.
choices.C: The entropy of an organism decreases with time as the organism grows in complexity.
choices.D: Organisms are unable to transform energy from the different states in which it can exist.

questions.answer_text: The organism must ultimately obtain all the necessary energy for life from its environment.

questions.stem: Choose the pair of terms that correctly completes this sentence: Catabolism is to anabolism as ________ is to ________.

choices.C: free energy; entropy
choices.D: work; energy

questions.answer_text: exergonic; endergonic

questions.stem: Most cells cannot harness heat to perform work because

choices.A: heat does not involve a transfer of energy.
choices.B: cells do not have much thermal energy; they are relatively cool.
choices.C: temperature is usually uniform throughout a cell.
choices.D: heat can never be used to do work.

questions.answer_text: temperature is usually uniform throughout a cell.

questions.stem: Which of the following metabolic processes can occur without a net influx of energy from some other process?

choices.D: Amino acids → Protein

questions.stem: If an enzyme in solution is saturated with substrate, the most effective way to obtain a faster yield of products is to

choices.C: add more substrate.
choices.D: add a noncompetitive inhibitor.

questions.answer_text: add more of the enzyme.

questions.stem: Some bacteria are metabolically active in hot springs because

choices.A: they are able to maintain a lower internal temperature.
choices.C: their enzymes have high optimal temperatures.
choices.D: their enzymes are completely insensitive to temperature.

questions.answer_text: their enzymes have high optimal temperatures.

questions.stem: If an enzyme is added to a solution where its substrate and product are in equilibrium, what will occur?

choices.B: The reaction will change from endergonic to exergonic.
choices.C: The free energy of the system will change.
choices.D: Nothing; the reaction will stay at equilibrium.

questions.answer_text: Nothing; the reaction will stay at equilibrium.

questions.stem: In which reactions of cellular respiration and fermentation does substrate-level phosphorylation occur?

choices.B: only in the citric acid cycle
choices.C: only in the electron transport chain
choices.D: in both glycolysis and the citric acid cycle

questions.answer_text: in both glycolysis and the citric acid cycle

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes what happens to a molecule that functions as the reducing agent (electron donor) in a redox or oxidation-reduction reaction?

choices.A: It gains electrons and gains potential energy.
choices.B: It loses electrons and loses potential energy.
choices.C: It gains electrons and loses potential energy.
choices.D: It loses electrons and gains potential energy.

questions.answer_text: It loses electrons and loses potential energy.

questions.stem: What happens when electrons are passed from one atom to a more electronegative atom?

choices.A: The more electronegative atom is reduced, and energy is released.
choices.B: The more electronegative atom is reduced, and energy is consumed.
choices.C: The more electronegative atom is oxidized, and energy is consumed.
choices.D: The more electronegative atom is oxidized, and energy is released.

questions.answer_text: The more electronegative atom is reduced, and energy is released.

questions.stem: Which of the summary statements below describes the results of the following reaction? C6H12O6 + 6 O2 → 6 CO2 + 6 H2O + Energy

choices.A: C6H12O6 is oxidized and O2 is reduced.
choices.B: O2 is oxidized and H2O is reduced.
choices.C: CO2 is reduced and O2 is oxidized.
choices.D: O2 is reduced and CO2 is oxidized.

questions.answer_text: C6H12O6 is oxidized and O2 is reduced.

questions.stem: What happens to a glucose molecule when it loses a hydrogen atom as the result of an oxidation-reduction reaction?

choices.B: The glucose molecule is an oxidizing agent.
choices.C: The glucose molecule is oxidized.
choices.D: The glucose molecule is reduced.

questions.answer_text: The glucose molecule is oxidized.

questions.stem: When a molecule of NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) gains a hydrogen atom (not a proton), the molecule becomes ________.

choices.C: reduced
choices.D: redoxed

questions.answer_text: reduced

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about NAD+ is true?

choices.A: NAD+ is reduced to NADH during glycolysis, pyruvate oxidation, and the citric acid cycle.
choices.B: NAD+ has more chemical energy than NADH.
choices.C: NAD+ can donate electrons for use in oxidative phosphorylation.
choices.D: In the absence of NAD+, glycolysis can still function.

questions.answer_text: NAD+ is reduced to NADH during glycolysis, pyruvate oxidation, and the citric acid cycle.

questions.stem: The oxygen consumed during cellular respiration is directly involved in which of the following processes or events?

choices.B: accepting electrons at the end of the electron transport chain
choices.C: the citric acid cycle
choices.D: the oxidation of pyruvate to acetyl CoA

questions.answer_text: accepting electrons at the end of the electron transport chain

questions.stem: Why are carbohydrates and fats frequently considered high-energy foods?

choices.C: They contain many electrons associated with hydrogen atoms.
choices.D: They are strong oxidizing molecules.

questions.answer_text: They contain many electrons associated with hydrogen atoms.

questions.stem: A cell has enough available ATP to meet its needs for about 30 seconds. What is likely to happen when an athlete exhausts his or her ATP supply?

choices.A: He or she has to sit down and rest.
choices.B: Catabolic processes are activated that generate more ATP.
choices.C: ATP is transported into the cell from the circulatory system.
choices.D: Other cells take over, and the muscle cells that have used up their ATP cease to function.

questions.answer_text: Catabolic processes are activated that generate more ATP.

questions.stem: Substrate-level phosphorylation accounts for approximately what percentage of the ATP formed by the reactions of glycolysis?

The free energy for the oxidation of glucose to CO2 and water is -686 kcal/mol, and the free energy for the reduction of NAD+ to NADH is +53 kcal/mol. Why are only two molecules of NADH formed during glycolysis when it appears that as many as a dozen could be formed?

choices.A: Most of the free energy available from the oxidation of glucose is used in the production of ATP in glycolysis.
choices.B: Glycolysis is a very inefficient reaction, with much of the energy of glucose released as heat.
choices.C: Most of the free energy available from the oxidation of glucose remains in pyruvate, one of the products of glycolysis.
choices.D: There is no CO2 or water produced as products of glycolysis.

questions.answer_text: Most of the free energy available from the oxidation of glucose remains in pyruvate, one of the products of glycolysis.

questions.stem: Starting with one molecule of glucose, glycolysis results in the net production of which of the following sets of energy-containing products?

choices.C: 4 NADH, 2 pyruvate, and 4 ATP
choices.D: 6 CO2, 2 pyruvate, and 2 ATP

questions.answer_text: 2 NADH, 2 pyruvate, and 2 ATP

questions.stem: In glycolysis, for each molecule of glucose oxidized to pyruvate, ________.

choices.A: two molecules of ATP are used, and two molecules of ATP are produced
choices.B: two molecules of ATP are used, and four molecules of ATP are produced
choices.C: four molecules of ATP are used, and two molecules of ATP are produced
choices.D: two molecules of ATP are used, and six molecules of ATP are produced

questions.answer_text: two molecules of ATP are used, and four molecules of ATP are produced

questions.stem: Which kind of metabolic poison would most directly interfere with glycolysis?

choices.A: an agent that reacts with oxygen and depletes its concentration in the cell
choices.B: an agent that binds to pyruvate and inactivates it
choices.C: an agent that closely mimics the structure of glucose but is not metabolized
choices.D: an agent that reacts with NADH and oxidizes it to NAD+

questions.answer_text: an agent that closely mimics the structure of glucose but is not metabolized

questions.stem: During which of the following metabolic processes is most of the CO2 from the catabolism of glucose is released?

choices.C: oxidation of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA
choices.D: the citric acid cycle

questions.answer_text: the citric acid cycle

questions.stem: Following glycolysis and the citric acid cycle, but before the electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation, the carbon skeleton of glucose has been broken down to CO2 with some net gain of ATP. Most of the energy from the original glucose molecule at that point in the process, however, is stored in the form of which of the following molecules?

choices.C: pyruvate
choices.D: NADH

questions.answer_text: NADH

questions.stem: Which electron carrier(s) function in the citric acid cycle?

choices.C: the electron transport chain
choices.D: ADP and ATP

questions.answer_text: NADH and FADH2

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question below. The citric acid cycle. If you were to add one of the eight citric acid cycle intermediates to the culture medium of yeast growing in the laboratory, what do you think would happen to the rates of ATP and carbon dioxide production?

choices.A: There would be no change in ATP production, but the rate of carbon dioxide production would increase.
choices.B: The rates of ATP production and carbon dioxide production would both increase.
choices.C: The rate of ATP production would increase, but the rate of carbon dioxide production would decrease.
choices.D: The rates of ATP and carbon dioxide production would both decrease.

questions.answer_text: The rates of ATP production and carbon dioxide production would both increase.

questions.stem: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is released during which of the following stages of cellular respiration?

choices.A: glycolysis and the oxidation of pyruvate to acetyl CoA
choices.B: oxidation of pyruvate to acetyl CoA and the citric acid cycle
choices.C: oxidative phosphorylation and fermentation
choices.D: fermentation and glycolysis

questions.answer_text: oxidation of pyruvate to acetyl CoA and the citric acid cycle

questions.stem: If glucose is the sole energy source, what fraction of the carbon dioxide exhaled by animals is generated only by the reactions involved in oxidation of pyruvate to acetyl CoA?

choices.D: all of it

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question below. The citric acid cycle. For each mole of glucose (C6H12O6) oxidized by cellular respiration, how many moles of CO2 are released in the citric acid cycle (see the accompanying figure)?

Use the following information to answer the question below. The citric acid cycle. If pyruvate oxidation is blocked, what will happen to the levels of oxaloacetate and citric acid in the citric acid cycle shown in the accompanying figure?

choices.A: Oxaloacetate will decrease and citric acid will accumulate.
choices.B: Oxaloacetate will accumulate and citric acid will decrease.
choices.C: Both oxaloacetate and citric acid will decrease.
choices.D: Both oxaloacetate and citric acid will accumulate.

questions.answer_text: Oxaloacetate will accumulate and citric acid will decrease.

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question below. The citric acid cycle. Starting with citrate, which of the following combinations of products would result from three acetyl CoA molecules entering the citric acid cycle?

choices.C: 3 ATP, 6 CO2, 9 NADH, and 3 FADH2
choices.D: 6 ATP, 6 CO2, 3 NADH, and 12 FADH2

questions.answer_text: 3 ATP, 6 CO2, 9 NADH, and 3 FADH2

questions.stem: In the presence of oxygen, the three-carbon compound pyruvate can be catabolized in the citric acid cycle. First, however, the pyruvate (1) loses a carbon, which is given off as a molecule of CO2, (2) is oxidized to form a two-carbon compound called acetate, and (3) is bonded to coenzyme A. Which of the following sets of products result from these reactions?

choices.C: acetyl CoA, NADH, and CO2
choices.D: acetyl CoA, NAD+, ATP, and CO2

questions.answer_text: acetyl CoA, NADH, and CO2

questions.stem: Which one of the following is formed by the removal of a carbon (as CO2) from a molecule of pyruvate?

choices.C: citrate
choices.D: water

questions.answer_text: acetyl CoA

questions.stem: Which of the following events takes place in the electron transport chain?

choices.A: the breakdown of glucose into six carbon dioxide molecules
choices.B: the breakdown of an acetyl group to carbon dioxide
choices.C: the harnessing of energy from high-energy electrons derived from glycolysis and the citric acid cycle
choices.D: substrate-level phosphorylation

questions.answer_text: the harnessing of energy from high-energy electrons derived from glycolysis and the citric acid cycle

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the electron transport chain is true?

choices.A: It is driven by ATP hydrolysis.
choices.B: It includes a series of hydrolysis reactions associated with mitochondrial membranes.
choices.C: It consists of a series of redox reactions
choices.D: It occurs in the cytoplasm of both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

questions.answer_text: It consists of a series of redox reactions

questions.stem: Which of the following processes is driven by chemiosmosis?

choices.C: ATP hydrolysis
choices.D: reduction of NAD+ to NADH

questions.answer_text: oxidative phosphorylation

questions.stem: Which of the following sequences describes the path by which electrons travel downhill energetically in aerobic respiration?

choices.A: glucose → NADH → electron transport chain → oxygen
choices.C: glucose → pyruvate → electron transport chain → NADH → ATP
choices.D: food → glycolysis → citric acid cycle → NADH → ATP

questions.answer_text: glucose → NADH → electron transport chain → oxygen

questions.stem: Where are the proteins of the electron transport chain located?

choices.C: mitochondrial intermembrane space
choices.D: mitochondrial matrix

questions.answer_text: mitochondrial inner membrane

questions.stem: During aerobic respiration, which of the following molecules directly donates electrons to the electron transport chain at the lowest energy level?

choices.C: water
choices.D: FADH2

questions.answer_text: FADH2

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the primary role played by oxygen in cellular respiration?

choices.A: It yields energy in the form of ATP as it is passed down the electron transport chain.
choices.B: It oxidizes glucose to form two molecules of pyruvate.
choices.C: It serves as an acceptor for carbon, forming CO2 in the citric acid cycle.
choices.D: It serves as the final acceptor for electrons from the electron transport chain.

questions.answer_text: It serves as the final acceptor for electrons from the electron transport chain.

questions.stem: Water is one of the end products of aerobic respiration. What is the source of the oxygen atom used in formation of the water?

choices.C: molecular oxygen (O2)
choices.D: pyruvate (C3H3O3 -)

questions.answer_text: molecular oxygen (O2)

questions.stem: In chemiosmosis, what is the most direct source of energy that is used to convert ADP + i to ATP?

choices.A: energy released as electrons flow through the electron transport chain
choices.C: energy released from movement of protons through ATP synthase, down their electrochemical gradient
choices.D: energy released as electrons are transported across the inner mitochondrial membrane

questions.answer_text: energy released from movement of protons through ATP synthase, down their electrochemical gradient

questions.stem: Energy released by the electron transport chain is used to pump H+ ions into which location in eukaryotic cells?

choices.A: cytoplasm adjacent to the mitochondrial outer membrane
choices.C: mitochondrial intermembrane space
choices.D: mitochondrial matrix

questions.answer_text: mitochondrial intermembrane space

questions.stem: Which of the following processes generates a proton-motive force in mitochondria?

choices.A: the flow of protons through ATP synthase down their concentration gradient
choices.B: the reduction of NAD+ by the first electron carrier in the electron transport chain
choices.C: lowering of pH in the mitochondrial matrix
choices.D: pumping of hydrogen ions from the mitochondrial matrix across the inner membrane and into the intermembrane space

questions.answer_text: pumping of hydrogen ions from the mitochondrial matrix across the inner membrane and into the intermembrane space

questions.stem: Approximately how many molecules of ATP are produced from the complete oxidation of one molecule of glucose (C6H12O6) in aerobic cellular respiration?

The synthesis of ATP by oxidative phosphorylation, using the energy released by movement of protons across the membrane down their electrochemical gradient, is an example of which of the following processes?

choices.C: a reaction with a positive ΔG
choices.D: coupling of an endergonic reaction to an exergonic reaction

questions.answer_text: coupling of an endergonic reaction to an exergonic reaction

questions.stem: If a cell is able to synthesize 30 ATP molecules for each molecule of glucose completely oxidized to carbon dioxide and water, approximately how many ATP molecules can the cell synthesize for each molecule of pyruvate oxidized to carbon dioxide and water?
In liver cells, the inner mitochondrial membranes are about five times the area of the outer mitochondrial membranes. What purpose must this serve?

choices.A: It allows for an increased rate of glycolysis.
choices.B: It allows for an increased rate of the citric acid cycle.
choices.C: It increases the surface for oxidative phosphorylation.
choices.D: It increases the surface for substrate-level phosphorylation.

questions.answer_text: It increases the surface for oxidative phosphorylation.

questions.stem: A person on a strict diet and exercise regimen lost 7 kg (about 15 pounds) of body fat in just two weeks. What is the most likely way that the lost fat left the body?

choices.A: It was released as CO2 and H2O.
choices.B: It was converted to heat and then released.
choices.C: It was converted to ATP, which weighs much less than fat.
choices.D: It was eliminated from the body as feces.

questions.answer_text: It was released as CO2 and H2O.

questions.stem: Exposing inner mitochondrial membranes to ultrasonic vibrations will disrupt the membranes. However, the fragments will reseal "inside out." The little vesicles that result can still transfer electrons from NADH to oxygen and synthesize ATP. After the disruption, which components involved in oxidative phosphorylation must be present for electron transfer and ATP synthesis to still occur?

choices.C: all of the electron transport system and the proteins that add CoA to acetyl groups
choices.D: all of the electron transport system and ATP synthase

questions.answer_text: all of the electron transport system and ATP synthase

questions.stem: Exposing inner mitochondrial membranes to ultrasonic vibrations will disrupt the membranes. However, the fragments will reseal "inside out." The little vesicles that result can still transfer electrons from NADH to oxygen and synthesize ATP. Which of the following statements about these inside-out membrane vesicles is true?

choices.A: The inside of the vesicles will become acidic when NADH is added.
choices.B: The inside of the vesicles will become alkaline when NADH is added.
choices.C: ATP will be produced from ADP and i in the interior of the vesicle.
choices.D: The vesicles will pump protons out of the interior of the vesicle to the exterior using energy from ATP hydrolysis.

questions.answer_text: The inside of the vesicles will become acidic when NADH is added.

questions.stem: What kinds of cells carry out ATP synthesis by chemiosmosis?

choices.A: all cells, both prokaryotic and eukaryotic, exclusively using oxygen as the electron acceptor
choices.B: only animal cells in mitochondria, exclusively using oxygen as the electron acceptor
choices.C: only eukaryotic cells, both plant and animal, using either oxygen or other electron acceptors
choices.D: all respiring cells, both prokaryotic and eukaryotic, using either oxygen or other electron acceptors

questions.answer_text: all respiring cells, both prokaryotic and eukaryotic, using either oxygen or other electron acceptors

questions.stem: Which of the following metabolic processes normally occurs regardless of whether or not oxygen (O2) is present?

choices.C: lactate fermentation
choices.D: oxidative phosphorylation

questions.answer_text: glycolysis

questions.stem: Which of the following metabolic processes take place in the cytosol of a eukaryotic cell?

choices.C: oxidation of pyruvate to acetyl CoA
choices.D: citric acid cycle

questions.answer_text: glycolysis and fermentation

questions.stem: In the absence of oxygen, yeast cells can obtain energy by fermentation, which results in the production of which of the following sets of molecules?

choices.C: ATP, NADH, and ethanol
choices.D: ATP, CO2, and acetyl CoA

questions.answer_text: ATP, CO2, and ethanol (ethyl alcohol)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes a primary function of both alcohol fermentation and lactic acid fermentation?

choices.C: oxidation of NADH to NAD+
choices.D: hydrolysis of ATP to ADP + i

questions.answer_text: oxidation of NADH to NAD+

questions.stem: An organism is discovered that thrives in both the presence and absence of oxygen. Interestingly, as oxygen is removed from the organism's environment, the rate of sugar consumption increases while the growth rate decreases. What do these observations suggest about the likely identity of this organism?

choices.A: It is an unremarkable eukaryotic organism.
choices.C: It is an obligate anaerobic organism.
choices.D: It is a facultative anaerobic organism.

questions.answer_text: It is a facultative anaerobic organism.

questions.stem: Why is glycolysis considered to be one of the first metabolic pathways to have evolved?

choices.A: It produces much less ATP than does oxidative phosphorylation.
choices.B: It does not involve organelles or specialized structures, does not require oxygen, and is present in most organisms.
choices.C: It is present in prokaryotic cells but not in eukaryotic cells.
choices.D: It requires the presence of membrane-enclosed cell organelles found only in eukaryotic cells.

questions.answer_text: It does not involve organelles or specialized structures, does not require oxygen, and is present in most organisms.

questions.stem: Yeast cells that have defective mitochondria incapable of respiration will be able to grow by catabolizing which of the following carbon sources for energy?

choices.C: fatty acids
choices.D: amino acids

questions.answer_text: glucose

questions.stem: What is the oxidizing agent in the following reaction? Pyruvate + NADH + H+ → Lactate + NAD+

choices.C: lactate
choices.D: pyruvate

questions.answer_text: pyruvate

questions.stem: High levels of citric acid inhibit the enzyme phosphofructokinase, a key enzyme in glycolysis. Citric acid binds to the enzyme at a different location from the active site. This is an example of ________.

choices.C: the specificity of enzymes for their substrates
choices.D: positive feedback regulation

questions.answer_text: allosteric regulation

questions.stem: The enzyme phosphofructokinase (PFK) catalyzes a key step in glycolysis. PFK is inhibited by high levels of which of the following molecules?

choices.C: ATP and citrate
choices.D: citrate and CO2

questions.answer_text: ATP and citrate

questions.stem: The enzyme phosphofructokinase (PFK) catalyzes a key step in glycolysis. About 10% of Springer spaniels suffer from canine PFK deficiency. Given its critical role in glycolysis, which of the following conditions would be a likely consequence for dogs afflicted with this disorder?

choices.B: They would have elevated blood-glucose levels, which may result in a high incidence of diabetes.
choices.C: They would be lethargic and readily tire from exercise.
choices.D: They would carry out elevated levels of oxidative phosphorylation.

questions.answer_text: They would be lethargic and readily tire from exercise.

questions.stem: A young dog has never had much energy. He is brought to a veterinarian for help, and she decides to conduct several diagnostic tests. She discovers that the dog's mitochondria can use only fatty acids and amino acids for respiration, and his cells produce more lactate than normal. Of the following, which is the best explanation of the dog's condition?

choices.A: His mitochondria lack the transport protein that moves pyruvate across the outer mitochondrial membrane.
choices.B: His cells cannot move NADH from glycolysis into the mitochondria.
choices.C: His cells lack the enzyme in glycolysis that forms pyruvate.
choices.D: His cells have a defective electron transport chain, so glucose is metabolized to lactate instead of to acetyl CoA.

questions.answer_text: His mitochondria lack the transport protein that moves pyruvate across the outer mitochondrial membrane.

questions.stem: Even though plants cells carry out photosynthesis, they still use their mitochondria for oxidation of pyruvate. Under what conditions will plant cell mitochondria be active in this process?

choices.A: only in photosynthetic cells in the light, while photosynthesis occurs concurrently
choices.B: only in cells that store glucose in the form of starch and only in the dark
choices.C: in all cells, with or without light
choices.D: in photosynthesizing cells in the light, and in other cells in the dark

questions.answer_text: in all cells, with or without light

questions.stem: Beta oxidation generates substrates for cellular respiration through which of the following processes?

choices.C: catabolism of proteins
choices.D: catabolism of fatty acids

questions.answer_text: catabolism of fatty acids

questions.stem: Fatty acids usually have an even number of carbons in their structures. Catabolism of fatty acids produces two-carbon fragments that are converted to acetyl CoA molecules. What is the most likely way in which these acetyl CoA molecules would be metabolized in aerobic cellular respiration?

choices.A: They would directly enter the electron transport chain.
choices.B: They would directly enter the energy-yielding phase of glycolysis.
choices.C: They would be converted to pyruvate and then undergo pyruvate oxidation upon transport into mitochondria.
choices.D: They would directly enter the citric acid cycle.

questions.answer_text: They would directly enter the citric acid cycle.

questions.stem: New biosensors, applied like a temporary tattoo to the skin, can alert serious athletes that they are about to "hit the wall" and will find it difficult to continue exercising. These biosensors monitor lactate, a form of lactic acid, released in sweat during strenuous exercise. Which of the statements below is the best explanation of why athletes would need to monitor lactate levels?

choices.A: During aerobic respiration, muscle cells cannot produce enough lactate to fuel muscle cell contractions, and muscles begin to cramp, thus athletic performance suffers.
choices.B: During anaerobic respiration, lactate levels increase when muscles cells need more energy; however, muscles cells eventually fatigue, thus athletes should modify their activities to increase aerobic respiration.
choices.C: During aerobic respiration, muscles cells produce too much lactate, which causes a rise in the pH of the muscle cells, thus athletes must consume increased amounts of sports drinks, high in electrolytes, to buffer the pH.
choices.D: During anaerobic respiration, muscle cells receive too little oxygen and begin to convert lactate to pyruvate (pyruvic acid), thus athletes experience cramping and fatigue.

questions.answer_text: During anaerobic respiration, lactate levels increase when muscles cells need more energy; however, muscles cells eventually fatigue, thus athletes should modify their activities to increase aerobic respiration.

questions.stem: The immediate energy source that drives ATP synthesis by ATP synthase during oxidative phosphorylation is the

choices.A: oxidation of glucose and other organic compounds.
choices.B: flow of electrons down the electron transport chain.
choices.C: H+ concentration gradient across the membrane holding ATP synthase.
choices.D: transfer of phosphate to ADP.

questions.answer_text: H+ concentration gradient across the membrane holding ATP synthase.

questions.stem: Which metabolic pathway is common to both fermentation and cellular respiration of a glucose molecule?

choices.C: glycolysis
choices.D: reduction of pyruvate to lactate

questions.answer_text: glycolysis

questions.stem: The final electron acceptor of the electron transport chain that functions in aerobic oxidative phosphorylation is

choices.C: NAD+.
choices.D: pyruvate.

questions.answer_text: oxygen.

questions.stem: In mitochondria, exergonic redox reactions

choices.A: are the source of energy driving prokaryotic ATP synthesis.
choices.B: provide the energy that establishes the proton gradient.
choices.C: reduce carbon atoms to carbon dioxide.
choices.D: are coupled via phosphorylated intermediates to endergonic processes.

questions.answer_text: provide the energy that establishes the proton gradient.

questions.stem: What is the oxidizing agent in the following reaction? Pyruvate + NADH + H- Lactate + NAD-

choices.C: lactate
choices.D: pyruvate

questions.answer_text: pyruvate

questions.stem: When electrons flow along the electron transport chains of mitochondria, which of the following changes occurs?

choices.A: The pH of the matrix increases.
choices.B: ATP synthase pumps protons by active transport.
choices.C: The electrons gain free energy.
choices.D: NAD+ is oxidized.

questions.answer_text: The pH of the matrix increases.

questions.stem: Most CO2 from catabolism is released during

choices.C: lactate fermentation.
choices.D: electron transport.

questions.answer_text: the citric acid cycle.

questions.stem: In which of the following organisms did the process of photosynthesis most likely originate?

choices.C: in fungi
choices.D: three separate times during evolution

questions.answer_text: in prokaryotes

questions.stem: In autotrophic bacteria, where is chlorophyll located?

choices.C: in the nucleoid
choices.D: in infolded regions of the plasma membrane

questions.answer_text: in infolded regions of the plasma membrane

questions.stem: Under what conditions do photosynthesis and cellular respiration occur in plants?

choices.A: Photosynthesis and cellular respiration occur only in the light.
choices.B: Photosynthesis occurs only in the light, and cellular respiration occurs only in the dark.
choices.C: Photosynthesis occurs only in the light, and cellular respiration occurs in both the dark and the light.
choices.D: Photosynthesis and cellular respiration occur in both the dark and the light.

questions.answer_text: Photosynthesis occurs only in the light, and cellular respiration occurs in both the dark and the light.

questions.stem: Use the following figure to answer the question. If photosynthesizing green algae are provided with CO2 containing heavy oxygen (18O), which of the following molecules produced by the algae (refer to the accompanying figure) will fail to contain 18O in later biochemical analyses?

choices.C: ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP)
choices.D: ADP

questions.answer_text: ADP

questions.stem: The oxygen released by photosynthesis is produced by which of the following processes?

choices.C: the electron transfer system of photosystem I
choices.D: the electron transfer system of photosystem II

questions.answer_text: splitting water molecules

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes a distinction between autotrophs and heterotrophs?

choices.A: Cellular respiration is unique to heterotrophs.
choices.C: Autotrophs, but not heterotrophs, can nourish themselves beginning with CO2 and other nutrients that are inorganic.
choices.D: Only heterotrophs require oxygen.

questions.answer_text: Autotrophs, but not heterotrophs, can nourish themselves beginning with CO2 and other nutrients that are inorganic.

questions.stem: Use the following figure to answer the question. The figure shows the absorption spectrum for chlorophyll a and the action spectrum for photosynthesis. Why are they different?

choices.A: Green and yellow wavelengths inhibit the absorption of red and blue wavelengths.
choices.B: Oxygen given off during photosynthesis interferes with the absorption of light.
choices.C: Other pigments absorb light in addition to chlorophyll a.
choices.D: Aerobic bacteria take up oxygen, which changes the measurement of the rate of photosynthesis.

questions.answer_text: Other pigments absorb light in addition to chlorophyll a.

questions.stem: Use the following figure to answer the question. What wavelength of light in the figure is most effective in driving photosynthesis?

choices.C: 625 nm
choices.D: 730 nm

questions.answer_text: 420 nm

questions.stem: Theodor W. Engelmann illuminated a filament of algae with light that passed through a prism, thus exposing different segments of algae to different wavelengths of light.
