He added aerobic bacteria and then noted in which areas the bacteria congregated. He noted that the largest groups were found in the areas illuminated by the red and blue light. What did Engelmann conclude about the congregation of bacteria in the red and blue areas?

choices.A: Bacteria congregated in these areas due to an increase in the temperature of the red and blue light.
choices.B: Bacteria congregated in these areas because these areas had the most oxygen being released.
choices.C: Bacteria are attracted to red and blue light and thus these wavelengths are more reactive than other wavelengths.
choices.D: Bacteria congregated in these areas due to an increase in the temperature caused by an increase in photosynthesis.

questions.answer_text: Bacteria congregated in these areas because these areas had the most oxygen being released.

questions.stem: Theodor W. Engelmann illuminated a filament of algae with light that passed through a prism, thus exposing different segments of algae to different wavelengths of light. He added aerobic bacteria and then noted in which areas the bacteria congregated. He noted that the largest groups were found in the areas illuminated by the red and blue light. Which of the following statements describes a relationship that Engelmann's experiment helped to determine?

choices.A: the relationship between wavelength of light and the rate of aerobic respiration
choices.B: the relationship between wavelength of light and the amount of heat released
choices.C: the relationship between wavelength of light and the rate of photosynthesis
choices.D: the relationship between carbon dioxide concentration and the rate of photosynthesis

questions.answer_text: the relationship between wavelength of light and the rate of photosynthesis

questions.stem: A spaceship is designed to support animal life for a multiyear voyage to the outer planets of the solar system. Plants will be grown to provide oxygen and to recycle carbon dioxide. Since the spaceship will be too far from the sun for photosynthesis, an artificial light source will be needed. What wavelengths of light should be used to maximize plant growth with a minimum of energy expenditure?

choices.C: a mixture of blue and red light
choices.D: UV light

questions.answer_text: a mixture of blue and red light

questions.stem: A spaceship is designed to support animal life for a multiyear voyage to the outer planets of the solar system. Plants will be grown to provide oxygen and to recycle carbon dioxide. Since the spaceship will be too far from the sun for photosynthesis, an artificial light source will be needed. Suppose a plant has a unique photosynthetic pigment and the leaves of this plant appear to be reddish yellow. What wavelengths of visible light are absorbed by this pigment?

choices.C: green and yellow
choices.D: green and red

questions.answer_text: blue and violet

questions.stem: Use the following figure to answer the question. Halobacterium has a photosynthetic membrane that appears purple. Its photosynthetic action spectrum is the inverse of the action spectrum for green plants (see figure). That is, the Halobacterium action spectrum has a peak where the green plant action spectrum has a trough. What wavelengths of light do the Halobacterium photosynthetic pigments absorb?

choices.C: green and yellow
choices.D: blue and red

questions.answer_text: green and yellow

questions.stem: Why are the reaction centers of photosystems composed of several structurally different pigments?

choices.A: Excited electrons must pass through several pigments before they can be transferred to electron acceptors of the electron transport chain.
choices.B: This arrangement enables the plant to absorb light energy of a variety of wavelengths.
choices.C: This arrangement enables the plant to absorb more photons from light energy, all of which are at the same wavelength.
choices.D: This arrangement enables the reaction center to excite electrons to a higher energy level.

questions.answer_text: This arrangement enables the plant to absorb light energy of a variety of wavelengths.

questions.stem: Paper chromatography is a technique used to separate molecules based upon their size and solubility in a particular solvent. If pigments from a particular species of plant are extracted and subjected to paper chromatography, which of the following results is most likely?

choices.A: Paper chromatography would produce a single band of pigment that is characteristic of that particular plant.
choices.B: Paper chromatography would separate the pigments into two bands that appear green.
choices.C: Paper chromatography would separate the pigments into several bands that appear green or yellow/orange.
choices.D: Paper chromatography would separate the pigments into two bands, one that appears blue and one that appears red.

questions.answer_text: Paper chromatography would separate the pigments into several bands that appear green or yellow/orange.

questions.stem: In autumn, chlorophyll is degraded in the leaves of deciduous trees. Why do the leaves change color to shades of yellow, orange, or red?

choices.A: Sugars from sap fill the leaves prior to winter.
choices.B: Degraded chlorophyll changes into many other colors.
choices.C: In the absence of photosynthesis, the leaves produce energy exclusively by aerobic cellular respiration.
choices.D: Other pigments such as carotenoids are still present in the leaves.

questions.answer_text: Other pigments such as carotenoids are still present in the leaves.

questions.stem: Which of the following events accompanies absorption of energy by chlorophyll molecules of the reaction-center complex?

choices.A: ATP is synthesized from the energy absorbed.
choices.C: NADP+ is reduced to NADPH.
choices.D: A molecule of water is split.

questions.answer_text: An electron is excited.

questions.stem: What happens to the free energy released as electrons are passed from photosystem II to photosystem I through a series of electron carriers?

choices.A: It excites electrons of the reaction center in photosystem I.
choices.B: It is used to establish and maintain a proton gradient.
choices.C: It is used to synthesize ATP through substrate-level phosphorylation.
choices.D: It is used to phosphorylate NAD+ to NADPH.

questions.answer_text: It is used to establish and maintain a proton gradient.

questions.stem: Which molecule is the final electron acceptor for electrons from photosystem I?

choices.C: carbon dioxide
choices.D: NADP+

questions.answer_text: NADP+

questions.stem: What is the function of the pigment molecules in a light-harvesting complex in the thylakoid membranes?

choices.A: They split water and release oxygen from the reaction-center chlorophyll.
choices.B: They absorb and transfer light energy to the reaction-center chlorophyll.
choices.C: They synthesize ATP from ADP and i.
choices.D: They transfer electrons to NADP+.

questions.answer_text: They absorb and transfer light energy to the reaction-center chlorophyll.

questions.stem: Which of the following processes is directly associated with photosystem I?

choices.A: receiving electrons from the thylakoid membrane electron transport chain
choices.C: extraction of hydrogen electrons from the splitting of water
choices.D: passing electrons to NADP+

questions.answer_text: receiving electrons from the thylakoid membrane electron transport chain

questions.stem: Some photosynthetic organisms contain chloroplasts that lack photosystem II, yet are able to survive. Which of the following approaches would be the best way to detect the lack of photosystem II in these organisms?

choices.A: Determine whether they have thylakoid membranes.
choices.B: Determine whether they consume CO2 in the dark.
choices.C: Determine whether they produce O2 in the light.
choices.D: Determine the action spectrum for photosynthesis in these organisms.

questions.answer_text: Determine whether they produce O2 in the light.

questions.stem: What are the products of linear electron flow during the light reactions of photosynthesis?

choices.C: ATP and NADPH
choices.D: ADP and NADP+

questions.answer_text: ATP and NADPH

questions.stem: What are the products of cyclic electron flow during the light reactions of photosynthesis?

choices.C: ATP and NADPH
choices.D: ADP and NADP+

questions.answer_text: ATP

questions.stem: As a research scientist, you measure the amount of ATP and NADPH consumed by the Calvin cycle in one hour. You find that 30,000 molecules of ATP were consumed, but only 20,000 molecules of NADPH were consumed. What is the source of the extra ATP molecules?

choices.C: cyclic electron flow
choices.D: linear electron flow

questions.answer_text: cyclic electron flow

questions.stem: Which of the following processes would be most directly affected if a thylakoid membrane is punctured so that the interior of the thylakoid is no longer separated from the stroma?

choices.B: flow of electrons from photosystem II to photosystem I
choices.C: synthesis of ATP
choices.D: reduction of NADP+

questions.answer_text: synthesis of ATP

questions.stem: Where are ATP synthase complexes located in plant cells?

choices.C: thylakoid membrane and inner mitochondrial membrane
choices.D: thylakoid membrane and plasma membrane

questions.answer_text: thylakoid membrane and inner mitochondrial membrane

questions.stem: In mitochondria, an electron transport chain pumps protons from the matrix into the intermembrane space, whereas in chloroplasts, an electron transport chain pumps protons from the ________.

choices.C: thylakoid space to the matrix
choices.D: thylakoid space to the stroma

questions.answer_text: stroma to the thylakoid space

questions.stem: Which of the following events are associated with chemiosmosis in chloroplasts?

choices.A: The pH of the stroma increases and ATP is synthesized.
choices.B: The pH of the thylakoid space increases and ATP is synthesized.
choices.C: The pH of the cytoplasm outside the chloroplast decreases and ATP is synthesized.
choices.D: The pH of the stroma decreases and ATP is hydrolyzed.

questions.answer_text: The pH of the thylakoid space increases and ATP is synthesized.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the relationship between photosynthesis and cellular respiration?

choices.A: Cellular respiration runs the biochemical pathways of photosynthesis in reverse.
choices.B: Photosynthesis stores energy in complex organic molecules; cellular respiration releases energy from complex organic molecules.
choices.C: Photosynthesis occurs only in plants; cellular respiration occurs only in animals.
choices.D: Photosynthesis is catabolic; cellular respiration is anabolic.

questions.answer_text: Photosynthesis stores energy in complex organic molecules; cellular respiration releases energy from complex organic molecules.

questions.stem: In photosynthetic cells, synthesis of ATP by chemiosmosis occurs during ________.

choices.C: photosynthesis and respiration
choices.D: photosynthesis, respiration, and fermentation

questions.answer_text: photosynthesis and respiration

questions.stem: Carbon dioxide is split to form oxygen gas and carbon compounds in which of the following metabolic pathways?

choices.C: photosynthesis and respiration
choices.D: neither photosynthesis nor respiration

questions.answer_text: neither photosynthesis nor respiration

questions.stem: What is the relationship between the wavelength of light and the quantity of energy per photon?

choices.A: They have a direct, linear relationship.
choices.C: They are logarithmically related.
choices.D: They are separate phenomena.

questions.answer_text: They are inversely related.

questions.stem: P680+ is said to be the strongest biological oxidizing agent. Given its function, why is this necessary?

choices.A: It is the receptor for the most excited electron in either photosystem of photosynthesis.
choices.B: It is the molecule that transfers electrons to plastoquinone (Pq) of the electron transfer system.
choices.C: It transfers its electrons to reduce NADP+ to NADPH.
choices.D: It obtains electrons from the oxygen atom in a water molecule, so it must have a stronger attraction for electrons than oxygen has.

questions.answer_text: It obtains electrons from the oxygen atom in a water molecule, so it must have a stronger attraction for electrons than oxygen has.

questions.stem: Carotenoids are often found in foods that are considered to have antioxidant properties in human nutrition. What related function do they have in plants?

choices.A: They serve as accessory pigments to increase light absorption.
choices.B: They protect against oxidative damage from excessive light energy.
choices.C: They shield the sensitive chromosomes of the plant from harmful ultraviolet radiation.
choices.D: They reflect orange light and enhance red light absorption by chlorophyll.

questions.answer_text: They protect against oxidative damage from excessive light energy.

questions.stem: In a plant, which of the following reactions produce molecular oxygen (O2)?

choices.C: the light reactions and the Calvin cycle
choices.D: neither the light reactions nor the Calvin cycle

questions.answer_text: the light reactions alone

questions.stem: The mechanism of photophosphorylation is most similar to which of the following processes?

choices.C: the Calvin cycle
choices.D: reduction of NADP+

questions.answer_text: oxidative phosphorylation in cellular respiration

questions.stem: Which of the following processes is most directly driven by light energy?

choices.A: creation of a pH gradient by pumping protons across the thylakoid membrane
choices.C: reduction of NADP+ molecules
choices.D: removal of electrons from chlorophyll molecules

questions.answer_text: removal of electrons from chlorophyll molecules

questions.stem: A gardener is concerned that her greenhouse is getting too hot from too much light and seeks to shade her plants with colored translucent plastic sheets, the color of which allows passage of only that wavelength. What color should she use to reduce overall light energy but still maximize plant growth?

choices.C: orange
choices.D: Any color will work equally well.

questions.answer_text: blue

questions.stem: A flask containing photosynthetic green algae and a control flask containing water with no algae are both placed under a bank of lights that is set to cycle between 12 hours of light and 12 hours of dark. The dissolved oxygen concentrations in both flasks are monitored. Predict what the relative dissolved oxygen concentrations will be in the flask with algae compared to the control flask. The dissolved oxygen in the flask with algae will ________.

choices.C: be higher in the light, but the same in the dark
choices.D: be higher in the light, but lower in the dark

questions.answer_text: be higher in the light, but lower in the dark

questions.stem: Which of the following molecules are products of the light reactions of photosynthesis that are utilized in the Calvin cycle?

choices.C: ADP, i, and NADP+
choices.D: ATP and NADPH

questions.answer_text: ATP and NADPH

questions.stem: Where in a plant cell does the Calvin cycle take place?

choices.C: interior of the thylakoid (thylakoid space)
choices.D: outer membrane of the chloroplast

questions.answer_text: stroma of the chloroplast

questions.stem: In the initial step in carbon fixation, a molecule of CO2 is attached to RuBP to produce a six- carbon molecule, which is immediately split to produce two molecules of 3-phosphoglycerate. After phosphorylation and reduction produces glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate (G3P), what more needs to occur to complete the Calvin cycle?

choices.A: addition of a pair of electrons from NADPH
choices.C: regeneration of RuBP
choices.D: regeneration of NADP+

questions.answer_text: regeneration of RuBP

questions.stem: Use the following figure to answer the question. Refer to the accompanying figure and the molecules labeled A, B, C, D, and E. If the carbon atom of each of the incoming CO2 molecules is labeled with a radioactive isotope of carbon, which organic molecules will be radioactively labeled after one cycle?

choices.C: C, D, and E only
choices.D: B and C only

questions.answer_text: B, C, D, and E

questions.stem: To identify the molecule that accepts CO2, Calvin and Benson manipulated the carbon- fixation cycle by either cutting off CO2 or cutting off light from cultures of photosynthetic algae. They then measured the concentrations of various metabolites immediately following the manipulation. How would these experiments help identify the CO2 acceptor?

choices.A: The CO2 acceptor concentration would decrease when either the CO2 or light are cut off.
choices.B: The CO2 acceptor concentration would increase when either the CO2 or light are cut off.
choices.C: The CO2 acceptor concentration would decrease when the CO2 is cut off, but increase when the light is cut off.
choices.D: The CO2 acceptor concentration would increase when the CO2 is cut off, but decrease when the light is cut off.

questions.answer_text: The CO2 acceptor concentration would increase when the CO2 is cut off, but decrease when the light is cut off.

questions.stem: Which of the following sequences correctly represents the flow of electrons during photosynthesis?

choices.C: NADPH → chlorophyll → Calvin cycle
choices.D: NADPH → electron transport chain → O2

questions.answer_text: H2O → NADPH → Calvin cycle

questions.stem: Which of the following processes occurs during the Calvin cycle?

choices.C: regeneration of the CO2 acceptor
choices.D: production of ATP

questions.answer_text: regeneration of the CO2 acceptor

questions.stem: The reducing power for Calvin cycle reactions is provided by which of the following molecules?

choices.C: NADP+
choices.D: NADPH

questions.answer_text: NADPH

questions.stem: What would be the expected effect on plants if the atmospheric CO2 concentration was doubled?

choices.A: All plants would have faster growth rates.
choices.B: C3 plants would have faster growth rates; C4 plants would be minimally affected.
choices.C: C4 plants would have faster growth rates; C3 plants would be minimally affected.
choices.D: C3 plants would have faster growth rates; C4 plants would have slower growth rates.

questions.answer_text: C3 plants would have faster growth rates; C4 plants would be minimally affected.

questions.stem: Why are C4 plants able to photosynthesize with no apparent photorespiration?

choices.A: They do not participate in the Calvin cycle.
choices.B: They use PEP carboxylase to initially fix CO2.
choices.C: They conserve water more efficiently.
choices.D: They exclude oxygen from their tissues.

questions.answer_text: They use PEP carboxylase to initially fix CO2.

questions.stem: CAM plants keep stomata closed in the daytime, thus reducing loss of water. They can do this because they ________.

choices.A: fix CO2 into organic acids during the night
choices.B: fix CO2 into sugars in the bundle-sheath cells
choices.C: fix CO2 into pyruvate in the mesophyll cells
choices.D: use photosystem I and photosystem II at night

questions.answer_text: fix CO2 into organic acids during the night

questions.stem: Why might the alternative pathways of photosynthesis using C4 or CAM systems be described as metabolic compromises?

choices.A: Both pathways increase the rate of photosynthesis but also increase the rate of water loss.
choices.B: The CAM pathway allows more CO2 into the plant but also increases the rate of water loss.
choices.C: The C4 pathway decreases water loss but also increases the rate of photorespiration.
choices.D: Both pathways minimize photorespiration but also expend more ATP during carbon fixation.

questions.answer_text: Both pathways minimize photorespiration but also expend more ATP during carbon fixation.

questions.stem: What would be a likely consequence of a mutation in plants that results in a photorespiration deficiency?

choices.A: Photosynthetic efficiency would be reduced at low light intensities.
choices.B: Cells would carry on the Calvin cycle at a much slower rate.
choices.C: There would be more cellular damage from harmful products of the light reactions of photosynthesis.
choices.D: Less oxygen would be produced by photosynthesis.

questions.answer_text: There would be more cellular damage from harmful products of the light reactions of photosynthesis.

questions.stem: Compared to C3 plants, C4 plants ________.

choices.A: can continue to fix CO2 even at lower CO2 concentrations and higher oxygen concentrations
choices.C: do not use rubisco for carbon fixation
choices.D: make a four-carbon compound, oxaloacetate, which is then delivered to the citric acid cycle in mitochondria

questions.answer_text: can continue to fix CO2 even at lower CO2 concentrations and higher oxygen concentrations

questions.stem: Use the following figure to answer the question. Which of the following statements is true concerning the accompanying figure?

choices.A: It represents a C4 photosynthetic system.
choices.B: It represents an adaptation that maximizes photorespiration.
choices.C: It represents a C3 photosynthetic system.
choices.D: It represents a CAM photosynthetic system.

questions.answer_text: It represents a C4 photosynthetic system.

questions.stem: Use the following figure to answer the question. Referring to the accompanying figure, where would elevated concentrations of oxygen inhibit carbon fixation reactions?

choices.C: neither cell I nor cell II
choices.D: both cell I and cell II

questions.answer_text: cell II only

questions.stem: Which of the following statements summarizes the metabolic results of photorespiration?

choices.A: It produces ATP and consumes oxygen and carbon dioxide.
choices.B: It produces carbon dioxide and consumes ATP and oxygen.
choices.C: It produces oxygen and consumes ATP and carbon dioxide.
choices.D: It produces oxygen and ATP and consumes carbon dioxide.

questions.answer_text: It produces carbon dioxide and consumes ATP and oxygen.

questions.stem: Students conducted an experiment to determine the effect of light intensity on the rate of photosynthesis. They punched 40 leaf disks from spinach leaves and used a syringe partially filled with water to pull the gases from the leaf disks so that all leaf disks sunk to the bottom of the syringe. Ten leaf disks from the syringe were placed in each of four cups and covered with 50 ml of the solutions as indicated below. All leaf disks were resting on the bottom of the cups when the experiment began. The volume of liquid in each cup and the temperature of the solutions were held constant. All cups were placed 0.5 meters from the designated light source. A large beaker of water was placed between the light and the cups to act as a heat sink to prevent a change in temperature. At the end of 10 minutes, the number of disks floating in each cup was recorded. Grams of Wattage of Disks floating Trial baking soda light bulb at 10 minutes (CO2 source) 1 0.5 25 3 2 0.5 50 5 3 0.5 75 9 4 0 75 0 Use your knowledge of the mechanism of photosynthesis and the data presented in the chart to determine which of the statements is a correct explanation for the students' data.

choices.A: Cup 1 had a low rate of photosynthesis because 0.5 grams of baking soda did not provide a sufficient amount of CO2.
choices.B: Cup 2 had the highest rate of photosynthesis because it had the highest ratio of disks floating to wattage of light.
choices.C: Cup 3 had the same rate of photosynthesis as Cup 1 because they had the same ratio of disks floating to wattage of light.
choices.D: Cup 4 had the lowest rate of photosynthesis because it had the least CO2.

questions.answer_text: Cup 4 had the lowest rate of photosynthesis because it had the least CO2.

questions.stem: The light reactions of photosynthesis supply the Calvin cycle with

choices.C: H2O and NADPH.
choices.D: ATP and NADPH.

questions.answer_text: ATP and NADPH.

questions.stem: Which of the following sequences correctly represents the flow of electrons during photosynthesis?

choices.C: H2O → photosystem I → photosystem II
choices.D: NADP → Helectron transport chain → O2

questions.answer_text: H2O → NADPH → Calvin cycle

questions.stem: How is photosynthesis similar in C4 plants and CAM plants?

choices.A: In both cases, only photosystem I is used.
choices.B: Both types of plants make sugar without the Calvin cycle.
choices.C: In both cases, rubisco is not used to fix carbon initially.
choices.D: Both types of plants make most of their sugar in the dark.

questions.answer_text: In both cases, rubisco is not used to fix carbon initially.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is a correct distinction between autotrophs and heterotrophs?

choices.A: Autotrophs, but not heterotrophs, can nourish themselves beginning with CO2 and other nutrients that are inorganic.
choices.B: Only heterotrophs require chemical compounds from the environment.
choices.C: Cellular respiration is unique to heterotrophs.
choices.D: Only heterotrophs have mitochondria.

questions.answer_text: Autotrophs, but not heterotrophs, can nourish themselves beginning with CO2 and other nutrients that are inorganic.

questions.stem: Which of the following does not occur during the Calvin cycle?

choices.C: release of oxygen
choices.D: regeneration of the CO2 acceptor

questions.answer_text: release of oxygen

questions.stem: In mechanism, photophosphorylation is most similar to

choices.C: carbon fixation.
choices.D: reduction of NADP+.

questions.answer_text: oxidative phosphorylation in cellular respiration.

questions.stem: Which process is most directly driven by light energy?

choices.A: creation of a pH gradient by pumping protons across the thylakoid membrane
choices.C: transfer of energy from pigment molecule to pigment molecule
choices.D: ATP synthesis

questions.answer_text: transfer of energy from pigment molecule to pigment molecule

questions.stem: In yeast signal transduction, a yeast cell releases a mating factor, which ________.

choices.A: acts back on the same cell that secreted the mating factor, changing its development
choices.B: passes through the membranes of neighboring cells, binds to DNA, and initiates transcription
choices.C: binds to receptors on the membranes of other types of yeast cells
choices.D: diffuses through the membranes of distant cells, causing them to produce factors that initiate long-distance migrations

questions.answer_text: binds to receptors on the membranes of other types of yeast cells

questions.stem: Yeast cells of mating type a are genetically engineered to produce only mating factor α instead of the normal mating factor a. The gene for the mating factor receptor was unaltered. How will these engineered cells behave in terms of mating?

choices.A: They will only mate with normal mating type a cells.
choices.B: They will only mate with normal mating type α cells.
choices.C: They will mate with each other or with normal mating type a cells, but not with normal mating type α cells.
choices.D: They will only mate each other and not with normal mating type a or α cells.

questions.answer_text: They will mate with each other or with normal mating type a cells, but not with normal mating type α cells.

questions.stem: In the formation of biofilms, such as those forming on unbrushed teeth, cell signaling serves which function?

choices.B: aggregation of bacteria that can cause cavities
choices.C: secretion of substances that inhibit foreign bacteria
choices.D: digestion of unwanted parasite populations

questions.answer_text: aggregation of bacteria that can cause cavities

questions.stem: Which of the following is a type of local signaling in which a cell secretes a signal molecule that affects neighboring cells?

choices.C: paracrine signaling
choices.D: synaptic signaling

questions.answer_text: paracrine signaling

questions.stem: Hormones are chemical substances produced in one organ that are released into the bloodstream and affect the function of a target organ. Which of the following conditions is required for the target organ to respond to a particular hormone?

choices.A: Cells in the target organ must modify their plasma membranes to allow the hormone to enter the cytoplasm.
choices.B: The target organ must be the same as the organ that produced the hormone.
choices.C: The target organ must have the opposite mating type of the organ that produced the hormone.
choices.D: The target organ must have receptors that recognize and bind the hormone molecule.

questions.answer_text: The target organ must have receptors that recognize and bind the hormone molecule.

questions.stem: In which of the following ways do plant hormones differ from hormones in animals?

choices.A: Plant hormones frequently travel through the air as a gas.
choices.B: Animal hormones are only local regulators.
choices.C: Plant hormones commonly travel through the soil from one plant to another.
choices.D: Animal hormones typically travel from the hormone producing cell to an adjacent responding cell through gap junctions.

questions.answer_text: Plant hormones frequently travel through the air as a gas.

questions.stem: When a neuron responds to a particular neurotransmitter by opening gated ion channels, the neurotransmitter is serving as which part of the signal pathway?

choices.C: signal molecule
choices.D: response molecule

questions.answer_text: signal molecule

questions.stem: Use the following figure to answer the question. Which of the following types of signaling is represented in the figure?

choices.C: hormonal
choices.D: synaptic

questions.answer_text: synaptic

questions.stem: Use the following figure to answer the question. In the figure, the dots in the space between the two structures represent which of the following?

choices.C: neurotransmitters
choices.D: hormones

questions.answer_text: neurotransmitters

questions.stem: Which observation suggested to Sutherland the involvement of a second messenger in epinephrine's effect on liver cells?

choices.A: Receptor studies indicated that epinephrine was a ligand.
choices.B: Glycogen breakdown was observed only when epinephrine was administered to intact cells.
choices.C: Glycogen breakdown was observed when epinephrine and glycogen phosphorylase were combined in a cell-free system.
choices.D: Epinephrine was known to have different effects on many types of cells.

questions.answer_text: Glycogen breakdown was observed only when epinephrine was administered to intact cells.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about a G protein signaling pathway is true?

choices.A: A G protein-coupled receptor bound to GTP is in its active state.
choices.B: A G protein bound to GTP is in its active state.
choices.C: A G protein bound to GDP is in its active state.
choices.D: Hydrolysis of bound GTP by a G protein activates the G protein.

questions.answer_text: A G protein bound to GTP is in its active state.

questions.stem: What is the most likely mechanism by which testosterone functions inside a cell?

choices.A: It acts as a signal receptor that activates tyrosine kinases.
choices.B: It binds with a receptor protein that enters the nucleus and activates expression of specific genes.
choices.C: It acts as a steroid signal receptor that activates ion channel proteins in the plasma membrane.
choices.D: It coordinates a phosphorylation cascade that reduces spermatogenesis.

questions.answer_text: It binds with a receptor protein that enters the nucleus and activates expression of specific genes.

questions.stem: Scientists have found that extracellular matrix components may induce specific gene expression in embryonic tissues such as the liver and testes. For this to happen, there must be direct communication between the extracellular matrix and the developing cells. Which kind of transmembrane protein would most likely be involved in this kind of induction?

choices.C: actin microfilaments
choices.D: receptor tyrosine kinases

questions.answer_text: integrins

questions.stem: One of the major categories of receptors in the plasma membrane functions by forming dimers, adding phosphate groups, and then activating relay proteins. Which type does this?

choices.C: steroid receptors
choices.D: receptor tyrosine kinases

questions.answer_text: receptor tyrosine kinases

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes a likely effect of a drug designed that inhibits the cellular response to testosterone?

choices.A: The cytoplasmic levels of cAMP would decrease.
choices.B: The transcription of certain genes would decrease.
choices.C: The cytosolic calcium concentration would increase.
choices.D: The activity of G proteins would decrease.

questions.answer_text: The transcription of certain genes would decrease.

questions.stem: Many G protein-coupled receptors contain seven transmembrane α-helical domains. The amino end of the protein lies at the exterior of the plasma membrane. Loops of amino acids connect the helices either at the exterior surface or on the cytosolic surface of the membrane. The loop on the cytosolic side between helices 5 and 6 is usually substantially longer than the others. Where would you expect to find the carboxyl end of the protein?

choices.C: connected with the loop at H5 and H6
choices.D: embedded in the phospholipid bilayer of the membrane

questions.answer_text: at the cytosolic surface

questions.stem: Many G protein-coupled receptors contain seven transmembrane α-helical domains. The amino end of the protein lies at the exterior of the plasma membrane. Loops of amino acids connect the helices either at the exterior surface or on the cytosolic surface of the membrane. The loop on the cytosolic side between helices 5 and 6 is usually substantially longer than the others. Where would a coupled G protein most likely interact with this receptor?

choices.C: along the exterior margin
choices.D: at the loop between H5 and H6

questions.answer_text: at the loop between H5 and H6

questions.stem: Binding of a signaling molecule to which type of receptor leads directly to a change in the distribution of ions on opposite sides of the membrane?

choices.C: ligand-gated ion channel
choices.D: steroid receptor

questions.answer_text: ligand-gated ion channel

questions.stem: Why does testosterone, a lipid-soluble signaling molecule that crosses the membranes of all cells, affect only target cells?

choices.A: Only target cells retain the appropriate genes regulated by testosterone.
choices.B: Intracellular receptors for testosterone are present only in target cells.
choices.C: Only target cells possess the cytosolic enzymes that transduce the signal from testosterone to adenylyl cyclase.
choices.D: Only in target cells is testosterone able to initiate the phosphorylation cascade leading to activated transcription factor.

questions.answer_text: Intracellular receptors for testosterone are present only in target cells.

questions.stem: If an animal cell suddenly lost the ability to produce GTP, what might happen to its signaling system?

choices.A: It would not be able to activate G proteins on the cytoplasmic side of the plasma membrane.
choices.B: It would be able to carry out reception and transduction but would not be able to respond to a signal.
choices.C: It would use ATP instead of GTP to activate G proteins on the cytoplasmic side of the plasma membrane.
choices.D: It would not be able to activate receptor tyrosine kinases.

questions.answer_text: It would not be able to activate G proteins on the cytoplasmic side of the plasma membrane.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true of steroid receptors?

choices.A: The receptor molecules are themselves lipids or glycolipids.
choices.B: The receptor may be inside the nucleus of a target cell.
choices.C: The unbound steroid receptors are quickly recycled by lysosomes.
choices.D: Steroid receptors are typically bound to the external surface of the nuclear membrane.

questions.answer_text: The receptor may be inside the nucleus of a target cell.

questions.stem: Particular receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs) that promote excessive cell division are found at high levels in various cancer cells. HER2 is an RTK that is present at excessively high levels in some breast cancer cells. Herceptin is a protein that binds to HER2 and inhibits cell division. Herceptin may be an effective treatment for breast cancer treatment under which of the following conditions?

choices.A: If injection of HER2 in the patient's cancer cells stimulates cell division.
choices.B: If the patient's cancer cells have excessive levels of HER2.
choices.C: If the patient's genome codes for the HER2.
choices.D: If the patient has excessive levels of other RTKs in cancer cells.

questions.answer_text: If the patient's cancer cells have excessive levels of HER2.

questions.stem: Which of the following activities would be inhibited by a drug that specifically blocks the addition of phosphate groups to proteins?

choices.A: binding of G proteins to G protein-coupled receptors
choices.C: adenylyl cyclase activity
choices.D: receptor tyrosine kinase activity

questions.answer_text: receptor tyrosine kinase activity

questions.stem: The receptors for steroid hormones are located inside the cell instead of the membrane surface like most other signal receptors. How do steroids gain access to their receptors?

choices.A: Steroid hormone receptors undergo conformational changes that relocate them on the membrane surface.
choices.B: Both steroid hormones and their receptors are produced by the same cells.
choices.C: Steroid hormones are lipid soluble, so they can readily diffuse through the lipid bilayer of the cell membrane.
choices.D: Steroid hormones first bind to a steroid activator and this complex is transported across the cell membrane by a steroid transport protein.

questions.answer_text: Steroid hormones are lipid soluble, so they can readily diffuse through the lipid bilayer of the cell membrane.

questions.stem: Not all intercellular signals require transduction. Which one of the following signals would be processed without transduction?

choices.B: a signal that is weakly bound to a nucleotide
choices.C: a signal that binds to a receptor in the cell membrane
choices.D: a signal that binds to the extracellular matrix

questions.answer_text: a lipid-soluble signal

questions.stem: What does it mean to say that a signal is transduced?

choices.A: The signal enters the cell directly and binds to a receptor inside.
choices.B: The physical form of the signal changes as it passes from the cell membrane to the ultimate intracellular target.
choices.C: The signal is amplified, such that even one signal molecule evokes a large response.
choices.D: The signal triggers a sequence of phosphorylation events inside the cell.

questions.answer_text: The physical form of the signal changes as it passes from the cell membrane to the ultimate intracellular target.

questions.stem: Which of the following processes generally requires protein phosphorylation?

choices.C: activation of G protein-coupled receptors
choices.D: activation ligand-gated ion channels

questions.answer_text: activation of receptor tyrosine kinases

questions.stem: A signal transmitted via phosphorylation of a series of proteins is generally associated with which of the following events?

choices.A: conformational changes to each protein in the series
choices.B: binding of a hormone to an intracellular receptor
choices.C: activation of a ligand-gated ion channel
choices.D: production of ATP in the process of signal transduction

questions.answer_text: conformational changes to each protein in the series

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most plausible explanation for why an animal cell would be unable to reduce the Ca2+ concentration in its cytosol compared with the extracellular fluid?

choices.A: inactivation of calcium-gated ion channels in the cell membrane
choices.B: excessive transport of calcium from the cytosol into the endoplasmic reticulum
choices.C: insufficient ATP levels in the cytosol
choices.D: insufficient levels of protein kinase in the cell

questions.answer_text: insufficient ATP levels in the cytosol

questions.stem: How does the toxin of Vibrio cholerae cause profuse diarrhea?

choices.A: It modifies a G protein involved in regulating salt and water secretion.
choices.B: It modifies adenylyl cyclase and triggers excess formation of cAMP.
choices.C: It signals IP3 to act as a second messenger for the release of calcium.
choices.D: It modifies a ligand-gated ion channel.

questions.answer_text: It modifies a G protein involved in regulating salt and water secretion.

questions.stem: Which of the following results would most likely be an immediate result of a growth factor binding to its receptor?

choices.C: cAMP activity
choices.D: phosphorylase activity

questions.answer_text: protein kinase activity

questions.stem: The activity of adenylyl cyclase is essentially the opposite of which of the following enzymes?

choices.C: phosphodiesterase
choices.D: phosphorylase

questions.answer_text: phosphodiesterase

questions.stem: Caffeine is an inhibitor of phosphodiesterase. Therefore, the cells of a person who has recently consumed coffee would have increased levels of which of the following molecules?

choices.C: adenylyl cyclase
choices.D: activated G proteins

questions.answer_text: cAMP

questions.stem: An inhibitor of which of the following enzymes could be used to block the release of calcium from the endoplasmic reticulum?

choices.C: phospholipase C
choices.D: adenylyl cyclase

questions.answer_text: phospholipase C

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true of signal molecules?

choices.A: When signal molecules first bind to receptor tyrosine kinases, the receptors phosphorylate a number of nearby molecules.
choices.B: In response to some G protein-mediated signals, a special type of lipid molecule associated with the plasma membrane is cleaved to form IP3 and calcium.
choices.C: In most cases, signal molecules interact with the cell at the plasma membrane, enter the cell, and eventually enter the nucleus.
choices.D: Protein kinase A activation is one possible result of signal molecules binding to G protein- coupled receptors.

questions.answer_text: Protein kinase A activation is one possible result of signal molecules binding to G protein- coupled receptors.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct association?

choices.A: kinase activity and the addition of a tyrosine
choices.B: phosphodiesterase activity and the removal of phosphate groups
choices.C: GTPase activity and hydrolysis of GTP to GDP
choices.D: adenylyl cyclase activity and the conversion of cAMP to AMP

questions.answer_text: GTPase activity and hydrolysis of GTP to GDP

questions.stem: Protein kinase is an enzyme that functions in which of the following ways?

choices.B: as a receptor for various signal molecules
choices.C: activates or inactivates other proteins by adding a phosphate group to them
choices.D: activates a G protein

questions.answer_text: activates or inactivates other proteins by adding a phosphate group to them

questions.stem: Viagra causes dilation of blood vessels and increased blood flow to the penis, facilitating erection. Viagra acts by inhibiting which of the following events?

choices.C: dephosphorylation of cGMP
choices.D: formation of cGMP from GTP

questions.answer_text: hydrolysis of cGMP to GMP

questions.stem: Which of the following amino acids are most frequently phosphorylated by protein kinases in the cytoplasm during signal transduction?

choices.C: serine and threonine
choices.D: glycine and glutamic acid

questions.answer_text: serine and threonine

questions.stem: What role do phosphatases play in signal transduction pathways?

choices.A: They transfer a phosphate group from one protein in the pathway to the next molecule in the series.
choices.B: They activate protein kinases by phosphorylation.
choices.C: They amplify the second messenger cAMP.
choices.D: They inactivate protein kinases to turn off signal transduction.

questions.answer_text: They inactivate protein kinases to turn off signal transduction.

questions.stem: If a pharmaceutical company wished to design a drug to maintain low blood sugar levels, one approach might be to design a compound that does which of the following?

choices.A: activates epinephrine receptors in liver cells
choices.B: increases cAMP production in liver cells
choices.C: blocks G protein activity in liver cells
choices.D: increases glycogen phosphorylase activity in liver cells

questions.answer_text: blocks G protein activity in liver cells

questions.stem: If a pharmaceutical company wished to design a drug to maintain low blood sugar levels, one approach might be to design a compound that does which of the following?

choices.A: increases glycogen phosphorylase activity in liver cells
choices.B: activates adenylyl cyclase in liver cells
choices.C: stimulates G protein activity in liver cells
choices.D: increases phosphodiesterase activity in liver cells

questions.answer_text: increases phosphodiesterase activity in liver cells

questions.stem: Consider this pathway: epinephrine → G protein-coupled receptor → G protein → adenylyl cyclase → cAMP The second messenger in this pathway is ________.

choices.C: adenylyl cyclase
choices.D: G protein-coupled receptor

questions.answer_text: cAMP

questions.stem: Sutherland discovered that the signaling molecule epinephrine is responsible for which of the following events?

choices.C: Interacting directly with glycogen phosphorylase.
choices.D: Elevating cytosolic concentrations of cyclic AMP.

questions.answer_text: Elevating cytosolic concentrations of cyclic AMP.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true during a typical cAMP-mediated signal transduction event?

choices.A: The second messenger is the last part of the system to be activated.
choices.B: A hormone activates the second messenger by directly binding to it.
choices.C: The second messenger amplifies the hormonal response by attracting more hormones to the cell being affected.
choices.D: Adenylyl cyclase is activated after the hormone binds to the cell and before phosphorylation of proteins occurs.

questions.answer_text: Adenylyl cyclase is activated after the hormone binds to the cell and before phosphorylation of proteins occurs.

questions.stem: Put the steps of the process of signal transduction in the order they occur. 1. A conformational change in the signal-receptor complex activates an enzyme. 2. Protein kinases are activated. 3. A signal molecule binds to a receptor. 4. Target proteins are phosphorylated. 5. Second messenger molecules are released.
What is a primary function of transcription factors?

choices.A: They regulate the synthesis of DNA in response to a signal.
choices.C: They control gene expression.
choices.D: They regulate the release of calcium from the endoplasmic reticulum.

questions.answer_text: They control gene expression.

questions.stem: At puberty, an adolescent female body changes in both structure and function of several organ systems, primarily under the influence of changing concentrations of estrogen and other steroid hormones. How can one hormone, such as estrogen, mediate so many effects?

choices.A: Estrogen is produced in very large concentration by nearly every tissue of the body.
choices.B: Each cell responds in the same way when steroids bind to the cell surface.
choices.C: Estrogen is kept away from the surface of any cells, not able to bind it at the surface.
choices.D: Estrogen binds to specific receptors inside many kinds of cells, each with different responses.

questions.answer_text: Estrogen binds to specific receptors inside many kinds of cells, each with different responses.

questions.stem: What are scaffolding proteins?

choices.A: microtubule arrays that allow lipid-soluble hormones to get from the cell membrane to the nuclear pores
choices.B: large molecules to which several relay proteins attach to facilitate cascade effects
choices.C: relay proteins that orient receptors and their ligands in appropriate directions to facilitate complex formation
choices.D: proteins that enter the nucleus of a cell to regulate transcription

questions.answer_text: large molecules to which several relay proteins attach to facilitate cascade effects

questions.stem: Phosphorylation cascades involving a series of protein kinases are useful for cellular signal transduction because they ________.

choices.B: always lead to the same cellular response
choices.C: amplify the original signal many times
choices.D: counter the harmful effects of phosphatases

questions.answer_text: amplify the original signal many times

questions.stem: A mutation that knocks out the GTPase activity of a G protein would have what effect on a cell?

choices.A: The concentration of available GTP would decrease.
choices.B: The number of G proteins in the cell would increase.
choices.C: The G protein would be inactivated by a G protein-coupled receptor/signal molecule complex.
choices.D: The G protein would always be active.

questions.answer_text: The G protein would always be active.

questions.stem: Why has C. elegans proven to be a useful model for understanding apoptosis?

choices.A: C. elegans does not naturally use apoptosis, but can be induced to do so in the laboratory.
choices.B: C. elegans undergoes a fixed and easy-to-visualize number of apoptotic events during its normal development.
choices.C: C. elegans has large cells wherein apoptosis is easily observed without the aid of a microscope.
choices.D: As C. elegans ages, its cells die progressively until the whole organism is dead.

questions.answer_text: C. elegans undergoes a fixed and easy-to-visualize number of apoptotic events during its normal development.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes the events of apoptosis?

choices.A: The cell dies, it is lysed, its organelles are phagocytized, and its contents are recycled.
choices.B: The cell's DNA and organelles become fragmented, the cell dies, and it is phagocytized.
choices.C: The cell's DNA and organelles become fragmented, the cell shrinks and forms blebs, and the cell's parts are packaged in vesicles that are digested by specialized cells.
choices.D: The cell's nucleus and organelles are lysed, and then the cell enlarges and bursts.

questions.answer_text: The cell's DNA and organelles become fragmented, the cell shrinks and forms blebs, and the cell's parts are packaged in vesicles that are digested by specialized cells.

questions.stem: If an adult person has a faulty version of the human analog to ced-4 of the nematode, which of the following is most likely to result?

choices.A: activation of a developmental pathway found in the worm but not in humans
choices.B: a form of cancer in which there is insufficient apoptosis
choices.C: formation of molecular pores in the mitochondrial outer membrane
choices.D: excess skin loss

questions.answer_text: a form of cancer in which there is insufficient apoptosis

questions.stem: In the nematode C. elegans, ced-9 prevents apoptosis in a normal cell in which of the following ways?

choices.A: It prevents the caspase activity of ced-3 and ced-4.
choices.B: Ced-9 remains inactive until it is signaled by ced-3 and other caspases.
choices.C: Ced-9 cleaves to produce ced-3 and ced-4.
choices.D: Ced-9 prevents blebbing by its action on the cell membrane.

questions.answer_text: It prevents the caspase activity of ced-3 and ced-4.

questions.stem: In research on aging (both cellular aging and organismal aging), it has been found that aged cells do not progress through the cell cycle as they had previously. Which of the following, if found in cells or organisms as they age, would provide evidence that this is related to cell signaling?

choices.A: Growth factor ligands do not bind as efficiently to receptors.
choices.C: cAMP levels change very frequently.
choices.D: Enzymatic activity declines.

questions.answer_text: Growth factor ligands do not bind as efficiently to receptors.

questions.stem: Which of the following provides the best evidence that cell-signaling pathways evolved early in the history of life?

choices.A: Cell-signaling pathways are seen in "primitive" cells such as bacteria and yeast.
choices.B: Bacteria and yeast cells signal each other in a process called quorum sensing.
choices.C: Signal transduction molecules identified in distantly related organisms are similar.
choices.D: Most signals in all types of cells are received by cell surface receptors.

questions.answer_text: Signal transduction molecules identified in distantly related organisms are similar.

questions.stem: Cells that are infected, damaged, or have reached the end of their functional life span often undergo "programmed cell death." This controlled cell suicide is called apoptosis. Select the appropriate description of this event on a cell's life cycle.

choices.A: Apoptosis is regulated by cell surface receptors that signal when a cell has reached its density-dependent limits.
choices.B: During apoptosis, dying cells leak out their contents, including digestive enzymes that also destroy healthy cells.
choices.C: During apoptosis, cellular agents chop up the DNA and fragment the organelles and other cytoplasmic components of a cell.
choices.D: Each cell organelle has protein signals that initiate the breakdown of the organelle's components, which leads to cell death.

questions.answer_text: During apoptosis, cellular agents chop up the DNA and fragment the organelles and other cytoplasmic components of a cell.

questions.stem: Binding of a signaling molecule to which type of receptor leads directly to a change in the distribution of substances on opposite sides of the membrane?

questions.stem: The activation of receptor tyrosine kinases is characterized by

choices.C: a phosphorylation cascade.
choices.D: GTP hydrolysis.

questions.answer_text: dimerization and phosphorylation.

questions.stem: Lipid-soluble signaling molecules, such as aldosterone, cross the membranes of all cells but affect only target cells because

questions.stem: Protein phosphorylation is commonly involved with all of the following except

questions.stem: In the cells of many eukaryotic species, the nuclear envelope has to disappear to permit which of the following events in the cell cycle?

choices.C: separation of the centrosomes

questions.answer_text: attachment of microtubules to kinetochores

questions.stem: The mitotic spindle plays a critical role in which of the following processes?

choices.A: splitting of the cell (cytokinesis) following mitosis

choices.D: separation of sister chromatids

questions.stem: Metaphase is characterized by ________.

choices.D: separation of sister chromatids

questions.answer_text: alignment of chromosomes on the equator of the cell

questions.stem: In what way do kinetochore microtubules facilitate the process of splitting the centromeres?

choices.A: They use motor proteins to hydrolyze the centromere at specific arginine residues.
choices.B: They create tension by pulling toward opposite poles.
choices.C: They slide past each other like actin microfilaments.
choices.D: They phosphorylate the centromere, thereby changing its conformation.

questions.answer_text: They create tension by pulling toward opposite poles.

questions.stem: Certain cell types normally have several nuclei per cell. How could such multinucleated cells be explained?

choices.A: The cell underwent repeated cytokinesis but no mitosis.
choices.B: The cell underwent repeated mitosis with simultaneous cytokinesis.
choices.C: The cell underwent repeated mitosis, but cytokinesis did not occur.
choices.D: The cell had multiple S phases before it entered mitosis.

questions.answer_text: The cell underwent repeated mitosis, but cytokinesis did not occur.

questions.stem: How is plant cell cytokinesis different from animal cell cytokinesis?

choices.A: The contractile filaments found in plant cells are structures composed of carbohydrates; the cleavage furrow in animal cells is composed of contractile proteins.
choices.B: Plant cells deposit vesicles containing cell wall building blocks on the metaphase plate; animal cells form a cleavage furrow.
choices.C: The structural proteins of plant cells separate the two cells; in animal cells, a cell membrane separates the two daughter cells.
choices.D: Plant cells divide after metaphase but before anaphase; animal cells divide after anaphase.

questions.answer_text: Plant cells deposit vesicles containing cell wall building blocks on the metaphase plate; animal cells form a cleavage furrow.

questions.stem: FtsZ is a bacterial cytoskeletal protein that forms a contractile ring involved in binary fission. Its function is analogous to ________.

choices.A: the cleavage furrow of eukaryotic animal cells
choices.B: the cell plate of eukaryotic plant cells
choices.C: the mitotic spindle of eukaryotic cells
choices.D: the microtubule-organizing center of eukaryotic cells

questions.answer_text: the cleavage furrow of eukaryotic animal cells

questions.stem: At which phase of the cell cycle do centrioles begin to move apart in animal cells?

choices.C: metaphase
choices.D: prophase

questions.answer_text: prophase

Taxol is an anticancer drug extracted from the Pacific yew tree. In animal cells, Taxol prevents microtubule depolymerization. Thus, Taxol stops mitosis by interfering with which of the following structures or processes?

choices.D: chromosome condensation

questions.answer_text: the mitotic spindle

questions.stem: Movement of the chromosomes during anaphase would be most affected by a drug that prevents which of the following events in mitosis and cell division?

questions.stem: Measurements of the amount of DNA per nucleus were taken on a large number of cells from a growing fungus. The measured DNA levels ranged from 3 to 6 picograms per nucleus. In which stage of the cell cycle did the nucleus contain 6 picograms of DNA?

choices.C: G2
choices.D: G0

questions.answer_text: G2

questions.stem: A group of cells is assayed for DNA content immediately following mitosis and is found to have an average of 8 picograms of DNA per nucleus. How many picograms of DNA would be found in a nucleus at prophase of mitosis?
The beginning of anaphase is indicated by which of the following processes?

questions.answer_text: Enzymatic cleavage of cohesin.

questions.stem: During which phase of mitosis do the chromatids become chromosomes?

choices.C: prophase
choices.D: metaphase

questions.stem: A cleavage furrow is ________.

choices.A: a ring of vesicles forming a cell plate

questions.answer_text: a groove in the plasma membrane between daughter nuclei

questions.stem: Use the figure to answer the question below. The unlettered circle at the top of the figure shows a diploid nucleus with four chromosomes that have not yet replicated. questions.stem: Certain unicellular eukaryotes, including diatoms and some yeasts, have mechanisms of nuclear division that may resemble intermediate steps in the evolution of mitosis. Which of the following is a characteristic feature of nuclear division in these organisms?

choices.A: They reproduce by binary fission in their early stages of development and by mitosis when they are mature.
choices.B: They have circular chromosomes that are segregated by a mitotic spindle.
choices.C: Chromosomes are segregated by a mitotic spindle, but the nuclear envelope remains intact during division.
choices.D: Chromosomes are segregated by attachment to the plasma membrane.

questions.answer_text: Chromosomes are segregated by a mitotic spindle, but the nuclear envelope remains intact during division.

questions.stem: Several organisms, primarily protists, have what are called intermediate mitotic organization. What is the most probable hypothesis about these intermediate forms of cell division?

choices.A: They represent a form of cell reproduction that must have evolved completely separately from those of other organisms.
choices.B: They rely on totally different proteins for the processes they undergo.
choices.C: They may be more closely related to plant forms that also have unusual mitosis.
choices.D: They show some but not all of the evolutionary steps toward complete mitosis.

questions.answer_text: They show some but not all of the evolutionary steps toward complete mitosis.

questions.stem: Nucleotides can be radiolabeled before they are incorporated into newly synthesized DNA and, therefore, can be assayed to track their incorporation. choices.A: How many cells are produced by the culture per hour?
choices.B: What is the length of the S phase of the cell cycle?
choices.C: How many picograms of DNA are made per cell cycle?

questions.answer_text: What is the length of the S phase of the cell cycle?

questions.stem: Nucleotides can be radiolabeled before they are incorporated into newly forming DNA and, therefore, can be assayed to track their incorporation. questions.stem: Density-dependent inhibition is explained by which of the following processes?

questions.stem: If a horticulturist breeding gardenias succeeds in having a single plant with a particularly desirable set of traits, which of the following would be her most probable and efficient route to establishing a line of such plants?

questions.stem: Eukaryotic sexual life cycles show tremendous variation. Which of the following characteristics do all sexual life cycles have in common? I. Alternation of generations II. Meiosis III. Fertilization IV. Gametes V. Spores

questions.stem: In a human karyotype, chromosomes are arranged in 23 pairs. If we choose one of these pairs, such as pair 14, which of the following do the two chromosomes of the pair have in common?

choices.A: length and position of the centromere only
choices.B: length, centromere position, and staining pattern only
choices.C: length, centromere position, staining pattern, and traits coded for by their genes
choices.D: They have nothing in common except that they are X-shaped.

questions.answer_text: length, centromere position, staining pattern, and traits coded for by their genes

questions.stem: Which of the life cycles is typical for animals?

choices.C: III only
choices.D: I and III

questions.answer_text: I only

questions.stem: Which of the life cycles is typical for plants and some algae?

choices.C: III only
choices.D: I and III

questions.answer_text: III only

questions.stem: Which of the life cycles is typical for most fungi and some protists?

choices.C: III only
choices.D: I and II

questions.answer_text: II only

questions.stem: In a life cycle such as that shown in part III of the figure above, if the zygote's chromosome number is ten, which of the following statements will be true?

choices.A: The sporophyte's chromosome number per cell is ten and the gametophyte's is five.
choices.B: The sporophyte's chromosome number per cell is five and the gametophyte's is ten.
choices.C: The sporophyte and gametophyte each have ten chromosomes per cell.
choices.D: The sporophyte and gametophyte each have five chromosomes per cell.

questions.answer_text: The sporophyte's chromosome number per cell is ten and the gametophyte's is five.

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics do homologous chromosomes exhibit?

choices.A: They carry information for different traits.
choices.B: They carry information for the same traits.
choices.C: They carry the same alleles.
choices.D: They align on the metaphase plate in meiosis II.

questions.answer_text: They carry information for the same traits.

questions.stem: Many organisms spend most of their life cycle in the diploid state. If meiosis produces haploid cells, how is the diploid number restored for these types of organisms?

choices.B: through the transcription of DNA to RNA
choices.C: by synapsis of the homologous pairs of chromosomes during prophase of meiosis I
choices.D: by fertilization

questions.answer_text: by fertilization

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the human X chromosomes?

choices.A: It is present in every somatic cell of males and females.
choices.B: It is the same size as other chromosomes and has the same number of genes.
choices.C: It carries genes that determine an individual's biological sex.
choices.D: It is referred to as an autosome.

questions.answer_text: It carries genes that determine an individual's biological sex.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes a karyotype?

choices.A: It is a display of all of the cell types in an organism.
choices.B: It is an organized image of a cell's chromosomes.
choices.C: It reveals the appearance of an organism.
choices.D: It is a display of a cell's mitotic stages.

questions.answer_text: It is an organized image of a cell's chromosomes.

questions.stem: If a cell has completed meiosis I and the first cytokinesis, and is just beginning meiosis II, which of the following is an appropriate description of its genetic contents?

choices.A: It has half the amount of DNA as the cell that began meiosis.
choices.B: It has half the chromosomes but twice the DNA of the parent cell.
choices.C: It has one-fourth the DNA and one-half the chromosomes as the parent cell.
choices.D: It is genetically identical to another cell formed from the same meiosis I event.

questions.answer_text: It has half the amount of DNA as the cell that began meiosis.

questions.stem: The somatic cells of a privet shrub each contain a total of 46 chromosomes. How do the chromosomes of this plant differ from the chromosomes of humans, who also have a total of 46?

choices.A: Privet shrub cells cannot reproduce sexually.
choices.B: Privet shrub sex cells have chromosomes that can synapse with human chromosomes in the laboratory.
choices.C: Genes of privet shrub chromosomes are significantly different than those in humans.
choices.D: Privet shrubs must be metabolically more like animals than like other shrubs.

questions.answer_text: Genes of privet shrub chromosomes are significantly different than those in humans.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes the chromosomal makeup of each daughter cell after telophase of meiosis I?

choices.A: The cells are diploid, and the chromosomes are each composed of a single chromatid.
choices.B: The cells are diploid, and the chromosomes are each composed of two chromatids.
choices.C: The cells are haploid, and the chromosomes are each composed of a single chromatid.
choices.D: The cells are haploid, and the chromosomes are each composed of two chromatids.

questions.answer_text: The cells are haploid, and the chromosomes are each composed of two chromatids.

questions.stem: How do cells at the completion of meiosis compare with cells that are in prophase of meiosis I?

choices.A: The cells have half the number of chromosomes and half the amount of DNA.
choices.B: The cells have the same number of chromosomes and half the amount of DNA.
choices.C: The cells have half the number of chromosomes and one-fourth the amount of DNA.
choices.D: The cells have half the amount of cytoplasm and twice the amount of DNA.

questions.answer_text: The cells have half the number of chromosomes and one-fourth the amount of DNA.

questions.stem: Which of the following events happens at the conclusion of meiosis I?

choices.A: Homologous chromosomes of a pair are separated from each other.
choices.B: The chromosome number per cell remains the same.
choices.C: Sister chromatids are separated.
choices.D: Four daughter cells are formed.

questions.answer_text: Homologous chromosomes of a pair are separated from each other.

questions.stem: During which of the following processes do sister chromatids separate from each other?

choices.C: during both mitosis and meiosis I
choices.D: during both mitosis and meiosis II

questions.answer_text: during both mitosis and meiosis II

questions.stem: Which of the following processes occurs in meiosis but not in mitosis?

choices.C: alignment of chromosomes at the equator
choices.D: condensation of chromosomes

questions.answer_text: synapsis of chromosomes

questions.stem: When chiasmata can first be seen in cells using a microscope, which of the following processes has most likely occurred?

choices.C: prophase I
choices.D: the separation of homologs

questions.answer_text: prophase I

questions.stem: Homologous chromosomes are aligned at the equator of the spindle.

choices.C: IV
choices.D: VI

questions.answer_text: II

questions.stem: Centromeres of sister chromatids disjoin and chromatids separate.

choices.C: V
choices.D: VII

questions.answer_text: VII

questions.stem: Which diagram represents anaphase I of meiosis?

choices.C: IV
choices.D: V

questions.answer_text: I

questions.stem: Which diagram represents anaphase II of meiosis?

choices.C: IV
choices.D: V

questions.answer_text: V

questions.stem: Which sample of DNA might be from a cell that stopped the process of cell division in G0 phase of the cell cycle prior to meiosis?

choices.C: III
choices.D: either I or II

questions.answer_text: I

questions.stem: Which sample of DNA might represent an animal cell in the G2 phase of the cell cycle prior to meiosis?

choices.C: III
choices.D: both I and II

questions.answer_text: II

questions.stem: Which sample of DNA might represent a zygote?

choices.C: III
choices.D: either I or II

questions.answer_text: I

questions.stem: A certain female's number 12 chromosomes both have the blue gene and number 19 chromosomes both have the long gene. As cells in her ovaries undergo meiosis, which of the following combinations of genes and chromosomes will her eggs have?

choices.A: either two number 12 chromosomes with blue genes or two with orange genes
choices.B: either two number 19 chromosomes with long genes or two with short genes
choices.C: either one blue or one orange gene in addition to either one long or one short gene
choices.D: one chromosome 12 with one blue gene and one chromosome 19 with one long gene

questions.answer_text: one chromosome 12 with one blue gene and one chromosome 19 with one long gene

questions.stem: If a female of this species has one chromosome 12 with a blue gene and another chromosome 12 with an orange gene, and has both number 19 chromosomes with short genes, which of the following combinations of genes will her eggs have?

choices.C: one half blue short and one half orange short gene eggs
choices.D: three fourths blue short and one fourth orange short gene eggs

questions.answer_text: one half blue short and one half orange short gene eggs

questions.stem: A female with a paternal set of one orange and one long gene chromosome and a maternal set comprised of one blue and one short gene chromosome would be expected to produce which of the following types of eggs after meiosis?

choices.A: All eggs will have maternal types of gene combinations.
choices.B: All eggs will have paternal types of gene combinations.
choices.C: Half the eggs will have maternal and half will have paternal combinations.
choices.D: Each egg has a one-fourth chance of having either blue long, blue short, orange long, or orange short combinations.

questions.answer_text: Each egg has a one-fourth chance of having either blue long, blue short, orange long, or orange short combinations.

questions.stem: Somatic cells of roundworms have four individual chromosomes per cell. How many chromosomes would you expect to find in an ovum from a roundworm?

choices.C: eight
choices.D: a diploid number

questions.answer_text: two

questions.stem: Which of the following processes occur during meiosis but not mitosis?

choices.A: Haploid cells fuse to form diploid cells.
choices.B: Haploid cells multiply into more haploid cells.
choices.C: Diploid cells form haploid cells.
choices.D: A diploid cell combines with a haploid cell.

questions.answer_text: Diploid cells form haploid cells.

questions.stem: During which of the following phases of meiosis do homologous chromosomes separate?

choices.C: mitosis
choices.D: anaphase I

questions.answer_text: anaphase I

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes a major difference between meiosis II and mitosis in a diploid animal?

choices.A: Homologous chromosomes align on the metaphase plate in meiosis II.
choices.B: Sister chromatids separate in mitosis, and homologous chromosomes separate in meiosis II.
choices.C: Meiosis II occurs in a haploid cell, while mitosis occurs in diploid cells.
choices.D: Crossing over of chromosomes takes place in meiosis II.

questions.answer_text: Meiosis II occurs in a haploid cell, while mitosis occurs in diploid cells.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes a major difference between mitosis and meiosis I in a diploid organism?

choices.A: Sister chromatids separate in mitosis, while homologous pairs of chromosomes separate in meiosis I.
choices.B: Sister chromatids separate in mitosis, while homologous pairs of chromosomes separate in meiosis II.
choices.C: DNA replication takes place prior to mitosis, but not before meiosis I.
choices.D: Only meiosis I results in daughter cells that contain identical genetic information.

questions.answer_text: Sister chromatids separate in mitosis, while homologous pairs of chromosomes separate in meiosis I.

questions.stem: Crossing over of chromosomes normally takes place during which of the following processes?

choices.C: mitosis
choices.D: mitosis and meiosis II

questions.answer_text: meiosis I

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes one characteristic of each chromosome in a cell during the entire process of meiosis I?

choices.A: Each chromosome is paired with a homologous chromosome.
choices.B: Each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids joined by a centromere.
choices.C: Each chromosome consists of a single strand of DNA.
choices.D: Each chromosome is joined with its homologous pair to form a synaptonemal complex.

questions.answer_text: Each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids joined by a centromere.

questions.stem: During which of the following processes do homologous pairs of chromosomes align adjacent to one another at the metaphase plate of a cell?

choices.C: telophase II of meiosis
choices.D: metaphase II of meiosis

questions.answer_text: metaphase I of meiosis

questions.stem: During which of the following phases of meiosis do centromeres split and sister chromatids migrate to opposite poles of the cell?

choices.C: anaphase II
choices.D: telophase II

questions.answer_text: anaphase II

questions.stem: During which of the following processes does independent assortment of chromosomes occur?

choices.C: in mitosis and meiosis I
choices.D: in mitosis and meiosis II

questions.answer_text: in meiosis I only

questions.stem: For a species with a haploid number of 23 chromosomes, how many different combinations of maternal and paternal chromosomes are possible for the gametes based on the independent assortment of chromosomes during meiosis?

choices.C: about 1,000
choices.D: about 8 million

questions.answer_text: about 8 million

questions.stem: Independent assortment of chromosomes is a result of which of the following processes?

choices.A: the random way each pair of homologous chromosomes lines up at the metaphase plate during meiosis I
choices.B: the random combinations of eggs and sperm during fertilization
choices.C: the random distribution of the sister chromatids to the two daughter cells during anaphase II
choices.D: the diverse combination of alleles that may be found within any given chromosome

questions.answer_text: the random way each pair of homologous chromosomes lines up at the metaphase plate during meiosis I

questions.stem: Which of the following processes occurs when homologous chromosomes cross over in meiosis I?

choices.A: Two sister chromatids get tangled, resulting in one re-sequencing its DNA.
choices.B: Two sister chromatids exchange identical pieces of DNA.
choices.C: Corresponding segments of non-sister chromatids are exchanged.
choices.D: Maternal alleles are "corrected" to be like paternal alleles and vice versa.

questions.answer_text: Corresponding segments of non-sister chromatids are exchanged.

questions.stem: How does natural selection apply to sexual reproduction as opposed to asexual reproduction?

choices.A: Sexual reproduction results in many new gene combinations, some of which will lead to differential reproduction.
choices.B: Sexual reproduction results in the greatest number of new mutations.
choices.C: Sexual reproduction allows the greatest number of offspring to be produced.
choices.D: Sexual reproduction utilizes far less energy than asexual reproduction.

questions.answer_text: Sexual reproduction results in many new gene combinations, some of which will lead to differential reproduction.

questions.stem: The bulldog ant has a diploid number of two chromosomes. Therefore, following meiosis, each daughter cell will have a single chromosome. In addition to mutations, how might genetic diversity be generated in this species?

choices.C: crossing over and random fertilization
choices.D: nothing else

questions.answer_text: crossing over and random fertilization

questions.stem: Which of the following processes facilitates the fastest way for organisms to adapt to a changing environment?

choices.C: sexual reproduction
choices.D: mitosis

questions.answer_text: sexual reproduction

questions.stem: Imagine that there are 25 different species of protists living in a tide pool. Some of these species reproduce both sexually and asexually, and some of them can reproduce only asexually. The pool gradually becomes infested with disease-causing viruses and bacteria. Which species are more likely to thrive in the changing environment?

choices.A: The sexually reproducing species is likely to thrive.
choices.B: The asexually reproducing species is likely to thrive.
choices.C: Sexually and asexually reproducing species are equally likely to thrive.
choices.D: Neither species will be able to thrive.

questions.answer_text: The sexually reproducing species is likely to thrive.

questions.stem: In eukaryotes, genetic information is passed to the next generation by processes that include mitosis or meiosis. Which of the following explanations correctly identifies the process and supports the claim that heritable information is passed from one generation to another?

choices.A: During mitosis, DNA replication occurs twice within the cell cycle to insure a full set of chromosomes within each of the daughter cells produced.
choices.B: Mitosis, followed by cytokinesis, produces daughter cells that are genetically different from the parent cell, thus insuring variation within the population.
choices.C: In asexual reproduction, a single individual is the sole parent and passes copies of its genes to its offspring without the fusion of gametes.
choices.D: Single-celled organisms can fuse their cells, reproducing asexually through mitosis to form new cells that are not identical to the parent cell.

questions.answer_text: In asexual reproduction, a single individual is the sole parent and passes copies of its genes to its offspring without the fusion of gametes.

questions.stem: Genetic variation leads to genetic diversity in populations and is the raw material for evolution.
