Biological systems have multiple processes, such as reproduction, that affect genetic variation. They are evolutionarily conserved and shared by various organisms. Which of the following statements best represents the connection between reproduction and evolution?

choices.A: Plants that use sexual reproduction are rare since this type of reproduction in plants does not contribute to genetic diversity.
choices.B: In order to increase genetic diversity for evolution in sexually reproducing organisms, mutations must occur in the zygote after fertilization.
choices.C: Since prokaryotic organisms reproduce asexually, there is no mechanism for them to add genetic diversity for evolution.
choices.D: Sexual reproduction increases genetic variation because random mutations can be shuffled between organisms.

questions.answer_text: Sexual reproduction increases genetic variation because random mutations can be shuffled between organisms.

questions.stem: A human cell containing 22 autosomes and a Y chromosome is

choices.C: a zygote.
choices.D: a somatic cell of a male.

questions.answer_text: a sperm.

questions.stem: The two homologs of a pair move toward opposite poles of dividing cell during

choices.C: meiosis II.
choices.D: fertilization.

questions.answer_text: meiosis I.

questions.stem: Meiosis II is similar to mitosis in that

choices.C: the daughter cells are diploid.
choices.D: homologous chromosomes synapse.

questions.answer_text: sister chromatids separate during anaphase.

questions.stem: If the DNA content of a diploid cell in the G1 phase of the cell cycle is x, then the DNA content of the same cell at metaphase of meiosis I will be

choices.C: x.

questions.stem: If we continue to follow the cell lineage from question 4, then the DNA content of a single cell at metaphase of meiosis II will be

choices.C: x.

questions.answer_text: x.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct in describing the terms monohybrid cross and dihybrid cross?

choices.A: A monohybrid cross involves a single parent, whereas a dihybrid cross involves two parents.
choices.B: A dihybrid cross involves organisms that are heterozygous for two characters that are being studied, and a monohybrid cross involves organisms that are heterozygous for only one character being studied.
choices.C: A monohybrid cross is performed for one generation, whereas a dihybrid cross is performed for two generations.
choices.D: A monohybrid cross results in a 9:3:3:1 ratio, whereas a dihybrid cross gives a 3:1 ratio.

questions.answer_text: A dihybrid cross involves organisms that are heterozygous for two characters that are being studied, and a monohybrid cross involves organisms that are heterozygous for only one character being studied.

questions.stem: What was the most significant conclusion that Gregor Mendel drew from his experiments with pea plants?

choices.A: There is considerable genetic variation in garden peas.
choices.B: Traits are inherited in discrete units and are not the result of "blending."
choices.C: Recessive genes occur more frequently in the F1 generation than do dominant ones.
choices.D: Genes are composed of DNA.

questions.answer_text: Traits are inherited in discrete units and are not the result of "blending."

questions.stem: How many unique gametes could be produced through independent assortment by an individual with the genotype AaBbCCDdEE?
The individual with genotype AaBbCCDdEE can make many kinds of gametes. Which of the following correctly describes why this situation is possible?

choices.B: crossing over during prophase I leads to genetic variety
choices.C: different possible assortment of chromosomes into gametes occurs
choices.D: there is a tendency for dominant alleles to segregate together

questions.answer_text: different possible assortment of chromosomes into gametes occurs

questions.stem: Mendel continued some of his experiments into the F2 or F3 generation in order to ________.

choices.A: obtain a larger number of offspring on which to base statistics
choices.B: observe whether or not a recessive trait would reappear
choices.C: observe whether or not the dominant trait would reappear
choices.D: distinguish which alleles were segregating

questions.answer_text: observe whether or not a recessive trait would reappear

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about independent assortment or segregation is correct?

choices.A: The law of independent assortment describes the behavior of two or more genes relative to one another.
choices.B: The law of segregation describes the behavior of two or more genes relative to one another.
choices.C: The law of independent assortment is accounted for by observations of prophase I of meiosis.
choices.D: The law of segregation is accounted for by anaphase of mitosis.

questions.answer_text: The law of independent assortment describes the behavior of two or more genes relative to one another.

questions.stem: A sexually reproducing animal has two unlinked genes, one for head shape (H) and one for tail length (T). Its genotype is HhTt. Which of the following genotypes is possible in a gamete from this organism?

choices.C: T
choices.D: HT

questions.answer_text: HT

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes how Mendel accounted for the observation that traits had disappeared in the F1 generation and then reappeared in the F2 generation?

choices.A: New mutations were frequently generated in the F2 progeny, causing traits that had been lost in the F1 to reappear in the F2.
choices.B: The mechanism controlling the appearance of traits was different between the F1 and the F2 plants.
choices.C: Traits can be dominant or recessive, and the recessive traits were "hidden" by the dominant ones in the F1.
choices.D: Members of the F1 generation had only one allele for each trait, but members of the F2 had two alleles for each trait.

questions.answer_text: Traits can be dominant or recessive, and the recessive traits were "hidden" by the dominant ones in the F1.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly explains the fact that all seven of the pea plant traits studied by Mendel obeyed the principle of independent assortment?

choices.A: None of the traits obeyed the law of segregation.
choices.B: The diploid number of chromosomes in the pea plants was seven.
choices.C: All of the genes controlling the traits were located on the same chromosome.
choices.D: All of the genes controlling the traits behaved as if they were on different chromosomes.

questions.answer_text: All of the genes controlling the traits behaved as if they were on different chromosomes.

questions.stem: Mendel's observation of the segregation of alleles in gamete formation has its basis in which of the following phases of cell division?

choices.C: metaphase II of meiosis
choices.D: anaphase I of meiosis

questions.answer_text: anaphase I of meiosis

questions.stem: Mendel's law of independent assortment has its basis in which of the following events of meiosis I?

choices.B: crossing over of homologous pairs of chromosomes
choices.C: alignment of pairs of homologous chromosomes along the middle of the cell
choices.D: the division of cells at telophase

questions.answer_text: alignment of pairs of homologous chromosomes along the middle of the cell

questions.stem: Use the figure and the following description to answer the question. In a particular plant, leaf color is controlled by gene locus D. Plants with at least one allele D have dark green leaves, and plants with the homozygous recessive dd genotype have light green leaves. A true-breeding, dark-leaved plant is crossed with a light-leaved one, and the F1 offspring is allowed to self-pollinate. The predicted outcome of the F2 is diagrammed in the Punnett square shown in the figure, where 1, 2, 3, and 4 represent the genotypes corresponding to each box within the square. Which of the boxes marked 1-4 correspond to plants with dark leaves?

choices.C: 4 only

questions.stem: Use the figure and the following description to answer the question. In a particular plant, leaf color is controlled by gene locus D. Plants with at least one allele D have dark green leaves, and plants with the homozygous recessive dd genotype have light green leaves. A true-breeding, dark-leaved plant is crossed with a light-leaved one, and the F1 offspring is allowed to self-pollinate. The predicted outcome of the F2 is diagrammed in the Punnett square shown in the figure, where 1, 2, 3, and 4 represent the genotypes corresponding to each box within the square. Which of the boxes marked 1-4 correspond to plants with a heterozygous genotype?

choices.C: 2 and 3

questions.answer_text: 2 and 3

questions.stem: Use the figure and the following description to answer the question. In a particular plant, leaf color is controlled by gene locus D. Plants with at least one allele D have dark green leaves, and plants with the homozygous recessive dd genotype have light green leaves. A true-breeding, dark-leaved plant is crossed with a light-leaved one, and the F1 offspring is allowed to self-pollinate. The predicted outcome of the F2 is diagrammed in the Punnett square shown in the figure, where 1, 2, 3, and 4 represent the genotypes corresponding to each box within the square. Which of the boxes marked 1-4 correspond to plants that will be true-breeding?

choices.D: 1 only

questions.answer_text: 1 and 4 only

questions.stem: Skin color in a certain species of fish is inherited by a single gene with four different alleles. How many different types of gametes would be possible in this organism?
Why did all of the F1 offspring of Mendel's classic pea cross always look like one of the two parental varieties?

choices.A: No genes interacted to produce the parental phenotype.
choices.C: The traits blended together during fertilization.
choices.D: One allele was dominant.

questions.answer_text: One allele was dominant.

questions.stem: Mendel crossed yellow-seeded and green-seeded pea plants and then allowed the offspring to self-pollinate to produce an F2 generation. The results were as follows: 6,022 yellow and 2,001 green (8,023 total). Which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship of the allele for green seeds to the allele for yellow seeds?

choices.A: The green allele is dominant to the yellow allele.
choices.B: The two alleles exhibit incomplete dominance.
choices.C: The green allele is recessive to the yellow allele.
choices.D: The two alleles are codominant.

questions.answer_text: The green allele is recessive to the yellow allele.

questions.stem: Albinism is a recessive trait. A man and woman both show normal pigmentation, but both have one parent who has albinism (without melanin pigmentation). What is the probability that their first child will have albinism?

Albinism is a recessive trait. A man and woman who both have normal pigmentation have one child out of three who has albinism (without melanin pigmentation). What are the genotypes of this child's parents?

choices.A: One parent must be homozygous for the recessive allele; the other parent can be homozygous dominant, homozygous recessive, or heterozygous.
choices.B: One parent must be heterozygous; the other parent can be homozygous dominant, homozygous recessive, or heterozygous.
choices.C: Both parents must be heterozygous.
choices.D: One parent must be homozygous dominant; the other parent must be heterozygous.

questions.answer_text: Both parents must be heterozygous.

questions.stem: A black guinea pig crossed with a guinea pig with albinism produced 12 black offspring. When the albino was crossed with a second black animal, six blacks and six albinos were obtained. What is the best explanation for this genetic situation?

choices.A: Albinism is a recessive trait; black is a dominant trait.
choices.B: Albinism is a dominant trait; black is incompletely dominant.
choices.C: Albinism and black are codominant.
choices.D: Albinism is a recessive trait; black is codominant.

questions.answer_text: Albinism is a recessive trait; black is a dominant trait.

questions.stem: Gray seed color in peas is dominant to white. Assume that Mendel conducted a series of experiments where plants with gray seeds were crossed among themselves, and the following progeny were produced: 302 gray and 98 white. What is the most probable genotype of each parent?

choices.C: GG × Gg
choices.D: gg × Gg

questions.answer_text: Gg × Gg

questions.stem: When Mendel crossed yellow-seeded and green-seeded pea plants, all the offspring were yellow-seeded. When he took these F1 yellow-seeded plants and crossed them to green-seeded plants, what genotypic ratio was expected?

Black fur in mice (B) is dominant to brown fur (b). Short tails (T) are dominant to long tails (t). What fraction of the progeny of crosses BbTt × BBtt will be expected to have black fur and long tails?

In pea plants, the tall phenotype is dominant to the dwarf phenotype. If a heterozygous pea plant is crossed with a homozygous tall pea plant, what is the probability that the offspring will be dwarf in size?
What is the probability of producing the genotype AABBCC in a cross of individuals who both possess this genotype: AaBbCc?

Given the following genotypes for two parents, AABBCc × AabbCc, assume that all traits exhibit simple dominance and independent assortment. What proportion of the progeny of this cross will be expected to phenotypically resemble the first parent with the genotype AABBCc?
Which of the following statements best describes the addition rule of probability?

choices.A: the probability that two or more independent events will occur simultaneously
choices.B: the probability that either one of two independent events will occur
choices.C: the probability of producing two or more heterozygous offspring
choices.D: the likelihood that a trait is due to two or more meiotic events

questions.answer_text: the probability that either one of two independent events will occur

questions.stem: Which of the following calculations require the use of the addition rule of probability?

choices.A: Calculate the probability of black offspring from the cross AaBb × AaBb, where B is the symbol for black.
choices.B: Calculate the probability of children with both cystic fibrosis and polydactyly when parents are each heterozygous for both genes.
choices.C: Calculate the probability of each of four children having cystic fibrosis if the parents are both heterozygous.
choices.D: Calculate the probability of a child having either sickle-cell anemia or cystic fibrosis if parents are each heterozygous for both.

questions.answer_text: Calculate the probability of a child having either sickle-cell anemia or cystic fibrosis if parents are each heterozygous for both.

questions.stem: Two true-breeding stocks of pea plants are crossed. One parent has red, axial flowers, and the other has white, terminal flowers; all F1 individuals have red, axial flowers. The genes for flower color and location assort independently. Among the F2 offspring, what is the probability of producing plants with white axial flowers?

A man has extra digits (six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot). His wife and their daughter have the normal number of digits (five fingers on each hand and five toes on each foot.) Having extra digits is a dominant trait. The couple's second child has extra digits. What is the probability that their next (third) child will have extra digits?

Phenylketonuria is an inherited disease caused by a recessive autosomal allele. If a woman and her husband are both carriers, what is the probability that their first child will be a phenotypically normal girl?
Assuming independent assortment for all gene pairs, what is the probability that a cross between the following parents, AABbCc × AaBbCc, will produce an AaBbCc offspring?
Suppose two individuals with the genotype AaBbCc are mated. Assuming that the genes are not linked, what fraction of the offspring are expected to be homozygous recessive for the three traits?

In cattle, roan coat color (mixed red and white hairs) occurs in the heterozygous (CRCW) offspring of red (CRCR) and white (CWCW) homozygotes. Which of the following crosses would produce offspring in the ratio of 1 red:2 roan:1 white?

choices.C: white × roan
choices.D: red × roan

questions.answer_text: roan × roan

questions.stem: Which of the following inheritance patterns describes the ability of a single allele to have multiple phenotypic effects?

choices.C: pleiotropy
choices.D: epistasis

questions.answer_text: pleiotropy

questions.stem: Which of the following phenotypes is an example of polygenic inheritance?

choices.B: the ABO blood group in humans
choices.C: white and purple flower color in peas
choices.D: skin pigmentation in humans

questions.answer_text: skin pigmentation in humans

questions.stem: Hydrangea plants of the same genotype are planted in a large flower garden. Some of the plants produce blue flowers and others pink flowers. This can be best explained by which of the following?

choices.A: the knowledge that multiple alleles are involved
choices.B: the allele for blue hydrangea is completely dominant over the allele for pink hydrangea
choices.C: the alleles are codominant
choices.D: environmental factors such as soil pH affect the phenotype

questions.answer_text: environmental factors such as soil pH affect the phenotype

questions.stem: Which of the following scenarios describes an example of epistasis?

choices.A: Recessive genotypes for each of two genes (aabb) results in an albino corn snake.
choices.B: In rabbits and many other mammals, one genotype (ee) prevents any fur color from developing.
choices.C: In Drosophila (fruit flies), white eyes can be due to an X-linked gene or to a combination of other genes.
choices.D: In cacti, there are several genes for the type of spines.

questions.answer_text: In rabbits and many other mammals, one genotype (ee) prevents any fur color from developing.

questions.stem: Radish flowers may be red, purple, or white. A cross between a red-flowered plant and a white-flowered plant yields all-purple offspring. The part of the radish we eat may be oval or long, with long being the dominant trait. If true-breeding red long radishes are crossed with true- breeding white oval radishes, the F1 will be expected to exhibit which of the following phenotypes?

choices.C: purple and long
choices.D: purple and oval

questions.answer_text: purple and long

questions.stem: Radish flowers may be red, purple, or white. A cross between a red-flowered plant and a white-flowered plant yields all-purple offspring. The flower color trait in radishes is an example of which of the following inheritance patterns?

choices.C: codominance
choices.D: incomplete dominance

questions.answer_text: incomplete dominance

questions.stem: Skin color in a certain species of fish is inherited via a single gene with four different alleles. One fish of this type has alleles 1 and 3 (S1S3), and its mate has alleles 2 and 4 (S2S4). If each allele confers a unit of color darkness such that S1 has one unit, S2 has two units, and so on, then what proportion of their offspring would be expected to have five units of color?

Gene S controls the sharpness of spines in a type of cactus. Cacti with the dominant allele, S, have sharp spines, whereas homozygous recessive ss cacti have dull spines. At the same time, a second gene, N, determines whether or not cacti have spines. Homozygous recessive nn cacti have no spines at all. The relationship between genes S and N is an example of which of the following inheritance patterns?

choices.C: pleiotropy
choices.D: codominance

questions.answer_text: epistasis

questions.stem: Gene S controls the sharpness of spines in a type of cactus. Cacti with the dominant allele, S, have sharp spines, whereas homozygous recessive ss cacti have dull spines. At the same time, a second gene, N, determines whether or not cactuses have spines. Homozygous recessive nn cactuses have no spines at all. A cross between a true-breeding sharp-spined cactus and a spineless cactus would produce ________.

choices.C: 25% sharp-spined, 50% dull-spined, 25% spineless progeny
choices.D: It is impossible to determine the phenotypes of the progeny.

questions.answer_text: all sharp-spined progeny

questions.stem: Gene S controls the sharpness of spines in a type of cactus. Cacti with the dominant allele, S, have sharp spines, whereas homozygous recessive ss cacti have dull spines. At the same time, a second gene, N, determines whether or not cacti have spines. Homozygous recessive nn cacti have no spines at all. If cacti heterozygous for both traits, SsNn, were allowed to self-pollinate, the offspring would segregate into which of the following phenotype ratios?

choices.C: 1 sharp-spined:1 dull-spined:1 spineless
choices.D: 9 sharp-spined:3 dull-spined:4 spineless

questions.answer_text: 9 sharp-spined:3 dull-spined:4 spineless

questions.stem: Feather color in budgies is determined by two different genes: Y for pigment on the outside of the feather, and B for pigment on the inside of the feather. YYBB, YyBB, or YYBb is green; yyBB or yyBb is blue; YYbb or Yybb is yellow; and yybb is white. A blue budgie is crossed with a white budgie. Which of the following results in the offspring is most possible?

choices.C: blue offspring only
choices.D: blue and white offspring

questions.answer_text: blue and white offspring

questions.stem: Feather color in budgies is determined by two different genes, Y for pigment on the outside of the feather, and B for pigment on the inside of the feather. YYBB, YyBB, or YYBb is green; yyBB or yyBb is blue; YYbb or Yybb is yellow; and yybb is white. Two blue budgies were crossed. Over the years, they produced 22 offspring, five of which were white. What are the most likely genotypes for the two blue budgies?

choices.C: yyBb and yyBb
choices.D: yyBb and yybb

questions.answer_text: yyBb and yyBb

questions.stem: In human blood types, Rh positive is a trait that shows simple dominance over Rh negative. A woman who has blood type A positive has a daughter who is type O positive and a son who is type B negative. Which of the following phenotypes is possible for the father?

choices.C: B positive
choices.D: AB negative

questions.answer_text: B positive

questions.stem: A gene for the MN blood group has codominant alleles M and N. If both children in a family are of blood type M, which of the following situations is possible?

choices.A: Each parent is either M or MN.
choices.B: Each parent must be type M.
choices.C: Both children are heterozygous for this gene.
choices.D: Neither parent can have the N allele.

questions.answer_text: Each parent is either M or MN.

questions.stem: Marfan syndrome in humans is caused by an abnormality of the connective tissue protein fibrillin. Patients are usually very tall and thin, with long spindly fingers, curvature of the spine, sometimes weakened arterial walls, and sometimes eye problems, such as lens dislocation. Which of the following would you conclude about Marfan syndrome from this information?

choices.C: It is pleiotropic.
choices.D: It is epistatic.

questions.answer_text: It is pleiotropic.

questions.stem: In rabbits, the homozygous genotype LCLC has normal legs, LCLc results in deformed legs, and LcLc results in very short legs. The genotype FBFB produces black fur, FBFb brown fur, and FbFb white fur. If a cross is made between brown rabbits with deformed legs and white rabbits with deformed legs, what percentage of the offspring would be expected to have deformed legs and white fur?

In humans, ABO blood types refer to glycoproteins in the membranes of red blood cells. There are three alleles for this autosomal gene: IA, IB, and i. The IA allele codes for the A glycoprotein, The IB allele codes for the B glycoprotein, and the i allele doesn't code for any membrane glycoprotein. IA and IB are codominant, and i is recessive to both IA and IB. People with type A blood have the genotypes IAIA or IAi, people with type B blood are IBIB or IBi, people with type AB blood are IAIB, and people with type O blood are ii. If a woman with type AB blood marries a man with type O blood, which of the following blood types could their children possibly have?

choices.C: A, B, and O
choices.D: A, B, AB, and O

questions.answer_text: A and B

questions.stem: An obstetrician knows that one of her patients is a pregnant woman whose fetus is at risk for a serious disorder that is detectable biochemically in fetal cells. The obstetrician would most reasonably offer which of the following procedures to her patient?

choices.A: karyotyping of the woman's somatic cells
choices.C: amniocentesis or CVS
choices.D: blood transfusion

questions.answer_text: amniocentesis or CVS

questions.stem: In some parts of Africa, the frequency of heterozygosity for the sickle-cell anemia allele is unusually high, presumably because this reduces the frequency of malaria. Such a relationship is related to which of the following?

choices.C: Darwin's explanation of natural selection
choices.D: the malarial parasite changing the allele

questions.answer_text: Darwin's explanation of natural selection

questions.stem: Phenylketonuria (PKU) is a recessive human disorder in which an individual cannot appropriately metabolize the amino acid phenylalanine. This amino acid is not naturally produced by humans. Which of the following treatments would be most effective for people with PKU?

choices.A: Feed them the substrate that can be metabolized into phenylalanine.
choices.B: Regulate the diet of the affected persons to severely limit the uptake of phenylalanine.
choices.C: Feed the patients the missing enzymes in a regular cycle, such as twice per week.
choices.D: Feed the patients an excess of the missing product.

questions.answer_text: Regulate the diet of the affected persons to severely limit the uptake of phenylalanine.

questions.stem: Hutchinson-Gilford progeria is an exceedingly rare human genetic disorder in which there is very early senility and death, usually from coronary artery disease, at an average age of 13 years. Patients, who look very old even as children, do not live to reproduce. Which of the following statements represents the most likely assumption regarding this disorder?

choices.B: The disorder will increase in frequency in successive generations within a family.
choices.C: The disorder may be due to mutation in a single protein-coding gene.
choices.D: Each patient will have had at least one affected grandparent or parent.

questions.answer_text: The disorder may be due to mutation in a single protein-coding gene.

questions.stem: One of two major forms of a human condition called neurofibromatosis (NF1) is inherited as a dominant gene, although it may range from mildly to very severely expressed. Which of the following is the best explanation for why a young, affected child is the first in her family to be diagnosed?

choices.A: The mother carries the gene but does not express it.
choices.B: One of the parents has a mild expression of the gene.
choices.C: The condition skipped a generation in the family.
choices.D: The child has one more chromosome than either of the parents.

questions.answer_text: One of the parents has a mild expression of the gene.

questions.stem: The following question refers to the pedigree chart in the figure for a family, some of whose members exhibit the dominant trait, W. Affected individuals are indicated by a dark square or circle. What is the genotype of individual II-5?

choices.C: ww
choices.D: ww or Ww

questions.answer_text: ww

questions.stem: The following question refers to the pedigree chart in the figure for a family, some of whose members exhibit the dominant trait, W. Affected individuals are indicated by a dark square or circle. What is the likelihood that the offspring of IV-3 and IV-4 will have the trait?

The following question refers to the pedigree chart in the figure for a family, some of whose members exhibit the dominant trait, W. Affected individuals are indicated by a dark square or circle. What is the probability that individual III-1 is Ww?

The figure shows the pedigree for a family. Dark-shaded symbols represent individuals with one of the two major types of colon cancer. Numbers under the symbols are the individual's age at the time of diagnosis. Males are represented by squares, females by circles. From this pedigree, this trait seems to be inherited ________.

choices.C: as a result of epistasis
choices.D: as an autosomal dominant

questions.answer_text: as an autosomal dominant

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is a correct explanation for the observation that all offspring exhibit a phenotype for a particular trait that appears to be a blend of the two parental varieties?

choices.A: Neither of the parental genes is dominant over the other.
choices.B: The genes for the trait are dominant in both of the parents.
choices.C: The genes are linked and do not separate during meiosis.
choices.D: The genes for the trait are recessive in both of the parents.

questions.answer_text: Neither of the parental genes is dominant over the other.

questions.stem: The pattern of inheritance can be predicted from data if one is given the parent or offspring genotypes or phenotypes. Two organisms, with genotypes BbDD and BBDd, are mated. Assuming independent assortment of the B/b and D/d genes, determine the genotypic ratios in offspring that would occur.

choices.C: 9/16 BBDD, 3/16 BbDD, 3/16 BBDd, 1/16 bbdd
choices.D: 1/4 BBDD, 1/2 BbDd, 1/4 bbdd

questions.answer_text: 1/4 BBDD, 1/4 BbDD, 1/4 BBDd, 1/4 BbDd

questions.stem: When Thomas Hunt Morgan crossed his red-eyed F1 generation flies to each other, the F2 generation included both red- and white-eyed flies. Remarkably, all the white-eyed flies were male. What was the explanation for this result?

choices.A: The gene involved is located on the Y chromosome.
choices.B: The gene involved is located on the X chromosome.
choices.C: The gene involved is located on an autosome, but only in males.
choices.D: Other male-specific factors influence eye color in flies.

questions.answer_text: The gene involved is located on the X chromosome.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes the meaning of the chromosome theory of inheritance as expressed in the early 20th century?

choices.A: Individuals inherit particular chromosomes attached to genes.
choices.B: Mendelian genes are at specific loci on the chromosome and, in turn, segregate during meiosis.
choices.C: No more than a single pair of chromosomes can be found in a healthy normal cell.
choices.D: Natural selection acts on certain chromosome combinations rather than on genes.

questions.answer_text: Mendelian genes are at specific loci on the chromosome and, in turn, segregate during meiosis.

questions.stem: Why are males more often affected by sex-linked traits than females?

choices.A: Male hormones such as testosterone often alter the effects of mutations on the X chromosome.
choices.B: Female hormones such as estrogen often compensate for the effects of mutations on the X chromosome.
choices.C: X chromosomes in males generally have more mutations than X chromosomes in females.
choices.D: Males are hemizygous for the X chromosome.

questions.answer_text: Males are hemizygous for the X chromosome.

questions.stem: The SRY gene is best described as ________.

choices.A: a gene present on the X chromosome that triggers female development
choices.B: an autosomal gene that is required for the expression of genes on the Y chromosome
choices.C: a gene present on the Y chromosome that triggers male development
choices.D: an autosomal gene that is required for the expression of genes on the X chromosome

questions.answer_text: a gene present on the Y chromosome that triggers male development

questions.stem: In cats, black fur color is determined by an X-linked allele; the other allele at this locus determines orange color. The heterozygote is tortoiseshell. What kinds of offspring would you expect from the cross of a black female and an orange male?

choices.C: tortoiseshell females; black males
choices.D: orange females; black males

questions.answer_text: tortoiseshell females; black males

questions.stem: Red-green color blindness is a sex-linked recessive trait in humans. Two people with normal color vision have a color-blind son. What are the genotypes of the parents?

choices.C: XNXN and XNY
choices.D: XNXn and XNY

questions.answer_text: XNXn and XNY

questions.stem: Cinnabar eye color is a sex-linked, recessive characteristic in fruit flies. If a female having cinnabar eyes is crossed with a wild-type male, what percentage of the F1 males will have cinnabar eyes?
Generally, only female cats have the tortoiseshell phenotype for fur color. Which of the following statements explains this phenomenon?

choices.A: A male inherits only one allele of the X-linked gene controlling hair color.
choices.B: The Y chromosome has a gene blocking orange coloration.
choices.C: Only males can have Barr bodies.
choices.D: Multiple crossovers on the Y chromosome prevent orange pigment production.

questions.answer_text: A male inherits only one allele of the X-linked gene controlling hair color.

questions.stem: In birds, sex is determined by a ZW chromosome scheme. Males are ZZ and females are ZW. A recessive lethal allele that causes death of the embryo is sometimes present on the Z chromosome in pigeons. What would be the sex ratio in the offspring of a cross between a male that is heterozygous for the lethal allele and a normal female?

choices.C: 1:1 male to female
choices.D: 3:1 male to female

questions.answer_text: 2:1 male to female

questions.stem: Sex determination in mammals is due to the SRY gene found on the Y chromosome. Which of the following situations could allow a person with an XX karyotype to develop a male phenotype?

choices.A: the loss of the SRY gene from an autosome
choices.B: translocation of SRY to an X chromosome
choices.C: the presence of an extra autosomal chromosome
choices.D: the presence of one normal and one shortened (deleted) X

questions.answer_text: translocation of SRY to an X chromosome

questions.stem: In humans, clear gender differentiation occurs not at fertilization, but after the second month of gestation. Which of the following statements describes the first event of this differentiation?

choices.A: formation of testosterone in male embryos
choices.B: formation of estrogens in female embryos
choices.C: activation of SRY in male embryos and masculinization of the gonads
choices.D: activation of SRY in females and feminization of the gonads

questions.answer_text: activation of SRY in male embryos and masculinization of the gonads

questions.stem: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is a serious condition caused by a recessive allele of a gene on the human X chromosome. The patients have muscles that weaken over time because they have absent or decreased dystrophin, a muscle protein. They rarely live past their 20s. How likely is it for a woman to have this condition?

choices.A: Women can never have this condition.
choices.B: One-fourth of the daughters of an affected man would have this condition.
choices.C: One-half of the daughters of an affected father and a carrier mother could have this condition.
choices.D: Only if a woman is XXX could she have this condition.

questions.answer_text: One-half of the daughters of an affected father and a carrier mother could have this condition.

questions.stem: All female mammals have one active X chromosome per cell instead of two. What causes this to happen?

choices.A: activation of the XIST gene on the X chromosome that will become the Barr body
choices.B: activation of the BARR gene on one X chromosome, which then becomes inactive
choices.C: inactivation of the XIST gene on the X chromosome derived from the male parent
choices.D: attachment of methyl (-CH3) groups to the X chromosome that will remain active

questions.answer_text: activation of the XIST gene on the X chromosome that will become the Barr body

questions.stem: A man who is a dwarf with achondroplasia and normal vision marries a color-blind woman of normal height. The man's father was six feet tall, and both the woman's parents were of average height. Dwarfism caused by achondroplasia is autosomal dominant, and red-green color blindness is X-linked recessive. How many of their daughters might be expected to be color- blind with achondroplasia?

choices.C: one out of four
choices.D: three out of four

questions.answer_text: none

questions.stem: A man who is a dwarf with achondroplasia and normal vision marries a color-blind woman of normal height. The man's father was six feet tall, and both the woman's parents were of average height. Dwarfism caused by achondroplasia is autosomal dominant, and red-green color blindness is X-linked recessive. What proportion of their sons would be color blind and of normal height?

choices.C: one out of four
choices.D: all

questions.answer_text: half

questions.stem: Pseudohypertrophic muscular dystrophy is a human disorder that causes gradual deterioration of the muscles. Only boys are affected, and they are always born to phenotypically normal parents. Due to the severity of the disease, the boys die in their teens. Is this disorder likely to be caused by a dominant or recessive allele? Is the inheritance of this trait sex-linked or autosomal?

choices.C: recessive, sex-linked
choices.D: incomplete dominant, sex-linked

questions.answer_text: recessive, sex-linked

questions.stem: A recessive allele on the X chromosome is responsible for red-green color blindness in humans. A woman with normal vision whose father is color blind marries a color-blind male. What is the probability that this couple's first son will be color blind?
Which of the following individuals will inherit an X-linked allele from a man who carries it?

choices.C: all of his sons
choices.D: all of his children

questions.answer_text: all of his daughters

questions.stem: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency (G6PD) is inherited as an X-linked recessive allele in humans. A woman whose father suffered from G6PD marries a normal man. What proportion of their sons is expected to be G6PD?

choices.D: zero

questions.stem: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency (G6PD) is inherited as an X-linked recessive allele in humans. A woman whose father suffered from G6PD marries a man who has the disease. What proportion of their sons would have the disease?

choices.D: zero

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. In a Drosophila experiment, a cross was made between homozygous wild-type females and yellow-bodied males. All of the resulting F1s were phenotypically wild type. However, adult flies of the F2 generation (resulting from matings of the F1s) had the characteristics shown in the figure. How is the mutant allele for yellow body inherited?

choices.C: It is dominant.
choices.D: It is incompletely dominant.

questions.answer_text: It is recessive.

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. In a Drosophila experiment, a cross was made between homozygous wild-type females and yellow-bodied males. All of the resulting F1s were phenotypically wild type. However, adult flies of the F2 generation (resulting from matings of the F1s) had the characteristics shown in the figure. How is the mutant allele for yellow body inherited?

choices.C: It is inherited by X inactivation.
choices.D: It is Y-linked.

questions.answer_text: It is X-linked.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding gene linkage is correct?

choices.A: The closer two genes are on a chromosome, the lower the probability that a crossover will occur between them.
choices.B: The observed frequency of recombination of two genes that are far apart from each other has a maximum value of 100%.
choices.C: All of the traits that Mendel studied—seed color, pod shape, flower color, and others—are due to genes linked on the same chromosome.
choices.D: Linked genes are found on different chromosomes.

questions.answer_text: The closer two genes are on a chromosome, the lower the probability that a crossover will occur between them.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements would explain a testcross involving F1 dihybrid flies in which more parental-type offspring than recombinant-type offspring are produced?

choices.A: The two genes are closely linked on the same chromosome.
choices.B: The two genes are linked but on different chromosomes.
choices.C: Recombination did not occur in the cell during meiosis.
choices.D: Both of the characters are controlled by more than one gene.

questions.answer_text: The two genes are closely linked on the same chromosome.

questions.stem: What does a recombination frequency of 50% indicate?

choices.A: The two genes are likely to be located on different chromosomes.
choices.B: All of the offspring have combinations of traits that match one of the two parents.
choices.C: The genes are located on sex chromosomes.
choices.D: Abnormal meiosis has occurred.

questions.answer_text: The two genes are likely to be located on different chromosomes.

questions.stem: Which of the following phrases correctly defines what one map unit is?

choices.A: the physical distance between two linked genes
choices.B: a 1% frequency of recombination between two genes
choices.C: 1 nanometer of distance between two genes
choices.D: the recombination frequency between two genes assorting independently

questions.answer_text: a 1% frequency of recombination between two genes

questions.stem: Which of the following occurrences describes how recombination between linked genes comes about?

choices.A: Nonrecombinant chromosomes break and then rejoin with one another.
choices.C: Linked genes travel together at anaphase.
choices.D: Crossovers between these genes result in chromosomal exchange.

questions.answer_text: Crossovers between these genes result in chromosomal exchange.

questions.stem: What is an adaptive advantage of recombination between linked genes?

choices.A: Recombination is required for independent assortment.
choices.B: Recombination must occur or genes will not assort independently.
choices.C: New allele combinations are acted upon by natural selection.
choices.D: The forces on the cell during meiosis II result in recombination.

questions.answer_text: New allele combinations are acted upon by natural selection.

questions.stem: Map units on a linkage map cannot be relied upon to calculate physical distances on a chromosome for which of the following reasons?

choices.A: The frequency of crossing over varies along the length of the chromosome.
choices.B: The relationship between recombination frequency and map units is different in every individual.
choices.C: Physical distances between genes change during the course of the cell cycle.
choices.D: The gene order on the chromosomes is slightly different in every individual.

questions.answer_text: The frequency of crossing over varies along the length of the chromosome.

questions.stem: Use the following map of four genes on a chromosome to answer the question. Between which two genes would you expect the highest frequency of recombination?

choices.C: A and E
choices.D: A and G

questions.answer_text: A and G

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. In a series of mapping experiments, the recombination frequencies for four different linked genes of Drosophila were determined as shown in the figure. Based on this information, what is the order of these genes on a chromosome map?

choices.C: b-rb-cn-vg
choices.D: vg-cn-b-rb

questions.answer_text: b-rb-cn-vg

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. A plantlike organism on the planet Pandora can have three recessive genetic traits: bluish leaves, due to an allele (a) of gene A; a feathered stem, due to an allele (b) of gene B; and hollow roots due to an allele (c) of gene C. The three genes are linked and recombine. A geneticist performed a testcross with an organism that had been found to be heterozygous for the three recessive traits, and she was able to identify progeny of the following phenotypic distribution (+ = wild type): Phenotypes Leaves Stems Roots Number 1 a + + 14 2 a + c 0 3 a b + 32 4 a b c 440 5 + b + 0 6 + b c 16 7 + + c 28 8 + + + 470 Total 1000 Which of the following are the phenotypes of the parents in this cross?

choices.C: 4 and 8
choices.D: 3 and 7

questions.answer_text: 4 and 8

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. A plantlike organism on the planet Pandora can have three recessive genetic traits: bluish leaves, due to an allele (a) of gene A; a feathered stem, due to an allele (b) of gene B; and hollow roots due to an allele (c) of gene C. The three genes are linked and recombine. A geneticist performed a testcross with an organism that had been found to be heterozygous for the three recessive traits, and she was able to identify progeny of the following phenotypic distribution (+ = wild type): Phenotypes Leaves Stems Roots Number 1 a + + 14 2 a + c 0 3 a b + 32 4 a b c 440 5 + b + 0 6 + b c 16 7 + + c 28 8 + + + 470 Total 1000 Which of the progeny phenotypes will require recombination between genes A and B?

Use the following information to answer the question. A plantlike organism on the planet Pandora can have three recessive genetic traits: bluish leaves, due to an allele (a) of gene A; a feathered stem, due to an allele (b) of gene B; and hollow roots due to an allele (c) of gene C. The three genes are linked and recombine. A geneticist performed a testcross with an organism that had been found to be heterozygous for the three recessive traits, and she was able to identify progeny of the following phenotypic distribution (+ = wild type): Phenotypes Leaves Stems Roots Number 1 a + + 14 2 a + c 0 3 a b + 32 4 a b c 440 5 + b + 0 6 + b c 16 7 + + c 28 8 + + + 470 Total 1000 If recombination frequency is equal to distance in map units, what is the approximate distance between genes A and B?

choices.C: 15 map units
choices.D: 30 map units

questions.answer_text: 3 map units

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. A plantlike organism on the planet Pandora can have three recessive genetic traits: bluish leaves, due to an allele (a) of gene A; a feathered stem, due to an allele (b) of gene B; and hollow roots due to an allele (c) of gene C. The three genes are linked and recombine. A geneticist performed a testcross with an organism that had been found to be heterozygous for the three recessive traits, and she was able to identify progeny of the following phenotypic distribution (+ = wild type): Phenotypes Leaves Stems Roots Number 1 a + + 14 2 a + c 0 3 a b + 32 4 a b c 440 5 + b + 0 6 + b c 16 7 + + c 28 8 + + + 470 Total 1000 What is the greatest benefit of having used a testcross for this experiment?

choices.A: The homozygous recessive parents are obvious to the naked eye.
choices.B: The homozygous parents are the only ones whose crossovers make a difference.
choices.C: The phenotypes of the progeny reveal the allelic content of the gamete from the heterozygous parent.
choices.D: All of the progeny will be heterozygous.

questions.answer_text: The phenotypes of the progeny reveal the allelic content of the gamete from the heterozygous parent.

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. A plantlike organism on the planet Pandora can have three recessive genetic traits: bluish leaves, due to an allele (a) of gene A; a feathered stem, due to an allele (b) of gene B; and hollow roots due to an allele (c) of gene C. The three genes are linked and recombine. A geneticist performed a testcross with an organism that had been found to be heterozygous for the three recessive traits, and she was able to identify progeny of the following phenotypic distribution (+ = wild type): Phenotypes Leaves Stems Roots Number 1 a + + 14 2 a + c 0 3 a b + 32 4 a b c 440 5 + b + 0 6 + b c 16 7 + + c 28 8 + + + 470 Total 1000 The greatest distance among the three genes is between a and c. What does this mean?

choices.A: Gene c is between a and b.
choices.B: Genes are in the order: a-b-c.
choices.C: Gene a is not recombining with c.
choices.D: Gene a is between b and c.

questions.answer_text: Genes are in the order: a-b-c.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes the reason that closely linked genes are typically inherited together?

choices.A: They are located close together on the same chromosome.
choices.B: The number of genes in a cell is greater than the number of chromosomes.
choices.C: Alleles are paired together during meiosis.
choices.D: Genes align that way during metaphase I of meiosis.

questions.answer_text: They are located close together on the same chromosome.

questions.stem: A homozygous tomato plant with red fruit and yellow flowers was crossed with a homozygous tomato plant with golden fruit and white flowers. The F1 all had red fruit and yellow flowers. The F1 were testcrossed by crossing them to homozygous recessive individuals, and the following offspring were obtained: Red fruit and yellow flowers—41 Red fruit and white flowers—7 Golden fruit and yellow flowers—8 Golden fruit and white flowers—44 How many map units separate these genes?

In Drosophila melanogaster, vestigial wings are determined by a recessive allele of a gene that is linked to a gene with a recessive allele that determines black body color. T. H. Morgan crossed black-bodied, normal-winged females and gray-bodied, vestigial-winged males. The F1 were all gray bodied, normal winged. The F1 females were crossed to homozygous recessive males to produce testcross progeny. Morgan calculated the map distance to be 17 map units. Which of the following information is correct about the testcross progeny?

choices.A: black-bodied, normal-winged flies = 17% of the total
choices.B: black-bodied, normal-winged flies plus gray-bodied, vestigial-winged flies = 17% of the total
choices.C: gray-bodied, normal-winged flies plus black-bodied, vestigial-winged flies = 17% of the total
choices.D: black-bodied, vestigial-winged flies = 17% of the total

questions.answer_text: gray-bodied, normal-winged flies plus black-bodied, vestigial-winged flies = 17% of the total

questions.stem: If cell X enters meiosis, and nondisjunction of one chromosome occurs in one of its daughter cells during meiosis II, how will this affect the gametes at the completion of meiosis?

choices.A: All the gametes descended from cell X will be diploid.
choices.B: Half of the gametes descended from cell X will be n + 1, and half will be n - 1.
choices.C: One-quarter of the gametes descended from cell X will be n + 1, one-quarter will be n - 1, and half will be n.
choices.D: Two of the four gametes descended from cell X will be haploid, and two will be diploid.

questions.answer_text: One-quarter of the gametes descended from cell X will be n + 1, one-quarter will be n - 1, and half will be n.

questions.stem: One possible result of chromosomal breakage is for a fragment to join a nonhomologous chromosome. What is this type of chromosomal alteration called?

choices.C: translocation
choices.D: duplication

questions.answer_text: translocation

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes what happens to a chromosome after a nonreciprocal translocation occurs?

choices.A: A deletion of part of the chromosome occurs.
choices.B: A duplication of part of the chromosome occurs.
choices.C: Nondisjunction of pairs of homologous occurs.
choices.D: A chromosome transfers a fragment but receives none in return.

questions.answer_text: A chromosome transfers a fragment but receives none in return.

questions.stem: Of the following human aneuploidies, which is the one that generally has the most severe impact on the health of the individual?

choices.C: 47, XXX

questions.answer_text: 47, trisomy 21

questions.stem: A phenotypically normal prospective couple seeks genetic counseling because the man knows that he has a translocation of a portion of his chromosome 4, which has been exchanged with a portion of his chromosome 12. Although his translocation is balanced, he and his wife want to know the probability that his sperm will be abnormal. What is your prognosis regarding his sperm?

choices.A: One-quarter will carry the two normal chromosomes, 4 and 12, one-quarter will have only the two translocation chromosomes and no normal chromosomes 4 and 12, and half will have one normal and one translocated chromosome.
choices.B: All will carry the same translocation as the father.
choices.C: None will carry the translocation.
choices.D: Half will be normal, and the rest will have the father's translocation.

questions.answer_text: One-quarter will carry the two normal chromosomes, 4 and 12, one-quarter will have only the two translocation chromosomes and no normal chromosomes 4 and 12, and half will have one normal and one translocated chromosome.

questions.stem: Abnormal chromosomes are frequently found in malignant tumors. Errors such as translocations may place a gene in close proximity to different control regions. Which of the following events might then occur to make the cancer worse?

choices.C: a decrease in mitotic frequency
choices.D: failure of the cancer cells to multiply

questions.answer_text: expression of inappropriate gene products

questions.stem: A couple has a child with Down syndrome. The mother is 39 years old at the time of delivery. Which of the following is the most probable cause of the child's condition?

choices.A: The woman inherited this tendency from her parents.
choices.B: The mother had a chromosomal duplication.
choices.C: One member of the couple underwent nondisjunction in somatic cell production.
choices.D: One of the gametes in the mother most likely underwent nondisjunction during meiosis.

questions.answer_text: One of the gametes in the mother most likely underwent nondisjunction during meiosis.

questions.stem: What is a syndrome?

choices.B: a trait that leads to cancer at some stage in life
choices.C: a group of traits typically found in conjunction with a particular chromosomal aberration or gene mutation
choices.D: a specific characteristic that appears in conjunction with one specific aneuploidy

questions.answer_text: a group of traits typically found in conjunction with a particular chromosomal aberration or gene mutation

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes a Philadelphia chromosome?

choices.A: a human chromosome 22 that has had a specific translocation
choices.B: a human chromosome 9 that is found only in one type of cancer
choices.C: an animal chromosome found primarily in the mid-Atlantic area of the United States
choices.D: a chromosome found only in mitochondria

questions.answer_text: a human chromosome 22 that has had a specific translocation

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is generally true of aneuploidies in newborns?

choices.A: A monosomy is more frequent than a trisomy.
choices.B: Monosomy X is the only viable monosomy known to occur in humans.
choices.C: Human aneuploidy usually conveys an adaptive advantage in humans.
choices.D: An aneuploidy resulting in the deletion of a chromosome segment is less serious than a duplication.

questions.answer_text: Monosomy X is the only viable monosomy known to occur in humans.

questions.stem: A woman is found to have 47 chromosomes, including three X chromosomes. Which of the following statements describes her expected phenotype?

choices.A: a female with masculine characteristics such as facial hair
choices.B: an apparent male who is sterile
choices.C: healthy female of slightly above-average height
choices.D: a sterile female

questions.answer_text: healthy female of slightly above-average height

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of monosomy in humans?

choices.C: Down syndrome
choices.D: trisomy X

questions.answer_text: Turner syndrome

questions.stem: Genomic imprinting is generally due to the addition of methyl (-CH3) groups to C nucleotides and chemical histone changes to silence a given gene. If this depends on the sex of the parent who transmits the gene, which of the following statements must be true?

choices.A: Genes required for early development stages must not be imprinted.
choices.B: Methylation of this kind must occur more in males than in females.
choices.C: Methylation must be reversible in ovarian and testicular cells.
choices.D: The imprints are transmitted only to gamete-producing cells.

questions.answer_text: Methylation must be reversible in ovarian and testicular cells.

questions.stem: German scientist Carl Correns found that the inheritance of variegated color on the leaves of certain plants was determined only by the maternal parent. What phenomenon explains this pattern of inheritance?

choices.C: genomic imprinting
choices.D: sex linkage

questions.answer_text: inheritance of plastid genes

questions.stem: Mitochondrial DNA is primarily involved in coding for proteins needed for protein complexes of the electron transport chain and ATP synthase. Therefore, mutations in mitochondrial genes would most affect which of the following processes?

choices.A: DNA synthesis in cells of the immune system
choices.B: the movement of oxygen into erythrocytes
choices.C: generation of ATP in muscle cells
choices.D: the storage of urine in the urinary bladder

questions.answer_text: generation of ATP in muscle cells

questions.stem: Use the following figure to answer the question. The pedigree in the figure shows the transmission of a trait in a particular family. Based on this pattern of transmission, the trait is most likely ________.

choices.C: sex-linked recessive
choices.D: autosomal dominant

questions.answer_text: mitochondrial

questions.stem: A certain kind of snail can have a right-handed direction of shell coiling (DD or Dd) or left- handed coiling (dd). However, if direction of coiling is due to a protein deposited by the mother in the egg cytoplasm, then a Dd egg-producing snail and a dd sperm-producing snail will have offspring of which genotype(s) and phenotype(s)?

choices.C: 1/2 Dd: 1/2 dd; half right-coiling and half left-coiling
choices.D: all Dd; half right-coiling and half left-coiling

questions.answer_text: 1/2 Dd:1/2 dd; all right-coiling

questions.stem: During meiosis, a defect occurs in a cell that results in the failure of spindle microtubules binding at the kinetochores. Which of the following statements describes the most likely result of such a defect?

choices.A: New microtubules with more effective binding capabilities to kinetochores will be synthesized to compensate for the defect.
choices.B: Excessive cell divisions will occur resulting in cancerous tumors and an increase in the chromosome numbers known as polyploidy.
choices.C: The defect will be bypassed in order to ensure normal chromosome distribution in the new cells.
choices.D: The resulting cells will not receive the correct number of chromosomes in the gametes, a condition known as aneuploidy.

questions.answer_text: The resulting cells will not receive the correct number of chromosomes in the gametes, a condition known as aneuploidy.

questions.stem: Inheritance patterns cannot always be explained by Mendel's models of inheritance. If a pair of homologous chromosomes fails to separate during meiosis I, select the choice that shows the chromosome number of the four resulting gametes with respect to the normal haploid number (n)?
In his transformation experiments, what phenomenon did Griffith observe?

choices.A: Mixing a heat-killed pathogenic strain of bacteria with a living nonpathogenic strain can convert some of the living cells into the pathogenic form.
choices.B: Mixing a heat-killed nonpathogenic strain of bacteria with a living pathogenic strain makes the pathogenic strain nonpathogenic.
choices.C: Infecting mice with nonpathogenic strains of bacteria makes them resistant to pathogenic strains.
choices.D: Mice infected with a pathogenic strain of bacteria can spread the infection to other mice.

questions.answer_text: Mixing a heat-killed pathogenic strain of bacteria with a living nonpathogenic strain can convert some of the living cells into the pathogenic form.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes the process of transformation in bacteria?

choices.A: A strand of DNA is created from an RNA molecule.
choices.B: A strand of RNA is created from a DNA molecule.
choices.C: Bacterial cells are infected by a phage DNA molecule.
choices.D: External DNA is taken into a cell, becoming part of the cell's genome.

questions.answer_text: External DNA is taken into a cell, becoming part of the cell's genome.

questions.stem: A heat-killed, phosphorescent (light-emitting) strain of bacteria is mixed with a living, non- phosphorescent strain. Further observations of the mixture show that some of the living cells are now phosphorescent. Which of the following observations would provide the best evidence that the ability to phosphoresce is a heritable trait?

choices.A: evidence that DNA was passed from the heat-killed strain to the living strain
choices.B: evidence that protein passed from the heat-killed strain to the living strain
choices.C: especially bright phosphorescence in the living strain
choices.D: phosphorescence in descendants of the living cells

questions.answer_text: phosphorescence in descendants of the living cells

questions.stem: Which of the following facts did Hershey and Chase make use of in trying to determine whether DNA or protein is the genetic material?

choices.A: DNA contains sulfur, whereas protein does not.
choices.B: DNA contains phosphorus, whereas protein does not.
choices.C: DNA contains nitrogen, whereas protein does not.
choices.D: DNA contains purines, whereas protein includes pyrimidines.

questions.answer_text: DNA contains phosphorus, whereas protein does not.

questions.stem: Which of the following investigators was (were) responsible for the discovery that in DNA from any species, the amount of adenine equals the amount of thymine, and the amount of guanine equals the amount of cytosine?

choices.B: Oswald Avery, Maclyn McCarty, and Colin MacLeod
choices.C: Erwin Chargaff
choices.D: Matthew Meselson and Franklin Stahl

questions.answer_text: Erwin Chargaff

questions.stem: Cytosine makes up 42% of the nucleotides in a sample of DNA from an organism. Approximately what percentage of the nucleotides in this sample will be thymine?
Thymine makes up 28% of the nucleotides in a sample of DNA from an organism. Approximately what percentage of the nucleotides in this sample will be guanine?

It became apparent to Watson and Crick after completion of their model that the DNA molecule could carry a vast amount of hereditary information. Which of the following characteristics of DNA is responsible for this?

choices.C: complementary pairing of bases
choices.D: side groups of nitrogenous bases

questions.answer_text: sequence of bases

questions.stem: In an analysis of the nucleotide composition of a molecule of DNA, which of the following combinations of base pairs will be found?

choices.C: A + C = G + T
choices.D: G + C = T + A

questions.answer_text: A + C = G + T

questions.stem: For a science fair project, two students decided to repeat the Hershey and Chase experiment, with modifications. They decided to radioactively label the nitrogen of the DNA, rather than the phosphate. They reasoned that each nucleotide has only one phosphate and two to five nitrogen atoms. Thus, labeling the nitrogen atoms would provide a stronger signal than labeling the phosphates. Why won't this experiment work?

choices.A: There is no radioactive isotope of nitrogen.
choices.B: Radioactive nitrogen has a half-life of 100,000 years, and the material would be too dangerous for too long.
choices.C: Although there are more nitrogens in a nucleotide, labeled phosphates actually have 16 extra neutrons; therefore, they are more radioactive.
choices.D: Amino acids (and thus proteins) also have nitrogen atoms; thus, the radioactivity would not distinguish between DNA and proteins.

questions.answer_text: Amino acids (and thus proteins) also have nitrogen atoms; thus, the radioactivity would not distinguish between DNA and proteins.

questions.stem: Hershey and Chase set out to determine what molecule served as the unit of inheritance. They completed a series of experiments in which E. coli was infected by a T2 virus. Which molecular component of the T2 virus actually ended up inside the cell?

choices.C: ribosome
choices.D: DNA

questions.answer_text: DNA

questions.stem: In the polymerization of DNA, a phosphodiester bond is formed between a phosphate group of the nucleotide being added and which of the following atoms or molecules of the last nucleotide in the polymer?

choices.C: the 3' OH
choices.D: a nitrogen from the nitrogen-containing base

questions.answer_text: the 3' OH

questions.stem: Which of the following statements accurately describes the differences between DNA replication in prokaryotes and DNA replication in eukaryotes?

choices.A: Prokaryotic chromosomes have histones, whereas eukaryotic chromosomes do not.
choices.B: Prokaryotic chromosomes have a single origin of replication, whereas eukaryotic chromosomes have many.
choices.C: The rate of elongation during DNA replication is slower in prokaryotes than in eukaryotes.
choices.D: Prokaryotes produce Okazaki fragments during DNA replication, but eukaryotes do not.

questions.answer_text: Prokaryotic chromosomes have a single origin of replication, whereas eukaryotic chromosomes have many.

questions.stem: What is meant by the description "antiparallel" regarding the two strands that make up the DNA double helix?

choices.A: The double helix structure of DNA creates nonparallel strands.
choices.B: The 5' to 3' direction of one strand runs counter to the 5' to 3' direction of the other strand.
choices.C: Base pairings create unequal spacing between the two DNA strands.
choices.D: One strand contains only purines and the other contains only pyrimidines.

questions.answer_text: The 5' to 3' direction of one strand runs counter to the 5' to 3' direction of the other strand.

questions.stem: Suppose you are provided with an actively dividing culture of E. coli bacteria to which radioactive thymine has been added. What would happen if a cell replicates once in the presence of this radioactive base?

choices.A: One of the daughter cells, but not the other, would have radioactive DNA.
choices.B: Neither of the two daughter cells would be radioactive.
choices.C: All four bases of the DNA would be radioactive.
choices.D: DNA in both daughter cells would be radioactive.

questions.answer_text: DNA in both daughter cells would be radioactive.

questions.stem: In E. coli, there is a mutation in a gene called dnaB that alters the helicase that normally acts at the origin of replication. Which of the following events would you expect to occur as a result of this mutation?

choices.B: No replication fork will be formed.
choices.C: Replication will occur via RNA polymerase alone.
choices.D: Replication will require a DNA template from another source.

questions.answer_text: No replication fork will be formed.

questions.stem: In E. coli, which enzyme catalyzes the elongation of a new DNA strand in the 5' → 3' direction?

choices.C: DNA polymerase III
choices.D: helicase

questions.answer_text: DNA polymerase III

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics of eukaryotic telomeres cause them to replicate differently than the rest of the chromosome?

choices.B: DNA polymerase that cannot replicate the leading strand template to its 5' end
choices.C: gaps left at the 5' end of the lagging strand template
choices.D: gaps left at the 3' end of the lagging strand because of the need for a primer

questions.answer_text: gaps left at the 5' end of the lagging strand template

questions.stem: How does the enzyme telomerase meet the challenge of replicating the ends of linear chromosomes?

choices.A: It adds a single 5' cap structure that resists degradation by nucleases.
choices.B: It causes specific double-strand DNA breaks that result in blunt ends on both strands.
choices.C: It catalyzes the lengthening of telomeres, compensating for the shortening that could occur during replication without telomerase activity.
choices.D: It adds numerous GC pairs, which resist hydrolysis and maintain chromosome integrity.

questions.answer_text: It catalyzes the lengthening of telomeres, compensating for the shortening that could occur during replication without telomerase activity.

questions.stem: At a specific area of a chromosome, the sequence of nucleotides below is present where the chain opens to form a replication fork: 3' C C T A G G C T G C A A T C C 5' An RNA primer is formed starting at the underlined T (T) of the template. Which of the following represents the primer sequence?

choices.A: 5' G C C T A G G 3'
choices.B: 5' A C G T T A G G 3'
choices.C: 5' A C G U U A G G 3'
choices.D: 5' G C C U A G G 3'

questions.answer_text: 5' A C G U U A G G 3'

questions.stem: In E. coli, to repair a thymine dimer by nucleotide excision repair, in which order do the necessary enzymes act?

choices.C: DNA ligase, nuclease, helicase
choices.D: nuclease, DNA polymerase, DNA ligase

questions.answer_text: nuclease, DNA polymerase, DNA ligase

questions.stem: In E. coli, what is the function of DNA polymerase III?

choices.A: to unwind the DNA helix during replication
choices.B: to seal together the broken ends of DNA strands
choices.C: to add nucleotides to the 3' end of a growing DNA strand
choices.D: to degrade damaged DNA molecules

questions.answer_text: to add nucleotides to the 3' end of a growing DNA strand

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes the difference between ATP and the nucleotides used during DNA synthesis?

choices.A: The nucleotides have the sugar deoxyribose; ATP has the sugar ribose.
choices.B: The nucleotides have two phosphate groups; ATP has three phosphate groups.
choices.C: ATP contains three high-energy bonds; the nucleotides have two.
choices.D: ATP is found only in human cells; the nucleotides are found in all animal and plant cells.

questions.answer_text: The nucleotides have the sugar deoxyribose; ATP has the sugar ribose.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes the difference between the leading and the lagging strands of DNA during DNA replication?

choices.A: The leading strand is synthesized in the same direction as the movement of the replication fork, and the lagging strand is synthesized in the opposite direction.
choices.B: The leading strand is synthesized by adding nucleotides to the 3' end of the growing strand, and the lagging strand is synthesized by adding nucleotides to the 5' end.
choices.C: The lagging strand is synthesized continuously, whereas the leading strand is synthesized in short fragments that are ultimately stitched together.
choices.D: The leading strand is synthesized at twice the rate of the lagging strand.

questions.answer_text: The leading strand is synthesized in the same direction as the movement of the replication fork, and the lagging strand is synthesized in the opposite direction.

questions.stem: Why does a new DNA strand elongate only in the 5' to 3' direction during DNA replication?

choices.A: DNA polymerase begins adding nucleotides at the 5' end of the template.
choices.B: The polarity of the DNA molecule prevents addition of nucleotides at the 3' end.
choices.C: Replication must progress toward the replication fork.
choices.D: DNA polymerase can add nucleotides only to the free 3' end.

questions.answer_text: DNA polymerase can add nucleotides only to the free 3' end.

questions.stem: What is the function of the enzyme topoisomerase in DNA replication?

choices.A: relieving strain in the DNA ahead of the replication fork caused by the untwisting of the double helix
choices.B: elongating new DNA at a replication fork by adding nucleotides to the existing chain
choices.C: reattaching the hydrogen bonds between the base pairs in the double helix
choices.D: building RNA primers using the parental DNA strand as a template

questions.answer_text: relieving strain in the DNA ahead of the replication fork caused by the untwisting of the double helix

questions.stem: What is the role of DNA ligase in the elongation of the lagging strand during DNA replication?

choices.A: It synthesizes RNA nucleotides to make a primer.
choices.C: It unwinds the parental double helix.
choices.D: It stabilizes the unwound parental DNA.

questions.answer_text: It joins Okazaki fragments together.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of molecules help to hold the DNA strands apart while they are being replicated?

choices.C: DNA polymerase
choices.D: single-strand DNA binding proteins

questions.answer_text: single-strand DNA binding proteins

questions.stem: Individuals with the disorder xeroderma pigmentosum are hypersensitive to sunlight, and mutations to the DNA in their skin cells are left uncorrected. Why are the mutations not corrected in individuals with this disorder?

choices.A: The disorder makes cells unable to replicate DNA.
choices.B: The disorder causes mitosis to stop during metaphase.
choices.C: The disorder makes cells unable to form chromosomes.
choices.D: The disorder causes cells to be unable to repair thymine dimers.

questions.answer_text: The disorder causes cells to be unable to repair thymine dimers.

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics would you expect of a eukaryotic organism that lacks the enzyme telomerase?

choices.A: a high probability of somatic cells becoming cancerous
choices.B: an inability to produce Okazaki fragments
choices.C: an inability to repair thymine dimers
choices.D: a reduction in chromosome length in gametes

questions.answer_text: a reduction in chromosome length in gametes

questions.stem: Use the figure to answer the following question. In the late 1950s, Meselson and Stahl grew bacteria in a medium containing "heavy" (radioactive) nitrogen (13N) and then transferred them to a medium containing 14N (non- radioactive). Which of the results in the figure would be expected after one round of DNA replication in the presence of 14N?

choices.C: C
choices.D: D

questions.answer_text: D

questions.stem: Use the figure to answer the following question. A space probe returns with a culture of a microorganism found on a distant planet. Analysis shows that it is a carbon-based life-form that has DNA. You grow the cells in 15N medium for several generations and then transfer them to 14N medium. Which pattern in the figure would you expect if the DNA was replicated in a conservative manner?

choices.C: C
choices.D: D

questions.answer_text: B

questions.stem: After the first replication was observed in their experiments testing the nature of DNA replication, Meselson and Stahl could be confident of which of the following conclusions?

choices.C: Replication is not conservative.
choices.D: Replication is neither dispersive nor conservative.

questions.answer_text: Replication is not conservative.

questions.stem: You briefly expose bacteria undergoing DNA replication to radioactively labeled nucleotides. When you centrifuge the DNA isolated from the bacteria, the DNA separates into two classes. One class of labeled DNA includes very large molecules (thousands or even millions of nucleotides long), and the other includes short stretches of DNA (several hundred to a few thousand nucleotides in length). Which two classes of DNA do these different samples represent?

choices.C: Okazaki fragments and RNA primers
choices.D: leading strands and RNA primers

questions.answer_text: leading strands and Okazaki fragments

questions.stem: Within a double-stranded DNA molecule, adenine forms hydrogen bonds with thymine, and cytosine forms hydrogen bonds with guanine. What is the significance of the structural arrangement?

choices.A: It allows variable width of the double helix.
choices.C: It determines the tertiary structure of a DNA molecule.
choices.D: It determines the type of protein produced.

questions.answer_text: It permits complementary base pairing.

questions.stem: Semiconservative replication involves a template. What is the template?

choices.C: one strand of the DNA molecule
choices.D: an RNA molecule

questions.answer_text: one strand of the DNA molecule

questions.stem: In DNA replication, the resulting daughter molecules contain one strand of the original parental DNA and one new strand. What is the explanation for this phenomenon?

choices.C: DNA replication is not conservative.
choices.D: RNA synthesis is conservative.

questions.answer_text: DNA replication is semiconservative.

questions.stem: Who performed classic experiments that supported the semiconservative model of DNA replication?

choices.C: Hershey and Chase
choices.D: Franklin and Wilkins

questions.answer_text: Meselson and Stahl

questions.stem: DNA contains the template needed to copy itself, but it has no catalytic activity in cells. What catalyzes the formation of phosphodiester bonds between adjacent nucleotides in the DNA polymer being formed during DNA replication?

choices.C: ATP
choices.D: RNA primers

questions.answer_text: DNA polymerase

questions.stem: Use the figure to answer the following question. Referring to the figure, what bases will be added to the primer as DNA replication proceeds?

choices.A: 5′ C, A, G, C, A, G, A 3′
choices.B: 3′ T, C, T, G, C, T, G 5′
choices.C: 5′ A, G, A, C, G, A, C 3′
choices.D: 3′ G, T, C, G, T, C, T 5′

questions.answer_text: 5′ A, G, A, C, G, A, C 3′

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes the difference between the leading strand and the lagging strand in DNA replication?

choices.A: The leading strand is synthesized in the 3' → 5' direction in a discontinuous fashion, while the lagging strand is synthesized in the 5' → 3' direction in a continuous fashion.
choices.B: The leading strand is synthesized continuously in the 5' → 3' direction, while the lagging strand is synthesized discontinuously in the 5' → 3' direction.
choices.C: The leading strand requires an RNA primer, whereas the lagging strand does not.
choices.D: There are different DNA polymerases involved in elongation of the leading strand and the lagging strand.

questions.answer_text: The leading strand is synthesized continuously in the 5' → 3' direction, while the lagging strand is synthesized discontinuously in the 5' → 3' direction.

questions.stem: What are telomeres?

choices.A: the structures that hold two sister chromatids together
choices.B: enzymes that elongate the DNA strand during replication
choices.C: the sites of origin of DNA replication
choices.D: the ends of linear chromosomes

questions.answer_text: the ends of linear chromosomes

questions.stem: Telomere shortening puts a limit on the number of times a cell can divide. Research has shown that telomerase can extend the life span of cultured human cells. How might adding telomerase affect cellular aging?

choices.A: Telomerase will speed up the rate of cell proliferation.
