choices.B: Telomerase eliminates telomere shortening and retards aging.
choices.C: Telomerase shortens telomeres, which delays cellular aging.
choices.D: Telomerase would have no effect on cellular aging.

questions.answer_text: Telomerase eliminates telomere shortening and retards aging.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of cells are affected most by telomere shortening?

choices.C: cells in prokaryotes and eukaryotes
choices.D: only animal cells

questions.answer_text: only eukaryotic cells

questions.stem: Which of the following effects might be caused by reduced or very little active telomerase activity?

choices.C: Cells age and begin to lose function.
choices.D: Cells maintain normal functioning.

questions.answer_text: Cells age and begin to lose function.

questions.stem: Researchers found a strain of E. coli bacteria that had mutation rates one hundred times higher than normal. Which of the following statements correctly describes the most likely cause of these results?

choices.A: The single-strand binding proteins were malfunctioning during DNA replication.
choices.B: There were one or more base pair mismatches in the RNA primer.
choices.C: The proofreading mechanism of DNA polymerase was not working properly.
choices.D: The DNA polymerase was unable to add bases to the 3′ end of the growing nucleic acid chain.

questions.answer_text: The proofreading mechanism of DNA polymerase was not working properly.

questions.stem: In a healthy eukaryotic cell, the rate of DNA repair is typically equal to the rate of DNA mutation. When the rate of repair lags behind the rate of mutation, what is a possible fate of the cell?

choices.A: The cell can be transformed into a cancerous cell.
choices.B: RNA may be used instead of DNA as inheritance material.
choices.C: DNA replication will proceed more quickly.
choices.D: DNA replication will continue by a new mechanism.

questions.answer_text: The cell can be transformed into a cancerous cell.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements accurately describes the structure of a eukaryotic chromosome?

choices.A: It is composed of a single strand of DNA.
choices.B: It is constructed as a series of nucleosomes wrapped around two DNA molecules.
choices.C: It has different numbers of genes in different cell types of an organism.
choices.D: It is a single linear molecule of double-stranded DNA plus proteins.

questions.answer_text: It is a single linear molecule of double-stranded DNA plus proteins.

questions.stem: If a cell were unable to produce histone proteins, which of the following results would be a likely effect on the cell?

choices.A: There would be an increase in the amount of DNA produced during replication.
choices.B: The cell's DNA could not be packed into its nucleus.
choices.C: Spindle fibers would not form during prophase.
choices.D: Amplification of other genes would compensate for the lack of histones.

questions.answer_text: The cell's DNA could not be packed into its nucleus.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements accurately describes one characteristic of histones?

choices.A: Each nucleosome consists of two molecules of histone H1.
choices.B: Histone H1 is not present in the nucleosome bead; instead, it draws the nucleosomes together.
choices.C: The carboxyl end of each histone extends outward from the nucleosome and is called a "histone tail."
choices.D: Histones are found in mammals, but not in other animals or in plants or fungi.

questions.answer_text: Histone H1 is not present in the nucleosome bead; instead, it draws the nucleosomes together.

questions.stem: Which of the following molecular characteristics cause histones to bind tightly to DNA?

choices.A: Histones are positively charged, and DNA is negatively charged.
choices.B: Histones are negatively charged, and DNA is positively charged.
choices.C: Both histones and DNA are strongly hydrophobic.
choices.D: Histones are covalently linked to the DNA.

questions.answer_text: Histones are positively charged, and DNA is negatively charged.

questions.stem: Which of the following lists represents the order of increasingly higher levels of organization of chromatin?

choices.C: nucleosome, looped domain, 30-nm chromatin fiber
choices.D: 30-nm chromatin fiber, nucleosome, looped domain

questions.answer_text: nucleosome, 30-nm chromatin fiber, looped domain

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes the structure of chromatin?

choices.A: Heterochromatin is composed of DNA, whereas euchromatin is made of DNA and RNA.
choices.B: Both heterochromatin and euchromatin are found in the cytoplasm.
choices.C: Heterochromatin is highly condensed, whereas euchromatin is less compact.
choices.D: Euchromatin is not transcribed, whereas heterochromatin is transcribed.

questions.answer_text: Heterochromatin is highly condensed, whereas euchromatin is less compact.

questions.stem: Which of the following structural characteristics is most critical for the association between histones and DNA?

choices.B: Histones are highly conserved (that is, histones are very similar in every eukaryote).
choices.C: There are at least five different histone proteins in every eukaryote.
choices.D: Histones are positively charged.

questions.answer_text: Histones are positively charged.

questions.stem: In DNA replication in E. coli, the enzyme primase is used to attach a 5 to 10 base ribonucleotide strand complementary to the parental DNA strand. The RNA strand serves as a starting point for the DNA polymerase that replicates the DNA. If a mutation occurred in the primase gene, which of the following results would you expect?

choices.A: Replication would only occur on the leading strand.
choices.B: Replication would only occur on the lagging strand.
choices.C: Replication would not occur on either the leading or lagging strand.
choices.D: Replication would not be affected as the enzyme primase in involved with RNA synthesis.

questions.answer_text: Replication would not occur on either the leading or lagging strand.

questions.stem: Hershey and Chase used a DNA-based virus for their work. How might the results have been different if they had used an RNA virus?

choices.A: With an RNA virus, radioactive protein would have been in the final pellet.
choices.B: With an RNA virus, radioactive RNA would have been in the final pellet.
choices.C: With an RNA virus, neither sample would have had a radioactive pellet.
choices.D: With an RNA virus, the protein shell would have been radioactive in both samples.

questions.answer_text: With an RNA virus, radioactive RNA would have been in the final pellet.

questions.stem: The lagging strand is characterized by a series of short segments of DNA (Okazaki fragments) that will be joined together to form a finished lagging strand. The experiments that led to the discovery of Okazaki fragments gave evidence for which of the following ideas?

choices.A: DNA polymerase is an enzyme that synthesizes leading and lagging strands during replication only in one direction.
choices.B: DNA is a polymer consisting of four monomers: adenine, thymine, guanine, and cytosine.
choices.C: DNA is the genetic material.
choices.D: Bacterial replication is fundamentally different from eukaryotic replication. The key should not be way longer than the distractors.

questions.answer_text: DNA polymerase is an enzyme that synthesizes leading and lagging strands during replication only in one direction.

questions.stem: In his work with pneumonia-causing bacteria and mice, Griffith found that

choices.A: the protein coat from pathogenic cells was able to transform nonpathogenic cells.
choices.C: some substance from pathogenic cells was transferred to nonpathogenic cells, making them pathogenic.
choices.D: the polysaccharide coat of bacteria caused pneumonia.

questions.answer_text: some substance from pathogenic cells was transferred to nonpathogenic cells, making them pathogenic.

questions.stem: What is the basis for the difference in how the leading and lagging strands of DNA molecules are synthesized?

choices.A: The origins of replication occur only at the 5′ end.
choices.B: Helicases and single-strand binding proteins work at the 5′ end.
choices.C: DNA polymerase can join new nucleotides only to the 3′ end of a pre-existing strand, and the strands are antiparallel.
choices.D: DNA ligase works only in the 3′ → 5′ direction.

questions.answer_text: DNA polymerase can join new nucleotides only to the 3′ end of a pre-existing strand, and the strands are antiparallel.

questions.stem: In analyzing the number of different bases in a DNA sample, which result would be consistent with the base-pairing rules?

questions.answer_text: A + G = C + T

questions.stem: The elongation of the leading strand during DNA synthesis

choices.D: depends on the action of DNA polymerase.

questions.answer_text: depends on the action of DNA polymerase.

questions.stem: In a nucleosome, the DNA is wrapped around

choices.C: polymerase molecules.
choices.D: a thymine dimer.

questions.answer_text: histones.

questions.stem: E. coli cells grown on 15N medium are transferred to 14N medium and allowed to grow for two more generations (two rounds of DNA replication). DNA extracted from these cells is centrifuged. What density distribution of DNA would you expect in this experiment?

choices.A: one high-density and one low-density band
choices.C: one high-density and one intermediate-density band
choices.D: one low-density and one intermediate-density band

questions.answer_text: one low-density and one intermediate-density band

questions.stem: A biochemist isolates, purifies, and combines in a test tube a variety of molecules needed for DNA replication. choices.C: Okazaki fragments
choices.D: primase

questions.answer_text: DNA ligase

questions.stem: The spontaneous loss of amino groups from adenine in DNA results in hypoxanthine, an uncommon base, opposite thymine. What combination of proteins could repair such damage?

choices.D: DNA ligase, replication fork proteins, adenylyl cyclase

questions.answer_text: nuclease, DNA polymerase, DNA ligase

questions.stem: During the elongation phase of translation, which site in the ribosome represents the location where a codon is being read?

choices.C: A site
choices.D: the large ribosomal subunit

questions.answer_text: A site

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: Once a peptide bond has been formed between the amino acid attached to the tRNA in the P site and the amino acid associated with the tRNA in the A site, what process occurs next?

choices.B: reading of the next codon of mRNA
choices.C: initiation
choices.D: The codon-anticodon hydrogen bonds holding the tRNA in the A site are broken.

questions.answer_text: translocation

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: Which one of the following structures, if missing, would usually prevent translation from starting?

choices.C: AUG codon
choices.D: poly-A tail

questions.answer_text: AUG codon

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: Which of the following processes occurs when termination of translation takes place?

choices.A: The end of the mRNA molecule is reached.
choices.C: The 5′ cap is reached.
choices.D: The poly-A tail is reached.

questions.answer_text: A stop codon is reached.

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: Post-translational modifications of proteins may include which of the following processes?

choices.C: addition of a poly-A tail
choices.D: addition of carbohydrates to form a glycoprotein

questions.answer_text: addition of carbohydrates to form a glycoprotein

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about protein synthesis in prokaryotes?

choices.A: Extensive RNA processing is required before prokaryotic transcripts can be translated.
choices.B: Translation can begin while transcription is still in progress.
choices.C: Prokaryotic cells have complicated mechanisms for targeting proteins to the appropriate cellular organelles.
choices.D: Unlike eukaryotes, prokaryotes require no initiation or elongation factors.

questions.answer_text: Translation can begin while transcription is still in progress.

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: Which of the following types of mutation, resulting in an error in the mRNA just after the AUG start of translation, is likely to have the most serious effect on the polypeptide product?

choices.C: a substitution of the third nucleotide in an ACC codon
choices.D: a substitution of the first nucleotide of a GGG codon

questions.answer_text: a deletion of two nucleotides

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes the effect a nonsense mutation would have on a gene?

choices.A: It changes an amino acid in the encoded protein.
choices.B: It has no effect on the amino acid sequence of the encoded protein.
choices.C: It introduces a premature stop codon into the mRNA.
choices.D: It alters the reading frame of the mRNA.

questions.answer_text: It introduces a premature stop codon into the mRNA.

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: Which of the following DNA mutations is most likely to damage the protein it specifies?

choices.C: a substitution in the last base of a codon
choices.D: a codon deletion

questions.answer_text: a base-pair deletion

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: The most commonly occurring mutation in people with cystic fibrosis is a deletion of a single codon. What is the result of this type of mutation?

choices.C: a polypeptide missing an amino acid
choices.D: a nonsense mutation

questions.answer_text: a polypeptide missing an amino acid

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is the most current description of a gene?

choices.A: a unit of heredity that causes formation of a phenotypic characteristic
choices.B: a DNA subunit that codes for a single complete protein
choices.C: a DNA sequence that is expressed to form a functional product: either RNA or polypeptide
choices.D: a discrete unit of hereditary information that consists of a sequence of amino acids

questions.answer_text: a DNA sequence that is expressed to form a functional product: either RNA or polypeptide

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: How might a single base substitution in the sequence of a gene affect the amino acid sequence of a protein encoded by the gene?

choices.A: Only a single amino acid could change, because the reading frame would be unaffected.
choices.B: The amino acid sequence would be substantially altered, because the reading frame would change with a single base substitution.
choices.C: All amino acids following the substitution would be affected, because the reading frame would be shifted.
choices.D: It is not possible for a single base substitution to affect protein structure, because each codon is three bases long.

questions.answer_text: Only a single amino acid could change, because the reading frame would be unaffected.

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: An original section of DNA has the base sequence AGCGTTACCGT. A mutation in this DNA strand results in the base sequence AGGCGTTACCGT. What type of mutation does this change represent?

choices.C: a silent mutation
choices.D: frameshift mutation

questions.answer_text: frameshift mutation

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: A single base substitution mutation is likely to have a less deleterious effect when the base change exhibits which of the following results?

choices.B: a codon that specifies the same amino acid as the original codon
choices.C: an amino acid substitution that alters the tertiary structure of the protein
choices.D: an amino acid substitution at the active site of an enzyme

questions.answer_text: a codon that specifies the same amino acid as the original codon

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: Rank the following one-base point mutations with respect to their likelihood of affecting the structure of the corresponding polypeptide (from most likely to least likely). 1. insertion mutation deep within an intron 2. substitution mutation at the third position of a codon in an exon 3. substitution mutation at the second position of a codon in an exon 4. deletion mutation within the first exon of the gene

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: In eukaryotic cells, transcription cannot begin until

choices.A: the two DNA strands have completely separated and exposed the promoter.
choices.B: several transcription factors have bound to the promoter.
choices.C: the 5 caps are removed from the mRNA.
choices.D: the DNA introns are removed from the template.

questions.answer_text: several transcription factors have bound to the promoter.

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true of a codon?

choices.A: It may code for the same amino acid as another codon.
choices.B: It never codes for more than one amino acid.
choices.C: It extends from one end of a tRNA molecule.
choices.D: It is the basic unit of the genetic code.

questions.answer_text: It extends from one end of a tRNA molecule.

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: The anticodon of a particular tRNA molecule is

choices.A: complementary to the corresponding mRNA codon.
choices.B: complementary to the corresponding triplet in rRNA.
choices.C: the part of tRNA that bonds to a specific amino acid.
choices.D: catalytic, making the tRNA a ribozyme.

questions.answer_text: complementary to the corresponding mRNA codon.

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true of RNA processing?

choices.A: Exons are cut out before mRNA leaves the nucleus.
choices.B: Nucleotides may be added at both ends of the RNA.
choices.C: Ribozymes may function in RNA splicing.
choices.D: RNA splicing can be catalyzed by spliceosomes.

questions.answer_text: Exons are cut out before mRNA leaves the nucleus.

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: Which component is not directly involved in translation?

choices.C: tRNA
choices.D: ribosomes

questions.answer_text: DNA

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: Using Figure 17.6, identify a 5′ → 3′ sequence of nucleotides in the DNA template strand for an mRNA coding for the polypeptide sequence Phe-Pro-Lys.

choices.C: 5-CTTCGGGAA-3
choices.D: 5-AAACCCUUU-3

questions.answer_text: 5-CTTCGGGAA-3

chapter.title: Gene Expression: From Gene to Protein

questions.stem: Which of the following mutations would be most likely to have a harmful effect on an organism?

choices.A: a deletion of three nucleotides near the middle of a gene
choices.B: a single nucleotide deletion in the middle of an intron
choices.C: a single nucleotide deletion near the end of the coding sequence
choices.D: a single nucleotide insertion downstream of, and close to, the start of the coding sequence

questions.answer_text: a single nucleotide insertion downstream of, and close to, the start of the coding sequence

questions.stem: Which of the following molecules is a protein produced by a regulatory gene?

choices.C: promoter
choices.D: repressor

questions.answer_text: repressor

questions.stem: Which of the following molecules helps to "turn off" genes in a cell?

choices.C: promoter
choices.D: corepressor

questions.answer_text: corepressor

questions.stem: When taken up by a cell, which of the following molecules binds to a repressor so that the repressor no longer binds to the operator?

choices.C: repressor
choices.D: corepressor

questions.answer_text: inducer

questions.stem: Most repressor proteins are allosteric. Which of the following molecules binds with the repressor to alter its conformation and therefore affect its function?

choices.C: transcription factor
choices.D: cAMP

questions.answer_text: inducer

questions.stem: Which of the following processes would result from a mutation that deactivates a regulatory gene of a repressible operon in an E. coli cell?

choices.A: continuous transcription of the structural gene controlled by that regulator
choices.B: complete inhibition of transcription of the structural gene controlled by that regulator
choices.C: irreversible binding of the repressor to the operator
choices.D: continuous translation of the mRNA because of alteration of its structure

questions.answer_text: continuous transcription of the structural gene controlled by that regulator

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions is most likely to cause the lactose operon to be transcribed?

choices.A: There is more glucose in the cell than lactose.
choices.B: There is glucose but no lactose in the cell.
choices.C: The cyclic AMP and lactose levels are both high within the cell.
choices.D: The cAMP level is high and the lactose level is low.

questions.answer_text: The cyclic AMP and lactose levels are both high within the cell.

questions.stem: How does the transcription of structural genes in an inducible operon occur?

choices.A: It occurs continuously in the cell.
choices.B: It starts when the pathway's substrate is present.
choices.C: It starts when the pathway's product is present.
choices.D: It stops when the pathway's product is present.

questions.answer_text: It starts when the pathway's substrate is present.

questions.stem: For a repressible operon to be transcribed, which of the following conditions must occur?

choices.B: RNA polymerase and the active repressor must be present.
choices.C: RNA polymerase must bind to the promoter, and the repressor must be inactive.
choices.D: RNA polymerase must not occupy the promoter, and the repressor must be inactive.

questions.answer_text: RNA polymerase must bind to the promoter, and the repressor must be inactive.

questions.stem: Altering patterns of gene expression in prokaryotes would most likely serve an organism's survival by ________.

choices.A: organizing gene expression, so that genes are expressed in a given order
choices.B: allowing each gene to be expressed an equal number of times
choices.C: allowing an organism to adjust to changes in environmental conditions
choices.D: allowing environmental changes to alter a prokaryote's genome

questions.answer_text: allowing an organism to adjust to changes in environmental conditions

questions.stem: In positive control of several sugar metabolism-related operons, the cAMP receptor protein (CRP) binds to DNA to stimulate transcription. Which of the following environmental conditions causes an increase in CRP activity in stimulating transcription?

choices.A: an increase in glucose and an increase in cAMP
choices.B: a decrease in glucose and an increase in cAMP
choices.C: an increase in glucose and a decrease in cAMP
choices.D: a decrease in glucose and a decrease in the repressor

questions.answer_text: a decrease in glucose and an increase in cAMP

questions.stem: There is a mutation that is found in E. coli in the repressor that results in a molecule known as a super-repressor because it represses the lac operon permanently. Which of the following characteristics would you expect to observe in such a mutant?

choices.A: It cannot bind to the operator.
choices.B: It cannot make a functional repressor.
choices.C: It cannot bind to the inducer.
choices.D: It makes a repressor that binds CAP.

questions.answer_text: It cannot bind to the inducer.

questions.stem: Suppose an experimenter becomes proficient with a technique that allows her to move DNA sequences within a prokaryotic genome. If a researcher moves the promoter for the lac operon to the region between the beta galactosidase (lacZ) gene and the permease (lacY) gene, which of the following results would be most likely?

choices.A: The three genes of the lac operon will be expressed normally.
choices.B: RNA polymerase will no longer transcribe permease.
choices.C: The operon will still transcribe the lacZ and lacY genes, but the mRNA will not be translated.
choices.D: Beta galactosidase will not be produced.

questions.answer_text: Beta galactosidase will not be produced.

questions.stem: Suppose an experimenter becomes proficient with a technique that allows her to move DNA sequences within a prokaryotic genome. If a researcher moves the operator to the far end of the operon, past the transacetylase (lacA) gene, which of the following processes would likely occur when the cell is exposed to lactose?

choices.A: The inducer will no longer bind to the repressor.
choices.B: The repressor will no longer bind to the operator.
choices.C: The operon will never be transcribed.
choices.D: The genes of the lac operon will be transcribed continuously.

questions.answer_text: The genes of the lac operon will be transcribed continuously.

questions.stem: Suppose an experimenter becomes proficient with a technique that allows her to move DNA sequences within a prokaryotic genome. If a researcher moves the repressor gene (lacI), along with its promoter, to a position at some several thousand base pairs away from its normal position, which of the following results would be expected?

choices.A: The repressor will no longer bind to the operator.
choices.B: The repressor will no longer bind to the inducer.
choices.C: The lac operon will be expressed continuously.
choices.D: The lac operon will function normally.

questions.answer_text: The lac operon will function normally.

questions.stem: Which of the following results would occur if the repressor of an inducible operon were mutated so that it could not bind the operator?

choices.A: the irreversible binding of the repressor to the promoter
choices.B: the reduced transcription of the operon's genes
choices.C: the continuous transcription of the operon's genes
choices.D: the overproduction of cAMP receptor protein (CRP)

questions.answer_text: the continuous transcription of the operon's genes

questions.stem: According to the lac operon model proposed by Jacob and Monod, what is predicted to occur if the operator is removed from the operon?

choices.A: The lac operon would be transcribed continuously.
choices.C: Only lacY would be transcribed.
choices.D: Galactosidase permease would be produced, but would be incapable of transporting lactose.

questions.answer_text: The lac operon would be transcribed continuously.

questions.stem: Under what conditions does the trp repressor block transcription of the trp operon?

choices.A: when the repressor binds to the inducer
choices.B: when the repressor binds to tryptophan
choices.C: when the repressor is not bound to tryptophan
choices.D: when the repressor is not bound to the operator

questions.answer_text: when the repressor binds to tryptophan

questions.stem: How does extracellular glucose inhibit transcription of the lac operon?

choices.A: by strengthening the binding of the repressor to the operator
choices.B: by weakening the binding of the repressor to the operator
choices.C: by inhibiting RNA polymerase from opening the strands of DNA to initiate transcription
choices.D: by reducing the levels of intracellular cAMP

questions.answer_text: by reducing the levels of intracellular cAMP

questions.stem: The cAMP receptor protein (CRP) is said to be responsible for positive regulation of the lac operon because ________.

choices.B: CRP binds to the CAP-binding site
choices.C: CRP prevents binding of the repressor to the operator
choices.D: CRP bound to the CRP-binding site stimulates the transcription of the lac operon

questions.answer_text: CRP bound to the CRP-binding site stimulates the transcription of the lac operon

questions.stem: Imagine that you've isolated a yeast mutant that contains histones resistant to acetylation. What phenotype would you predict for this mutant?

choices.B: The mutant will require galactose for growth.
choices.C: The mutant will show decreased levels of gene expression.
choices.D: The mutant will show increased levels of gene expression.

questions.answer_text: The mutant will show decreased levels of gene expression.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes the primary difference between enhancers and proximal control elements?

choices.A: Enhancers are transcription factors; proximal control elements are DNA sequences.
choices.B: Enhancers improve transcription; proximal control elements inhibit transcription.
choices.C: Enhancers are located considerable distances from the promoter; proximal control elements are close to the promoter.
choices.D: Enhancers are DNA sequences; proximal control elements are proteins.

questions.answer_text: Enhancers are located considerable distances from the promoter; proximal control elements are close to the promoter.

questions.stem: The reason for differences in the sets of proteins expressed in a nerve and a pancreatic cell of the same individual is that nerve and pancreatic cells contain different ________.

choices.C: sets of regulatory proteins
choices.D: promoters

questions.answer_text: sets of regulatory proteins

questions.stem: Gene expression is often assayed by measuring the level of mRNA produced from a gene. What level of the control of gene expression can by analyzed by this type of assay?

choices.C: alternative splicing
choices.D: translational control

questions.answer_text: transcriptional control

questions.stem: Which of the following processes would allow the detection of alternative splicing of transcripts from a given gene?

choices.A: Compare the DNA sequence of the given gene to that of a similar gene in a related organism.
choices.B: Measure the relative rates of transcription of the given gene compared to that of a gene known to be constitutively spliced.
choices.C: Compare the sequences of different primary transcripts made from the given gene.
choices.D: Compare the sequences of different mRNAs made from the given gene.

questions.answer_text: Compare the sequences of different mRNAs made from the given gene.

questions.stem: Which of the following mechanisms is used to coordinate the expression of multiple, related genes in eukaryotic cells?

choices.A: Environmental signals enter the cell and bind directly to promoters.
choices.B: A given gene may have multiple enhancers, but each enhancer is generally associated with only that gene and no other.
choices.C: The genes are organized into a large operon, allowing them to be coordinately controlled as a single unit.
choices.D: A single repressor is able to turn off several related genes.

questions.answer_text: A given gene may have multiple enhancers, but each enhancer is generally associated with only that gene and no other.

questions.stem: DNA methylation and histone acetylation are examples of which of the following processes?

choices.C: epigenetic phenomena
choices.D: translocation

questions.answer_text: epigenetic phenomena

questions.stem: Which of the following functions are characteristic of general transcription factors in eukaryotes?

choices.A: They bind to other proteins or to the TATA box.
choices.B: They inhibit RNA polymerase binding to the promoter and begin transcribing.
choices.C: They usually lead to a high level of transcription even without additional specific transcription factors.
choices.D: They bind to sequences just after the start site of transcription.

questions.answer_text: They bind to other proteins or to the TATA box.

questions.stem: How do steroid hormones produce their effects in cells?

choices.A: by binding to the regulatory gene in an operon
choices.B: by activating translation of certain mRNAs
choices.C: by promoting the degradation of specific mRNAs
choices.D: by binding to intracellular receptors and promoting transcription of specific genes

questions.answer_text: by binding to intracellular receptors and promoting transcription of specific genes

questions.stem: How are bacteria able to change their patterns of protein synthesis so quickly in response to environmental changes?

choices.A: mRNAs that are produced are short-lived and degraded within a few minutes of being synthesized.
choices.B: mRNA have long lifespans, allowing the bacteria to use them many times for translation.
choices.C: mRNA is stored for later use.
choices.D: Operons are activated in the presence of transcription factors.

questions.answer_text: mRNAs that are produced are short-lived and degraded within a few minutes of being synthesized.

questions.stem: A researcher found a method she could use to manipulate and quantify phosphorylation and methylation in embryonic cells in culture. In one set of experiments, she succeeded in increasing acetylation of histone tails in the chromatin of the cells. Which of the following results would she most likely see in these cells?

choices.C: decreased binding of transcription factors
choices.D: inactivation of the selected genes

questions.answer_text: decreased chromatin condensation

questions.stem: A researcher found a method she could use to manipulate and quantify phosphorylation and methylation in embryonic cells in culture. One of her colleagues suggested she try increased methylation of cytosine (C) nucleotides in the DNA of promoters of a mammalian system. Which of the following results would she most likely see?

choices.B: activation of histone tails for enzymatic function
choices.C: higher levels of transcription of certain genes
choices.D: inactivation of the selected genes

questions.answer_text: inactivation of the selected genes

questions.stem: Which of the following methods is utilized by eukaryotes to control their gene expression that is different from the type of control found in bacteria?

choices.C: transcriptional control
choices.D: control of both RNA splicing and chromatin remodeling

questions.answer_text: control of both RNA splicing and chromatin remodeling

questions.stem: Which of the following processes destroys RNA molecules in a cell if they have a sequence complementary to an introduced double-stranded RNA?

choices.C: RNA blocking
choices.D: RNA disposal

questions.answer_text: RNA interference

questions.stem: At the beginning of this century, there was a general announcement regarding the sequencing of the human genome and the genomes of many other multicellular eukaryotes. Many people were surprised that the number of protein-coding sequences was much smaller than they had expected. Which of the following types of DNA make up the rest of the human genome?

choices.A: DNA that consists of histone coding sequences
choices.B: DNA that is translated directly without being transcribed
choices.C: non-protein-coding DNA that is transcribed into several kinds of small RNAs with biological function
choices.D: non-protein-coding DNA that serves as binding sites for reverse transcriptase

questions.answer_text: non-protein-coding DNA that is transcribed into several kinds of small RNAs with biological function

questions.stem: Among the newly discovered small noncoding RNAs, one type helps to reestablish ethylation patterns during gamete formation and blocks expression of some transposons. Which of the following types of RNA is responsible for this function?

choices.C: lncRNA
choices.D: siRNA

questions.answer_text: piRNA

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the characteristics of siRNA?

choices.A: a double-stranded RNA, one of whose strands can complement and inactivate a sequence of mRNA
choices.B: a single-stranded RNA that can, where it has internal complementary base pairs, fold into cloverleaf patterns
choices.C: a double-stranded RNA that is formed by cleavage of hairpin loops in a larger precursor
choices.D: a portion of rRNA that allows it to bind to several ribosomal proteins in forming large or small subunits

questions.answer_text: a double-stranded RNA, one of whose strands can complement and inactivate a sequence of mRNA

questions.stem: A researcher introduces double-stranded RNA into a culture of mammalian cells and can identify its location or that of its smaller subsections experimentally, using a fluorescent probe. Some time later, she finds that the introduced strand separates into single-stranded RNAs, one of which is degraded. What does this enable the remaining strand to do?

choices.A: attach to histones in the chromatin
choices.B: bind to complementary regions of target mRNAs
choices.C: activate other siRNAs in the cell
choices.D: bind to noncomplementary RNA sequences

questions.answer_text: bind to complementary regions of target mRNAs

questions.stem: A researcher introduces double-stranded RNA into a culture of mammalian cells and can identify its location or that of its smaller subsections experimentally, using a fluorescent probe. When she finds that the introduced strand separates into single-stranded RNAs, what other evidence of this single-stranded RNA piece's activity would she find?

choices.A: She can measure the degradation rate of the remaining single strand.
choices.B: The rate of accumulation of the polypeptide encoded by the target mRNA is reduced.
choices.C: The amount of miRNA is multiplied by its replication.
choices.D: The cell's translation ability is entirely shut down.

questions.answer_text: The rate of accumulation of the polypeptide encoded by the target mRNA is reduced.

questions.stem: The fact that plants can be cloned from somatic cells demonstrates that ________.

choices.A: differentiated cells retain all the genes of the zygote
choices.C: the differentiated state is normally very unstable
choices.D: differentiation does not occur in plants

questions.answer_text: differentiated cells retain all the genes of the zygote

questions.stem: Which of the following molecules are involved in pattern formation during development?

choices.C: cAMP
choices.D: transcription factors

questions.answer_text: cytoplasmic determinants

questions.stem: What essential information does the product of the bicoid gene in Drosophila provide during development?

choices.C: segmentation
choices.D: orientation of the anterior-posterior axis

questions.answer_text: orientation of the anterior-posterior axis

questions.stem: What would be the result of a mutation in a maternal effect gene in a female Drosophila?

choices.A: She will not develop past the early embryonic stage.
choices.B: All of her offspring will show the mutant phenotype, regardless of their genotype.
choices.C: Only her male offspring will show the mutant phenotype.
choices.D: Only her female offspring will show the mutant phenotype.

questions.answer_text: All of her offspring will show the mutant phenotype, regardless of their genotype.

questions.stem: Mutations in which of the following genes lead to transformations in the identity of entire body parts?

choices.C: homeotic genes
choices.D: inducers

questions.answer_text: homeotic genes

questions.stem: Which of the following are maternal effect genes that control the orientation of the egg and thus the Drosophila embryo?

choices.C: egg-polarity genes
choices.D: morphogens

questions.answer_text: egg-polarity genes

questions.stem: The bicoid gene product is normally localized to the anterior end of the embryo. If large amounts of the product were injected into the posterior end as well, which of the following developmental events would occur?

choices.A: The embryo would grow extra wings and legs.
choices.B: The embryo would probably show no anterior development and die.
choices.C: Anterior structures would form in both ends of the embryo.
choices.D: The embryo would develop normally.

questions.answer_text: Anterior structures would form in both ends of the embryo.

questions.stem: In colorectal cancer, several genes must be mutated for a cell to develop into a cancer cell. Which of the following kinds of genes would you expect to be mutated?

choices.A: genes coding for enzymes that act in the colon
choices.B: genes involved in control of the cell cycle
choices.C: genes that are especially susceptible to mutation
choices.D: genes of the bacteria, which are abundant in the colon

questions.answer_text: genes involved in control of the cell cycle

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes a cell that is considered to be differentiated?

choices.A: The cell replicates by the process of mitosis.
choices.B: The cell loses connections to the surrounding cells.
choices.C: The cell produces proteins specific to a particular cell type.
choices.D: The cell appears to be different from the surrounding cells.

questions.answer_text: The cell produces proteins specific to a particular cell type.

questions.stem: When the Bicoid protein is expressed in Drosophila, divisions between cells in the embryo are not yet fully developed. This information helps to explain which observation by Nüsslein- Volhard and Wieschaus?

choices.A: mRNA from the egg is translated into the Bicoid protein.
choices.B: Bicoid protein diffuses throughout the embryo in a concentration gradient.
choices.C: Bicoid protein serves as a transcription regulator.
choices.D: Bicoid protein determines the dorso-ventral axis of the embryo.

questions.answer_text: Bicoid protein diffuses throughout the embryo in a concentration gradient.

questions.stem: Which axis in the embryo does the protein product of the bicoid gene in Drosophila determine?

choices.C: posterior-dorsal axis
choices.D: posterior-ventral axis

questions.answer_text: anterior-posterior axis

questions.stem: Which of the following types of mutation would convert a proto-oncogene into an oncogene?

choices.A: a mutation that blocks transcription of the proto-oncogene
choices.B: a mutation that creates an unstable proto-oncogene mRNA
choices.C: a mutation that greatly increases the amount of the proto-oncogene protein
choices.D: a deletion of most of the proto-oncogene coding sequence

questions.answer_text: a mutation that greatly increases the amount of the proto-oncogene protein

questions.stem: Which of the following processes do normal proto-oncogenes typically exhibit?

choices.C: They stimulate normal cell growth and division.
choices.D: They are underexpressed in cancer cells.

questions.answer_text: They stimulate normal cell growth and division.

questions.stem: Which of the following functions does the product of the p53 gene carry out?

choices.B: It slows down the rate of DNA replication by interfering with the binding of DNA polymerase.
choices.C: It causes cells to reduce expression of genes involved in DNA repair.
choices.D: It allows cells to pass on mutations due to DNA damage.

questions.answer_text: It inhibits the cell cycle.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes a characteristic of tumor-suppressor gene?

choices.A: They are frequently overexpressed in cancerous cells.
choices.B: They are cancer-causing genes introduced into cells by viruses.
choices.C: They encode proteins that help prevent uncontrolled cell growth.
choices.D: They often encode proteins that stimulate the cell cycle.

questions.answer_text: They encode proteins that help prevent uncontrolled cell growth.

questions.stem: Why are BRCA1 and BRCA2 considered to be tumor-suppressor genes?

choices.A: Their normal products participate in repair of DNA damage.
choices.B: The mutant forms of either one of these prevent breast cancer.
choices.C: The normal genes make estrogen receptors.
choices.D: They block penetration of breast cells by chemical carcinogens.

questions.answer_text: Their normal products participate in repair of DNA damage.

questions.stem: Forms of the Ras protein found in tumors usually cause which of the following events to occur?

choices.C: cell division to cease
choices.D: excessive cell division

questions.answer_text: excessive cell division

questions.stem: A genetic test to detect predisposition to cancer would likely examine the APC gene for involvement in which type(s) of cancer?

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. The herpesviruses are important enveloped DNA viruses that cause disease in vertebrates and in some invertebrates such as oysters. Some of the human forms are herpes simplex virus (HSV) types I and II, causing facial and genital lesions, and the varicella zoster virus (VSV), causing chicken pox and shingles. Each of these three actively infects nervous tissue. Primary infections are fairly mild, but the virus is not then cleared from the host; rather, viral genomes are maintained in cells in a latent phase. The virus can later reactivate, replicate again, and infect others. In electron micrographs of HSV infection, it can be seen that the intact virus initially reacts with cell-surface proteoglycans, then with specific receptors. This is later followed by viral capsids docking with nuclear pores. Afterward, the capsids go from being full to being "empty." Which of the following statements best fits these observations?

choices.A: Viral capsids are needed for the cell to become infected; only the capsids enter the nucleus.
choices.B: The viral envelope is not required for infectivity, since the envelope does not enter the nucleus.
choices.C: Only the genetic material of the virus is involved in the cell's infectivity, and is injected like the genome of a phage.
choices.D: The viral envelope mediates entry into the cell, the capsid mediates entry into the nuclear membrane, and the genome is all that enters the nucleus.

questions.answer_text: The viral envelope mediates entry into the cell, the capsid mediates entry into the nuclear membrane, and the genome is all that enters the nucleus.

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. Poliovirus is an RNA virus of the picornavirus group, which uses its RNA as mRNA. At its 5′ end, the RNA genome has a viral protein (VPg) instead of a 5′ cap. This is followed by a non- translated leader sequence, and then a single long protein-coding region (~7,000 nucleotides), followed by a poly-A tail. Observations were made that used radioactive amino acids similar in structure to those that are found in viruses and other organisms. Short-period use of the radioactive amino acids result in labeling of only very long proteins, while longer periods of labeling result in several different short polypeptides. What conclusion is most consistent with the results of the radioactive labeling experiment?

choices.A: Host cell ribosomes only translate the viral code into short polypeptides.
choices.B: The RNA is only translated into a single long polypeptide, which is then cleaved into shorter ones.
choices.C: The RNA is translated into short polypeptides, which are subsequently assembled into large ones.
choices.D: The large radioactive polypeptides are coded by the host, whereas the short ones are coded for by the virus.

questions.answer_text: The RNA is only translated into a single long polypeptide, which is then cleaved into shorter ones.

questions.stem: Use the following figure and information to answer the question(s) below. Cells were infected with approximately 1,000 copies of either virus A or virus B at the 0 time point. questions.stem: HIV is inactivated in the laboratory after a few minutes of sitting at room temperature, but the flu virus is still active after sitting for several hours. What are the practical consequences of these findings?

choices.A: HIV can be transmitted more easily from person to person than the flu virus.

questions.stem: Viruses use the host cell's machinery to make copies of themselves. However, some human viruses require a type of replication that humans do not normally have. For example, humans normally do not have the ability to convert RNA into DNA. How can these types of viruses infect humans, when human cells cannot perform a particular role that the virus requires?

choices.A: The virus causes mutations in the human cells, resulting in the formation of new enzymes that are capable of performing these roles.

questions.stem: The first class of antiviral drugs developed to treat HIV infection, such as AZT, were known as reverse transcriptase inhibitors. How did these drugs carry out their functions?

questions.stem: The difference between vertical and horizontal transmission of plant viruses is that vertical transmission is ________.

questions.stem: What are prions?

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. Some of the human forms are herpes simplex virus (HSV) types I and II, causing facial and genital lesions, and the varicella zoster virus (VSV), causing chicken pox and shingles. Primary infections are fairly mild, but the virus is not then cleared from the host; rather, viral genomes are maintained in cells in a latent phase. questions.stem: What is difference between an epidemic and a pandemic?

questions.stem: Will treating a viral infection with antibiotics affect the course of the infection?

questions.answer_text: No; antibiotics work by inhibiting enzymes specific to bacteria. Antibiotics have no effect on eukaryotic or virally encoded enzymes.

questions.stem: Why do scientists consider HIV to be an emerging virus?

choices.C: HIV suddenly became apparent and widespread in the 1980s.
