questions.stem: To cause a human pandemic, the H5N1 avian flu virus would have to

choices.A: spread to primates such as chimpanzees.
choices.B: develop into a virus with a different host range.
choices.C: become capable of human-to-human transmission.
choices.D: become much more pathogenic.

questions.answer_text: become capable of human-to-human transmission.

questions.stem: A bacterium is infected with an experimentally constructed bacteriophage composed of the T2 phage protein coat and T4 phage DNA. The new phages produced would have

choices.C: T2 protein and T2 DNA.
choices.D: T4 protein and T4 DNA.

questions.answer_text: T4 protein and T4 DNA.

questions.stem: RNA viruses require their own supply of certain enzymes because

choices.A: host cells rapidly destroy the viruses.
choices.B: host cells lack enzymes that can replicate the viral genome.
choices.C: these enzymes translate viral mRNA into proteins.
choices.D: these enzymes penetrate host cell membranes.

questions.answer_text: host cells lack enzymes that can replicate the viral genome.

questions.stem: Which of the following processes helps bacterial cells protect their own DNA from restriction enzymes (endonucleases)?

choices.A: adding methyl groups to adenines and cytosines
choices.B: using DNA ligase to seal the bacterial DNA into a closed circle
choices.C: adding histones to protect the double-stranded DNA
choices.D: forming "sticky ends" of bacterial DNA to prevent the enzyme (endonuclease) from attaching

questions.answer_text: adding methyl groups to adenines and cytosines

questions.stem: What is the most logical sequence of steps for splicing foreign DNA into a plasmid and inserting the plasmid into a bacterium? I. Transform bacteria with a recombinant DNA molecule. II. Cut the plasmid DNA using restriction enzymes (endonucleases). III. Extract plasmid DNA from bacterial cells. IV. Hydrogen-bond the plasmid DNA to non-plasmid DNA fragments. V. Use ligase to seal plasmid DNA to non-plasmid DNA.

choices.C: III, IV, V, I, II
choices.D: IV, V, I, II, III

questions.answer_text: III, II, IV, V, I

questions.stem: A principal problem with inserting an unmodified mammalian gene into a plasmid and then getting that gene expressed in bacteria is that ________.

choices.A: prokaryotes use a different genetic code from that of eukaryotes
choices.B: bacteria translate only mRNAs that have multiple messages
choices.C: bacteria cannot remove eukaryotic introns
choices.D: bacterial RNA polymerase cannot make RNA complementary to mammalian DNA

questions.answer_text: bacteria cannot remove eukaryotic introns

questions.stem: Why are yeast cells frequently used as hosts for cloning?

choices.B: They can remove exons from mRNA.
choices.C: They do not have plasmids.
choices.D: They are eukaryotic cells.

questions.answer_text: They are eukaryotic cells.

questions.stem: Why is sequencing an entire genome, such as that of C. elegans, a nematode, important for genetic research?

choices.A: It allows researchers to use the sequence to build a "better" nematode, which is resistant to disease.
choices.B: It allows research on a group of organisms we do not usually care much about.
choices.C: A sequence that is found to have a particular function in the nematode is likely to have a closely related function in vertebrates.
choices.D: A sequence that is found to have no introns in the nematode genome is likely to have acquired the introns from higher organisms.

questions.answer_text: A sequence that is found to have a particular function in the nematode is likely to have a closely related function in vertebrates.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods would be most successful in attempting to introduce a particular piece of DNA into an animal cell?

choices.B: introducing a plasmid into the cell
choices.C: infecting the mouse cell with a Ti plasmid
choices.D: transcription and translation

questions.answer_text: electroporation followed by recombination

questions.stem: Why is it so important to be able to amplify DNA fragments when studying genes?

choices.A: Before amplification, DNA fragments are likely to bind to RNA and would no longer be able to be analyzed.
choices.B: A gene may represent only a millionth of the cell's DNA.
choices.C: Restriction enzymes (endonucleases) cut DNA into fragments that are too small.
choices.D: A clone requires multiple copies of each gene per clone.

questions.answer_text: A gene may represent only a millionth of the cell's DNA.

questions.stem: Pax-6 is a gene that is involved in eye formation in many invertebrates, such as Drosophila. Pax-6 is also found in vertebrates. A Pax-6 gene from a mouse can be expressed in a fly and the protein (PAX-6) leads to a compound fly eye. This information suggests which of the following characteristics of this gene?

choices.A: Pax-6 genes are identical in nucleotide sequence.
choices.B: PAX-6 proteins have identical amino acid sequences.
choices.C: Pax-6 is highly conserved and shows shared evolutionary ancestry.
choices.D: PAX-6 proteins are different for formation of different kinds of eyes.

questions.answer_text: Pax-6 is highly conserved and shows shared evolutionary ancestry.

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics of Taq polymerase make it useful in the PCR process?

choices.A: It is heat stable and can withstand the heating step of PCR.
choices.B: Only minute amounts are needed for each cycle of PCR.
choices.C: It binds more readily than other polymerases to the primers.
choices.D: It has regions that are complementary to the primers.

questions.answer_text: It is heat stable and can withstand the heating step of PCR.

questions.stem: Use the figure to answer the following question. Which of the following enzymes was used to produce the molecule of DNA in the figure?

choices.C: RNA polymerase
choices.D: DNA polymerase

questions.answer_text: a restriction enzyme (endonuclease)

questions.stem: Use the figure to answer the following question. The segment of DNA shown in the figure has restriction sites I and II, which create restriction fragments A, B, and C. Which of the gels produced by electrophoresis best represents the separation and identity of these fragments?
For which of the following processes can dideoxyribonucleotides be used?

choices.A: to separate different sized DNA fragments
choices.C: to sequence a DNA fragment
choices.D: to visualize DNA expression

questions.answer_text: to sequence a DNA fragment

questions.stem: Many identical copies of genes cloned in bacteria are produced as a result of which of the following processes?

choices.C: transformation
choices.D: plasmid and bacterial cell reproduction

questions.answer_text: plasmid and bacterial cell reproduction

questions.stem: Which of the following sequences is most likely to be cut by a restriction enzyme?

choices.C: 5′-AAAATT-3′ 3′-TTTTAA-5′
choices.D: 5′-ACTACT-3′ 3′-TGATGA-5′

questions.answer_text: 5′-AATATT-3′ 3′-TTATAA-5′

questions.stem: What information is critical to the success of polymerase chain reaction (PCR) itself?

choices.A: The DNA sequence of the ends of the DNA to be amplified must be known.
choices.B: The complete DNA sequence of the DNA to be amplified must be known.
choices.C: The sequence of restriction-enzyme recognition sites in the DNA to be amplified must be known.
choices.D: The sequence of restriction-enzyme recognition sites in the DNA to be amplified and in the plasmid where the amplified DNA fragment will be cloned must be known.

questions.answer_text: The DNA sequence of the ends of the DNA to be amplified must be known.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly lists the processes in order for one cycle of polymerase chain reaction (PCR)?

choices.A: denature DNA; add fresh enzyme; anneal primers; add dNTPs; extend primers
choices.B: anneal primers; denature DNA; extend primers
choices.C: extend primers; anneal primers; denature DNA
choices.D: denature DNA; anneal primers; extend primers

questions.answer_text: denature DNA; anneal primers; extend primers

questions.stem: The final step in a Sanger DNA sequencing reaction is to run the DNA fragments on a gel. What purpose does this serve?

choices.A: It adds ddNTP to the end of each DNA fragment.
choices.B: It changes the length of the DNA fragments.
choices.C: It separates DNA fragments based on their charge.
choices.D: It separates DNA fragments generated during the sequencing reaction based on one- nucleotide differences in their size.

questions.answer_text: It separates DNA fragments generated during the sequencing reaction based on one- nucleotide differences in their size.

questions.stem: How can a gene that contains introns be made shorter (but remain functional) for genetic engineering purposes?

choices.A: using a restriction enzyme (endonuclease) to cut the gene into shorter pieces
choices.B: using reverse transcriptase to reconstruct the gene from its mRNA
choices.C: using DNA polymerase to reconstruct the gene from its polypeptide product
choices.D: using DNA ligase to put together fragments of the DNA that code for a particular polypeptide

questions.answer_text: using reverse transcriptase to reconstruct the gene from its mRNA

questions.stem: Which of the following enzymes is required to make complementary DNA (cDNA) from RNA?

choices.C: DNA ligase
choices.D: reverse transcriptase

questions.answer_text: reverse transcriptase

questions.stem: How have DNA microarrays made a huge impact on genomic studies?

choices.A: They can be used to eliminate the function of any gene in the genome.
choices.B: They can be used to introduce entire genomes into bacterial cells.
choices.C: They allow the expression of many or even all of the genes in the genome to be compared at once.
choices.D: They allow physical maps of the genome to be assembled in a very short time.

questions.answer_text: They allow the expression of many or even all of the genes in the genome to be compared at once.

questions.stem: RNAi methodology uses double-stranded pieces of RNA to trigger breakdown of a specific mRNA or inhibit its translation. For which of the following processes might this technique be useful?

choices.A: to decrease the production from a harmful mutated gene
choices.B: to destroy an unwanted allele in a homozygous individual
choices.C: to form a knockout organism that will not pass the deleted sequence to its progeny
choices.D: to raise the concentration of a desired protein

questions.answer_text: to decrease the production from a harmful mutated gene

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes how RNA interference (RNAi) silences selected genes?

choices.A: Synthetic double-stranded RNA molecules stop transcription from occurring.
choices.B: Synthetic double-stranded RNA molecules stop DNA replication from occurring.
choices.C: Synthetic double-stranded RNA molecules trigger the breakdown of a gene's messenger RNA.
choices.D: Synthetic double-stranded RNA molecules stop mitosis from occurring.

questions.answer_text: Synthetic double-stranded RNA molecules trigger the breakdown of a gene's messenger RNA.

questions.stem: In large scale, genome-wide association studies in humans, what types of genetic markers do researchers look for?

choices.A: lengthy sequences that might be shared by most members of a population
choices.B: SNPs where one allele is found more often in persons with a particular disorder than in healthy controls
choices.C: SNPs where one allele is found in families with a particular introns sequence
choices.D: SNPs where one allele is found in two or more adjacent genes

questions.answer_text: SNPs where one allele is found more often in persons with a particular disorder than in healthy controls

questions.stem: For a particular microarray assay (DNA chip), cDNA has been made from the mRNAs of a dozen patients' breast tumor biopsies. Which of the following types of evidence will researchers be looking for in order to determine if the cells are cancerous?

choices.A: a particular gene that is amplified in all or most of the patient samples
choices.B: a pattern of fluorescence that indicates which cells are over proliferating
choices.C: a pattern shared among some or all of the samples that indicates gene expression differing from control samples
choices.D: a group of cDNAs that match those in non-breast cancer control samples from the same population

questions.answer_text: a pattern shared among some or all of the samples that indicates gene expression differing from control samples

questions.stem: In a comparison of two DNA sequences found in the same location on homologous chromosomes, one of the homologs carries the sequence 5′-AACTACGA-3′, and the other homolog carries the sequence 5′-AACTTCGA-3′. Within a population, you discover that each of these sequences is common. Which of the following statements correctly describes theses sequences?

choices.A: They contain a SNP that may be useful for genetic mapping.
choices.B: They can identify a protein-coding region of a gene.
choices.C: They may cause disease.
choices.D: They may carry out RNA interference.

questions.answer_text: They contain a SNP that may be useful for genetic mapping.

questions.stem: Which of the following processes uses labeled probes to visualize the expression of genes in whole tissues and organisms?

choices.C: DNA microarrays
choices.D: RNA interference

questions.answer_text: in situ hybridization

questions.stem: Which of the following processes is most like the formation of identical twins?

choices.C: use of adult stem cells
choices.D: organismal cloning

questions.answer_text: organismal cloning

questions.stem: In 1997, Dolly the sheep was cloned. Which of the following processes was used?

choices.A: replication and dedifferentiation of adult stem cells from sheep bone marrow
choices.B: separation of an early stage sheep blastula into separate cells, one of which was incubated in a surrogate ewe
choices.C: transfer of an adult cell's nucleus into an enucleated sheep egg, followed by incubation in a surrogate
choices.D: isolation of stem cells from a lamb embryo and production of a zygote equivalent

questions.answer_text: transfer of an adult cell's nucleus into an enucleated sheep egg, followed by incubation in a surrogate

questions.stem: Which of the following problems with animal cloning might result in premature death of the clones?

choices.A: use of pluripotent instead of totipotent stem cells
choices.B: use of nuclear DNA as well as mtDNA
choices.C: abnormal gene regulation due to variant methylation
choices.D: the indefinite replication of totipotent stem cells

questions.answer_text: abnormal gene regulation due to variant methylation

questions.stem: Reproductive cloning of human embryos is generally considered unethical. However, on the subject of therapeutic cloning, there is a wider divergence of opinion. Which of the following statements provides a likely explanation?

choices.A: The use of adult stem cells is likely to produce more cell types than the use of embryonic stem cells.
choices.B: Cloning to produce embryonic stem cells may lead to great medical benefits for many.
choices.C: Cloning to produce stem cells relies on a different initial procedure than reproductive cloning.
choices.D: A clone that lives until the blastocyst stage does not yet have human DNA.

questions.answer_text: Cloning to produce embryonic stem cells may lead to great medical benefits for many.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes one of the main differences between embryonic stem cells and adult stem cells?

choices.A: Embryonic stem cells only differentiate into only eggs and sperm, and adult stem cells differentiate into any type of cell.
choices.B: Embryonic stem cells can give rise to all cell types in the organism, and adult stem cells cannot.
choices.C: Embryonic stem cells can continue to reproduce for an indefinite period, and adult stem cells cannot.
choices.D: One aim of using embryonic stem cells is to provide cells for repair of diseased tissue.

questions.answer_text: Embryonic stem cells can give rise to all cell types in the organism, and adult stem cells cannot.

questions.stem: A researcher is using adult stem cells and comparing them to other adult cells from the same tissue. Which of the following findings is likely from this comparison?

choices.A: The cells from the two sources exhibit different patterns of DNA methylation.
choices.B: Adult stem cells have more DNA nucleotides than their counterparts.
choices.C: The two kinds of cells have virtually identical gene expression patterns in microarrays.
choices.D: The non-stem cells have fewer repressed genes.

questions.answer_text: The cells from the two sources exhibit different patterns of DNA methylation.

questions.stem: In animals, what is the difference between reproductive cloning and therapeutic cloning?

choices.A: Reproductive cloning uses totipotent cells, whereas therapeutic cloning does not.
choices.B: Reproductive cloning uses embryonic stem cells, whereas therapeutic cloning does not.
choices.C: Therapeutic cloning uses nuclei of adult cells transplanted into enucleated unfertilized eggs.
choices.D: Therapeutic cloning supplies cells for repair of diseased or injured organs.

questions.answer_text: Therapeutic cloning supplies cells for repair of diseased or injured organs.

questions.stem: The first cloned cat, called Carbon Copy, was a calico, but she looked significantly different from her female parent. Why was this the case with this clone?

choices.A: The cloning was done poorly and it was likely that some contaminating cat DNA became part of Carbon Copy's genome.
choices.B: Fur color genes in cats is determined by differential acetylation patterns.
choices.C: Cloned animals have been found to have a higher frequency of transposon activation.
choices.D: X chromosome inactivation in the embryo is random and produces different patterns.

questions.answer_text: X chromosome inactivation in the embryo is random and produces different patterns.

questions.stem: In recent times, it has been shown that adult cells can be induced to become pluripotent stem cells (iPS). To make this conversion, what has been done to the adult cells?

choices.A: A retrovirus is used to introduce four specific master regulatory genes.
choices.B: The adult stem cells must be fused with embryonic cells.
choices.C: Cytoplasm from embryonic cells is injected into the adult cells.
choices.D: The nucleus of an embryonic cell is used to replace the nucleus of an adult cell.

questions.answer_text: A retrovirus is used to introduce four specific master regulatory genes.

questions.stem: Suppose that a researcher is successful at producing induced pluripotent stem cells (iPS) for replacement of pancreatic insulin-producing cells for people with type 1 diabetes. Which of the following could still pose problems for this individual? I. the possibility that, once introduced into the patient, the iPS cells produce non-pancreatic cells II. the failure of the iPS cells to take up residence in the pancreas III. the inability of the iPS cells to respond to appropriate regulatory signals

choices.C: III only
choices.D: I, II, and III

questions.answer_text: I, II, and III

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes one characteristic of genetically engineered plants?

choices.A: They are more difficult to develop than genetically engineered animals.
choices.B: They include transgenic rice plants that can grow in water more salty than seawater.
choices.C: They are used in research but not yet in commercial agricultural production.
choices.D: They are banned throughout the world.

questions.answer_text: They include transgenic rice plants that can grow in water more salty than seawater.

questions.stem: Scientists developed a set of guidelines to address the safety of DNA technology. Which of the following safety measures is one that has been adopted by researchers?

choices.A: Microorganisms used in recombinant DNA experiments must be genetically crippled to ensure that they cannot survive outside of the laboratory.
choices.B: Genetically modified organisms are not allowed to be part of our food supply.
choices.C: Transgenic plants are engineered so that the plant genes cannot hybridize.
choices.D: Experiments involving HIV or other potentially dangerous viruses have been banned.

questions.answer_text: Microorganisms used in recombinant DNA experiments must be genetically crippled to ensure that they cannot survive outside of the laboratory.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes one of the technical reasons why gene therapy is problematic in humans?

choices.A: Most cells with an engineered gene do not produce gene product.
choices.B: Cells with transferred genes are unlikely to replicate.
choices.C: Transferred genes may not have appropriately controlled activity.
choices.D: mRNA from transferred genes cannot be translated.

questions.answer_text: Transferred genes may not have appropriately controlled activity.

questions.stem: One possible use of transgenic plants is in the production of human proteins, such as vaccines. Which of the following issues is a possible hindrance that must be overcome in order for this process to work properly?

choices.A: prevention of transmission of plant allergens to the vaccine recipients
choices.B: prevention of vaccine-containing plants being consumed by insects
choices.C: use of plant cells to translate non-plant-derived mRNA
choices.D: inability of the human digestive system to accept plant-derived protein

questions.answer_text: prevention of transmission of plant allergens to the vaccine recipients

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics of short tandem repeats (STRs) DNA makes it useful for DNA fingerprinting?

choices.A: The number of repeats is highly variable from person to person or animal to animal.
choices.B: The sequence of DNA that is repeated varies significantly from individual to individual.
choices.C: The sequence variation is acted upon differently by natural selection in different environments.
choices.D: Every racial and ethnic group has inherited different short tandem repeats.

questions.answer_text: The number of repeats is highly variable from person to person or animal to animal.

questions.stem: Transgenic mice are useful to human researchers because they ________.

choices.A: can be valuable animal models of human disease
choices.B: are essential for mapping human genes
choices.C: are now used in place of bacteria for cloning human genes
choices.D: were instrumental in pinpointing the location of the huntingtin gene

questions.answer_text: can be valuable animal models of human disease

questions.stem: Which of the following information or processes does gene therapy require?

choices.A: the knowledge and availability of the defective gene but not the normal allele
choices.B: the ability to introduce the normal allele into the patient
choices.C: the ability to express the introduced gene at any time in the tissue site within the patient
choices.D: the ability to introduce a defective allele into a patient

questions.answer_text: the ability to introduce the normal allele into the patient

questions.stem: What is the most favorable characteristic of retroviruses that makes them useful in gene therapy applications?

choices.C: DNA copies of retroviral genomes become integrated into the genome of the infected cell.
choices.D: Retroviruses mutate often.

questions.answer_text: DNA copies of retroviral genomes become integrated into the genome of the infected cell.

questions.stem: Why might using retroviral vectors for gene therapy increase the patient's risk of developing cancer?

choices.A: Retroviral vectors may introduce proteins from the virus.
choices.B: Retroviral vectors do not express the genes that were introduced into a patient's cells.
choices.C: Retroviral vectors do not integrate their recombinant DNA into the patient's genome.
choices.D: Retroviral vectors integrate recombinant DNA into the genome in ways that may misregulate the expression of genes at or near the site of integration.

questions.answer_text: Retroviral vectors integrate recombinant DNA into the genome in ways that may misregulate the expression of genes at or near the site of integration.

questions.stem: In the form of gene therapy used successfully for severe combined immunodeficiency syndrome, SCID-X1, how is the genetic engineering of human cells achieved?

choices.A: by injecting engineered viruses into the patient's bloodstream
choices.B: by injecting engineered viruses into the patient's bone marrow
choices.C: by treating a relative's cultured bone marrow cells with genetically engineered viruses and then injecting these cells into the patient's bone marrow
choices.D: by isolating the patient's bone marrow cells, infecting them with genetically engineered viruses, and injecting them back into the patient's bone marrow

questions.answer_text: by isolating the patient's bone marrow cells, infecting them with genetically engineered viruses, and injecting them back into the patient's bone marrow

questions.stem: One predicted aspect of climate change is that climates, including precipitation and temperature, over most of Earth will become more variable. Which of the following is a good strategy for genetically engineering crops if this is true?

choices.A: Use only plant crops that are genetically engineered.
choices.B: Genetically engineer most crops to withstand very long droughts.
choices.C: Genetically engineer several genotypes within single crop types.
choices.D: Genetically engineer the fastest growing crops possible.

questions.answer_text: Genetically engineer several genotypes within single crop types.

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. In an experiment, DNA from the linear form of the bacteriophage Lambda was cut into fragments using the restriction enzyme Hind III. Hind III cuts the Lambda DNA between the adenine nucleotides on the complimentary strands in a specific sequence, as indicated in the diagram, producing eight different size fragments. These fragments are then separated with an electrical current based on size after the DNA fragments are placed in a porous gel, a process called gel electrophoresis. Select an observation that best describes a correct aspect of the two processes of restriction digest and gel electrophoresis.

choices.A: When separated on a gel, the pattern of DNA bands will be characteristic of those cut with Hind III; different restriction enzymes will not produce these same fragments.
choices.B: The sequence 5′-AAGCTT-3′ is found eight times in the Lambda genome, and the restriction enzyme Hind III finds each location.
choices.C: If an electrical current is not used, eight separate DNA bands would be visible, but they would not be separated as much as when an electrical current is used.
choices.D: Only the restriction enzyme Hind III can be used to cut Lambda DNA since restriction enzymes are specific to the type of DNA they can cut.

questions.answer_text: When separated on a gel, the pattern of DNA bands will be characteristic of those cut with Hind III; different restriction enzymes will not produce these same fragments.

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. Organisms share many conserved core processes and features, including transcription and translation, using a uniform genetic code. Scientists have used these shared processes and features in biotechnology. For example, for the process of some transformations, a plasmid is constructed when a eukaryotic gene of interest is added with an antibiotic resistant gene such as beta-lactamase, which is used for ampicillin resistance. This plasmid is then inserted into a prokaryotic bacterial cell, such as E. coli, through a transformation process that leads to the production of the product protein from the eukaryotic organism. To culture the bacteria and obtain the protein product, the bacteria must grow. Select the appropriate condition to determine if the plasmid has entered the E. coli bacterial cell.

choices.A: nutrient broth to which no antibiotic has been added
choices.B: water to which ampicillin has been added
choices.C: nutrient broth to which ampicillin has been added
choices.D: nutrient broth to which other resistant bacteria have been added

questions.answer_text: nutrient broth to which ampicillin has been added

questions.stem: In DNA technology, the term vector can refer to

choices.A: the enzyme that cuts DNA into restriction fragments.
choices.B: the sticky end of a DNA fragment.
choices.C: a SNP marker.
choices.D: a plasmid used to transfer DNA into a living cell.

questions.answer_text: a plasmid used to transfer DNA into a living cell.

questions.stem: Which of the following tools of DNA technology is incorrectly paired with its use?

choices.B: DNA ligase—cutting DNA, creating sticky ends of restriction fragments
choices.C: DNA polymerase—polymerase chain reaction to amplify sections of DNA
choices.D: reverse transcriptase—production of cDNA from mRNA

questions.answer_text: DNA ligase—cutting DNA, creating sticky ends of restriction fragments

questions.stem: Plants are more readily manipulated by genetic engineering than are animals because

choices.A: plant genes do not contain introns.
choices.B: more vectors are available for transferring recombinant DNA into plant cells.
choices.C: a somatic plant cell can often give rise to a complete plant.
choices.D: plant cells have larger nuclei.

questions.answer_text: a somatic plant cell can often give rise to a complete plant.

questions.stem: A paleontologist has recovered a bit of tissue from the 400-year-old preserved skin of an extinct dodo (a bird). To compare a specific region of the DNA from a sample with DNA from living birds, which of the following would be most useful for increasing the amount of dodo DNA available for testing?

choices.C: electroporation
choices.D: gel electrophoresis

questions.answer_text: polymerase chain reaction (PCR)

questions.stem: DNA technology has many medical applications. Which of the following is not done routinely at present?

choices.A: production of hormones for treating diabetes and dwarfism
choices.B: analysis of gene expression for more informed cancer treatments
choices.C: gene editing by the CRISPR-Cas9 system in viable human embryos to correct genetic diseases
choices.D: prenatal identification of genetic disease alleles

questions.answer_text: gene editing by the CRISPR-Cas9 system in viable human embryos to correct genetic diseases

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true of cDNA produced using human brain tissue as the starting material?

choices.A: It can be amplified by the polymerase chain reaction.
choices.B: It was produced from pre-mRNA using reverse transcriptase.
choices.C: It can be labeled and used as a probe to detect genes expressed in the brain.
choices.D: It lacks the introns of the pre-mRNA.

questions.answer_text: It was produced from pre-mRNA using reverse transcriptase.

questions.stem: Expression of a cloned eukaryotic gene in a bacterial cell involves many challenges. The use of mRNA and reverse transcriptase is part of a strategy to solve the problem of

choices.C: nucleic acid hybridization.
choices.D: restriction fragment ligation.

questions.answer_text: post-transcriptional processing.

questions.stem: Which of the following sequences in double-stranded DNA is most likely to be recognized as a cutting site for a restriction enzyme?

choices.C: ACCA TGGT
choices.D: AAAA TTTT

questions.answer_text: GGCC CCGG

questions.stem: What is metagenomics?

choices.A: genomics as applied to a species that most typifies the average phenotype of its genus
choices.B: the sequencing of one or two representative genes from several species
choices.C: the sequencing of only the most highly conserved genes in a lineage
choices.D: sequencing DNA from a group of species from the same ecosystem

questions.answer_text: sequencing DNA from a group of species from the same ecosystem

questions.stem: Which of the following processes is an early step in the whole-genome shotgun approach to sequencing?

choices.A: break genomic DNA at random sites
choices.B: map the position of cloned DNA fragments
choices.C: randomly select DNA primers and hybridize these to random positions of chromosomes in preparation for sequencing

questions.answer_text: break genomic DNA at random sites

questions.stem: Using modern techniques of sequencing by synthesis and the shotgun approach, sequences are assembled into chromosomes by ________.

choices.A: placing them on previously generated genetic maps
choices.C: computer analysis looking for sequence overlaps
choices.D: cloning them into plasmid vectors, placing them on previously generated genetic maps, followed by computer analysis looking for sequence overlaps

questions.answer_text: computer analysis looking for sequence overlaps

questions.stem: Which of the following statements defines proteomics?

choices.A: It is the linkage of each gene to a particular protein.
choices.B: It is the study of the full protein set and its properties.
choices.C: It is the totality of the functional possibilities of a single protein.
choices.D: It is the study of how amino acids are ordered in a protein.

questions.answer_text: It is the study of the full protein set and its properties.

questions.stem: Bioinformatics can be used to scan for short sequences that specify known mRNAs, called ________.

choices.C: proteomes
choices.D: short tandem repeats

questions.answer_text: expressed sequence tags

questions.stem: Which of the following processes correctly describes gene annotation in bioinformatics?

choices.A: finding transcriptional start and stop sites, RNA splice sites, and ESTs in DNA sequences
choices.B: assigning names to newly discovered genes
choices.C: describing the functions of noncoding regions of the genome
choices.D: matching the corresponding phenotypes of different species

questions.answer_text: finding transcriptional start and stop sites, RNA splice sites, and ESTs in DNA sequences

questions.stem: Bioinformatics includes ________. I. using computer programs to align DNA sequences II. creating recombinant DNA from separate species III. developing computer-based tools for genome analysis IV. using mathematical tools to make sense of biological systems

choices.C: II and IV
choices.D: I, III, and IV

questions.answer_text: I, III, and IV

questions.stem: After finding a new medicinal plant, a pharmaceutical company decides to determine if the plant has genes similar to those of other known medicinal plants. What would annotation of the genome of this plant allow the company to determine?

choices.A: what proteins are produced by the plant
choices.B: what mRNA transcripts are produced by the plant
choices.C: identify genes and determine their functions
choices.D: identify the location of mRNA within the plant cells

questions.answer_text: identify genes and determine their functions

questions.stem: If the sequence of a cDNA has matches with DNA sequences in the genome, then this genomic DNA could be described by which of the following statements?

choices.A: The sequence codes for a protein.
choices.B: The sequence codes for an rRNA.
choices.C: The sequence is part of an intron.
choices.D: The sequence is a regulatory sequence.

questions.answer_text: The sequence codes for a protein.

questions.stem: Which of the following techniques would be most appropriate to test the hypothesis that humans and chimps differ in the expression of a large set of shared genes?

choices.C: DNA sequencing
choices.D: protein-protein interaction assays

questions.answer_text: DNA microarray analysis

questions.stem: What can proteomics reveal that genomics cannot?

choices.A: the number of genes characteristic of a species
choices.C: the set of proteins present within a cell or tissue type
choices.D: the movement of transposable elements within the genome

questions.answer_text: the set of proteins present within a cell or tissue type

questions.stem: A sequence database such as GenBank could be used to carry out which of the following processes?

choices.A: Determine the expression pattern for specific human genes.
choices.B: Construct a tree to determine the evolutionary relationships between various bird species.
choices.C: Search for genes that have not yet been identified in eukaryotic genomes.
choices.D: Compare patterns of gene expression in cancerous and non-cancerous cells.

questions.answer_text: Construct a tree to determine the evolutionary relationships between various bird species.

questions.stem: Current analysis indicates that less than 2% of the human genome codes for proteins. Based on the systems approach employed by the ENCODE project, what percentage of the genome is estimated to be transcribed at some point in at least one cell type?

choices.C: about 75%

questions.answer_text: about 75%

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is a correct representation of gene density?

choices.C: Humans have ~20,000 protein-encoding genes in a 3,000 Mb.
choices.D: Saccharomyces has a genome 40 times the size of a human genome.

questions.answer_text: Humans have ~20,000 protein-encoding genes in a 3,000 Mb.

questions.stem: Why might the cricket genome have eleven times as many base pairs as that of Drosophila melanogaster?

choices.C: Crickets must have more noncoding DNA.
choices.D: Crickets must make many more proteins.

questions.answer_text: Crickets must have more noncoding DNA.

questions.stem: Which of the following conclusions has led to the comparison between the number of human genes and those of other animal species?

choices.A: The density of the human genome is far higher than in most other animals.
choices.B: The number of proteins expressed by the human genome is far greater than the number of its genes.
choices.C: Most human DNA consists of genes for protein, tRNA, rRNA, and miRNA.
choices.D: The genomes of most other organisms are significantly smaller than the human genome.

questions.answer_text: The number of proteins expressed by the human genome is far greater than the number of its genes.

questions.stem: Why is it more difficult to identify eukaryotic genes than prokaryotic genes using genomic techniques?

choices.A: The proteins are larger in eukaryotes than in prokaryotes.
choices.B: The coding portions of genes in eukaryotes are shorter than in prokaryotes.
choices.C: There are no start codons in eukaryotic genes.
choices.D: There are introns in eukaryotic genes.

questions.answer_text: There are introns in eukaryotic genes.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes one of the characteristics of alternative splicing in vertebrate genomes?

choices.A: Vertebrate genomes can produce more than one polypeptide from a single gene.
choices.B: Vertebrate genomes can produce only one polypeptide from a single gene.
choices.C: Vertebrate genomes are always smaller than other organisms.
choices.D: Alternative splicing leaves introns in vertebrate genes after they are transcribed.

questions.answer_text: Vertebrate genomes can produce more than one polypeptide from a single gene.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes one characteristic of a multigene family?

choices.A: A multigene family includes multiple genes whose products must be coordinately expressed.
choices.B: A multigene family includes genes whose sequences are very similar and that probably arose by duplication.
choices.C: A multigene family includes a gene whose exons can be spliced in a number of different ways.
choices.D: A multigene family includes a highly conserved gene found in a number of different species.

questions.answer_text: A multigene family includes genes whose sequences are very similar and that probably arose by duplication.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes one characteristic of retrotransposons?

choices.A: They use an RNA molecule as an intermediate in transposition.
choices.B: They are found only in animal cells.
choices.C: They generally move by a cut-and-paste mechanism.
choices.D: They contribute a significant portion of the genetic variability seen within a population of gametes.

questions.answer_text: They use an RNA molecule as an intermediate in transposition.

questions.stem: In humans, the embryonic and fetal forms of hemoglobin have a higher affinity for oxygen than that of adults. Why is this the case?

choices.A: Nonidentical genes produce different versions of globins during development.
choices.B: Pseudogenes interfere with gene expression in adults.
choices.C: The attachment of methyl groups to cytosine following birth changes the type of hemoglobin produced.
choices.D: Histone proteins change shape during embryonic development.

questions.answer_text: Nonidentical genes produce different versions of globins during development.

questions.stem: Why is sequencing of eukaryotic genomes more difficult than sequencing genomes of bacteria or archaea?

choices.A: It is due to the large size of eukaryotic proteins.
choices.B: Eukaryotic genomes contain sequences for hard-to-find proteins.
choices.C: There is a high proportion of G-C base pairs in eukaryotic DNA, which makes sequencing difficult to complete.
choices.D: The large size of eukaryotic genomes and the large amount of eukaryotic repetitive DNA make sequencing difficult.

questions.answer_text: The large size of eukaryotic genomes and the large amount of eukaryotic repetitive DNA make sequencing difficult.

questions.stem: How do transposons and retrotransposons differ in how they move around in a genome?

choices.A: Transposons move by viruses and retrotransposons move by plasmids.
choices.B: Transposons move by means of a DNA intermediate and retrotransposons move by means of an RNA intermediate.
choices.C: Transposons move by means of a RNA intermediate and retrotransposons move by means of an DNA intermediate.
choices.D: Transposons move by viruses and retrotransposons move by bacteria.

questions.answer_text: Transposons move by means of a DNA intermediate and retrotransposons move by means of an RNA intermediate.

questions.stem: How do transposable elements and short tandem repeats (STRs) differ?

choices.A: STRs occur within exons; transposable elements occur within introns.
choices.B: STRs occur within introns; transposable elements occur within exons.
choices.C: STRs make up only a small percentage of a given genome while transposable elements often make up larger parts of a given genome.
choices.D: The repeated unit in STRs is much larger than the repeated unit of transposable elements.

questions.answer_text: STRs make up only a small percentage of a given genome while transposable elements often make up larger parts of a given genome.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be duplicated in a genome?

choices.C: only entire chromosomes
choices.D: DNA sequences, chromosomes, or sets of chromosomes

questions.answer_text: DNA sequences, chromosomes, or sets of chromosomes

questions.stem: Unequal crossing over during prophase I can result in one sister chromosome with a deletion and another with a duplication. A mutated form of hemoglobin, so-called hemoglobin Lepore, exists in the human population. Hemoglobin Lepore has a deleted series of amino acids. If this mutated form was caused by unequal crossing over, what would be an expected consequence?

choices.A: There should also be persons whose hemoglobin contains two copies of the series of amino acids that is deleted in hemoglobin Lepore.
choices.B: Each of the genes in the hemoglobin gene family must show the same deletion.
choices.C: The deleted gene must have undergone exon shuffling.
choices.D: The deleted region must be located in a different area of the individual's genome.

questions.answer_text: There should also be persons whose hemoglobin contains two copies of the series of amino acids that is deleted in hemoglobin Lepore.

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. The figure shows a diagram of blocks of genes on human chromosome 16 and the locations of blocks of similar genes on four chromosomes of the mouse. Which of the following statements describes the result of the movement of these blocks?

choices.A: During evolutionary time, these sequences have separated and have returned to their original positions.
choices.B: DNA sequences within these blocks have become increasingly divergent.
choices.C: Sequences represented have duplicated at least three times.
choices.D: Chromosomal translocations have moved blocks of sequences to other chromosomes.

questions.answer_text: Chromosomal translocations have moved blocks of sequences to other chromosomes.

questions.stem: Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes, and chimps have 24 pairs of chromosomes. What is the most likely explanation for these differences in human and chimp genomes?

choices.A: The common ancestor of humans and chimps had 24 pairs of chromosomes. During human evolution, two human chromosomes fused end to end.
choices.B: In the evolution of chimps, new adaptations resulted from additional chromosomal material.
choices.C: At some point in evolution, human and chimp ancestors reproduced with each other.
choices.D: Errors in mitosis resulted in an additional pair of chromosomes in chimps.

questions.answer_text: The common ancestor of humans and chimps had 24 pairs of chromosomes. During human evolution, two human chromosomes fused end to end.

questions.stem: During which of the following processes does exon shuffling occur?

choices.C: meiotic recombination
choices.D: translation

questions.answer_text: meiotic recombination

questions.stem: When gene duplication occurs to its ultimate extent by doubling all genes in a genome, which of the following results has occurred?

choices.C: creation of a polyploid
choices.D: creation of a diploid

questions.answer_text: creation of a polyploid

questions.stem: Which of the following types of genes or gene families may be created by mutations that occur in one member of a gene pair that arose from gene duplication?

choices.B: only a gene with a new function
choices.C: only a gene family with two distinct but related members
choices.D: a pseudogene, a gene with a new function, and a gene family with two distinct but related members

questions.answer_text: a pseudogene, a gene with a new function, and a gene family with two distinct but related members

questions.stem: Based on the data in the Amino Acid Sequence Identity Table, which two members of the human globin gene family are the most divergent?

choices.C: α1 and a2
choices.D: α1 and G?

questions.answer_text: α1 and G?

questions.stem: Fragments of DNA have been extracted from the remnants of extinct woolly mammoths, amplified, and sequenced. How can these fragments of DNA now be used?

choices.A: to introduce certain mammoth traits into relatives, such as elephants
choices.C: to understand the reasons why mammoths went extinct
choices.D: to better understand the evolutionary relationships among members of related taxa

questions.answer_text: to better understand the evolutionary relationships among members of related taxa

questions.stem: Homeotic genes contain a homeobox sequence that is highly conserved among very diverse species. The homeobox is the code for the domain of a protein that binds to DNA in a regulatory developmental process. Which of the following statements is therefore correct regarding homeotic genes?

choices.A: Homeotic genes are selectively expressed as an organism develops.
choices.B: Homeoboxes cannot be expressed in nonhomeotic genes.
choices.C: Homeotic genes in apes and humans are very different.
choices.D: All organisms must have homeotic genes.

questions.answer_text: Homeotic genes are selectively expressed as an organism develops.

questions.stem: A recent study compared the Homo sapiens genome with that of Neanderthals. The results of the study indicated that there was a mixing of the two genomes at some period in evolutionary history. Which of the following potential discoveries of additional data might be consistent with this hypothesis?

choices.A: some Neanderthal sequences not found in living humans
choices.B: a few modern H. sapiens with some Neanderthal sequences
choices.C: duplications of several Neanderthal genes on a Neanderthal chromosome
choices.D: some Neanderthal chromosomes that are shorter than their counterparts in living humans

questions.answer_text: a few modern H. sapiens with some Neanderthal sequences

questions.stem: Several of the different globin genes are expressed in humans, but at different times in development. Which of the listed mechanisms could allow for this?

choices.C: differential translation of mRNAs
choices.D: differential gene regulation over time

questions.answer_text: differential gene regulation over time

questions.stem: Biologists now routinely test for homology between genes in different species. If genes are determined to be homologous, how are they related to each other?

choices.A: by descent from a common ancestor
choices.C: by chance mutations
choices.D: in function but not structure

questions.answer_text: by descent from a common ancestor

questions.stem: A current view of how the human and chimpanzee can share most of their nucleotide sequences yet exhibit significant phenotypic differences is that many of the most important sequence differences alter ________.

choices.C: regulatory sequences
choices.D: environmental factors

questions.answer_text: regulatory sequences

questions.stem: Studies in knockout mice have demonstrated an important role of the FOXP2 transcription factor in the development of vocalizations. Recent sequence comparisons of the FOXP2 gene in Neanderthals and modern humans show that while the DNA sequence may be different, the protein sequence it codes for is identical. Which of the following conclusions might logically be inferred from this information?

choices.A: There was a problem with the experiment because different DNA sequences cannot result in the same protein sequence.
choices.B: The differences in DNA sequence support the hypothesis that Neanderthals were primitive beings that could only grunt.
choices.C: Human and Neanderthal vocalizations may have been more similar than previously thought.
choices.D: The experiments in mice demonstrating the function of the FOXP2 gene are not relevant to humans and Neanderthals because they are not primates.

questions.answer_text: Human and Neanderthal vocalizations may have been more similar than previously thought.

questions.stem: Comparisons of DNA sequences within the human species have revealed many variations. Which of the following variations involves duplication of relatively long stretches of DNA?

choices.C: STRs
choices.D: Transposable elements

questions.answer_text: CNVs

questions.stem: A microarray is a tool used in genetic research to determine the mRNAs being produced in a particular tissue, and their relative level of expression. Known genes can therefore be assayed for their expression in different situations. One use of the technology is in cancer diagnosis and treatment. If a known gene functions as a tumor suppressor, predict which of the following pieces of evidence would be most useful in diagnosis of a cancer due to a mutation in this tumor- suppressor gene.

choices.A: The tissue sample shows a high level of gene expression relative to a control (noncancerous) sample.
choices.B: The tissue sample responds to treatment with a mitosis-promoting compound.
choices.C: The mRNAs for the targeted tumor suppressor sequence are not being produced.
choices.D: The mRNAs for cyclins and kinases show unusually high levels of expression.

questions.answer_text: The mRNAs for the targeted tumor suppressor sequence are not being produced.

questions.stem: Bioinformatics includes all of the following except

choices.A: using computer programs to align DNA sequences.
choices.B: using DNA technology to combine DNA from two different sources in a test tube.
choices.C: developing computer-based tools for genome analysis.
choices.D: using mathematical tools to make sense of biological systems.

questions.answer_text: using DNA technology to combine DNA from two different sources in a test tube.

questions.stem: Homeotic genes

choices.A: encode transcription factors that control the expression of genes responsible for specific anatomical structures.
choices.B: are found only in Drosophila and other arthropods.
choices.C: are the only genes that contain the homeobox domain.
choices.D: encode proteins that form anatomical structures in the fly.

questions.answer_text: encode transcription factors that control the expression of genes responsible for specific anatomical structures.

questions.stem: Two eukaryotic proteins have one domain in common but are otherwise very different. Which of the following processes is most likely to have contributed to this similarity?

choices.C: exon shuffling
choices.D: random point mutations

questions.answer_text: exon shuffling

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Darwin and Wallace's theory of evolution by natural selection was revolutionary because it ________.

choices.A: was the first theory to refute the ideas of special creation
choices.B: proved that individuals acclimated to their environment over time
choices.C: dismissed the idea that species are constant and emphasized the importance of variation and change in populations
choices.D: was the first time a biologist had proposed that species changed through time

questions.answer_text: dismissed the idea that species are constant and emphasized the importance of variation and change in populations

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: The Linnaeus classification system grouped organisms by ________.

choices.A: linear hierarchy of the scala naturae
choices.C: increasingly more complex categories
choices.D: environmental location

questions.answer_text: increasingly more general categories

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Fossils found in strata reveal that ________.

choices.A: older strata carry fossils that differ greatly from living organisms
choices.B: geologic changes occur quickly on Earth
choices.C: unused body parts decrease in size
choices.D: innate drive to complexity of life

questions.answer_text: older strata carry fossils that differ greatly from living organisms

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Prior to the work of Lyell and Darwin, the prevailing belief was that Earth is ________.

choices.A: a few thousand years old, and populations are unchanging
choices.B: a few thousand years old, and populations gradually change
choices.C: millions of years old, and populations rapidly change
choices.D: millions of years old, and populations are unchanging

questions.answer_text: a few thousand years old, and populations are unchanging

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best explains why modification or change in an organ or tissue during the lifetime of an individual is not inherited?

choices.A: Characteristics acquired during an organism's life are generally not passed on through genes.
choices.B: Spontaneous mutations can result in the appearance of new traits.
choices.C: Only favorable adaptations have survival value.
choices.D: Disuse of an organ may lead to its eventual disappearance.

questions.answer_text: Characteristics acquired during an organism's life are generally not passed on through genes.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: When Cuvier considered the fossils found in the vicinity of Paris, he concluded that the extinction of species ________.

choices.A: does not occur, but evolution does occur
choices.B: and the evolution of species both occur
choices.C: and the evolution of species do not occur
choices.D: occurs, but that there is no evolution

questions.answer_text: occurs, but that there is no evolution

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: For which one of the following observations were both Lamarck's hypothesis and Darwin's hypothesis in complete agreement?

choices.A: Use and disuse of organs determines their size in progeny.
choices.B: Gradual evolutionary change explains why organisms are well-suited to their environments.
choices.C: Acquired characteristics are inherited.
choices.D: More complex species are descended from less complex species.

questions.answer_text: Gradual evolutionary change explains why organisms are well-suited to their environments.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

If x indicates the location of fossils of two closely related species, then fossils of their most- recent common ancestor are most likely to occur in which stratum?

choices.C: C
choices.D: D

questions.answer_text: C

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: If x indicates the fossils of two closely related species, neither of which is extinct, then their remains may be found in how many of these strata?

choices.C: three strata
choices.D: four strata

questions.answer_text: two strata

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: The following questions refer to the evolutionary tree in the figure below. The horizontal axis of the cladogram depicted below is a timeline that extends from 100,000 years ago to the present; the vertical axis represents nothing in particular. The labeled branch points on the tree (V-Z) represent various common ancestors. Let's say that only since 50,000 years ago has there been enough variation between the lineages depicted here to separate them into distinct species, and only the tips of the lineages on this tree represent distinct species. In Darwin's tree of life, each fork in the tree represents ________.

choices.C: the most recent common ancestor of the subsequent branches
choices.D: morphologic gaps in the fossil record

questions.answer_text: the most recent common ancestor of the subsequent branches

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Which pair of scientists below would probably have agreed with the process that is depicted by this tree?

choices.C: Aristotle and Lyell
choices.D: Wallace and Linnaeus

questions.answer_text: Darwin and Wallace

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: The cow Bos primigenius (which is bred for meat and milk) has a smaller brain and larger eyes than closely related wild species of ungulates. These traits most likely arose by ________.

choices.A: natural selection, because these traits evolved in the population over time
choices.B: natural selection, because these traits were not consciously selected by humans
choices.C: artificial selection, because changes in these traits co-occurred with human selection for high milk output and high muscle content
choices.D: artificial selection, because these animals differ from their close relatives and common ancestor

questions.answer_text: artificial selection, because changes in these traits co-occurred with human selection for high milk output and high muscle content

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Starting from the wild mustard Brassica oleracea, breeders have created the strains known as Brussels sprouts, broccoli, kale, and cabbage. Therefore, which of the following statements is correct?

choices.A: In this wild mustard, there is enough heritable variation to permit these different varieties.
choices.B: Heritable variation is low in wild mustard—otherwise this wild strain would have different characteristics.
choices.C: Natural selection is rare in wild populations of wild mustard.
choices.D: In wild mustard, most of the variation is due to differences in soil or other aspects of the environment.

questions.answer_text: In this wild mustard, there is enough heritable variation to permit these different varieties.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: What are adaptations?

choices.C: inherited characteristics of organisms that enhance their survival
choices.D: descent with modification from a common ancestor

questions.answer_text: inherited characteristics of organisms that enhance their survival

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Which of these conditions are always true of populations evolving due to natural selection? Condition 1: The population must vary in traits that are heritable. Condition 2: Some heritable traits must increase reproductive success. Condition 3: Individuals pass on most traits that they acquire during their lifetime.

choices.C: Conditions 1 and 2
choices.D: Conditions 2 and 3

questions.answer_text: Conditions 1 and 2

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: A farmer uses triazine herbicide to control pigweed in his field. For the first few years, the triazine works well and almost all the pigweed dies; but after several years, the farmer sees more and more pigweed. Which of these statements explains why the pigweed reappeared?

choices.A: The herbicide company lost its triazine formula and started selling poor-quality triazine.
choices.B: Natural selection caused the pigweed to mutate, creating a new triazine-resistant species.
choices.C: Triazine-resistant pigweed has less-efficient photosynthesis metabolism.
choices.D: Triazine-resistant weeds were more likely to survive and reproduce.

questions.answer_text: Triazine-resistant weeds were more likely to survive and reproduce.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements best defines artificial selection?

choices.A: Process that occurs when individuals inherit traits that enable them to survive and reproduce
choices.B: Process where humans decide which plants and/or animals will not breed
choices.C: Process of human directed breeding aimed to produce selective traits in selected species
choices.D: Process that favors beneficial mutations

questions.answer_text: Process of human directed breeding aimed to produce selective traits in selected species

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: After the drought of 1977, researchers hypothesized that on the Galápagos Island Daphne Major, medium ground finches with large, deep beaks survived better than those with smaller beaks because they could more easily crack and eat the tough Tribulus cistoides fruits. A tourist company sets up reliable feeding stations with a variety of bird seeds (different types and sizes) so that tourists can get a better look at the finches. Which of these events is now most likely to occur to finch beaks on this island?

choices.A: evolution of yet larger, deeper beaks over time, until all birds have relatively large, deep beaks
choices.B: evolution of smaller, pointier beaks over time, until all birds have relatively small, pointy beaks
choices.C: increased variation in beak size and shape over time
choices.D: no change in beak size and shape over time

questions.answer_text: increased variation in beak size and shape over time

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: The following question is based on information from Frank M. Frey, "Opposing Natural Selection from Herbivores and Pathogens May Maintain Floral-Color Variation in Claytonia virginica (Portulacaceae)," Evolution 58(11), 2004: 2426-37. Claytonia virginica is a woodland spring herb with flowers that vary from white, to pale pink, to bright pink. Slugs prefer to eat pink-flowering over white-flowering plants (due to chemical differences between the two), and plants experiencing severe herbivory are more likely to die. The bees that pollinate this plant also prefer pink to white flowers, so that Claytonia with pink flowers have greater relative fruit set than Claytonia with white flowers. A researcher observes that the percentage of different flower colors remains stable in the study population from year to year. Given no other information, if the researcher removes all slugs from the study population, what do you expect to happen to the distribution of flower colors in the population over time?

choices.A: The percentage of pink flowers should increase over time.
choices.B: The percentage of white flowers should increase over time.
choices.C: The distribution of flower colors should not change.
choices.D: The distribution of flower colors should randomly fluctuate over time.

questions.answer_text: The percentage of pink flowers should increase over time.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Which statement illustrates the connection between natural selection and overreproduction of a population?

choices.A: Populations vary in their inherited traits.
choices.B: Species produce more offspring than can survive in the environment.
choices.C: Individuals with inherited traits that promote survival tend to have more surviving offspring.
choices.D: Individuals with traits that do not enhance survival cannot reproduce.

questions.answer_text: Individuals with inherited traits that promote survival tend to have more surviving offspring.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Darwin used the phrase "descent with modification" to explain ________.

choices.B: descent of all organisms from a single, ancient ancestor
choices.C: that habitat differences stimulate change in organisms
choices.D: evolution of the unity and diversity of life

questions.answer_text: evolution of the unity and diversity of life

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describe evolution?

choices.A: Individuals evolve in response to their environment.
choices.B: The match between organism and their environment decreases.
choices.C: Natural selection chooses the most popular trait.
choices.D: Quick changes occur in an individual's phenotype.

questions.answer_text: Individuals evolve in response to their environment.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life
