Poorly adapted individuals have decreased survivorship.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Which of the following factors could cause a surge in population size?

choices.B: an increase in the number of predators
choices.C: better eyesight evolves in the population
choices.D: decreased camouflage evolves in the population

questions.answer_text: better eyesight evolves in the population

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describe the effect of evolution on a population?

choices.A: increasingly better match between a population and its environment
choices.B: increased genetic variation among individuals in a population
choices.C: increased variation among individuals in a population
choices.D: increased sexual reproduction in a population

questions.answer_text: increasingly better match between a population and its environment

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Which of Darwin's ideas had the strongest connection to his reading of Malthus's essay on human population growth?

choices.B: variation among individuals in a population
choices.C: struggle for existence
choices.D: that the ancestors of the Galápagos finches had come from the South American mainland

questions.answer_text: struggle for existence

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: If Darwin had been aware of genes and their typical mode of transmission to subsequent generations, with which statement would he most likely have been in agreement?

choices.A: If natural selection can change gene frequency in a population over generations, given enough time and genetic diversity, then natural selection can cause sufficient genetic change to produce new species from old ones.
choices.B: If an organism's somatic cell genes change during its lifetime, making it more fit, then it will be able to pass these genes on to its offspring.
choices.C: If an organism acquires new genes by engulfing, or being infected by, another organism, then a new genetic species will result.
choices.D: A single mutation in a single gene in a single gamete, if inherited by future generations, will produce a new species.

questions.answer_text: If natural selection can change gene frequency in a population over generations, given enough time and genetic diversity, then natural selection can cause sufficient genetic change to produce new species from old ones.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Which one of the following observations did Darwin first make during his discovery of evolution?

choices.A: The ability of individuals to survive and reproduce is not equal.
choices.B: There is variation in inherited traits.
choices.C: Individuals who reproduce more leave more offspring.
choices.D: The unequal ability to reproduce leads to the accumulation of favorable traits in a population.

questions.answer_text: There is variation in inherited traits.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Currently, two extant elephant species (X and Y) are classified in the genus Loxodonta, and a third species (Z) is placed in the genus Elephas. Thus, which statement should be true?

choices.A: Species X and Y are not related to species Z.
choices.B: Species X and Y share a greater number of homologies with each other than either does with species Z.
choices.C: Species X and Y share a common ancestor that is alive today.
choices.D: Species X and Y are the result of artificial selection.

questions.answer_text: Species X and Y share a greater number of homologies with each other than either does with species Z.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: In a hypothetical environment, fishes called pike-cichlids are visual predators of large, adult algae-eating fish (in other words, they locate their prey by sight). The population of algae-eaters experiences predatory pressure from pike-cichlids. Which of the following is least likely to result in the algae-eater population in future generations?

choices.A: selection for drab coloration of the algae-eaters
choices.B: selection for nocturnal algae-eaters (active only at night)
choices.C: selection for larger female algae-eaters, bearing broods composed of more, and larger, young
choices.D: selection for algae-eaters that become sexually mature at smaller overall body sizes

questions.answer_text: selection for larger female algae-eaters, bearing broods composed of more, and larger, young

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Currently, two of the living elephant species (X and Y) are placed in the genus Loxodonta, and a third surviving species (Z) is placed in the genus Elephas. Assuming this classification reflects evolutionary relatedness, which of the following is the most accurate phylogenetic tree?

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Cotton-topped tamarins are small primates with tufts of long white hair on their heads. While studying these creatures, you notice that males with longer hair get more opportunities to mate and father more offspring. To test the hypothesis that having longer hair is adaptive in these males, you should ________.

choices.A: test whether other traits in these males are also adaptive
choices.B: look for evidence of hair in ancestors of tamarins
choices.C: determine if hair length is heritable
choices.D: test whether males with shaved heads are still able to mate

questions.answer_text: determine if hair length is heritable

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Fossils of Thrinaxodon, a species that lived during the Triassic period, have been found in both South Africa and Antarctica. Thrinaxodon had a reptile-like skeleton and laid eggs, but small depressions on the front of its skull suggest it had whiskers and, therefore, fur. Thrinaxodon may have been warm-blooded. The fossils of Thrinaxodon are consistent with the hypothesis that ________.

choices.A: fossils found in a given area look like the modern species in that same area
choices.B: the environment where it lived was very warm
choices.C: mammals evolved from a reptilian ancestor
choices.D: Antarctica and South Africa separated after Thrinaxodon went extinct

questions.answer_text: mammals evolved from a reptilian ancestor

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Many crustaceans (for example, lobsters, shrimp, and crayfish) use their tails to swim, but crabs have reduced tails that curl under their shells and are not used in swimming. This is an example of ________.

choices.C: natural selection
choices.D: a vestigial trait

questions.answer_text: a vestigial trait

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Scientific theories ________.

choices.A: are nearly the same things as hypotheses
choices.B: are supported by, and make sense of, many observations
choices.C: cannot be tested because the described events occurred only once
choices.D: are predictions of future events

questions.answer_text: are supported by, and make sense of, many observations

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: DDT was once considered a "silver bullet" that would permanently eradicate insect pests. Instead, DDT is largely useless against many insects. Which of these would have prevented this evolution of DDT resistance in insect pests?

choices.A: All habitats should have received applications of DDT at about the same time.
choices.B: The frequency of DDT application should have been higher.
choices.C: None of the insect pests would have genetic variations that resulted in DDT resistance.
choices.D: DDT application should have been continual.

questions.answer_text: None of the insect pests would have genetic variations that resulted in DDT resistance.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: If the bacterium Staphylococcus aureus experiences a cost for maintaining one or more antibiotic-resistance genes, what would happen in environments that lack antibiotics?

choices.A: These genes would be maintained in case the antibiotics appear.
choices.B: These bacteria would be outcompeted and replaced by bacteria that have lost these genes.
choices.C: These bacteria would try to make the cost worthwhile by locating and migrating to microenvironments where traces of antibiotics are present.
choices.D: The number of genes conveying antibiotic resistance would increase in these bacteria.

questions.answer_text: These bacteria would be outcompeted and replaced by bacteria that have lost these genes.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Of the following anatomical structures, which is homologous to the bones in the wing of a bird?

choices.A: bones in the hind limb of a kangaroo
choices.B: chitinous struts in the wing of a butterfly
choices.C: bony rays in the tail fin of a flying fish
choices.D: bones in the flipper of a whale

questions.answer_text: bones in the flipper of a whale

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Structures as different as human arms, bat wings, and dolphin flippers contain many of the same bones, which develop from similar embryonic tissues. These structural similarities are an example of ________.

choices.C: the evolution of common structure as a result of common function
choices.D: the evolution of similar appearance as a result of common function

questions.answer_text: homology

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Over long periods of time, many cave-dwelling organisms have lost their eyes. Tapeworms have lost their digestive systems. Whales have lost their hind limbs. How can natural selection account for these losses?

choices.A: Natural selection cannot account for losses, but accounts only for new structures and functions.
choices.B: Natural selection accounts for these losses by the principle of use and disuse.
choices.C: Under particular circumstances that persisted for long periods, each of these structures presented greater costs than benefits.
choices.D: The ancestors of these organisms experienced harmful mutations that forced them to lose these structures.

questions.answer_text: Under particular circumstances that persisted for long periods, each of these structures presented greater costs than benefits.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Which of the following evidence most strongly supports the common origin of all life on Earth? All organisms ________.

choices.B: use essentially the same genetic code
choices.C: reproduce
choices.D: show heritable variation

questions.answer_text: use essentially the same genetic code

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Members of two different species possess a similar-looking structure that they use in a similar way to perform about the same function. Which of the following would suggest that the relationship more likely represents homology instead of convergent evolution?

choices.A: The two species live at great distance from each other.
choices.B: The two species share many proteins.
choices.C: The structures in adult members of both species are similar in size.
choices.D: Both species are well adapted to their particular environments.

questions.answer_text: The two species share many proteins.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: What must be true of any organ described as vestigial?

choices.A: It must be analogous to some feature in an ancestor.
choices.B: It must be homologous to some feature in an ancestor.
choices.C: It must be both homologous and analogous to some feature in an ancestor.
choices.D: It need be neither homologous nor analogous to some feature in an ancestor.

questions.answer_text: It must be homologous to some feature in an ancestor.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Pseudogenes are ________.

choices.A: composed of RNA, rather than DNA
choices.C: unrelated genes that code for the same gene product
choices.D: nonfunctional vestigial genes

questions.answer_text: nonfunctional vestigial genes

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: It has been observed that organisms on islands are different from, but closely related to, similar forms found on the nearest continent. This is taken as evidence that ________.

choices.A: island forms are descended from mainland forms
choices.B: common environments are inhabited by the same organisms
choices.C: island forms and mainland forms have identical gene pools
choices.D: the island forms and mainland forms are converging

questions.answer_text: island forms are descended from mainland forms

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Given what we know about evolutionary biology, we expect to find the largest number of endemic species in which of the following geological features, which have existed for at least a few million years?

choices.A: an isolated ocean island in the tropics
choices.C: a grassland in the center of a large continent, with extreme climatic conditions
choices.D: a shallow estuary on a warm-water coast

questions.answer_text: an isolated ocean island in the tropics

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: The greatest number of endemic species is expected in environments that are ________.

choices.B: isolated and show little ecological diversity
choices.C: isolated and ecologically diverse
choices.D: easily reached and show little ecological diversity

questions.answer_text: isolated and show little ecological diversity

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: How many distinct species, both living and extinct, are depicted in this tree?

choices.C: nine
choices.D: eleven

questions.answer_text: eleven

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Which of the five common ancestors, labeled V-Z, is the common ancestor of the greatest number of species, both living and extinct?

choices.C: Y
choices.D: Z

questions.answer_text: Y

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Which of the five species, labeled V-Z, is the common ancestor of the fewest number of species?

choices.C: Y
choices.D: Z

questions.answer_text: V

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Evolutionary trees such as this are properly understood by scientists to be ________.

choices.C: dogmas
choices.D: facts

questions.answer_text: hypotheses

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: About thirteen different species of finches inhabit the Galápagos Islands today, all descendants of a common ancestor from the South American mainland that arrived a few million years ago. Genetically, there are four distinct lineages, but the thirteen species are currently classified among three genera. The first lineage to diverge from the ancestral lineage was the warbler finch (genus Certhidea). Next to diverge was the vegetarian finch (genus Camarhynchus), followed by five tree finch species (also in genus Camarhynchus) and six ground finch species (genus Geospiza). If the six ground finch species have evolved most recently, then which of these is the most logical prediction?

choices.A: They should be limited to the six islands that most recently emerged from the sea.
choices.B: Their genomes should be more similar to each other than are the genomes of the five tree finch species.
choices.C: They should share fewer anatomical homologies with each other than they share with the tree finches.
choices.D: The chances of hybridization between two ground finch species should be less than the chances of hybridization between two tree finch species.

questions.answer_text: Their genomes should be more similar to each other than are the genomes of the five tree finch species.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Which species is most closely related to species W?

choices.A: V is most closely related to species W.
choices.B: X is most closely related to species W.
choices.C: Y and Z are equally closely related to W.
choices.D: It is not possible to say from this tree.

questions.answer_text: V is most closely related to species W.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Which of these is the extant (that is, living) species most closely related to species X?

choices.C: Y
choices.D: Z

questions.answer_text: V

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Logically, which of these should cast the most doubt on the relationships depicted by an evolutionary tree?

choices.A: Some of the organisms depicted by the tree lived in different habitats.
choices.B: The skeletal remains of the organisms depicted by the tree were incomplete (in other words, some bones were missing).
choices.C: Transitional fossils had not been found.
choices.D: Relationships between DNA sequences among the species did not match relationships between skeletal patterns.

questions.answer_text: Relationships between DNA sequences among the species did not match relationships between skeletal patterns.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an observation or inference on which natural selection is based?

choices.A: There is heritable variation among individuals.
choices.B: Poorly adapted individuals never produce offspring.
choices.C: Species produce more offspring than the environment can support.
choices.D: Only a fraction of an individual's offspring may survive.

questions.answer_text: Poorly adapted individuals never produce offspring.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Which of the following observations helped Darwin shape his concept of descent with modification?

choices.A: Species diversity declines farther from the equator.
choices.B: Fewer species live on islands than on the nearest continents.
choices.C: Birds live on islands located farther from the mainland than the birds' maximum nonstop flight distance.
choices.D: South American temperate plants are more similar to the tropical plants of South America than to the temperate plants of Europe.

questions.answer_text: South American temperate plants are more similar to the tropical plants of South America than to the temperate plants of Europe.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: Within six months of effectively using methicillin to treat S. aureus infections in a community, all new S.aureus infections were caused by MRSA. How can this best be explained?

choices.A: A patient must have become infected with MRSA from another community.
choices.B: In response to the drug, S. aureus began making drug-resistant versions of the protein targeted by the drug.
choices.C: Some drug-resistant bacteria were present at the start of treatment, and natural selection increased their frequency.
choices.D: S. aureus evolved to resist vaccines.

questions.answer_text: Some drug-resistant bacteria were present at the start of treatment, and natural selection increased their frequency.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: The upper forelimbs of humans and bats have fairly similar skeletal structures, whereas the corresponding bones in whales have very different shapes and proportions. However, genetic data suggest that all three kinds of organisms diverged from a common ancestor at about the same time. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for these data?

choices.A: Forelimb evolution was adaptive in people and bats, but not in whales.
choices.B: Natural selection in an aquatic environment resulted in significant changes to whale forelimb anatomy.
choices.C: Genes mutate faster in whales than in humans or bats.
choices.D: Whales are not properly classified as mammals.

questions.answer_text: Natural selection in an aquatic environment resulted in significant changes to whale forelimb anatomy.

chapter.title: Descent with Modification: A Darwinian View of Life

questions.stem: DNA sequences in many human genes are very similar to the sequences of corresponding genes in chimpanzees. The most likely explanation for this result is that

choices.A: humans and chimpanzees share a relatively recent common ancestor.
choices.C: chimpanzees evolved from humans.
choices.D: convergent evolution led to the DNA similarities.

questions.answer_text: humans and chimpanzees share a relatively recent common ancestor.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best modern definition of evolution?

choices.B: change in the number of genes in a population over time
choices.C: survival of the fittest
choices.D: inheritance of acquired characters

questions.answer_text: descent with modification

questions.stem: Microevolutions occur when ________.

choices.A: a bird has a beak of a particular size that does not grow larger during a drought
choices.B: changes in allele frequencies in a population occur over generations
choices.C: gene flow evenly transfers alleles between populations
choices.D: individuals within all species vary in their phenotypic traits

questions.answer_text: changes in allele frequencies in a population occur over generations

questions.stem: Which statement about the beak size of finches on the island of Daphne Major during prolonged drought is true?

choices.A: Each bird evolved a deeper, stronger beak as the drought persisted.
choices.B: Each bird's survival was strongly influenced by the depth and strength of its beak as the drought persisted.
choices.C: Each bird that survived the drought produced only offspring with deeper, stronger beaks than seen in the previous generation.
choices.D: The frequency of the strong-beak alleles increased in each bird as the drought persisted.

questions.answer_text: Each bird's survival was strongly influenced by the depth and strength of its beak as the drought persisted.

questions.stem: Which statement about variation is true?

choices.A: All phenotypic variation is the result of genotypic variation.
choices.B: All genetic variation produces phenotypic variation.
choices.C: All nucleotide variability results in neutral variation.
choices.D: All new alleles are the result of nucleotide variability.

questions.answer_text: All new alleles are the result of nucleotide variability.

questions.stem: Which of the following descriptions illustrates phenotype variation caused by environment?

choices.B: diet of caterpillars changes their morphology
choices.C: variation in horse coat color
choices.D: average beak depth during drought

questions.answer_text: diet of caterpillars changes their morphology

questions.stem: Genetic variation ________.

choices.A: is created by the direct action of natural selection
choices.B: arises in response to changes in the environment
choices.C: must be present in a population before natural selection can act upon the population
choices.D: tends to be reduced when diploid organisms produce gametes

questions.answer_text: must be present in a population before natural selection can act upon the population

questions.stem: HIV's genome of RNA includes the code for reverse transcriptase (RT), an enzyme that acts early in infection to synthesize a DNA genome off of an RNA template. The HIV genome also codes for protease (PR), an enzyme that acts later in infection by cutting long viral polyproteins into smaller, functional proteins. Both RT and PR represent potential targets for antiretroviral drugs. Drugs called nucleoside analogs (NA) act against RT, whereas drugs called protease inhibitors (PI) act against PR. Which of the following treatment options would most likely avoid the evolution of drug-resistant HIV (assuming no drug interactions or side effects)?

choices.A: Use a series of NAs, one at a time, and change about once a week.
choices.B: Use a single PI, but slowly increase the dosage over the course of a week.
choices.C: Use high doses of NA and a PI at the same time for a period not to exceed one day.
choices.D: Use moderate doses of NA and two different PIs at the same time for several months.

questions.answer_text: Use moderate doses of NA and two different PIs at the same time for several months.

questions.stem: HIV's genome of RNA includes the code for reverse transcriptase (RT), an enzyme that acts early in infection to synthesize a DNA genome off of an RNA template. The HIV genome also codes for protease (PR), an enzyme that acts later in infection by cutting long viral polyproteins into smaller, functional proteins. Both RT and PR represent potential targets for antiretroviral drugs. Drugs called nucleoside analogs (NA) act against RT, whereas drugs called protease inhibitors (PI) act against PR. Which mechanism produces variation for evolution by shuffling existing alleles?

choices.C: mutation
choices.D: changes in chromosome numbers

questions.answer_text: sexual reproduction

questions.stem: The following experiment is used for the corresponding question. A researcher discovered a species of moth that lays its eggs on oak trees. Eggs are laid at two distinct times of the year: early in spring when the oak trees are flowering and in midsummer when flowering is past. Caterpillars from eggs that hatch in spring feed on oak flowers and look like oak flowers. But caterpillars that hatch in summer feed on oak leaves and look like oak twigs. How does the same population of moths produce such different-looking caterpillars on the same trees? To answer this question, the biologist caught many female moths from the same population and collected their eggs. He put at least one egg from each female into eight identical cups. The eggs hatched, and at least two larvae from each female were maintained in one of the four temperature and light conditions listed below. In each of the four environments, one of the caterpillars was fed oak flowers, the other oak leaves. Thus, there were a total of eight treatment groups (4 environments × 2 diets). Which of the following is a testable hypothesis that would explain the differences in caterpillar appearance observed in this population?

choices.A: The longer day lengths of summer trigger the development of twig-like caterpillars.
choices.B: Winter causes ugly caterpillar and trees.
choices.C: Differences in air pressure, due to differences in elevation, trigger the development of different types of caterpillars.
choices.D: Differences in diet trigger the development of different types of caterpillars.

questions.answer_text: Differences in diet trigger the development of different types of caterpillars.

questions.stem: Genetic drift produces variation for evolution when ________.

choices.A: a gene pool decreases because a smaller group establishes a new population
choices.B: chance events cause allele frequencies to fluctuate unpredictably
choices.C: sudden change in environment drastically reduces the gene pool
choices.D: a population has heritable traits better suited to the environment

questions.answer_text: chance events cause allele frequencies to fluctuate unpredictably

questions.stem: Homozygotes with two sickle-cell alleles are selected against because of mortality. However, heterozygotes for sickle-cell allele experience little effects of sickle allele and are more likely to survive malaria. The net effect of this exposure produced evolutionary change in areas where malaria is endemic by ________.

choices.C: distortion of red blood cells
choices.D: increasing the number of infected mosquitoes

questions.answer_text: increasing sickle-cell allele frequency

questions.stem: Cystic fibrosis is a genetic disorder in homozygous recessives that causes death during the teenage years. If 9 in 10,000 newborn babies have the disease, what are the expected frequencies of the dominant (A1) and recessive (A2) alleles according to the Hardy-Weinberg equation?

Suppose 64% of a remote mountain village can taste phenylthiocarbamide (PTC) and must, therefore, have at least one copy of the dominant PTC taster allele. If this population conforms to Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium for this gene, what percentage of the population must be heterozygous for this trait?
If individuals tend to mate within a subset of the population, there is ________.

choices.C: no gene flow
choices.D: random mating

questions.answer_text: random mating

questions.stem: Which Hardy-Weinberg condition is affected by population size?

choices.C: gene flow
choices.D: no mutation

questions.answer_text: genetic drift

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question below. Researchers studying a small milkweed population note that some plants produce a toxin and other plants do not. They identify the gene responsible for toxin production. The dominant allele (T) codes for an enzyme that makes the toxin, and the recessive allele (t) codes for a nonfunctional enzyme that cannot produce the toxin. Heterozygotes produce an intermediate amount of toxin. The genotypes of all individuals in the population are determined (see chart) and used to determine the actual allele frequencies in the population. Is this population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium?

choices.B: No; there are more heterozygotes than expected.
choices.C: No; there are more homozygotes than expected.
choices.D: More information is needed to answer this question.

questions.answer_text: No; there are more homozygotes than expected.

questions.stem: Which one of the following conditions would allow gene frequencies to change by chance?

choices.C: mutation
choices.D: gene flow

questions.answer_text: small populations

questions.stem: The higher the proportion of loci that are "fixed" in a population, the lower are that population's ________.

choices.C: average heterozygosity
choices.D: nucleotide variability and average heterozygosity

questions.answer_text: nucleotide variability and average heterozygosity

questions.stem: Whenever diploid populations are in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium at a particular locus, ________.

choices.A: the allele's frequency should not change from one generation to the next
choices.B: natural selection, gene flow, and genetic drift are acting equally to change an allele's frequency
choices.C: two alleles are present in equal proportions
choices.D: individuals within the population are evolving

questions.answer_text: the allele's frequency should not change from one generation to the next

questions.stem: In the formula for determining a population's genotype frequencies, the "2" in the term 2pq is necessary because ________.

choices.B: heterozygotes can come about in two ways
choices.C: the population is doubling in number
choices.D: heterozygotes have two alleles

questions.answer_text: heterozygotes can come about in two ways

questions.stem: In the formula for determining a population's genotype frequencies, the "pq" in the term 2pq is necessary because ________.

choices.B: heterozygotes can come about in two ways
choices.C: the population is doubling in number
choices.D: heterozygotes have two alleles

questions.answer_text: heterozygotes have two alleles

questions.stem: In a Hardy-Weinberg population with two alleles, A and a, that are in equilibrium, the frequency of the allele a is 0.3. What is the frequency of individuals that are homozygous for this allele?
In a Hardy-Weinberg population with two alleles, A and a, that are in equilibrium, the frequency of allele a is 0.2. What is the frequency of individuals that are heterozygous for this allele?
In a Hardy-Weinberg population with two alleles, A and a, that are in equilibrium, the frequency of allele a is 0.1. What is the frequency of individuals with AA genotype?
You sample a population of butterflies and find that 56% are heterozygous at a particular locus. What should be the frequency of the homozygous individuals in this population?

In peas, a gene controls flower color such that R = purple and r = white. In an isolated pea patch, there are 36 purple-flowering plants and 64 white-flowering plants. Assuming Hardy- Weinberg equilibrium, what is the value of q for this population?

A large population of laboratory animals has been allowed to breed randomly for a number of generations. After several generations, 25% of the animals display a recessive trait (aa), the same percentage as at the beginning of the breeding program. The rest of the animals show the dominant phenotype, with heterozygotes indistinguishable from the homozygous dominants. What is the most reasonable conclusion that can be drawn from the fact that the frequency of the recessive trait (aa) has not changed over time?

choices.A: The two phenotypes are about equally adaptive under laboratory conditions.
choices.C: There has been a high rate of mutation of allele A to allele a.
choices.D: There has been sexual selection favoring allele a.

questions.answer_text: The two phenotypes are about equally adaptive under laboratory conditions.

questions.stem: A large population of laboratory animals has been allowed to breed randomly for a number of generations. After several generations, 25% of the animals display a recessive trait (aa), the same percentage as at the beginning of the breeding program. The rest of the animals show the dominant phenotype, with heterozygotes indistinguishable from the homozygous dominants. What is the estimated frequency of allele A in the gene pool?

A large population of laboratory animals has been allowed to breed randomly for a number of generations. After several generations, 25% of the animals display a recessive trait (aa), the same percentage as at the beginning of the breeding program. The rest of the animals show the dominant phenotype, with heterozygotes indistinguishable from the homozygous dominants. What proportion of the population is probably heterozygous (Aa) for this trait?
Which one of these processes describes bottleneck effect?

choices.A: chance events that change allele frequency
choices.B: alleles transferred to the next generation in portions that differ from previous generation
choices.C: transfer of alleles in and out of a population due to movement of fertile individuals
choices.D: sudden change in environments that alters gene frequency of a population

questions.answer_text: sudden change in environments that alters gene frequency of a population

questions.stem: Comparisons of Neanderthal DNA revealed that there are more similarities to non-African DNA than reference sequences from West Africans. Additionally, scientists found that Neanderthal DNA is as closely related to East Asians as to Europeans. This indicates that interbreeding occurred before human migration further east. What process of population genetics generated these results?

choices.C: gene drift
choices.D: nonrandom mating

questions.answer_text: gene flow

questions.stem: Soon after the island of Hawaii rose above the sea surface (somewhat less than one million years ago), the evolution of life on this new island should have been most strongly influenced by ________.

choices.C: habitat differentiation
choices.D: the founder effect

questions.answer_text: the founder effect

questions.stem: In 1983, a population of dark-eyed junco birds became established on the campus of the University of California, San Diego (UCSD), which is located many miles from the junco's normal habitat in the mixed-coniferous temperate forests in the mountains. Juncos have white outer tail feathers that the males display during aggressive interactions and during courtship displays. Males with more white in their tail are more likely to win aggressive interactions, and females prefer to mate with males with more white in their tails. Females have less white in their tails than do males, and display it less often. (Pamela J. Yeh. 2004. Rapid evolution of a sexually selected trait following population establishment in a novel habitat. Evolution 58[1]:166-74.) The UCSD campus male junco population tails were, on average, 36% white, whereas the tails of males from nearby mountain populations averaged 40-45% white. If this observed trait difference were due to a difference in the original colonizing population, it would most likely be due to ________.

choices.C: a genetic bottleneck
choices.D: a founder effect

questions.answer_text: a founder effect

questions.stem: In 1983, a population of dark-eyed junco birds became established on the campus of the University of California, San Diego (UCSD), which is located many miles from the junco's normal habitat in the mixed-coniferous temperate forests in the mountains. Juncos have white outer tail feathers that the males display during aggressive interactions and during courtship displays. Males with more white in their tail are more likely to win aggressive interactions, and females prefer to mate with males with more white in their tails. Females have less white in their tails than do males, and display it less often. (Pamela J. Yeh. 2004. Rapid evolution of a sexually selected trait following population establishment in a novel habitat. Evolution 58[1]:166-74.) The UCSD campus male junco population tails are about 36% white, whereas the tails of males from nearby mountain populations are about 40-45% white. The founding stock of UCSD birds was likely from the nearby mountain populations because some of those birds overwinter on the UCSD campus each year. Population sizes on the UCSD campus have been reasonably large, and there are significant habitat differences between the UCSD campus and the mountain coniferous forests; UCSD campus has a more open environment (making birds more visible) and a lower junco density (decreasing intraspecific competition) than the mountain forests. Given this information, which of the following evolutionary mechanisms do you think is most likely responsible for the difference between the UCSD and mountain populations?

choices.C: gene flow
choices.D: mutation

questions.answer_text: natural selection

questions.stem: The Dunkers are a religious group that moved from Germany to Pennsylvania in the mid- 1700s. They do not marry with members outside their own immediate community. Today, the Dunkers are genetically unique and differ in gene frequencies, at many loci, from all other populations including those in their original homeland. Which of the following mechanisms likely explains the genetic uniqueness of this population?

choices.C: mutation and natural selection
choices.D: founder effect and genetic drift

questions.answer_text: founder effect and genetic drift

questions.stem: An earthquake decimates a ground-squirrel population, killing 98% of the squirrels. The surviving population happens to have broader stripes, on average, than the initial population. If broadness of stripes is genetically determined, what effect has the ground-squirrel population experienced during the earthquake?

choices.C: a founder event
choices.D: a genetic bottleneck

questions.answer_text: a genetic bottleneck

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most predictable outcome of increased gene flow between two populations?

choices.A: lower average fitness in both populations
choices.B: higher average fitness in both populations
choices.C: increased genetic difference between the two populations
choices.D: decreased genetic difference between the two populations

questions.answer_text: decreased genetic difference between the two populations

questions.stem: In 1986, a nuclear power accident in Chernobyl, USSR (now Ukraine), led to high radiation levels for miles surrounding the plant. The high levels of radiation caused elevated mutation rates in the surviving organisms, and evolutionary biologists have been studying rodent populations in the Chernobyl area ever since. Based on your understanding of evolutionary mechanisms, which of the following most likely occurred in the rodent populations following the accident?

choices.A: Mutations caused major changes in rodent physiology over time.
choices.B: Mutation led to increased genetic variation.
choices.C: Mutation caused genetic drift and decreased fitness.
choices.D: Mutation caused the fixation of new alleles.

questions.answer_text: Mutation led to increased genetic variation.

questions.stem: Over time, the movement of people on Earth has steadily increased. This has altered the course of human evolution by increasing ________.

choices.C: genetic drift
choices.D: gene flow

questions.answer_text: gene flow

questions.stem: You are maintaining a small population of fruit flies in the laboratory by transferring the flies to a new culture bottle after each generation. After several generations, you notice that the viability of the flies has decreased greatly. Recognizing that small population size is likely to be linked to decreased viability, the best way to reverse this trend is to ________.

choices.A: cross your flies with flies from another lab
choices.B: reduce the number of flies that you transfer at each generation
choices.C: transfer only the largest flies
choices.D: change the temperature at which you rear the flies

questions.answer_text: cross your flies with flies from another lab

questions.stem: The inability of organisms to evolve anything that could be an advantage reflects ________.

choices.A: the limits of choices of genes within a species
choices.C: the consequences of random mutations
choices.D: the consequences of inbreeding

questions.answer_text: the limits of choices of genes within a species

questions.stem: Why does the fitness of a phenotype depend on frequency-dependent selection?

choices.A: Because selection favors the least common phenotype.
choices.B: Because the least number of alleles are at that locus.
choices.C: Because sexual selection produces dimorphism.
choices.D: Because frequency-dependent selection acts against extreme phenotypes.

questions.answer_text: Because frequency-dependent selection acts against extreme phenotypes.

questions.stem: On the Bahamian island of Andros, mosquitofish populations live in various, now-isolated, freshwater ponds that were once united. Currently, some predator-rich ponds have mosquitofish that can swim in short, fast bursts; other predator-poor ponds have mosquitofish that can swim continuously for a long time. When placed together in the same body of water, the two kinds of female mosquitofish exhibit exclusive breeding preferences. If one builds a canal linking a predator-rich pond to a predator-poor pond, then what type of selection should subsequently be most expected among the mosquitofish in the original predator- rich pond, and what type should be most expected among the mosquitofish in the formerly predator-poor pond?

choices.C: less-intense directional selection; more-intense directional selection
choices.D: less-intense disruptive selection; more-intense disruptive selection

questions.answer_text: less-intense directional selection; more-intense directional selection

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question below. Martin Wikelski and L. Michael Romero (Body size, performance and fitness in Galápagos marine iguanas, Integrative and Comparative Biology 43 [2003]:376-86) measured the snout-to- vent (anus) length of Galápagos marine iguanas and observed the percent survival of different- sized animals, all of the same age. The graph shows the log snout-vent length (SVL, a measure of overall body size) plotted against the percent survival of these different size classes for males and females. Examine the figure. What type of selection for body size appears to be occurring in these marine iguanas?

choices.C: disruptive selection
choices.D: You cannot determine the type of selection from the above information.

questions.answer_text: stabilizing selection

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question below. Martin Wikelski and L. Michael Romero (Body size, performance and fitness in Galápagos marine iguanas, Integrative and Comparative Biology 43 [2003]:376-86) measured the snout-to- vent (anus) length of Galápagos marine iguanas and observed the percent survival of different- sized animals, all of the same age. The graph shows the log snout-vent length (SVL, a measure of overall body size) plotted against the percent survival of these different size classes for males and females. Currently the only predators of Galápagos marine iguanas are Galápagos hawks. Iguana body size is not correlated with risk of hawk predation, although small iguanas can sprint faster than large iguanas. If predators (for example, cats) that preferably catch and eat slower iguanas are introduced to the island, iguana body size is likely to ________ in the absence of other factors; the iguanas would then be under ________ selection.

choices.C: decrease; directional
choices.D: decrease; disruptive

questions.answer_text: decrease; directional

questions.stem: Three-spined stickleback fish (Gasterosteus aculeatus) show substantial heritable variation in gill-raker length related to differences in their diets. Longer gill rakers appear to function better for capturing open-water prey, while shorter gill rakers function better for capturing shallow-water prey. Which of the following types of selection is most likely to be found in a large lake (open water in the middle and shallow water around the sides) with a high density of these fish?

choices.C: disruptive selection
choices.D: sexual selection

questions.answer_text: disruptive selection

questions.stem: A biologist doing a long-term study on a wild spider population observes increased variation in silk thickness. Which of the following could the spider population be experiencing?

choices.C: disruptive selection
choices.D: genetic drift

questions.answer_text: disruptive selection

questions.stem: In some jacana species, males take care of the eggs and young, and females compete among themselves for territories that contain one to several males. Female jacanas are significantly larger than males. Which of these statements would you predict to be true of this bird species? 1. Male jacana fitness is primarily limited by ability to take care of eggs and raise young. 2. Female jacana fitness is limited by the number of males in her territory with which a female mates. 3. Variation in reproductive success should be greater in male jacanas than in females. 4. Variation in reproductive success should be greater in female jacanas than in males. 5. Males and females have equal variation in reproductive success.

The restriction enzymes of bacteria protect the bacteria from successful attack by bacteriophages, whose genomes can be degraded by the restriction enzymes. The bacterial genomes are not vulnerable to these restriction enzymes because bacterial DNA is methylated. This situation selects for bacteriophages whose genomes are also methylated. As new strains of resistant bacteriophages become more prevalent, this in turn selects for bacteria whose genomes are not methylated and whose restriction enzymes instead degrade methylated DNA. The outcome of the conflict between bacteria and bacteriophages at any point in time results from ________.

choices.C: heterozygote advantage
choices.D: neutral variation

questions.answer_text: frequency-dependent selection

questions.stem: The restriction enzymes of bacteria protect the bacteria from successful attack by bacteriophages, whose genomes can be degraded by the restriction enzymes. The bacterial genomes are not vulnerable to these restriction enzymes because bacterial DNA is methylated. This situation selects for bacteriophages whose genomes are also methylated. As new strains of resistant bacteriophages become more prevalent, this in turn selects for bacteria whose genomes are not methylated and whose restriction enzymes instead degrade methylated DNA. Over the course of evolutionary time, what should occur?

choices.A: Methylated DNA should become fixed in the gene pools of bacterial species.
choices.B: Nonmethylated DNA should become fixed in the gene pools of bacteriophages.
choices.C: Methylated DNA should become fixed in the gene pools of bacteriophages.
choices.D: Methylated and nonmethylated strains should be maintained among both bacteria and bacteriophages, with ratios that vary over time.

questions.answer_text: Methylated and nonmethylated strains should be maintained among both bacteria and bacteriophages, with ratios that vary over time.

questions.stem: Arrange the following in order from most general to most specific. 1 natural selection 2. microevolution 3. intrasexual selection 4. evolution 5. sexual selection

Adult male humans generally have deeper voices than do adult female humans, which is the direct result of higher levels of testosterone causing growth of the larynx. If the fossil records of apes and humans alike show a trend toward decreasing larynx size in adult females and increasing larynx size in adult males, then ________.

choices.A: sexual dimorphism was evolving over time in these species
choices.B: intrasexual selection seems to have occurred in both species
choices.C: stabilizing selection was occurring in these species concerning larynx size
choices.D: selection was acting more directly upon genotype than upon phenotype

questions.answer_text: sexual dimorphism was evolving over time in these species

questions.stem: Most Swiss starlings produce four to five eggs in each clutch. Starlings producing fewer or more than this have reduced fitness. Which of the following terms best describes this situation?

choices.C: disruptive selection
choices.D: sexual selection

questions.answer_text: stabilizing selection

questions.stem: When imbalances occur in the sex ratio of sexual species that have two sexes (that is, other than a 50:50 ratio), the members of the minority sex often receive a greater proportion of care and resources from parents than do the offspring of the majority sex. This is most clearly an example of ________.

choices.C: stabilizing selection
choices.D: frequency-dependent selection

questions.answer_text: frequency-dependent selection

questions.stem: A proficient engineer can easily design skeletal structures that are more functional than those currently found in the forelimbs of such diverse mammals as horses, whales, and bats. The actual forelimbs of these mammals do not seem to be optimally arranged because ________.

choices.A: natural selection has not had sufficient time to create the optimal design in each case, but will do so given enough time
choices.B: in many cases, phenotype is determined by genotype and the environment
choices.C: though we may not consider the fit between the current skeletal arrangements and their functions excellent, we should not doubt that natural selection ultimately produces the best design
choices.D: natural selection is generally limited to modifying structures that were present in previous generations and in previous species

questions.answer_text: natural selection is generally limited to modifying structures that were present in previous generations and in previous species

questions.stem: Anopheles mosquitoes, which carry the malaria parasite, cannot live above elevations of 5,900 feet. In addition, oxygen availability decreases with higher altitude. Consider a hypothetical human population that is adapted to life on the slopes of Mt. Kilimanjaro in Tanzania, a country in equatorial Africa. Mt. Kilimanjaro's base is about 2,600 feet above sea level and its peak is 19,341 feet above sea level. If the incidence of the sickle-cell allele in the population is plotted against altitude (feet above sea level), which of the following distributions is most likely, assuming little migration of people up or down the mountain?

In a very large population, a quantitative trait has the following distribution pattern. If there is no gene flow, the curve shifts to the left or to the right, and the population size consequently increases over successive generations, which of the following is most likely occurring?

choices.C: disruptive selection
choices.D: genetic drift

questions.answer_text: directional selection

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question below. In those parts of equatorial Africa where the malaria parasite is most common, the sickle-cell allele constitutes 20% of the β hemoglobin alleles in the human gene pool. In the United States, the parasite that causes malaria is not present, but it is present in African- Americans whose ancestors were from equatorial Africa. What should be happening to the sickle-cell allele in the United States, and what should be happening to it in equatorial Africa?

choices.C: directional selection; disruptive selection
choices.D: directional selection; stabilizing selection

questions.answer_text: directional selection; stabilizing selection

questions.stem: Swine are vulnerable to infection by bird flu virus and human flu virus, which can both be present in an individual pig at the same time. When this occurs, it is possible for genes from bird flu virus and human flu virus to be combined. If the human flu virus contributes a gene for Tamiflu resistance (Tamiflu is an antiviral drug) to the new virus, and if the new virus is introduced to an environment lacking Tamiflu, then what is most likely to occur?

choices.A: The new virus will maintain its Tamiflu-resistance gene, in case of future exposure to Tamiflu.
choices.B: The Tamiflu-resistance gene will undergo mutations that convert it into a gene that has a useful function in this environment.
choices.C: If the Tamiflu-resistance gene involves a cost, it will experience directional selection leading to reduction in its frequency.
choices.D: If the Tamiflu-resistance gene confers no benefit in the current environment, and has no cost, the virus will increase in frequency.

questions.answer_text: If the Tamiflu-resistance gene involves a cost, it will experience directional selection leading to reduction in its frequency.

questions.stem: Natural selection changes allele frequencies because some ________ survive and reproduce better than others.

choices.C: species
choices.D: individuals

questions.answer_text: individuals

questions.stem: No two people are genetically identical, except for identical twins. The main source of genetic variation among humans is

choices.A: new mutations that occurred in the preceding generation.
choices.C: the reshuffling of alleles in sexual reproduction.
choices.D: environmental effects.

questions.answer_text: the reshuffling of alleles in sexual reproduction.

questions.stem: If the nucleotide variability of a locus equals 0%, what is the gene variability and number of alleles at that locus?

choices.C: gene variability = 0%; number of alleles = 2
choices.D: gene variability > 0%; number of alleles = 2

questions.answer_text: gene variability = 0%; number of alleles = 1

questions.stem: There are 25 individuals in population 1, all with genotype AA, and there are 40 individuals in population 2, all with genotype aa. Assume that these populations are located far from each other and that their environmental conditions are very similar. Based on the information given here, the observed genetic variation most likely resulted from

choices.C: nonrandom mating.
choices.D: directional selection.

questions.answer_text: genetic drift.

questions.stem: A fruit fly population has a gene with two alleles, A1 and A2. Tests show that 70% of the gametes produced in the population contain the A1 allele. If the population is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, what proportion of the flies carry both A1 and A2?

Use the following information to answer the question. Two populations of birds with somewhat different coloration live on opposite sides of a peninsula. The habitat between the populations is not suitable for these birds. When birds from the two populations are brought together, they produce young whose appearance is intermediate between the two parents. These offspring will breed with each other or with birds from either parent population, and all offspring of these pairings appear intermediate to various degrees. What keeps the two populations separate?

choices.C: behavior isolates reproductive activities
choices.D: habitat isolation

questions.answer_text: habitat isolation

questions.stem: If biological species are defined in terms of reproductive compatibility, the formation of a new species hinges on ________.

choices.C: hybrid formation
choices.D: gene pool expansion

questions.answer_text: reproductive isolation

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes mechanical isolation prezygotic barrier?

choices.A: two species live in different habitats
choices.B: two species mate at different times
choices.C: two species share courtship activities
choices.D: two snails have shells that spiral in different directions

questions.answer_text: two species live in different habitats

questions.stem: Three populations of crickets look very similar, but the males have courtship songs that sound different. What function would this difference in song likely serve if the populations came in contact?

choices.C: a behavioral reproductive isolating mechanism
choices.D: a gametic reproductive isolating mechanism

questions.answer_text: a behavioral reproductive isolating mechanism

questions.stem: Many songbirds breed in North America in the spring and summer, and then migrate to Central and South America in the fall. They spend the winter in these warmer areas where they feed and prepare for the spring migration north and another breeding season. Two hypothetical species of sparrow, A and B, overwinter together in mixed flocks in Costa Rica. In spring, species A goes to the east coast of North America, and species B goes to the west coast. What can you say about the isolating mechanisms of these two species?

choices.A: They must have strong postzygotic isolating mechanisms to spend winter in such close proximity.
choices.B: They must have strong prezygotic isolating mechanisms to spend winter in such close proximity.
choices.C: These two species mate in different climates.
choices.D: Reinforcement must be occurring when they winter together.

questions.answer_text: These two species mate in different climates.

questions.stem: The peppered moth provides a well-known example of natural selection. The light-colored form of the moth was predominant in England before the Industrial Revolution. In the mid-19th century, a dark-colored form appeared. The difference is produced by a dominant allele of one gene. By about 1900, approximately 90% of the moths around industrial areas were dark colored, whereas light-colored moths were still abundant elsewhere. Apparently, birds could readily find the light moths against the soot-darkened background in industrial areas and, therefore, were eating more light moths. Recently, use of cleaner fuels has greatly reduced soot in the landscape, and the dark-colored moths have been disappearing. Should the two forms of moths be considered separate species?

choices.A: Yes; natural selection has affected the frequency of the two different forms.
choices.B: Yes; they have completely different coloration.
choices.C: Yes; they are reproductively isolated based on habitat.
choices.D: No; they still can interbreed.

questions.answer_text: No; they still can interbreed.

questions.stem: Which statement describes unity within a species?

choices.A: A species can be distinguished by body shape and other structural features.
choices.B: Members have the potential to interbreed in nature and produce viable, fertile offspring.
choices.C: A species is described in terms of its interaction with living and non-living environment.
choices.D: The DNA sequence lacks similarities.

questions.answer_text: Members have the potential to interbreed in nature and produce viable, fertile offspring.

questions.stem: The common edible frog of Europe is a hybrid between two species, Rana lessonae and Rana ridibunda. The hybrids were first described in 1758 and have a wide distribution, from France across central Europe to Russia. Both male and female hybrids exist, but when they mate among themselves, they are rarely successful in producing offspring. What can you infer from this information?

choices.A: Postzygotic isolation exists between the two frog species.
choices.B: Prezygotic isolation exists between the two frog species.
choices.C: These two species are likely in the process of fusing back into one species.
choices.D: The hybrids form a separate species under the biological species concept.

questions.answer_text: Postzygotic isolation exists between the two frog species.

questions.stem: Macroevolution is ________.

choices.A: the same as microevolution, but includes the origin of new species
choices.C: defined as the evolution of microscopic organisms into organisms that can be seen with the naked eye
choices.D: defined as a change in allele or gene frequency over the course of many generations

questions.answer_text: evolution above the species level

questions.stem: Which of the various species concepts distinguishes two species based on the degree of genetic exchange between their gene pools?

choices.C: biological
choices.D: morphological

questions.answer_text: biological

questions.stem: There is still some controversy among biologists about whether Neanderthals should be placed within the same species as modern humans or into a separate species of their own. Most DNA sequence data analyzed so far indicate that there was probably little or no gene flow between Neanderthals and Homo sapiens. Which species concept describing species relationship between modern humans and Neanderthals is most applicable in these observations?

choices.C: morphological
choices.D: biological

questions.answer_text: biological

questions.stem: You are confronted with a box of preserved grasshoppers of various species that are new to science and have not been described. Your assignment is to separate them into species. There is no accompanying information as to where or when they were collected. Which species concept will you have to use?

choices.C: ecological
choices.D: morphological

questions.answer_text: morphological

questions.stem: Dog breeders maintain the purity of breeds by keeping dogs of different breeds apart when they are fertile. This kind of isolation is most similar to which of the following reproductive isolating mechanisms?

choices.C: habitat isolation
choices.D: gametic isolation

questions.answer_text: habitat isolation

questions.stem: Rank the following in order from most general to most specific. 1. gametic isolation 2. reproductive isolating mechanism 3. sperm-egg incompatibility in sea urchins 4. prezygotic isolating mechanism
Two species of frogs belonging to the same genus occasionally mate, but the embryos stop developing after a day and then die. These two frog species separate by ________.

choices.C: reduced hybrid fertility
choices.D: gametic isolation

questions.answer_text: reduced hybrid viability

questions.stem: The production of sterile mules by interbreeding between female horses (mares) and male donkeys (jacks) is an example of ________.

choices.C: reduced hybrid fertility
choices.D: mechanical isolation

questions.answer_text: reduced hybrid fertility

questions.stem: Which postzygotic barriers prevent formation of hybrids beyond the first generations?

choices.C: hybrid breakdown
choices.D: hybrid gamete isolation

questions.answer_text: hybrid breakdown

questions.stem: Rocky Mountain juniper (Juniperus scopulorum) and one-seeded juniper (J. monosperma) have overlapping ranges. Pollen grains (which contain sperm cells) from one species are unable to germinate and make pollen tubes on female ovules (which contain egg cells) of the other species. These two juniper species are kept separate by ________.

choices.C: gametic isolation
choices.D: behavioral isolation

questions.answer_text: gametic isolation

questions.stem: What does the biological species concept use as the primary criterion for determining species boundaries?

choices.C: gene flow
choices.D: morphological similarity

questions.answer_text: gene flow

questions.stem: The largest unit within which gene flow can readily occur is ________.

choices.C: the entire range of a genus
choices.D: the hybrid zone

questions.answer_text: a species

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. About 3 million years ago, the Isthmus of Panama (a narrow strip of land connecting North and South America) formed, dividing marine organisms into Pacific and Caribbean populations. Researchers have examined species of snapping shrimp on both sides of the isthmus. Based on the morphological species concept, there appeared to be seven pairs of species, with one species of each pair in the Pacific and the other in the Caribbean. The different species pairs live at somewhat different depths in the ocean. Using mitochondrial DNA sequences, the researchers estimated phylogenies and found that each of these species pairs, separated by the isthmus, were indeed each other's closest relatives. The researchers investigated mating in the lab and found that many species pairs were not very interested in courting with each other, and any that did mate almost never produced fertile offspring. (Reference: Y. Kondo and A. Kashiwagi. 2004. Experimentally induced autotetraploidy and allotetraploidy in two Japanese pond frogs. Journal of Herpetology 38(3):381-92.) If the isthmus formed gradually rather than suddenly, what pattern of genetic divergence would you expect to find in these species pairs?

choices.A: similar percentages of difference in DNA sequence between all pairs of sister species
choices.B: greater percentage of difference in DNA sequence between species that inhabit deep water than between species that inhabit shallow water
choices.C: greater percentage of difference in DNA sequence between species that inhabit shallow water than between species that inhabit deep water
choices.D: smaller percentage of difference DNA sequence between species that inhabit than between shallow water

questions.answer_text: greater percentage of difference in DNA sequence between species that inhabit deep water than between species that inhabit shallow water

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the most likely order of events in allopatric speciation?

choices.C: divergence, genetic drift, genetic isolation
choices.D: genetic isolation, genetic drift, divergence

questions.answer_text: genetic isolation, genetic drift, divergence

questions.stem: You want to study divergence of populations, and you need to maximize the rate of divergence to see results within the period of your grant funding. You will form a new population by taking some individuals from a source population and isolating them so the two populations cannot interbreed. What combination of characteristics would maximize your chance of seeing divergence in this study? 1. Choose a random sample of individuals to form the new population. 2. Choose individuals from one extreme to form the new population. 3. Choose a species to study that produces many offspring. 4. Choose a species to study that produces a few, large offspring. 5. Place the new population in the same type of environment as the source population. 6. Place the new population in a novel environment compared to that of the source population.
Which of these animals could overcome the geographic barrier of water that causes allopatric speciation?

choices.C: small rodents
choices.D: mountain lions

questions.answer_text: mountain lions

questions.stem: How are two different species most likely to evolve from one ancestral species?

choices.A: sympatrically, by a point mutation affecting morphology or behavior
choices.C: allopatrically, due to extensive inbreeding
choices.D: allopatrically, after the ancestral species has split into two populations

questions.answer_text: allopatrically, after the ancestral species has split into two populations

questions.stem: House finches were found only in western North America until 1939, when a few individuals were released in New York City. These individuals established a breeding population and gradually expanded their range. The western population also expanded its range somewhat eastward, and the two populations have recently come in contact. If the two forms were unable to interbreed when their expanding ranges met, it would be an example of ________.

choices.C: allopatric speciation
choices.D: sympatric speciation

questions.answer_text: allopatric speciation

questions.stem: Most causes of speciation are relatively slow in that they may take many generations to see changes, with the exception of ________.

choices.C: colonization
choices.D: natural selection

questions.answer_text: polyploidy

questions.stem: Two researchers experimentally formed tetraploid frogs by fertilizing diploid eggs from Rana porosa brevipoda with diploid sperm from Rana nigromaculata. When they mated these tetraploid frogs with each other, most of the offspring that survived to maturity were tetraploid, with chromosome sets of both diploid parent species. Based on these results, if this type of tetraploid formed in the wild, what would be the result? (Reference: Y. Kondo and A. Kashiwagi. 2004. Experimentally induced autotetraploidy and allotetraploidy in two Japanese pond frogs. Journal of Herpetology 38(3):381−92.)

choices.A: The two parent species would interbreed and fuse into one species.
choices.B: The two parent species would recognize each other as mates.
choices.C: The tetraploids would be reproductively isolated from both parent species.
choices.D: The tetraploids would be selected against.

questions.answer_text: The tetraploids would be reproductively isolated from both parent species.

questions.stem: How can reproductive barriers form sympatric populations while their members remain in the same geographic area?

choices.C: decreased sexual selection
choices.D: habitat sharing

questions.answer_text: polyploidy

questions.stem: Two species of tree frogs that live sympatrically in the northeastern United States differ in ploidy: Hyla chrysoscelis is diploid, and Hyla versicolor is tetraploid. The frogs are identical in appearance, but their mating calls, which females use to find mates, differ. Which difference most likely evolved first?

choices.C: habitat differentiation
choices.D: Polyploidy and different mating calls must have evolved at the same time.

questions.answer_text: polyploidy

questions.stem: In a hypothetical situation, a certain species of flea feeds only on pronghorn antelopes. In the western United States, pronghorns and cattle often associate with one another in the same open rangeland. Some of these fleas develop a strong preference for cattle blood and mate only with other fleas that prefer cattle blood. The host mammal can be considered as the fleas' habitat. If this situation persists, and new species evolve, this would be an example of ________.

choices.C: allopatric speciation and habitat isolation
choices.D: allopatric speciation and gametic isolation

questions.answer_text: sympatric speciation and habitat isolation

questions.stem: The difference between geographic isolation and habitat differentiation (isolation) is the ________.

choices.A: relative location of two populations as speciation occurs
choices.B: speed (tempo) at which two populations undergo speciation
choices.C: amount of genetic variation that occurs among two gene pools as speciation occurs
choices.D: identity of the kingdom or domain in which these phenomena occur

questions.answer_text: relative location of two populations as speciation occurs

questions.stem: Among known plant species, which of these have been the two most commonly occurring phenomena that have led to the origin of new species?

choices.C: sympatric speciation and sexual selection

chapter.title: The History of Life on Earth

questions.stem: The following question refers to this hypothetical situation. A female fly, full of fertilized eggs, is swept by high winds to an island far out to sea. She is the first fly to arrive on this island and the only fly to arrive in this way. Thousands of years later, her numerous offspring occupy the island, but none of them resembles her. There are, instead, several species, each of which eats only a certain type of food. None of the species can fly, and their balancing organs (halteres) are now used in courtship displays. The male members of each species bear modified halteres that are unique in appearance to their species. Females bear vestigial halteres. The ranges of all of the daughter species overlap. questions.stem: One hypothesis that has been proposed regarding the origin of life suggests that life evolved from an "RNA world" to today's "DNA world." Considering the properties of RNA and DNA molecules, which questions would direct an investigation of the most insightful test of this hypothesis?

choices.A: Is it likely that RNA molecules functioned as ribozymes to synthesize DNA from amino acids, and that this role was reversed when DNA became the information source?
choices.B: Is it likely that simple, yet stable RNA molecules served as a primitive precursor to a less stable DNA molecule that was more capable of storing more information?
choices.C: Could RNA have provided a template for DNA assembly, thereby enabling a more stable molecule that is replicated more accurately?
choices.D: Since ribozymes could freely enter and leave the vesicles, could these molecules have brought external DNA into the cell as a less stable, but more reliable storage molecule of double- stranded DNA?

chapter.title: The History of Life on Earth

questions.stem: Endosymbiosis is an evolutionary theory that explains the origin of eukaryotes and suggests a specific order in which this might have occurred. Ancestral cells engulfed and then began to use the metabolic processes of the smaller cells. Based on shared-core processes and features, which statement most accurately describes the order, the theory, and the evolutionary implications for all organisms within domain Eukarya?

choices.A: Ancestral heterotrophic eukaryotes most likely engulfed both a heterotrophic and an autotrophic prokaryote, whereas ancestral photosynthetic eukaryotes probably provided the host cell for the first mitochondria. Over time, natural selection favored these relationships, and these cells became ancestors of all eukaryotes.
choices.B: All ancestral eukaryotes would have most likely consumed a nucleus-like prokaryote that eventually became the eukaryotic nucleus. These new eukaryotic cells would have had an advantage over prokaryotic cells by acquiring a nuclear command center for regulating cellular activities.
choices.C: As carbon dioxide levels were increasing over time, natural selection would have favored organisms that acquired a photosynthetic prokaryote to convert carbon dioxide into sugars. These would have likely been the first eukaryotic cells. These ancestral cells engulfed mitochondria- like prokaryotes, which would have provided an even greater advantage for cells in this environment.
choices.D: As Earth was becoming more aerobic, mitochondria would have provided an advantage to host cells by converting "toxic" oxygen into energy for heterotrophic cells. Since mitochondria are found in all eukaryotes, these combinations likely evolved first. Photosynthetic eukaryotes probably acquired an autotrophic prokaryote, which developed an advantageous symbiotic relationship with the host cell.

questions.answer_text: As Earth was becoming more aerobic, mitochondria would have provided an advantage to host cells by converting "toxic" oxygen into energy for heterotrophic cells. Since mitochondria are found in all eukaryotes, these combinations likely evolved first. Photosynthetic eukaryotes probably acquired an autotrophic prokaryote, which developed an advantageous symbiotic relationship with the host cell.

questions.stem: Termites eat wood, but many do not produce enzymes themselves that will digest the cellulose in the wood. questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. Nitrogenase, the enzyme that catalyzes nitrogen fixation, is inhibited whenever free oxygen (O2) reaches a critical concentration. Consequently, nitrogen fixation cannot occur in cells wherein photosynthesis produces free O2. Consider the colonial aquatic cyanobacterium, Anabaena, whose heterocysts are described as having "...a thickened cell wall that restricts entry of O2 produced by neighboring cells. Intercellular connections allow heterocysts to transport fixed nitrogen to neighboring cells in exchange for carbohydrates." Given that the enzymes that catalyze nitrogen fixation are inhibited by oxygen, what mechanism might nitrogen-fixing prokaryotes use to protect these enzymes from oxygen?

choices.B: package the nitrogen fixation enzymes in membranes that are impermeable to all gases
choices.C: live only in anaerobic environments

questions.answer_text: live only in anaerobic environments

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. For several decades now, amphibian species worldwide have been in decline. Chytrid sporangia reside within the epidermal cells of infected animals, animals that consequently show areas of sloughed skin. They can also be lethargic, which is expressed through failure to hide and failure to flee. The infection cycle typically takes four to five days, at the end of which zoospores are released from sporangia into the environment. In some amphibian species, mortality rates approach 100%; other species seem able to survive the infection. If infection primarily involves the outermost layers of adult amphibian skin, and if the chytrids use the skin as their sole source of nutrition, then which term best applies to the chytrids?

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. Healthy individuals of Paramecium bursaria contain photosynthetic algal endosymbionts of the genus Chlorella. The zoochlorellae provide their hosts with glucose and oxygen, and P. bursaria provides its zoochlorellae with protection and motility. P. bursaria can lose its zoochlorellae in two ways: (1) if kept in darkness, the algae will die; and (2) if prey items (mostly bacteria) are absent from its habitat, P. bursaria will digest its zoochlorellae. A P. bursaria cell that has lost its zoochlorellae is aposymbiotic. questions.answer_text: commensalistic
