questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. The mechanism of cell crawling in protist species is not well defined. Pseudopodia extension involves interactions between actin and myosin (the same molecules that are involved in vertebrate muscle contraction). However, prior to the study described below, no one had provided convincing data that actin and myosin were actually involved in cell crawling in protists. Anatomical studies had identified the cytoskeletal protein actin just below the surface of the cell membrane in several species of protist, but physiological studies had failed to show a functional link between actin, myosin, and cell crawling. In a study by N. Poulsen et al. (Diatom gliding is the result of an actin-myosin motility system, Cell Motility and the Cytoskeleton 44 (1999):23-22), researchers tested whether motility in a particular species of diatom involves interactions between actin and myosin. Refer to the study by Poulsen et al. and the figure above. Latrunculin A is a reversible toxin that disrupts the formation of actin fibers. A culture of a particular species of diatom was treated with this toxin diluted in a buffer, while another culture was treated only with the buffer (no toxin; control). The motility of cells in each culture was assessed by counting the number of cells that were moving during a defined period of time. Which of the following conclusions is reasonable based on the above figure?

choices.A: Formation of actin fibers is not necessary for the movement in this species of diatom.
choices.B: The buffer alone largely inhibited movement in this species of diatom.
choices.C: In this species of diatom, fully formed actin fibers are necessary for movement.
choices.D: In this species of diatom, fully formed myosin proteins are necessary for movement.

questions.answer_text: In this species of diatom, fully formed actin fibers are necessary for movement.

As the rainy season ends, tough-walled fruits, each containing 8-25 seeds (Brazil nuts), fall to the forest floor. Brazil nuts are composed primarily of endosperm. About $50 million worth of nuts are harvested each year. Scientists have discovered that the pale yellow flowers of Brazil nut trees cannot fertilize themselves and admit only female orchid bees as pollinators. The agouti (Dasyprocta spp.), a cat-sized rodent, is the only animal with teeth strong enough to crack the hard wall of Brazil nut fruits. It typically eats some of the seeds, buries others, and leaves still others inside the fruit, which moisture can then enter and allow the remaining seeds to germinate. The same bees that pollinate the flowers of the Brazil nut trees also pollinate orchids, which are epiphytes (in other words, plants that grow on other plants); however, orchids cannot grow on Brazil nut trees. These observations explain ________.

choices.A: the coevolution of Brazil nut trees and orchids
choices.B: why Brazil nut trees do not set fruit in monoculture (all one species) plantations
choices.C: why male orchid bees do not pollinate Brazil nut tree flowers
choices.D: why male orchid bees are smaller than female orchid bees

questions.answer_text: why Brazil nut trees do not set fruit in monoculture (all one species) plantations

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. Suzanne Simard and colleagues knew that the same mycorrhizal fungal species could colonize multiple types of trees. They wondered if the same fungal individual would colonize different trees, forming an underground network that potentially could transport carbon and nutrients from one tree to another (S. Simard et al. 1997. Net transfer of carbon between mycorrhizal tree species in the field. Nature 388:579-82). Pots containing seedlings of three different tree species were set up and grown under natural conditions for three years (Fig. A). Two of the three species (Douglas fir, birch) could form ectomycorrhizal connections with the same fungal species, but the third species (cedar) could not form an ectomycorrhizal connection with the fungal species. In some of the pots, the researchers placed airtight bags over the Douglas fir and birch seedlings and injected carbon dioxide made from carbon-13 into the bags with the Douglas fir and carbon dioxide made from carbon-14 into the bags with the birch. (13C and 14C are different isotopes of carbon that can be detected and measured by researchers.) As the seedlings photosynthesized, the carbon dioxide was converted into sugars that could be tracked and measured by the researchers. The researchers measured whether the sugars in each plant contained only the carbon isotope that was in the air of their plastic bag or also the carbon isotope from the air around the other plant. Figure A Which of the following results would support Simard et al.'s (1997) hypothesis that fungi can move carbon from one plant to another? [Hypothesis: Sugars made by one plant during photosynthesis can travel through a mycorrhizal fungus and be incorporated into the tissues of another plant.]

choices.A: Carbon-14 is found in the birch seedling's tissues and carbon-13 in the Douglas fir.
choices.B: Carbon-14 is found in the Douglas fir seedling's tissues and carbon-13 in the birch.
choices.C: Either carbon-13 or carbon-14 is found in the fungal tissues.
choices.D: Either carbon-13 or carbon-14 is found in the cedar seedling's tissues.

questions.answer_text: Carbon-14 is found in the Douglas fir seedling's tissues and carbon-13 in the birch.

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. There is much discussion in the media about protecting biodiversity. But does biodiversity really matter? Canadian and Swiss researchers wanted to know if the diversity of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) was important to the productivity of grasslands (M.G.A. van der Heijden, J. N. Klironomos, M. Ursic, P. Moutoglis, R. Streitwolf-Engel, T. Boler, A. Wiemken, and I. R. Sanders. 1998. Mycorrhizal fungal diversity determines plant biodiversity, ecosystem variability, and productivity. Nature 396:69-72). Specifically, they wanted to know if it mattered which specific AMF species were present, or just that some type of AMF was present. They grew various plants in combination with one of four AMF species (A, B, C, and D), no AMF species (O), or all four AMF species together (A + B + C + D); and they measured plant growth under each set of conditions. All plant species were grown in each plot, so they always competed with each other, with the only difference being which AMF species were present. On the graphs, the x-axis labels indicate the number and identity of AMF species (bar 0 = no fungi; bars A - D = individual AMF species; bar A + B + C + D = all AMF species together). The y-axis indicates the amount (grams) of plant biomass for the species shown in italics above each graph. Based on the graphs in the figure, which of the following plant species is most likely not to form mycorrhizal associations?

choices.C: Sanguisorba officinalis (graph c)
choices.D: Centaurium erythrea (graph d)

questions.answer_text: Carex flacca (graph a)

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. They took these samples to the laboratory and experimentally treated them with various chemicals to produce fractions that contained (A) only fungi, (B) only bacteria, (C) only protozoa, and (D) all of the potential mutualists. questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. Rose-picker's disease is caused by the yeast Sporothrix schenkii (S. schenkii). The yeasts then assume a hyphal morphology and grow along the interiors of lymphatic vessels until they reach a lymph node. This often results in the accumulation of pus in the lymph node, which subsequently ulcerates through the skin surface and then drains. questions.stem: Use the information to answer the question. Trichoplax adhaerens is the only living species in the phylum Placozoa. T. adhaerens feeds on marine microbes, mostly unicellular green algae, by crawling atop the algae and trapping it between its ventral surface and the substrate. questions.stem: Use the information to answer the following question. The nontaxonomic term sea slug encompasses a wide variety of marine gastropods. One feature they share as adults is the lack of a shell. One might think, therefore, that they represent defenseless morsels for predators. In fact, sea slugs have multiple defenses. Some sea slugs prey on sponges and concentrate sponge toxins in their tissues. Others feed on cnidarians, digesting everything except the nematocysts, which they then transfer to their own skins. Whereas the most brightly colored sea slugs are often highly toxic, others are nontoxic and mimic the coloration of the toxic species. Their colors are mostly derived from pigments in their prey. There are also sea slugs that use their coloration to blend into their environments. This nudibranch, a type of sea slug, has many reddish cerata on its dorsal surface, as well as two white-tipped rhinophores located on the head. The nematocysts most likely reach the skin of sea slugs through branches of the ________.

choices.C: nephridium
choices.D: pseudocoelom

questions.answer_text: intestine

questions.stem: Use the information to answer the following question. The nontaxonomic term sea slug encompasses a wide variety of marine gastropods. One feature they share as adults is the lack of a shell. One might think, therefore, that they represent defenseless morsels for predators. In fact, sea slugs have multiple defenses. Some sea slugs prey on sponges and concentrate sponge toxins in their tissues. Others feed on cnidarians, digesting everything except the nematocysts, which they then transfer to their own skins. Whereas the most brightly colored sea slugs are often highly toxic, others are nontoxic and mimic the coloration of the toxic species. Their colors are mostly derived from pigments in their prey. There are also sea slugs that use their coloration to blend into their environments. This nudibranch, a type of sea slug, has many reddish cerata on its dorsal surface, as well as two white-tipped rhinophores located on the head. The nematocysts of sea slugs should be most effective at protecting individual sea slugs from predation if the predators ________.

choices.A: remove small bites of flesh from sea slugs and have long-term memory
choices.B: remove small bites of flesh from sea slugs and have no long-term memory
choices.C: consume entire sea slugs in one gulp and have no long-term memory
choices.D: consume entire sea slugs in one gulp and have long-term memory

questions.answer_text: remove small bites of flesh from sea slugs and have long-term memory

questions.stem: Use the information and figure to answer the following question. The sea slug Pteraeolidia ianthina can harbor living dinoflagellates (photosynthetic protists) in its skin. These endosymbiotic dinoflagellates reproduce quickly enough to maintain their populations. Low populations do not affect the sea slugs very much, but high populations (> 5 × 105 cells/mg of sea slug protein) can promote sea slug survival. Percent of sea slug respiratory carbon demand provided by indwelling dinoflagellates. If the dinoflagellate-containing sea slug P. ianthina preys on coral animals, then it would be most surprising to find that ________.

choices.A: P. ianthina can tolerate the toxin in the nematocysts of its prey
choices.B: P. ianthina can locate its coral prey by chemicals released into the water by corals
choices.C: the coral prey harbor dinoflagellates in their tissues
choices.D: the coral prey transform themselves into medusas to flee from approaching P. ianthina

questions.answer_text: the coral prey transform themselves into medusas to flee from approaching P. ianthina

questions.stem: Use the information and figure to answer the following question. The sea slug Pteraeolidia ianthina can harbor living dinoflagellates (photosynthetic protists) in its skin. These endosymbiotic dinoflagellates reproduce quickly enough to maintain their populations. Low populations do not affect the sea slugs very much, but high populations (> 5 × 105 cells/mg of sea slug protein) can promote sea slug survival. In the graph, the percent of the oxygen demand contributed by the dinoflagellates is greater than 100% during much of the year. What is the fate of this "excess" energy?

choices.A: It is dispersed as "entropy" (disorder in the system).
choices.B: It is saved for producing offspring by the sea slug.

questions.stem: The sea slug Elysia chorotica has no nematocysts or dinoflagellates but, rather, has "naked" chloroplasts in its skin. It spends most of its time basking in shallow water on the surface of seaweeds. How should we expect its chloroplasts to benefit the Elysia sea slug?

choices.B: provide Elysia with fixed carbon dioxide
choices.C: provide Elysia with fixed oxygen

questions.answer_text: provide Elysia with fixed carbon dioxide

questions.stem: Parasitism is one of the most widespread lifestyles ever to evolve. Which of the following is consistent with this finding?

choices.B: Parasites, unlike predators, feed on almost all the tissues of their host.
choices.C: Parasites do not generally kill their hosts; thus they can feed on the same host throughout the host's normal life span and do not have competition from decomposers.
choices.D: Parasites generally kill their host and can feed for a very long time because they are much smaller than their host.

questions.stem: Use the following information and figures to answer the question. Many terrestrial arthropods exchange gases with their environments by using tracheae, tubes that lead from openings (called spiracles) in the animal's exoskeleton or cuticle directly to the animal's tissues. Some arthropods can control whether their spiracles are opened or closed; opening the spiracles allows the carbon dioxide produced in the tissues to travel down the tracheae and be released outside the animal. Klok et al. measured the carbon dioxide emitted over time (represented by VCO2) by several species of centipedes. The figures present graphs of their results for two species, Cormocephalus morsitans and Scutigerina weberi. (C. J. Klok, R. D. Mercer, and S. L. Chown. 2002. Discontinuous gas-exchange in centipedes and its convergent evolution in tracheated arthropods. Journal of Experimental Biology 205:1019-29.) Copyright 2002 The Company of Biologists and the Journal of Experimental Biology. Look at the graph for Cormocephalus morsitans in the figure. What is the best interpretation of these results?

choices.A: The centipede had its spiracles open the entire time.
choices.B: The centipede had its spiracles closed the entire time.
choices.C: The centipede had its spiracles open when carbon dioxide (CO2) emission peaked and closed when CO2 emission was low.
choices.D: The centipede had its spiracles closed when carbon dioxide (CO2) emission peaked and open when CO2 emission was low.

questions.answer_text: The centipede had its spiracles open when carbon dioxide (CO2) emission peaked and closed when CO2 emission was low.

chapter.title: Plant Responses to Internal and External Signals

chapter.title: Plant Responses to Internal and External Signals

questions.stem: Many plants flower in response to day-length cues. Which of the following statements best summarizes this phenomenon?

choices.A: As a rule, short-day plants flower in the summer.

chapter.title: Plant Responses to Internal and External Signals

chapter.title: Plant Responses to Internal and External Signals

choices.D: exposing flower buds of the hibiscus bush to short nights

choices.C: C

chapter.title: Plant Responses to Internal and External Signals

choices.D: protoplast fusion experiments with xerophytic plants

chapter.title: Plant Responses to Internal and External Signals

chapter.title: Plant Responses to Internal and External Signals

chapter.title: Plant Responses to Internal and External Signals

chapter.title: Plant Responses to Internal and External Signals

questions.stem: A particular species of virus carries a gene for salicylate hydroxylase, an enzyme that breaks down salicylic acid. Will this virus be more or less virulent to plants than other viruses?

choices.C: same virulent
choices.D: faster virulent

questions.answer_text: more virulent

chapter.title: Plant Responses to Internal and External Signals

questions.stem: Which event during the evolution of land plants favored the synthesis of secondary compounds?

questions.answer_text: the rise of herbivory

chapter.title: Plant Responses to Internal and External Signals

choices.D: phytoalexins must be released

questions.answer_text: volatile "signal" compounds must be perceived

chapter.title: Plant Responses to Internal and External Signals

questions.stem: You may have observed plants rotate towards a light source, thereby increasing the plant's ability to intercept light energy and increase photosynthesis. You, however, are given the task of preventing grass seedlings from rotating toward the light. Using your knowledge of phototropism, which of the following experimental procedures would you use to complete your task?

choices.A: Cover the growing tip of the grass seedling with black paper.
choices.B: Supply the seedlings with very dim light (red light does not induce a bend).
choices.C: Cover the portion of the seedling below the tip with a black shield.
choices.D: Supply the seedling with nutrient-rich fertilizer solution.

questions.answer_text: Cover the growing tip of the grass seedling with black paper.

chapter.title: Plant Responses to Internal and External Signals

questions.stem: A plant scientist was hired by a greenhouse operator to devise a way to force iris plants to bloom in the short days of winter. Iris normally blooms as a long-day (short-night) plant. Which of the following has the best chance of creating iris blooms in winter?

choices.A: Artificially increase the period of darkness in the greenhouse.
choices.B: Increase the temperature to more closely follow summer temperatures.
choices.C: Alternate four hours of darkness with four hours of light repeatedly over each 24-hour period.
choices.D: Interrupt the long winter nights with a brief period of light.

questions.answer_text: Interrupt the long winter nights with a brief period of light.

chapter.title: Plant Responses to Internal and External Signals

questions.stem: An individual plant was discovered that could not grow towards light. After some research, it was determined that the reason was a defective gene that did not allow for the level of cell elongation necessary for a phototropic response. This mutation greatly reduces the fitness of the individual plant. Which reason best describes the reason for the loss of fitness?

choices.A: The plant was too short to attract insects for pollination.
choices.B: The plant could not adjust to directional light, which reduced photosynthetic activity and therefore energy available for reproduction.
choices.C: Because the plant grew much taller and straighter, resources that could be used for reproduction were used for growth.
choices.D: The loss of a phototropic response meant that the plant's seeds could not germinate, so reproduction would be unsuccessful.

questions.answer_text: The plant could not adjust to directional light, which reduced photosynthetic activity and therefore energy available for reproduction.

chapter.title: Plant Responses to Internal and External Signals

chapter.title: Basic Principles of Animal Form and Function

questions.answer_text: Relative to their volume, the young have more surface area across which they can transport all the oxygen they need.

chapter.title: Basic Principles of Animal Form and Function

choices.C: a large body volume, a long, tubular body, and a set of wings

questions.answer_text: an external respiratory surface, a small body size, and a two-cell-layered body

choices.B: many layers of cells stacked together

choices.B: it contains more than one type of cell

choices.B: cells that lengthen when appropriately stimulated

chapter.title: Basic Principles of Animal Form and Function

chapter.title: Basic Principles of Animal Form and Function

chapter.title: Basic Principles of Animal Form and Function

choices.D: heart rate.

questions.answer_text: heart rate.

questions.stem: When you hold your breath, which of the following blood gas changes first leads to the urge to breathe?

choices.C: rising CO2
choices.D: falling CO2

questions.answer_text: rising CO2

questions.stem: One feature that amphibians and humans have in common is

choices.B: a complete separation of circuits for circulation.
choices.C: the number of circuits for circulation.
choices.D: a low blood pressure in the systemic circuit.

questions.answer_text: the number of circuits for circulation.

questions.stem: If a molecule of CO2 released into the blood in your left toe is exhaled from your nose, it must pass through all of the following except

choices.C: the right atrium.
choices.D: the right ventricle.

questions.answer_text: the pulmonary vein.

questions.stem: Compared with the interstitial fluid that bathes active muscle cells, blood reaching these cells in arterioles has a

choices.C: greater bicarbonate concentration.
choices.D: lower pH.

questions.answer_text: higher PO2.

questions.stem: Innate immunity ________.

choices.A: is the first, and most general, mechanism of protection against pathogens
choices.B: depends on an infected animal's previous exposure to a pathogen
choices.C: is based on recognition of antigens that are specific to a pathogen
choices.D: is found only in vertebrates

questions.answer_text: is the first, and most general, mechanism of protection against pathogens

questions.stem: A strain of fruit fly lacks the ability to produce Dicer-2 protein. You might expect this strain to be more susceptible to ________ infections.

choices.C: fungal
choices.D: protozoan

questions.answer_text: viral

questions.stem: Vertebrate immune cells, which are phagocytic, include ________. I) neutrophils II) macrophages III) dendritic cells IV) natural killer cells

choices.C: I and IV
choices.D: I, II, and III

questions.answer_text: I, II, and III

questions.stem: The cells and signaling molecules involved in the initial stages of the inflammatory response are ________.

choices.C: mast cells and histamines
choices.D: lymphocytes and interferons

questions.answer_text: mast cells and histamines

questions.stem: Inflammatory responses typically include ________.

choices.A: increased activity of phagocytes in an inflamed area
choices.B: reduced permeability of blood vessels to conserve plasma
choices.C: release of substances to decrease the blood supply to an inflamed area
choices.D: inhibiting the release of white blood cells from bone marrow

questions.answer_text: increased activity of phagocytes in an inflamed area

questions.stem: ________ are receptor molecules on mammalian cells that recognize macromolecules that are present in or on certain groups of pathogens.

choices.C: Interferons
choices.D: Complement proteins

questions.answer_text: Toll-like receptors

questions.stem: Septic shock, a systemic response including high fever and low blood pressure, is a response to ________.

choices.C: the presence of natural killer cells
choices.D: increased production of neutrophils

questions.answer_text: certain bacterial infections

questions.stem: ________ are cells of the mammalian innate immune response that help destroy tumors.

choices.C: Macrophages
choices.D: B cells

questions.answer_text: Natural killer cells

questions.stem: Use the graphs to answer the following question. Mutant fruit flies that make only one antimicrobial peptide were tested for survival after infection with Neurospora crassa fungi or with Micrococcus luteus bacteria. The results shown in the graphs support the hypothesis that ________.

choices.A: adding the defensin gene to such mutants protects them from death by bacterial infection
choices.B: adding the drosomycin gene to such mutants protects them from death by bacterial infection
choices.C: wild-type flies with the full set of genes for antimicrobial peptides are highly susceptible to both fungal and bacterial pathogens
choices.D: the presence of any single antimicrobial peptide protects against both fungal and bacterial pathogens

questions.answer_text: adding the defensin gene to such mutants protects them from death by bacterial infection

questions.stem: A boy falls while riding his bike. A scrape on his hand almost immediately begins to bleed and becomes red, warm, and swollen. What response is occurring?

choices.C: adaptive immune response
choices.D: autoimmune response

questions.answer_text: inflammatory response

questions.stem: Acidity in human sweat is an example of ________.

choices.C: adaptive immunity
choices.D: innate immunity

questions.answer_text: innate immunity

questions.stem: The eyes and the respiratory tract are both protected against infections by ________.

choices.C: the release of slightly alkaline secretions
choices.D: the secretion of lysozyme onto their surfaces

questions.answer_text: the secretion of lysozyme onto their surfaces

questions.stem: The complement system is ________.

choices.A: a set of proteins involved in innate but not acquired immunity
choices.B: a group of proteins that includes interferons and interleukins
choices.C: a group of proteins that act together in a cascade fashion
choices.D: a set of proteins that act individually to attack and lyse microbes

questions.answer_text: a group of proteins that act together in a cascade fashion

questions.stem: Bacteria entering the body through a small cut in the skin ________.

choices.B: stimulate apoptosis of nearby body cells
choices.C: stimulate release of interferons
choices.D: activate a group of proteins called complement

questions.answer_text: activate a group of proteins called complement

questions.stem: Mucus occurs in both the respiratory and digestive tracts. What is its main immunological function?

choices.C: destruction of pathogens because it is acidic
choices.D: increasing oxygen absorption

questions.answer_text: physically trapping of pathogens

questions.stem: You and a friend were in line for a movie when you noticed the woman in front of you sneezing and coughing. Both of you were equally exposed to the woman's virus, but over the next few days, only your friend acquired flu-like symptoms and was ill for almost a week before recovering. Which one of the following is a logical explanation for this?

choices.A: Your friend had antibodies to that virus.
choices.B: You had an immunological memory of that virus.
choices.C: Your friend had an autoimmune disorder.
choices.D: Your friend had allergies.

questions.answer_text: You had an immunological memory of that virus.

questions.stem: Within a differentiated B cell, the rearrangement of DNA sequences between variable regions and joining regions is accomplished by a(n)________.

choices.C: telomerase
choices.D: recombinase

questions.answer_text: recombinase

questions.stem: Clonal selection and differentiation of B cells activated by antigen exposure leads to the production of ________.

choices.A: large quantities of the antigen initially recognized
choices.B: vast numbers of B cells with random antigen-recognition receptors
choices.C: long-lived erythrocytes that can later secrete antibodies for the antigen
choices.D: short-lived plasma cells that secrete antibodies for the antigen

questions.answer_text: short-lived plasma cells that secrete antibodies for the antigen

questions.stem: A newborn who is accidentally given a drug that destroys the thymus would most likely ________.

choices.B: be unable to genetically rearrange antigen receptors
choices.C: be unable to differentiate and mature T cells
choices.D: have a reduced number of B cells and be unable to form antibodies

questions.answer_text: be unable to differentiate and mature T cells

questions.stem: Clonal selection is an explanation for how ________.

choices.A: V, J, and C gene segments are rearranged
choices.B: an antigen can provoke production of high amounts of specific antibodies
choices.C: HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) can disrupt the immune system
choices.D: macrophages can recognize specific T cells and B cells

questions.answer_text: an antigen can provoke production of high amounts of specific antibodies

questions.stem: An immunoglobulin (Ig) molecule, of any class, with regions symbolized as C or V, H or L, has a light chain made up of ________.

choices.A: one C region and one V region
choices.B: one H region and one L region
choices.C: three H regions and one L region
choices.D: two C regions and two V regions

questions.answer_text: one C region and one V region

questions.stem: Immunological memory accounts for ________.

choices.A: the human body's ability to distinguish self from non-self
choices.B: the observation that some strains of the pathogen that causes dengue fever cause more severe disease than others
choices.C: the ability of a helper T cell to signal B cells via cytokines
choices.D: the ancient observation that someone who had recovered from the plague could safely care for those newly diseased

questions.answer_text: the ancient observation that someone who had recovered from the plague could safely care for those newly diseased

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question(s) below. An otherwise healthy student in your class was infected with EBV (the virus that causes infectious mononucleosis) when she was a child, at which time she had merely experienced a mild sore throat and swollen lymph nodes in her neck. When she is exposed to EBV again later in life, she does not get sick or have any symptoms of mononucleosis. Which of the following statements explains why your class mate does not exhibit symptoms of EBV infection?

choices.A: She was likely infected with a weaker strain of EBV during her second exposure.
choices.B: Complement proteins effectively controlled the EBV during the second infection.
choices.C: Memory T cells quickly recognized the virus upon the second exposure and destroyed the virally infected cells.
choices.D: Her innate immune response was better at recognizing the EBV antigen during the second infection.

questions.answer_text: Memory T cells quickly recognized the virus upon the second exposure and destroyed the virally infected cells.

questions.stem: How is a viral antigen, like EBV, recognized by T cells?

choices.A: An antigen fragment is presented within class I MHC to the T cell receptor.
choices.B: Interferon proteins stick to the surface of infected cells.
choices.C: T cells recognize antibodies that have bound to viral particles.
choices.D: The virus is engulfed by T cells using Toll-like receptors.

questions.answer_text: An antigen fragment is presented within class I MHC to the T cell receptor.

questions.stem: Vaccination offers protection against future exposure to pathogens because it ________.

choices.C: promotes inflammation
choices.D: enhances the activity of macrophages

questions.answer_text: triggers clonal expansion of lymphocytes

questions.stem: ________ is a characteristic of adaptive immunity but not innate immunity.

choices.C: Interferons
choices.D: Lysozyme

questions.answer_text: Memory

questions.stem: Lymphocytes mature in the ________. I) spleen II) thymus III) bone marrow

choices.C: only II and III
choices.D: I, II, and III

questions.answer_text: only II and III

questions.stem: Which of the following statements are fundamental to the clonal selection theory of how the adaptive immune system functions? I) Each lymphocyte has a unique membrane receptor that recognizes one antigen. II) When the lymphocyte binds an antigen, it is activated and begins dividing to form many identical copies of itself. III) Cloned lymphocytes have slight differences and are selected by the spleen for removal if they do not bind an antigen. IV) Cloned cells descend from an activated lymphocyte and persist even after the pathogen is eliminated.

choices.C: only I, II, and IV
choices.D: only II, III, and IV

questions.answer_text: only I, II, and IV

questions.stem: What major advantage is conveyed by having a system of adaptive immunity?

choices.A: It enables a rapid defense against an antigen that has been previously encountered.
choices.B: It enables an animal to counter most pathogens almost instantly the first time they are encountered.
choices.C: It results in effector cells with specificity for a large number of antigens.
choices.D: It allows for the destruction of antibodies.

questions.answer_text: It enables a rapid defense against an antigen that has been previously encountered.

questions.stem: Which of the following are similarities between B cells and T cells? I) They both recognize antigen using immunoglobulin receptors. II) Both B cells and T cells undergo clonal selection after encountering an antigen. III) B cells and T cells both maintain an immunological memory of previously encountered antigens.

choices.C: both II and III
choices.D: both I and II

questions.answer_text: both II and III

questions.stem: A certain cell type has existed in the blood and tissue of its vertebrate host's immune system for over 20 years. One day, it recognizes a newly arrived antigen and binds to it, subsequently triggering a secondary immune response in the body. Which of the following cell types most accurately describes this cell?

choices.C: memory cell
choices.D: macrophage

questions.answer_text: memory cell

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about epitopes are correct? I) B cell receptors bind to epitopes. II) T cell receptors bind to epitopes. III) There can be 10 or more different epitopes on each antigen. IV) There is a one-to-one correspondence between antigen and epitope.

choices.C: only I, II, and III
choices.D: only II, III, and IV

questions.answer_text: only I, II, and III

questions.stem: Which of the following proteins can be classified as immunoglobulins? I) T cell receptors II) B cell receptors III) Antigens

choices.C: both II and III
choices.D: both I and II

questions.answer_text: only II

questions.stem: What type of immunity is associated with breast feeding?

choices.C: passive immunity
choices.D: cell-mediated immunity

questions.answer_text: passive immunity

questions.stem: Select the pathway that would lead to the activation of cytotoxic T cells.

choices.A: B cell contact antigen → helper T cell is activated → clonal selection occurs
choices.B: body cell becomes infected with a virus → new viral proteins appear → class I MHC molecule-antigen complex displayed on cell surface
choices.C: complement is secreted → B cell contacts antigen → helper T cell activated → cytokines released
choices.D: cytotoxic T cells → class II MHC molecule-antigen complex displayed → cytokines released → cell lysis

questions.answer_text: body cell becomes infected with a virus → new viral proteins appear → class I MHC molecule-antigen complex displayed on cell surface

questions.stem: Arrange in the correct sequence these components of the mammalian immune system as it first responds to a pathogen. I) Pathogen is destroyed. II) Lymphocytes secrete antibodies. III) Antigens from a pathogen bind to antigen receptors on lymphocytes. IV) Lymphocytes specific to antigens from a pathogen become numerous. V) Only memory cells remain.

choices.C: IV → II → III → I → V
choices.D: III → IV → II → I → V

questions.answer_text: III → IV → II → I → V

questions.stem: A nonfunctional CD4 protein on a helper T cell would result in the helper T cell being unable to ________.

choices.C: stimulate a cytotoxic T cell
choices.D: interact with a class II MHC-antigen complex

questions.answer_text: interact with a class II MHC-antigen complex

questions.stem: CD4 and CD8 are ________.

choices.B: receptors present on the surface of natural killer cells
choices.C: molecules present on the surface of T cells where they interact with major histocompatibility (MHC) molecules
choices.D: molecules on the surface of antigen-presenting cells where they enhance B cell activity

questions.answer_text: molecules present on the surface of T cells where they interact with major histocompatibility (MHC) molecules

questions.stem: T cells of the immune system include ________.

choices.C: plasma, antigen-presenting, and memory cells
choices.D: lymphocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells

questions.answer_text: cytotoxic and helper cells

questions.stem: B cells interacting with helper T cells are stimulated to differentiate when ________.

choices.C: cytotoxic T cells present the class II MHC molecule-antigen complex on their surface
choices.D: helper T cells release cytokines

questions.answer_text: helper T cells release cytokines

questions.stem: When antibodies bind antigens, the clumping of antigens results from ________.

choices.A: the antibody having at least two binding regions
choices.C: bonds between class I and class II MHC molecules
choices.D: denaturation of the antibodies

questions.answer_text: the antibody having at least two binding regions

questions.stem: Phagocytosis of microbes by macrophages is enhanced by ________. I) the binding of antibodies to the surface of microbes II) antibody-mediated opsonization of microbes III) the release of cytokines by activated B cells

choices.C: only I and III
choices.D: I, II, and, III

questions.answer_text: only I and II

questions.stem: Naturally acquired passive immunity can result from the ________.

choices.C: placental transfer of antibodies
choices.D: absorption of pathogens through mucous membranes

questions.answer_text: placental transfer of antibodies

questions.stem: Jenner's successful use of cowpox virus as a vaccine against the smallpox virus was due to the fact that ________.

choices.A: the immune system responds nonspecifically to antigens
choices.B: the cowpox virus made antibodies in response to the presence of smallpox
choices.C: there are some epitopes (antigenic determinants) common to both pox viruses
choices.D: cowpox and smallpox are caused by the same virus

questions.answer_text: there are some epitopes (antigenic determinants) common to both pox viruses

questions.stem: An individual who has been bitten by a poisonous snake that has a fast-acting toxin would likely benefit from ________.

choices.A: vaccination with a weakened form of the toxin
choices.B: injection of antibodies to the toxin
choices.C: injection of interleukin-1
choices.D: injection of interferon

questions.answer_text: injection of antibodies to the toxin

questions.stem: For the successful development of a vaccine to be used against a pathogen, it is necessary that ________.

choices.A: the surface antigens of the pathogen stay the same
choices.B: all of the surface antigens on the pathogen be identified
choices.C: the pathogen has only one epitope
choices.D: the major histocompatibility (MHC) molecules are heterozygous

questions.answer_text: the surface antigens of the pathogen stay the same

questions.stem: The switch of one B cell from producing one class of antibody to another class of antibody that is responsive to the same antigen is due to ________.

choices.A: the rearrangement of V region genes in that clone of responsive B cells
choices.B: a switch in the kind of antigen-presenting cell that is involved in the immune response
choices.C: a patient's reaction to the first kind of antibody made by the plasma cells
choices.D: the rearrangement of immunoglobulin heavy-chain C region DNA

questions.answer_text: the rearrangement of immunoglobulin heavy-chain C region DNA

questions.stem: The number of major histocompatibility (MHC) protein combinations possible in a given population is enormous. However, an individual in that diverse population has a far more limited array of MHC molecules because ________.

choices.A: the MHC proteins are made from several different gene regions that are capable of rearranging in a number of ways
choices.B: MHC proteins from one individual can only be of class I or class II
choices.C: each of the MHC genes has a large number of alleles, but each individual only inherits two for each gene
choices.D: once a B cell has matured in the bone marrow, it is limited to two MHC response categories

questions.answer_text: each of the MHC genes has a large number of alleles, but each individual only inherits two for each gene

questions.stem: A bone marrow transplant may not be appropriate from a given donor (Jane) to a given recipient (Jane's cousin, Bob), even though Jane has previously given blood for one of Bob's needed transfusions, because ________.

choices.A: even though Jane's blood type is a match to Bob's, her major histocompatibility (MHC) proteins may not be a match
choices.B: a blood type match is less stringent than a match required for transplant because blood is more tolerant of change
choices.C: for each gene, there is only one blood allele but many tissue alleles
choices.D: Jane's MHC class II genes are not expressed in bone marrow

questions.answer_text: even though Jane's blood type is a match to Bob's, her major histocompatibility (MHC) proteins may not be a match

questions.stem: An immune response to a tissue graft will differ from an immune response to a bacterium because ________.

choices.A: MHC molecules of the donor may stimulate rejection of the graft tissue, but bacteria lack MHC molecules
choices.B: the tissue graft, unlike the bacterium, is isolated from the circulation and will not enter into an immune response
choices.C: a bacterium cannot escape the immune system by replicating inside normal body cells
choices.D: the graft will stimulate an autoimmune response in the recipient

questions.answer_text: MHC molecules of the donor may stimulate rejection of the graft tissue, but bacteria lack MHC molecules

questions.stem: Which of the following components of the immune system destroys cancerous cells by punching holes in plasma membranes and triggering apoptosis?

choices.C: plasma cells
choices.D: cytotoxic T cells

questions.answer_text: cytotoxic T cells

questions.stem: Which of the following should be the same in identical twins?

choices.B: the set of major histocompatibility (MHC) molecules produced
choices.C: the set of T cell antigen receptors produced
choices.D: the susceptibility to a particular virus

questions.answer_text: the set of major histocompatibility (MHC) molecules produced

questions.stem: Which of the following is crucial to activation of the adaptive immune response?

choices.B: presentation of MHC (major histocompatibility complex)-antigen complex on a cell surface
choices.C: activation of complement proteins
choices.D: phagocytosis of antibody-antigen complex by macrophages in the blood

questions.answer_text: presentation of MHC (major histocompatibility complex)-antigen complex on a cell surface

questions.stem: Which of the following components of the immune system destroys bacteria by punching holes in the wall of the bacteria?

choices.C: plasma cells
choices.D: major histocompatibility complex proteins

questions.answer_text: complement protein

questions.stem: Yearly vaccination of humans for influenza viruses is necessary because ________.

choices.A: of an increase in immunodeficiency diseases
choices.B: the flu can generate anaphylactic shock
choices.C: surviving the flu one year exhausts the immune system to nonresponsiveness the second year
choices.D: rapid mutation in flu viruses alters the surface proteins in infected host cells

questions.answer_text: rapid mutation in flu viruses alters the surface proteins in infected host cells

questions.stem: A patient who has a high level of mast cell activity, dilation of blood vessels, and acute drop in blood pressure is likely suffering from ________.

choices.B: a typical skin allergy (contact dermatitis) that can be treated by antihistamines
choices.C: an organ transplant, such as a skin graft
choices.D: anaphylactic shock immediately following exposure to an allergen

questions.answer_text: anaphylactic shock immediately following exposure to an allergen

questions.stem: The ability of some viruses to remain inactive (latent) for a period of time is exemplified by ________.

choices.A: influenza, a particular strain of which returns every 10-20 years
choices.B: herpes simplex viruses (oral or genital) whose reproduction is triggered by physiological or emotional stress in the host
choices.C: Kaposi's sarcoma, which causes a skin cancer in people with AIDS but rarely in those not infected by HIV
choices.D: the virus that causes a form of the common cold, which recurs in patients many times in their lives

questions.answer_text: herpes simplex viruses (oral or genital) whose reproduction is triggered by physiological or emotional stress in the host

questions.stem: A patient complaining of watery, itchy eyes and sneezing after being given a flower bouquet as a birthday gift should first be treated with ________.

choices.C: antihistamines
choices.D: monoclonal antibodies

questions.answer_text: antihistamines

questions.stem: Which of the following would help a virus avoid triggering an effective adaptive immune response? I) having frequent mutations in genes for surface proteins II) building the viral shell from host proteins III) producing proteins very similar to those of other viruses IV) infecting and killing helper T cells

choices.C: only I, II, and III
choices.D: only II, III, and IV

questions.answer_text: only I, II, and IV

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of autoimmune disease?

choices.A: a condition in which B and T cells trigger anaphylactic shock in response to an antigen
choices.B: a condition in which the adaptive immune system fails to recognize the second infection by the same antigen
choices.C: a condition in which self molecules are treated as nonself (loss of self-tolerance)
choices.D: a condition in which the immune system creates random antibodies without being triggered by a specific antigen

questions.answer_text: a condition in which self molecules are treated as nonself (loss of self-tolerance)

questions.stem: If a person is prone to allergies, what treatment could redirect their immune response to help prevent future allergic reactions?

choices.A: stimulating activated B cells to switch antibody production from class IgE to class IgM
choices.B: blocking the antigen recognition sites of IgM antibodies
choices.C: reducing the number of helper T cells in the body
choices.D: reducing the number of cytotoxic cells

questions.answer_text: stimulating activated B cells to switch antibody production from class IgE to class IgM

questions.stem: In a humoral or antibody-mediated immune response, specific B cells are stimulated by helper T cells to transform into plasma cells that secrete antibodies. What would be an important feature added to the plasma cells during this transition process that allows them to better perform their function?

choices.A: duplication of specific gene sequences for the appropriate antibody
choices.B: increased rough endoplasmic reticulum for greater antibody production
choices.C: duplication of lysosomes in order to store the antibodies before transport
choices.D: increased antigen presentation on the surface of the plasma cells

questions.answer_text: increased rough endoplasmic reticulum for greater antibody production

questions.stem: Which of these is not part of insect immunity?

choices.C: phagocytosis by hemocytes
choices.D: production of antimicrobial peptides

questions.answer_text: activation of natural killer cells

questions.stem: An epitope associates with which part of an antigen receptor or antibody?

choices.C: variable regions of a heavy chain and light chain combined
choices.D: the light-chain constant regions only

questions.answer_text: variable regions of a heavy chain and light chain combined

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the difference between responses of effector B cells (plasma cells) and those of cytotoxic T cells?

choices.A: B cells confer active immunity; cytotoxic T cells confer passive immunity.
choices.B: B cells respond the first time a pathogen is present; cytotoxic T cells respond subsequent times.
choices.C: B cells secrete antibodies against a pathogen; cytotoxic T cells kill pathogen-infected host cells.
choices.D: B cells carry out the cell-mediated response; cytotoxic T cells carry out the humoral response.

questions.answer_text: B cells secrete antibodies against a pathogen; cytotoxic T cells kill pathogen-infected host cells.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is not true?

choices.A: An antibody has more than one antigen-binding site.
choices.B: A lymphocyte has receptors for multiple different antigens.
choices.C: An antigen can have different epitopes.
choices.D: A liver or muscle cell makes one class of MHC molecule.

questions.answer_text: A lymphocyte has receptors for multiple different antigens.

questions.stem: Which of the following should be the same in identical twins?

choices.B: the set of MHC molecules produced
choices.C: the set of T cell antigen receptors produced
choices.D: the set of immune cells eliminated as self-reactive

questions.answer_text: the set of MHC molecules produced

questions.stem: Vaccination increases the number of

choices.A: different receptors that recognize a pathogen.
choices.B: lymphocytes with receptors that can bind to the pathogen.
choices.C: epitopes that the immune system can recognize.
choices.D: MHC molecules that can present an antigen.

questions.answer_text: lymphocytes with receptors that can bind to the pathogen.

questions.stem: Which of the following would not help a virus avoid triggering an adaptive immune response?

choices.A: having frequent mutations in genes for surface proteins
choices.B: infecting cells that produce very few MHC molecules
choices.C: producing proteins very similar to those of other viruses
choices.D: infecting and killing helper T cells

questions.answer_text: producing proteins very similar to those of other viruses

questions.stem: The force driving simple diffusion is ________, while the energy source for active transport is ________.

choices.C: transmembrane pumps; electron transport
choices.D: phosphorylated protein carriers; ATP

questions.answer_text: the concentration gradient; ATP

questions.stem: To maintain homeostasis, freshwater fish must ________.

choices.C: excrete large quantities of water
choices.D: take in electrolytes through simple diffusion

questions.answer_text: excrete large quantities of water

questions.stem: Single-celled Paramecium live in pond water (a hypotonic environment relative to the cytosol). They have a structural feature, a contractile vacuole, which enables them to osmoregulate. If sucrose or saline was added to the pond water in different concentrations (in millimolars, mM), under which conditions would you expect the contractile vacuole to be most active?

choices.C: 0.08 mM sucrose
choices.D: 1.0 mM saline

questions.answer_text: 0.0 mM sucrose

questions.stem: Like other osmoregulatory animals that live in marine environments, sharks maintain tissue concentrations of sodium, potassium, and chloride that are hypoosmotic to the seawater. In contrast to the bony marine fishes, however, sharks do not need to drink seawater. Why?

choices.A: High urea and trimethylamine oxide concentrations keep shark tissues slightly hyperosmotic relative to seawater, so water is absorbed passively.
choices.B: Sodium, chloride, and potassium do not influence water balance in shark tissues.
choices.C: Shark blood is hypotonic to the surrounding tissues, so water always moves passively into the tissue from the blood.
choices.D: Sharks excrete large quantities of salt through their gills in exchange for water

questions.answer_text: High urea and trimethylamine oxide concentrations keep shark tissues slightly hyperosmotic relative to seawater, so water is absorbed passively.

questions.stem: What role do transport epithelia play in osmoregulation of marine fish with bony skeletons?

choices.A: They actively transport salt into the animal through the gills.
choices.B: They mediate the movement of water from seawater through the gills.
choices.C: They are involved in excretion of excess salt.
choices.D: They allow the fish to produce dilute urine.

questions.answer_text: They are involved in excretion of excess salt.

questions.stem: Salmon eggs hatch in fresh water. The fish then migrate to the ocean (a hypertonic solution) and, after several years of feeding and growing, return to fresh water to breed. How can these organisms make the transition from fresh water to ocean water and back to fresh water?

choices.A: The rectal gland functions in the ocean water, and chloride cells function in fresh water.
choices.B: The salt transport mechanisms of the gill epithelia change during migration.
choices.C: Salmon in fresh water excrete concentrated urine, and salmon in salt water secrete dilute urine.
choices.D: Their metabolism changes in salt water to degrade electrolytes.

questions.answer_text: The salt transport mechanisms of the gill epithelia change during migration.

questions.stem: Terrestrial organisms lose water through evaporation. In what ecosystem might an entomologist find a good study organism to examine the prevention of water loss?

choices.C: prairie
choices.D: chaparral

questions.answer_text: desert

questions.stem: An examination of a marine sea star that had died after it was mistakenly placed in fresh water would likely show that it died because ________.

choices.A: it was stressed and needed more time to acclimate to the new conditions
choices.B: it was so hypertonic to the fresh water that it could not osmoregulate
choices.C: its kidney had ruptured
choices.D: its cells dehydrated and lost the ability to metabolize

questions.answer_text: it was so hypertonic to the fresh water that it could not osmoregulate

questions.stem: The body fluids of an osmoconformer would be ________ with its ________ environment

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. Estrogens found in the environment have raised concerns about effects on reproductive health of animals. Researchers studied the effects that estrogens in the water have on sexual differentiation in zebrafish. They exposed embryo-larval (0-21 days post-hatching), juvenile (21-42 days post- hatching), and adult (over 200 days post-hatching) fish to three concentrations of 17β-estradiol (5, 25, and 100 nanograms/liter) that are within the range of concentrations found in water leaving sewage treatment plants in different countries. They then examined the proportion of males and females when the fish exposed at embryo-larval and juvenile stages reached adulthood. Embryo-larval stage fish that had been exposed to 100 ng/l 17β-estradiol resulted in adult populations that had substantially more females than males compared to control groups. Embryo-larval fish that had been exposed to 5 and 25 ng/l of 17β-estradiol did not show a statistically significant shift in the proportion of females. (Brion, F., C. R. Tyler, X. Palazzi, B. Laillet, J. M. Porcher, J. Garric, and P. Flammarion. 2004. Impacts of 17β-estradiol, including environmentally relevant concentrations, on reproduction after exposure during embryo-larval-, juvenile-, and adult-life stages in zebrafish (Danio rerio). Aquatic Toxicology 68:193-217.) What is the significance of using the concentrations of 5, 25, and 100 ng/l of 17β-estradiol in this experiment?

choices.A: These concentrations are similar to those found in many animals.
choices.B: These concentrations are found in the environment.
choices.C: These concentrations are effective, yet not lethal to the fish.
choices.D: These concentrations are standard in toxicology assays.

questions.answer_text: These concentrations are found in the environment.

questions.stem: The arrangement of organs and tissues in their characteristic places in 3-D space defines ________.

questions.stem: If the apical ectodermal ridge is surgically removed from an embryo, it will lose ________.

choices.C: unequal cytokinesis of blastomeres
choices.D: the developmental substrate for the kidneys

questions.answer_text: positional information for limb-bud pattern formation

questions.stem: The nematode Caenorhabditis elegans ________.

choices.A: is composed of about 1,000 cells, in which the developmental origin of each cell has been mapped
choices.B: has only a single chromosome, which has been fully sequenced
choices.C: has about 1,000 genes, each of which has been fully sequenced
choices.D: uniquely, among animals, utilizes programmed cell death during normal development

questions.answer_text: is composed of about 1,000 cells, in which the developmental origin of each cell has been mapped

questions.stem: In humans, identical twins are possible because ________.

choices.A: cytoplasmic determinants are distributed unevenly in unfertilized eggs
choices.B: extraembryonic cells interact with the zygote nucleus
choices.C: early blastomeres can form a complete embryo if isolated
choices.D: the gray crescent divides the dorsal-ventral axis into new cells

questions.answer_text: early blastomeres can form a complete embryo if isolated

questions.stem: Cells transplanted from the neural tube of a frog embryo to the ventral part of another embryo develop into nervous system tissues. This result indicates that the transplanted cells were ________.

choices.C: differentiated
choices.D: mesenchymal

questions.answer_text: determined

questions.stem: Embryonic induction, the influence of one group of cells on another group of cells, plays a critical role in embryonic development. In 1924, Hans Spemann and Hilde Mangold transplanted a piece of tissue that influences the formation of the notochord and neural tube, from the dorsal lip of an amphibian embryo to the ventral side of another amphibian embryo. If embryonic induction occurred, which of the following observations justifies the claim of embryonic induction?

choices.A: The transplanted tissue induced multiple limbs to develop on the ventral side of the recipient embryo.
choices.B: The transplanted tissue inhibited normal cell division on the dorsal side of the recipient embryo that lead to its death.
choices.C: The transplanted tissue had no effect on either the ventral or dorsal side of the recipient embryo so it continued to develop normally.
choices.D: The transplanted tissue induced the formation of a second notochord and neural tube on the ventral side of the developing embryo.

questions.answer_text: The transplanted tissue induced the formation of a second notochord and neural tube on the ventral side of the developing embryo.

questions.stem: Just prior to the onset of gastrulation in an embryo, the "organizer" cells are specified. If you were to experimentally block the specification of these cells, what would you expect the result to be in the developing embryo?

choices.A: There would be no effect on development.
choices.B: Gastrulation would not occur, and normal development would cease.
choices.C: The body axes would develop normally, but the embryo would not grow appendages.
choices.D: The embryo would not develop an intestine, but all other organs and tissues would develop normally.

questions.answer_text: Gastrulation would not occur, and normal development would cease.

questions.stem: The cortical reaction of sea urchin eggs functions directly in

choices.A: the formation of a fertilization envelope.
choices.B: the production of a fast block to polyspermy.
choices.C: the generation of an electrical impulse by the egg.
choices.D: the fusion of egg and sperm nuclei.

questions.answer_text: the formation of a fertilization envelope.

questions.stem: Which of the following is common to the development of both birds and mammals?

choices.C: trophoblast
choices.D: gray crescent

questions.answer_text: epiblast and hypoblast

questions.stem: The archenteron develops into

choices.C: the placenta.
choices.D: the lumen of the digestive tract.

questions.answer_text: the lumen of the digestive tract.

questions.stem: What structural adaptation in chickens allows them to lay their eggs in arid environments rather than in water?

choices.C: cleavage
choices.D: gastrulation

questions.answer_text: extraembryonic membranes

questions.stem: If an egg cell were treated with EDTA, a chemical that binds calcium and magnesium ions,

choices.A: the acrosomal reaction would be blocked.
choices.B: the fusion of sperm and egg nuclei would be blocked.
choices.C: the fast block to polyspermy would not occur.
choices.D: the fertilization envelope would not form.

questions.answer_text: the fertilization envelope would not form.

questions.stem: In humans, identical twins are possible because

choices.A: extraembryonic cells interact with the zygote nucleus.
choices.C: early blastomeres can form a complete embryo if isolated.

questions.answer_text: early blastomeres can form a complete embryo if isolated.

questions.stem: Cells transplanted from the neural tube of a frog embryo to the ventral part of another embryo develop into nervous system tissues. This result indicates that the transplanted cells were

choices.C: differentiated.
choices.D: mesenchymal.

questions.answer_text: determined.

questions.stem: The three stages of information processing in animals include ________.

choices.B: dendrites, a cell body, and an axon
choices.C: a presynaptic cell, neurotransmitters, and a postsynaptic cell
choices.D: sensory reception, an integrating center, and effectors (motor neurons)

questions.answer_text: sensory reception, an integrating center, and effectors (motor neurons)

questions.stem: Most of the neurons in the human central nervous system are ________.

choices.C: interneurons
choices.D: peripheral neurons

questions.answer_text: interneurons

questions.stem: The motor (somatic nervous) system can alter the activities of its targets, the skeletal muscle fibers, because ________.

choices.A: it is electrically coupled by gap junctions to the muscles
choices.B: its signals bind to receptor proteins on the muscles
choices.C: its signals reach the muscles via the blood
choices.D: it is connected to the internal neural network of the muscles

questions.answer_text: its signals bind to receptor proteins on the muscles

questions.stem: The point of connection between two communicating neurons is called the ________.

choices.C: synapse
choices.D: cell body

questions.answer_text: synapse

questions.stem: In a simple synapse, neurotransmitter chemicals are released by ________.

choices.C: cell bodies
choices.D: ducts on the smooth endoplasmic reticulum

questions.answer_text: the presynaptic membrane

questions.stem: In a simple synapse, neurotransmitter chemicals are received by ________.

choices.C: axon hillocks
choices.D: cell bodies

questions.answer_text: dendrites

questions.stem: Although the membrane of a "resting" neuron is highly permeable to potassium ions, its membrane potential does not exactly match the equilibrium potential for potassium because the neuronal membrane is also ________.

choices.C: impermeable to sodium ions
choices.D: highly permeable to chloride ions

questions.answer_text: slightly permeable to sodium ions

questions.stem: The operation of the sodium-potassium pump moves ________.

choices.A: sodium and potassium ions into the cell
choices.B: sodium and potassium ions out of the cell
choices.C: sodium ions into the cell and potassium ions out of the cell
choices.D: sodium ions out of the cell and potassium ions into the cell

questions.answer_text: sodium ions out of the cell and potassium ions into the cell

questions.stem: A researcher uses the chemical inhibitor cyanide to reduce ATP production in a neuron. What would be one effect of preventing ATP production?

choices.A: The sodium and potassium channels would all be closed.
choices.B: The membrane would become more permeable to sodium.
choices.C: Disruption to the normal "resting" distribution of potassium and sodium ions.
choices.D: A physical breakdown of the plasma membrane would occur.

questions.answer_text: Disruption to the normal "resting" distribution of potassium and sodium ions.

questions.stem: In a resting potential, an example of a cation that is more abundant as a solute in the cytosol of a neuron than it is in the interstitial fluid outside the neuron is ________.

choices.C: Na+
choices.D: K+

questions.answer_text: K+

questions.stem: The membrane potential in which there is no net movement of the ion across the membrane is called the ________.

choices.C: equilibrium potential
choices.D: action potential

questions.answer_text: equilibrium potential

questions.stem: Two fundamental concepts about the ion channels of a "resting" neuron are that the channels ________.

choices.A: are always open, but the concentration gradients of ions frequently change
choices.B: are always closed, but ions move closer to the channels during excitation
choices.C: are open or closed depending on their type, and are specific as to which ion can traverse them
choices.D: open in response to stimuli, and then close simultaneously, in unison

questions.answer_text: are open or closed depending on their type, and are specific as to which ion can traverse them

questions.stem: If you experimentally increase the concentration of Na+ outside a cell while maintaining other ion concentrations as they were, what would happen to the cell's membrane potential?

choices.A: The membrane potential would become more negative.
choices.B: The membrane potential would become more positive.
choices.C: The membrane potential would be unaffected.
choices.D: The answer depends on the thermodynamic potential.

questions.answer_text: The membrane potential would become more positive.

questions.stem: The concentrations of ions are very different inside and outside a nerve cell due to ________.

choices.C: sodium-potassium pumps
choices.D: symports and antiports

questions.answer_text: sodium-potassium pumps

questions.stem: Which of the following ions is most likely to cross the plasma membrane of a resting neuron?

choices.C: Ca2+
choices.D: Cl-

questions.answer_text: K+

questions.stem: The Nernst equation specifies the equilibrium potential for a particular ion. This equilibrium potential is a function of ________.

choices.C: osmotic gradient
choices.D: temperature (thermal) gradient

questions.answer_text: ion concentration gradient

questions.stem: Use the information in the table to answer the question. Extracellular concentration Intracellular concentration Ion (mM) (mM) Na+ 300 50 K+ 40 350 Calculate the equilibrium potential for potassium. Assume a temperature of 37°C.

Refer to the following graph of an action potential to answer the question. The membrane potential is closest to the equilibrium potential for potassium at label ________.

choices.C: C
choices.D: D

questions.stem: Refer to the following graph of an action potential to answer the question. The membrane's permeability to sodium ions is greatest at label ________.

choices.C: C
choices.D: D

questions.answer_text: B

questions.stem: Refer to the following graph of an action potential to answer the question. The minimum graded depolarization needed to operate the voltage-gated sodium and potassium channels is indicated by the label ________.

choices.C: D
choices.D: E

questions.answer_text: A

choices.C: D
choices.D: E

questions.answer_text: C

questions.stem: Refer to the following graph of an action potential to answer the question. The neuronal membrane is at its resting potential at label ________.

choices.C: D
choices.D: E

questions.stem: For a neuron with an initial membrane potential at -70 mV, an increase in the movement of potassium ions out of that neuron's cytoplasm would result in the ________.

choices.C: replacement of potassium ions with sodium ions
choices.D: replacement of potassium ions with calcium ions

questions.answer_text: hyperpolarization of the neuron

questions.stem: Opening all of the sodium channels on an otherwise typical neuron, with all other ion channels closed (which is an admittedly artificial setting), should move its membrane potential to ________.

choices.C: equilibrium potential for sodium
choices.D: The membrane potential would not change, only the ion concentrations would change.

questions.answer_text: equilibrium potential for sodium

questions.stem: A graded hyperpolarization of a membrane can be induced by ________.

choices.A: increasing its membrane's permeability to Na+
choices.B: decreasing its membrane's permeability to Cl-
choices.C: increasing its membrane's permeability to Ca++
choices.D: increasing its membrane's permeability to K+

questions.answer_text: increasing its membrane's permeability to K+

questions.stem: Conduction and refractory periods (states) are typical of ________.

choices.C: excitatory postsynaptic potentials
choices.D: threshold potentials

questions.answer_text: action potentials

questions.stem: The "threshold" potential of a membrane is the ________.

choices.A: lowest frequency of action potentials a neuron can produce
choices.B: minimum hyperpolarization needed to prevent the occurrence of action potentials
choices.C: minimum depolarization needed to operate the voltage-gated sodium and potassium channels
choices.D: peak amount of depolarization seen in an action potential

questions.answer_text: minimum depolarization needed to operate the voltage-gated sodium and potassium channels

questions.stem: Action potentials move along axons ________.

choices.A: more slowly in axons of large than in small diameter
choices.B: by activating the sodium-potassium "pump" at each point along the axonal membrane
choices.C: more rapidly in myelinated than in unmyelinated axons
choices.D: by reversing the concentration gradients for sodium and potassium ions

questions.answer_text: more rapidly in myelinated than in unmyelinated axons

questions.stem: Pyrethroid insecticides prevent the voltage-gated sodium channels of insects from inactivating. Neurons that were exposed to pyrethroids would ________.

choices.A: become hyperpolarized during an action potential
choices.B: not repolarize during an action potential
choices.C: not be able to open potassium channels
choices.D: not release neurotransmitter molecules

questions.answer_text: not repolarize during an action potential

questions.stem: After the depolarization phase of an action potential, the resting potential is restored by ________.

choices.A: the opening of voltage-gated potassium channels and the inactivation of sodium channels
choices.B: a decrease in the membrane's permeability to potassium and chloride ions
choices.C: a brief inhibition of the sodium-potassium pump
choices.D: the opening of more voltage-gated sodium channels

questions.answer_text: the opening of voltage-gated potassium channels and the inactivation of sodium channels

questions.stem: The "undershoot" phase of hyperpolarization is due to ________.

choices.A: slow opening of voltage-gated sodium channels
choices.B: sustained opening of voltage-gated potassium channels
choices.C: rapid opening of voltage-gated calcium channels
choices.D: slow restorative actions of the sodium-potassium ATPase

questions.answer_text: sustained opening of voltage-gated potassium channels

questions.stem: The fastest possible conduction velocity of action potentials is observed in ________.

choices.C: thick, unmyelinated neurons
choices.D: thick, myelinated neurons

questions.answer_text: thick, myelinated neurons

questions.stem: Action potentials are normally carried in only one direction: from the axon hillock toward the axon terminals. If you experimentally depolarize the middle of the axon to threshold, using an electronic probe, then ________.

choices.A: no action potential will be initiated
choices.B: an action potential will be initiated and proceed only in the normal direction toward the axon terminal
choices.C: an action potential will be initiated and proceed only back toward the axon hillock
choices.D: two action potentials will be initiated, one going toward the axon terminal and one going back toward the hillock

questions.answer_text: two action potentials will be initiated, one going toward the axon terminal and one going back toward the hillock

questions.stem: Why are action potentials usually conducted in one direction?

choices.A: The nodes of Ranvier conduct potentials in one direction.
choices.B: The brief refractory period prevents reopening of voltage-gated sodium channels.
choices.C: The axon hillock has a higher membrane potential than the terminals of the axon.
choices.D: Voltage-gated channels for both Na+ and K+ open in only one direction.

questions.answer_text: The brief refractory period prevents reopening of voltage-gated sodium channels.

questions.stem: If you experimentally increase the concentration of K+ inside a cell while maintaining other ion concentrations as they were, what would happen to the cell's membrane potential?

choices.A: The membrane potential would become more negative.
choices.B: The membrane potential would become less negative.
choices.C: The membrane potential would remain the same.
choices.D: The membrane potential would first become more negative and then less negative.

questions.answer_text: The membrane potential would become less negative.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about action potentials is correct?

choices.A: Action potentials for a given neuron vary in magnitude.
choices.B: Action potentials for a given neuron vary in duration.
choices.C: Action potentials are propagated down the length of the axon.
choices.D: Movement of ions during the action potential occurs mostly through the sodium pump.

questions.answer_text: Action potentials are propagated down the length of the axon.

questions.stem: Why do Na+ ions enter the cell when voltage-gated Na+ channels are opened in neurons?

choices.A: because the Na+ concentration is much lower outside the cell than it is inside
choices.B: because the Na+ ions are actively transported by the sodium-potassium pump into the cell
choices.C: because the Na+ concentration is much higher outside the cell than it is inside, and the Na+ ions are attracted to the negatively charged interior
choices.D: because the Na+ concentration is much higher outside the cell than it is inside, and the Na+ ions are actively transported by the sodium-potassium pump into the cell

questions.answer_text: because the Na+ concentration is much higher outside the cell than it is inside, and the Na+ ions are attracted to the negatively charged interior

questions.stem: What would probably happen if a long neuron had one continuous myelin sheath down the length of the axon with no nodes of Ranvier?

choices.A: The action potential would be propagated nearly instantaneously to the synapse.
choices.B: There could be no action potential generated at the axon hillock.
choices.C: The signal would fade because it is not renewed by the opening of more sodium channels.
choices.D: Only potassium could move across the membrane, but not sodium.

questions.answer_text: The signal would fade because it is not renewed by the opening of more sodium channels.

questions.stem: A neurophysiologist is investigating nerve reflexes in two different animals: a crab and a fish. Action potentials are found to pass more rapidly along the fish's neurons. What is the most likely explanation?

choices.A: The fish's axons are smaller in diameter; small axons transmit action potentials faster than large axons do.
choices.B: Unlike the crab, the fish's axons are wrapped in myelin.
choices.C: There are more ion channels in the axons of the crab compared with fish axons.
choices.D: Unlike the crab, the fish's axons are wrapped in myelin, and the fish's axons are smaller in diameter; small axons transmit action potentials faster than large axons do.

questions.answer_text: Unlike the crab, the fish's axons are wrapped in myelin.

questions.stem: Tetrodotoxin blocks voltage-gated sodium channels, and ouabain blocks sodium-potassium pumps. If you added both tetrodotoxin and ouabain to a solution containing neural tissue, what responses would you expect?

choices.B: immediate loss of action potential with gradual shift of resting potential
choices.C: slow decrease of resting potential and action potential amplitudes
choices.D: No effect; the substances counteract each other.

questions.answer_text: immediate loss of action potential with gradual shift of resting potential

questions.stem: Which of the following will increase the speed of an action potential moving down an axon? I) Action potentials move faster in wider axons. II) Action potentials move faster in axons lacking potassium ion channels. III) Action potentials move faster in myelinated axons.

choices.C: only I and III
choices.D: I, II, and III

questions.answer_text: only I and III

questions.stem: In multiple sclerosis, the myelin sheaths around the axons of the brain and spinal cord are damaged and demyelination results. How does this disease manifest at the level of the action potential? I) Action potentials move in the opposite direction on the axon. II) Action potentials move more slowly along the axon. III) No action potentials are transmitted.

choices.C: only III
choices.D: only II and III

questions.answer_text: only II

questions.stem: Neurotransmitters are released from axon terminals via ________.

questions.answer_text: exocytosis

questions.stem: Acetylcholine released into the junction between a motor neuron and a skeletal muscle binds to a sodium/potassium channel and opens it. This is an example of ________.

choices.D: a chemical that inhibits action potentials

questions.answer_text: a ligand-gated channel

choices.C: ATP
choices.D: all neurotransmitter molecules

questions.stem: An example of ligand-gated ion channels is ________.

choices.A: the spreading of action potentials in the heart

questions.stem: One-way synaptic transmission occurs because ________.

choices.A: only dendrites can respond to electrical signals

questions.answer_text: receptors for neurotransmitters are mostly found on the postsynaptic membrane

questions.stem: Neurotransmitters can affect postsynaptic cells by ________. I) initiating signal transduction pathways in the cells II) causing molecular changes in the cells III) altering ion channel proteins IV) altering the permeability of the cells

choices.C: III and IV

questions.stem: The amino acid that operates at most inhibitory synapses in the brain is ________.

choices.C: nitric oxide

questions.stem: The botulinum toxin, which causes botulism, reduces the synaptic release of ________.

choices.C: nitric oxide
choices.D: gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)

questions.answer_text: acetylcholine

questions.stem: The heart rate of a vertebrate will decrease in response to the arrival of ________.

choices.C: nitric oxide
choices.D: gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)

questions.answer_text: acetylcholine

questions.stem: A chemical that affects neuronal function but is not stored in presynaptic vesicles is ________.

choices.C: nitric oxide
choices.D: gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)
