questions.stem: Of those listed, which event occurs first following a depolarizing stimulus applied to the presynaptic membrane of an axon terminal?

questions.stem: How could you increase the magnitude of excitatory postsynaptic potentials (EPSPs) generated at a synapse?

questions.stem: What happens if twice as many inhibitory postsynaptic potentials (IPSPs) as excitatory postsynaptic potentials (EPSPs) arrive in close proximity at a postsynaptic neuron?

questions.stem: What happens when a resting neuron's membrane depolarizes?

questions.stem: A common feature of action potentials is that they

choices.D: synaptic vesicle membranes

questions.stem: Why are action potentials usually conducted in one direction?

questions.stem: Choose the correct match of glial cell type and function.

questions.answer_text: myosin cross-bridges binding to actin and transitioning from a high-energy to a low-energy state

questions.stem: Compared to oxidative skeletal muscle fibers, those classified as glycolytic typically have ________.

choices.C: a smaller diameter
choices.D: less resistance to fatigue

questions.answer_text: less resistance to fatigue

questions.stem: Myasthenia gravis is a form of muscle paralysis in which ________.

choices.A: motor neurons lose their myelination and the ability to rapidly fire action potentials
choices.B: acetylcholine receptors are destroyed by an overactive immune system
choices.C: ATP production becomes uncoupled from mitochondrial electron transport
choices.D: troponin molecules become unable to bind calcium ions

questions.answer_text: acetylcholine receptors are destroyed by an overactive immune system

questions.stem: A skeletal muscle deprived of adequate ATP supplies will ________.

choices.B: enter a state where actin and myosin are unable to separate
choices.C: fire many more action potentials than usual and enter a state of "rigor"
choices.D: sequester all free calcium ions into the sarcoplasmic reticulum

questions.answer_text: enter a state where actin and myosin are unable to separate

questions.stem: Most of the ATP supplies for a skeletal muscle undergoing one hour of sustained exercise come from ________.

choices.C: substrate phosphorylation
choices.D: oxidative phosphorylation

questions.answer_text: oxidative phosphorylation

questions.stem: The motor unit in vertebrate skeletal muscle refers to ________.

choices.A: one actin binding site and its myosin partner
choices.B: one sarcomere and all of its actin and myosin filaments
choices.C: one myofibril and all of its sarcomeres
choices.D: one motor neuron and all of the muscle fibers on which it has synapses

questions.answer_text: one motor neuron and all of the muscle fibers on which it has synapses

questions.stem: The muscles of a recently deceased human can remain in a contracted state, termed rigor mortis, for several hours, due to the lack of ________.

choices.A: ATP needed to break actin-myosin bonds
choices.B: calcium ions needed to bind to troponin
choices.C: oxygen supplies needed for myoglobin
choices.D: sodium ions needed to fire action potentials

questions.answer_text: ATP needed to break actin-myosin bonds

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct sequence that describes the excitation and contraction of a skeletal muscle fiber? 1. Tropomyosin shifts and unblocks the cross-bridge binding sites. 2. Calcium is released and binds to the troponin complex. 3. Transverse tubules depolarize the sarcoplasmic reticulum. 4. The thin filaments are ratcheted across the thick filaments by the heads of the myosin molecules using energy from ATP. 5. An action potential in a motor neuron causes the axon to release acetylcholine, which depolarizes the muscle cell membrane.
The leg muscles of a sprinter would differ from a marathon runner in that ________.

choices.A: per gram, the sprinter's muscles would have more mitochondria than the marathon runner's muscles
choices.B: per gram, the marathon runner's muscles would contain more myoglobin than the sprinter's muscles
choices.C: the marathon runner's muscles would have a greater rate of contraction than the sprinter's muscles
choices.D: per gram, the sprinter's muscles would use more oxygen than the marathon runner's muscles

questions.answer_text: per gram, the marathon runner's muscles would contain more myoglobin than the sprinter's muscles

questions.stem: Action potentials in the heart move from one contractile cell to the next via ________.

choices.C: intercalated disks
choices.D: non-myelinated motor neurons

questions.answer_text: intercalated disks

questions.stem: The venom of cobras contains a mixture of substances that have a variety of physiological effects. One substance in the venom works by preventing acetylcholine from binding to muscle receptors. How does the venom affect the prey of the cobra?

choices.A: Action potentials would be continuously generated, causing convulsive muscle contractions.
choices.B: Muscle contractions would be prevented, causing paralysis.
choices.C: Muscle contractions could still occur, but relaxation of the muscle would be impaired.
choices.D: Action potentials would be continuously generated, causing convulsive muscle contractions; muscle contractions would then be prevented, causing paralysis.

questions.answer_text: Muscle contractions would be prevented, causing paralysis.

questions.stem: When an action potential from a motor neuron arrives at the neuromuscular junction (NMJ), a series of events occurs that leads to muscle contraction. Which of the following events will occur last (that is, after all of the others listed below)?

choices.C: depolarization of the muscle cell
choices.D: release of Ca2+ from the sarcoplasmic reticulum

questions.answer_text: conformational change in troponin

questions.stem: A patient is hospitalized with muscle spasms caused by failure of back muscles to relax after contraction. Which of the following would be most likely to help?

choices.A: Inject calcium into the muscle cell, because it is not being released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
choices.B: Induce tropomyosin and troponin to bind to the myosin binding sites on actin.
choices.C: Increase the amount of acetylcholine at the synapses between motor neurons and muscle cells.
choices.D: Depolarize the motor neurons to send an action potential to the muscle cells.

questions.answer_text: Induce tropomyosin and troponin to bind to the myosin binding sites on actin.

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. "Marine cone snails from the genus Conus are estimated to consist of up to 700 species. These predatory molluscs have devised an efficient venom apparatus that allows them to successfully capture polychaete worms, other molluscs, or in some cases fish as their primary food sources. . . . conotoxins from Australian species of Conus . . . have the capacity to inhibit specifically the nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in higher animals." (B. G. Livett, K. R. Gayler, and Z. Khalil. 2004. Drugs from the sea: Conopeptides as potential therapeutics. Current Medicinal Chemistry 11:1715-23.) This particular conotoxin inhibits acetylcholine receptors that are located ________.

choices.C: on the presynaptic membrane of the neuromuscular junction
choices.D: on the postsynaptic membrane, on the muscle cell

questions.answer_text: on the postsynaptic membrane, on the muscle cell

questions.stem: Use the following information to answer the question. "Marine cone snails from the genus Conus are estimated to consist of up to 700 species. These predatory molluscs have devised an efficient venom apparatus that allows them to successfully capture polychaete worms, other molluscs, or in some cases fish as their primary food sources. . . . conotoxins from Australian species of Conus . . . have the capacity to inhibit specifically the nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in higher animals." (B. G. Livett, K. R. Gayler, and Z. Khalil. 2004. Drugs from the sea: Conopeptides as potential therapeutics. Current Medicinal Chemistry 11:1715-23.) What is the adaptive value of this toxin? I) It would cause muscle spasms in the prey. II) It would result in paralysis of the skeletal muscle of the prey. III) It would stimulate digestive tract smooth muscle to cause nausea and vomiting of the prey.

choices.C: only III
choices.D: only I and II

questions.answer_text: only II

questions.stem: An endoskeleton is the primary body support for the ________.

choices.C: cartilaginous fishes, including sharks
choices.D: bivalves, including clams

questions.answer_text: cartilaginous fishes, including sharks

questions.stem: A ball-and-socket joint connects ________.

choices.C: the ulna to the humerus
choices.D: the humerus to the scapula

questions.answer_text: the humerus to the scapula

questions.stem: Among these choices, the most energetically efficient locomotion per unit mass is likely ________.

choices.C: flying by a 100-gram bird
choices.D: swimming by a 100-kilogram tuna (bony fish)

questions.answer_text: swimming by a 100-kilogram tuna (bony fish)

questions.stem: The hydrostatic skeleton of the earthworm allows it to move around in its environment by ________.

choices.C: using peristaltic contractions of its circular and longitudinal muscles
choices.D: alternating contractions and relaxations of its flagella

questions.answer_text: using peristaltic contractions of its circular and longitudinal muscles

questions.stem: Chitin is a major component of the ________.

choices.C: exoskeleton of insects
choices.D: body hairs of mammals

questions.answer_text: exoskeleton of insects

questions.stem: Which of the following sensory receptors is incorrectly paired with its category?

choices.C: taste receptor—chemoreceptor
choices.D: olfactory receptor—electromagnetic receptor

questions.answer_text: olfactory receptor—electromagnetic receptor

questions.stem: The middle ear converts

choices.A: air pressure waves to fluid pressure waves.
choices.B: air pressure waves to nerve impulses.
choices.C: fluid pressure waves to nerve impulses.
choices.D: pressure waves to hair cell movements.

questions.answer_text: air pressure waves to fluid pressure waves.

questions.stem: During the contraction of a vertebrate skeletal muscle fiber, calcium ions

choices.A: break cross-bridges as a cofactor in hydrolysis of ATP.
choices.B: bind with troponin, changing its shape so that the myosin-binding sites on actin are exposed.
choices.C: transmit action potentials from the motor neuron to the muscle fiber.
choices.D: spread action potentials through the T tubules.

questions.answer_text: bind with troponin, changing its shape so that the myosin-binding sites on actin are exposed.

questions.stem: Which sensory distinction is not encoded by a difference in neuron identity?

choices.C: loud and faint
choices.D: salty and sweet

questions.answer_text: loud and faint

questions.stem: The transduction of sound waves into action potentials occurs

choices.A: in the tectorial membrane as it is stimulated by hair cells.
choices.B: when hair cells are bent against the tectorial membrane, causing them to depolarize and release neurotransmitter that stimulates sensory neurons.
choices.C: as the basilar membrane vibrates at different frequencies in response to the varying volume of sounds.
choices.D: within the middle ear as the vibrations are amplified by the malleus, incus, and stapes.

questions.answer_text: when hair cells are bent against the tectorial membrane, causing them to depolarize and release neurotransmitter that stimulates sensory neurons.

questions.stem: Although some sharks close their eyes just before they bite, their bites are on target. Researchers have noted that sharks often misdirect their bites at metal objects and that they can find batteries buried under sand. This evidence suggests that sharks keep track of their prey during the split second before they bite in the same way that

choices.A: a rattlesnake finds a mouse in its burrow.
choices.B: an insect avoids being stepped on.
choices.C: a star-nosed mole locates its prey in tunnels.
choices.D: a platypus locates its prey in a muddy river.

questions.answer_text: a platypus locates its prey in a muddy river.

questions.stem: What type of signal is long-lasting and works at night?

choices.C: auditory
choices.D: electrical

questions.answer_text: olfactory

questions.stem: What type of signal is brief and can work among obstructions at night?

choices.C: auditory
choices.D: magnetic

questions.answer_text: auditory

questions.stem: What type of signal is fast and requires daylight with no obstructions?

choices.C: auditory
choices.D: tactile

questions.answer_text: visual

questions.stem: Circannual rhythms in birds are influenced by ________.

choices.C: magnetic fields
choices.D: lunar cycles

questions.answer_text: periods of daylight and darkness

questions.stem: Upon returning to its hive, a European honeybee communicates to other worker bees the presence of a nearby food source it has discovered by ________.

choices.A: vibrating its wings at varying frequencies
choices.C: performing a waggle dance
choices.D: visual cues

questions.answer_text: performing a round dance

questions.stem: Displays of nocturnal mammals are usually ________.

choices.C: olfactory and auditory
choices.D: visual and olfactory

questions.answer_text: olfactory and auditory

questions.stem: A cage containing male mosquitoes has a small earphone placed on top, through which the sound of a female mosquito is played. All the males immediately fly to the earphone and go through all of the steps of copulation. What is the best explanation for this behavior?

choices.A: Copulation is a fixed action pattern, and the female flight sound is a sign stimulus that initiates it.
choices.B: The sound from the earphone irritates the male mosquitoes, causing them to attempt to sting it.
choices.C: The reproductive drive is so strong that when males are deprived of females, they will attempt to mate with anything that has even the slightest female characteristic.
choices.D: Through classical conditioning, the male mosquitoes have associated the inappropriate stimulus from the earphone with the normal response of copulation.

questions.answer_text: Copulation is a fixed action pattern, and the female flight sound is a sign stimulus that initiates it.

questions.stem: A stickleback fish will attack a fish model as long as the model has red coloring. What animal behavior idea is manifested by this observation?

choices.C: imprinting
choices.D: classical conditioning

questions.answer_text: sign stimulus

questions.stem: Which of the following experiments best addresses the hypothesis that moths stop flying in response to high-intensity bat sounds?

choices.A: Isolate and characterize the neurons that control flight muscle.
choices.B: Play prerecorded high-intensity bat sounds to flying moths.
choices.C: Observe responses of moths to bats in nature.
choices.D: Put bats and moths in an enclosure and make detailed observations of predator-prey interactions.

questions.answer_text: Play prerecorded high-intensity bat sounds to flying moths.

questions.stem: A lizard's bobbing dewlap (a colorful flap of skin hanging from an Anolis lizard's throat) is an example of a(n) ________.

choices.C: signal
choices.D: innate releasing mechanism

questions.answer_text: signal

questions.stem: Use the following figures to answer the question. From the figure, what can we determine about the location of the food source?

choices.A: The waggle dance in the top figure indicates that the food is directly under the hive.
choices.B: The waggle dance in the bottom figure indicates that the food is to the west of the hive.
choices.C: The waggle dance in the top figure indicates that the food is close to the hive.
choices.D: The waggle dance in the bottom figure indicates that the food is 90° to the right of the sun.

questions.answer_text: The waggle dance in the bottom figure indicates that the food is 90° to the right of the sun.

questions.stem: Use the following figures to answer the question. What could you conclude if the honeybee in the figure switched from the "waggle dance" to the "round dance"?

choices.A: The food source is no longer available; all the nectar has been harvested.
choices.B: The preferred food source was farther away.
choices.C: The bee is trying to conserve energy by switching to the round dance.
choices.D: The food source is close to the hive.

questions.answer_text: The food source is close to the hive.

questions.stem: Use the following figures to answer the question. If the figure shows the dances of bees in a hive at noon on June 21 in the northern hemisphere (the sun is directly north of the hive), which dance is communicating that the food is to the south of the hive?

choices.C: dance C
choices.D: It is not possible to tell if any of the dances indicate the food is to the south of the hive.

questions.answer_text: dance A

questions.stem: Scientists believe that the direction birds go when migrating is guided in part by ________. I) the stars in the night sky II) the sun during the day III) the magnetic field of the Earth

choices.C: only III
choices.D: I, II, and III

questions.answer_text: I, II, and III

questions.stem: Which of the following examples describes a behavioral pattern that results from a proximate cause?

choices.A: A cat kills a mouse to obtain nutrition.
choices.B: A male sheep fights with another male because it helps to improve its social position.
choices.C: A female bird lays its eggs because the amount of daylight is decreasing slightly each day.
choices.D: A goose squats and freezes motionless to escape a predator.

questions.answer_text: A female bird lays its eggs because the amount of daylight is decreasing slightly each day.

questions.stem: The proximate causes of behavior are interactions with the environment, but behavior is ultimately shaped by ________.

choices.C: pheromones
choices.D: the nervous system

questions.answer_text: evolution

questions.stem: During a field trip, an instructor touched a moth resting on a tree trunk. The moth raised its forewings to reveal large eyespots on its hind wings. The instructor asked why the moth lifted its wings. One student answered that sensory receptors had fired and triggered a neuronal reflex culminating in the contraction of certain muscles. A second student responded that the behavior might frighten predators. Which statement best describes these explanations?

choices.A: The first explanation is correct, but the second is incorrect.
choices.B: The first explanation refers to proximate causation, whereas the second refers to ultimate causation.
choices.C: The first explanation is testable as a scientific hypothesis, whereas the second is not.
choices.D: Both explanations are reasonable and simply represent a difference of opinion.

questions.answer_text: The first explanation refers to proximate causation, whereas the second refers to ultimate causation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is required for a behavioral trait to evolve by natural selection?

choices.A: The behavior is determined entirely by genes.
choices.B: The behavior is the same in all individuals in the population.
choices.C: An individual's reproductive success depends in part on how the behavior is performed.
choices.D: The behavior is not genetically inherited.

questions.answer_text: An individual's reproductive success depends in part on how the behavior is performed.

questions.stem: In testing a hypothesis that "territorial defense in European robins is a fixed action pattern that is released by the sight of orange feathers," researchers found that robins defended their territory by attacking anything that was of similar size and had an orange patch. What experiment would you perform next to determine that the color initiated the defense response?

choices.A: Repeat the experiment using a blue patch instead of an orange patch.
choices.B: Repeat the experiment by removing the patch completely.
choices.C: Repeat the experiment by using a model of a robin that was twice the size of a normal robin but with a small orange patch.
choices.D: Repeat the experiment by using a model of a robin that had an orange patch that was twice the size of a normal patch.

questions.answer_text: Repeat the experiment using a blue patch instead of an orange patch.

questions.stem: Squirrels will make alarm sounds when a model of an owl is placed in their territory. When a red block the same size of the owl is placed in the territory, the squirrel does not alarm. What can you conclude from these observations?

choices.A: The squirrel cannot see red objects, and so does not make alarm sounds.
choices.B: The owl model, but not the red block, is a sign that triggers the fixed action pattern of alarm vocalizations.
choices.C: The owl model is the ultimate cause of alarm vocalization behavior.
choices.D: The squirrel is trying to attract the owl into its territory.

questions.answer_text: The owl model, but not the red block, is a sign that triggers the fixed action pattern of alarm vocalizations.

questions.stem: Through trial and error, a rat learns to run a maze without mistakes to receive a food reward.

choices.C: C
choices.D: D

questions.answer_text: A

questions.stem: A human baby performs a sucking behavior perfectly when it is put in the presence of the nipple of its mother's breast.

choices.C: C
choices.D: D

questions.answer_text: C

questions.stem: A mother goat can recognize its own kid by smell.

choices.C: C
choices.D: D

questions.answer_text: D

questions.stem: A cat runs to its food dish when it hears the sound of a can opener.

choices.C: C
choices.D: E

questions.answer_text: B

questions.stem: Every morning at the same time, John went into the den to feed his new tropical fish. After a few weeks, he noticed that the fish swam to the top of the tank when he entered the room. This is an example of ________.

choices.C: classical conditioning
choices.D: operant conditioning

questions.answer_text: classical conditioning

questions.stem: Some dogs love attention, and Frodo the beagle learns that if he barks, he gets attention. Which of the following might you use to describe this behavior?

choices.A: The dog is displaying an instinctive fixed action pattern.
choices.B: The dog is trying to protect its territory.
choices.C: The dog has been classically conditioned.
choices.D: The dog's behavior is a result of operant conditioning.

questions.answer_text: The dog's behavior is a result of operant conditioning.

questions.stem: Scientists have tried raising endangered whooping cranes in captivity by using sandhill cranes as foster parents. This strategy is no longer used because ________.

choices.A: the fostered whooping cranes' critical period was variable such that different chicks imprinted on different "mothers"
choices.B: sandhill crane parents rejected their fostered whooping crane chicks soon after incubation
choices.C: none of the fostered whooping cranes formed a mating pair-bond with another whooping crane
choices.D: sandhill crane parents did not properly incubate whooping crane eggs

questions.answer_text: none of the fostered whooping cranes formed a mating pair-bond with another whooping crane

questions.stem: White-crowned sparrows can only learn the "crystallized" song for their species by ________.

choices.A: listening to adult sparrow songs during a sensitive period as a fledgling, followed by a practice period until the juvenile matches its melody to its memorized fledgling song
choices.B: listening to the song of its own species during a critical period so that it will imprint to its own species song and not the songs of other songbird species
choices.C: performing the crystallized song as adults when they become sexually mature, as the song is programmed into the innate behavior for the species
choices.D: observing and practicing after receiving social confirmation from other adults at a critical period during their first episode of courtship behavior

questions.answer_text: listening to adult sparrow songs during a sensitive period as a fledgling, followed by a practice period until the juvenile matches its melody to its memorized fledgling song

questions.stem: One way to understand how early environment influences behaviors in similar species is through the "cross-fostering" experimental technique. Suppose that the curly-whiskered mud rat differs from the bald mud rat in several ways, including being much more aggressive. How would you set up a cross-fostering experiment to determine if environment plays a role in the curly-whiskered mud rat's aggression?

choices.A: You would cross curly-whiskered mud rats and bald mud rats and hand-rear the offspring to see if any grew up to be aggressive.
choices.B: You would place newborn curly-whiskered mud rats with bald mud rat parents and place newborn bald mud rats with curly-whiskered mud rat parents. Finally, let some mud rats of both species be raised by their own species. Then you would compare the outcomes.
choices.C: You would remove the offspring of curly-whiskered mud rats and bald mud rats from their parents, raise them in the same environment but without parents, and then compare the outcomes.
choices.D: You would replace normal newborn mud rats with deformed newborn mud rats to see if it triggered an altruistic response.

questions.answer_text: You would place newborn curly-whiskered mud rats with bald mud rat parents and place newborn bald mud rats with curly-whiskered mud rat parents. Finally, let some mud rats of both species be raised by their own species. Then you would compare the outcomes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of innate behaviors? Innate behaviors ________.

choices.A: are only weakly influenced by genes
choices.B: occur in invertebrates and some vertebrates but not mammals
choices.C: are limited to invertebrate animals
choices.D: are expressed in most individuals in a population

questions.answer_text: are expressed in most individuals in a population

questions.stem: A region of the canary forebrain shrinks during the nonbreeding season and enlarges when breeding season begins. This change is probably associated with the annual ________.

choices.A: addition of new syllables to a canary's song repertoire
choices.B: crystallization of subsong into adult songs
choices.C: renewal of mating and nest-building behaviors
choices.D: elimination of the memorized template for songs sung the previous year

questions.answer_text: addition of new syllables to a canary's song repertoire

questions.stem: Although many chimpanzees live in environments containing oil palm nuts, members of only a few populations use stones to crack open the nuts. The likely explanation is that ________.

choices.A: the behavioral difference is caused by genetic differences between populations
choices.B: members of different populations have different nutritional requirements
choices.C: the cultural tradition of using stones to crack nuts has arisen in only some populations
choices.D: members of different populations differ in learning ability

questions.answer_text: the cultural tradition of using stones to crack nuts has arisen in only some populations

questions.stem: You observe a species of bird that, upon hatching, has contact with its parents only while being fed. You also never hear the parents sing during the feeding process. What would you propose about song learning in this species of bird?

choices.A: Song learning in this species is most likely learned.
choices.B: The period of imprinting is likely later in the bird's life.
choices.C: The males will learn song when they congregate with other males of their species during the winter.
choices.D: Song learning in this species is most likely innate.

questions.answer_text: Song learning in this species is most likely innate.

questions.stem: Learning has the most influence on behavior when ________.

choices.A: making mistakes does not result in death
choices.C: animals have enormous cognitive ability
choices.D: making mistakes results in death

questions.answer_text: making mistakes does not result in death

questions.stem: You have captured a number of rats from a wild population and quickly surmise with tests that they are very good at avoiding food with poisons. What would best explain this observation?

choices.A: Rats are probably just intelligent enough to avoid poison.
choices.B: Rats may experience a large variety of toxins in their environment and learn to avoid them.
choices.C: Rats are taught by their parents to test small bits of food first and then return later if the food seems safe.
choices.D: Rats may be able to tolerate large amounts of poison.

questions.answer_text: Rats may experience a large variety of toxins in their environment and learn to avoid them.

questions.stem: You observe scrub jays hiding food and notice that one particular individual only pretends to hide food. What kind of experiment could you perform to test whether this behavior was random or in response to another signal?

choices.A: Observe more of these behaviors in the wild and try to determine if the behavior is random.
choices.B: Hypothesize a set of signals that could produce this behavior and try to match the behaviors with the signals.
choices.C: Attempt to reproduce the behavior in captivity by using bird models and a computer simulation.
choices.D: Isolate the individual birds in a laboratory and repeat the observations.

questions.answer_text: Hypothesize a set of signals that could produce this behavior and try to match the behaviors with the signals.

questions.stem: You observe scrub jays hiding food and notice that one particular individual only pretends to hide food. Your experiments associate the presence of other individuals with the frequency of pretending to cache food. A colleague shows you animals of the same species that do not perform this pretend caching. How does this information affect your conclusions about this behavior?

choices.A: It suggests that this behavior might be learned.
choices.B: It prevents you from making conclusions.
choices.C: It suggests that your experimental design is flawed.
choices.D: It does not change your initial conclusions.

questions.answer_text: It suggests that this behavior might be learned.

questions.stem: You discover a rare new bird species, but you are unable to observe its mating behavior. You see that the male is large and ornamental compared with the female. On this basis, you can probably conclude that the species is ________.

choices.C: polyandrous
choices.D: agonistic

questions.answer_text: polygamous

questions.stem: Fred and Joe, two unrelated, mature male gorillas, encounter one another. Fred is courting a female. Fred grunts as Joe comes near. As Joe continues to advance, Fred begins drumming (pounding his chest) and bares his teeth. Joe then rolls on the ground on his back, gets up, and quickly leaves. This behavioral pattern is repeated several times during the mating season. Choose the most specific behavior described by this example.

choices.C: learned behavior
choices.D: fixed action pattern

questions.answer_text: agonistic behavior

questions.stem: Female spotted sandpipers aggressively court males and, after mating and egg laying, leave the clutch of young for the male to incubate. This sequence may be repeated several times with different males until no available males remain, forcing the female to incubate her last clutch. Which of the following terms best describes this behavior?

choices.C: polyandry
choices.D: promiscuity

questions.answer_text: polyandry

questions.stem: Feeding behavior with a high-energy intake-to-expenditure ratio is called ________.

choices.C: search scavenging
choices.D: optimal foraging

questions.answer_text: optimal foraging

questions.stem: Which of the following examples reflects the concept of optimal foraging?

choices.A: During foraging, a mule deer will consume food as soon as it finds it, regardless of the location.
choices.B: A cheetah will continue a chase for prey, regardless of how long the chase lasts or how much energy is consumed.
choices.C: A moose spends more time looking for food when the food is high quality than when the food is low quality.
choices.D: If an animal is hungry it will consume food as soon as it is found, regardless of the food quality or the risk.

questions.answer_text: A moose spends more time looking for food when the food is high quality than when the food is low quality.

questions.stem: The occurrence of sexual dimorphism in a species is a likely indicator of ________.

choices.C: certainty of paternity
choices.D: agonistic behavior

questions.answer_text: agonistic behavior

questions.stem: The head-butting behavior of male bighorn sheep to establish a mating hierarchy is an example of ________.

choices.C: agonistic behavior
choices.D: polygamy

questions.answer_text: agonistic behavior

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about certainty of paternity?

choices.A: Certainty of paternity is high in most species with internal fertilization because the acts of mating and birth are separated by time.
choices.B: Certainty of paternity is low when males guard females they have mated.
choices.C: Certainty of paternity is low when egg laying and mating occur together, as in external fertilization.
choices.D: Paternal behavior exists because it has been reinforced over generations by natural selection.

questions.answer_text: Paternal behavior exists because it has been reinforced over generations by natural selection.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes "game theory" as it applies to animal behavior?

choices.A: The fitness of a particular behavior is influenced by other behavioral phenotypes in a population.
choices.B: The total of all of the behavioral displays, both male and female, is related to courtship.
choices.C: The play behavior performed by juveniles allows them to perfect adult behaviors that are needed for survival, such as hunting, courtship, and so on.
choices.D: The evolutionary "game" is played between predator and prey. A behavior evolves in the prey in response to the nature of the predatory behavior.

questions.answer_text: The fitness of a particular behavior is influenced by other behavioral phenotypes in a population.

questions.stem: The color of throats of males in a population of side-blotched lizards is determined by ________.

choices.A: ambient temperature: blue = cold; orange = normal; yellow = hot
choices.C: their receptiveness to mate
choices.D: the success of the mating behavior of each of the throat-color phenotypes

questions.answer_text: the success of the mating behavior of each of the throat-color phenotypes

questions.stem: Use the following figure to answer the question. Based only on the information in the figure, which of the following conclusions is most logical?

choices.A: Females produce more eggs more quickly when exposed to breeding males.
choices.B: Females produce eggs more quickly when exposed to many males than females paired with a male.
choices.C: All non-isolated females do just as well as isolated females.
choices.D: After four weeks together, females with males produce mature follicles to the same extent as females without males.

questions.answer_text: Females produce more eggs more quickly when exposed to breeding males.

questions.stem: Use the following figure to answer the question. Based on the information in the figure, which of the following would you expect to observe in these animals? I) sexual dimorphism II) polygamy III) agonistic behavior

choices.C: I and III
choices.D: I, II, and III

questions.answer_text: I and III

questions.stem: Upon observing a golden eagle flying overhead, a sentry prairie dog gives a warning call to other foraging members of the prairie dog community.

choices.C: D
choices.D: E

questions.answer_text: E

questions.stem: The fru gene in fruit flies ________. I) is a master regulatory gene that directs expression of many other genes II) can be genetically manipulated in females so that they will perform male sex behaviors III) programs males for appropriate courtship behaviors

choices.C: only III
choices.D: I, II, III

questions.answer_text: I, II, III

questions.stem: Pair-bonding in a population of prairie voles can be prevented by ________.

choices.A: the ensuing confusion caused by introducing meadow voles
choices.B: administering a drug that inhibits the brain receptor for vasopressin in the central nervous system (CNS) of males
choices.C: dying the coat color from brown to blond in either male or female prairie voles
choices.D: allowing the population size to reach critically low levels

questions.answer_text: administering a drug that inhibits the brain receptor for vasopressin in the central nervous system (CNS) of males

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about evolution of behavior is correct?

choices.A: Natural selection will favor behavior that enhances survival and reproduction.
choices.B: An animal may show behavior that minimizes reproductive fitness.
choices.C: If a behavior is less than optimal, it will eventually become optimal through natural selection.
choices.D: Innate behaviors cannot be altered by natural selection.

questions.answer_text: Natural selection will favor behavior that enhances survival and reproduction.

questions.stem: How do altruistic behaviors arise through natural selection?

choices.A: By his/her actions, the altruist increases the likelihood that some of its genes will be passed on to the next generation.
choices.B: The altruist is appreciated by other members of the population because its survivability has been enhanced by virtue of its risky behavior.
choices.C: Animals that perform altruistic acts are allowed by their population to breed more, thereby passing on their behavior genes to future generations.
choices.D: Altruistic behaviors lower stress in populations, which increases the survivability of all the members of the population.

questions.answer_text: By his/her actions, the altruist increases the likelihood that some of its genes will be passed on to the next generation.

questions.stem: Which of the following has a coefficient of relatedness of 0.25?

choices.C: a brother to his brother
choices.D: a sister to her brother

questions.answer_text: an uncle to his nephew

questions.stem: Animals that help other animals of the same species ________.

choices.B: are bigger and stronger than the other animals
choices.C: are usually related to the other animals helped
choices.D: are always male

questions.answer_text: are usually related to the other animals helped

questions.stem: The presence of altruistic behavior is most likely due to kin selection, a theory maintaining that ________.

choices.A: genes enhance survival of copies of themselves by directing organisms to assist others who share those genes
choices.B: companionship is advantageous to animals because in the future they can help each other
choices.C: critical thinking abilities are normal traits for animals and they have arisen, like other traits, through natural selection
choices.D: natural selection has generally favored the evolution of exaggerated aggressive and submissive behaviors to resolve conflict without grave harm to participants

questions.answer_text: genes enhance survival of copies of themselves by directing organisms to assist others who share those genes

questions.stem: If a prairie dog had the opportunity to perform an altruistic act (that is, give an alarm call) to help its relatives, which combination of the following relatives would the prairie dog be most likely to help (base your answer solely on the genetic relationships)?

choices.A: two nieces, two cousins, and one half-brother
choices.C: one son, one niece, and one half-sister
choices.D: equal altruism to all combinations described

questions.answer_text: equal altruism to all combinations described

questions.stem: How would you classify the genetic basis for most behavioral traits in the animal kingdom?

choices.A: One gene typically codes for one behavior.
choices.B: One gene typically codes for many behaviors.
choices.C: Many genes typically code for one behavior.
choices.D: Behaviors are learned, not coded by genes.

questions.answer_text: Many genes typically code for one behavior.

questions.stem: What probably explains why coastal and inland garter snakes react differently to banana slug prey?

choices.A: Ancestors of coastal snakes that could eat the abundant banana slugs had increased fitness. No such selection occurred inland, where banana slugs were absent.
choices.B: Banana slugs are camouflaged, and inland snakes, which have poorer vision than coastal snakes, are less able to see them.
choices.C: Garter snakes learn about prey from other garter snakes. Inland garter snakes have fewer types of prey because they are less social.
choices.D: Inland banana slugs are distasteful, so inland snakes learn to avoid them. Coastal banana slugs are palatable to garter snakes.

questions.answer_text: Ancestors of coastal snakes that could eat the abundant banana slugs had increased fitness. No such selection occurred inland, where banana slugs were absent.

questions.stem: Behaviors are diverse and important for survival and reproduction. Some behaviors are learned, such as the species-specific song of a yellow warbler that is different from the song of a blue-winged warbler. Other behaviors are innate, such as a female cat in heat urinating more often and in many places to attract a mate or the honeybees' "dance" that indicates the distance and direction of a food source when they return to their hive. Which of the following statements supports the idea that behaviors are important in survival and therefore affect natural selection?

choices.B: Innate behaviors are the result of selection for individual survival and reproductive success.
choices.C: All behaviors are survival mechanisms that increase reproductive fitness by increasing mutation rates.
choices.D: Both innate and learned behaviors are entirely based on genes inherited from parents.

questions.answer_text: Innate behaviors are the result of selection for individual survival and reproductive success.

questions.stem: A male stickleback fish will attack other male sticklebacks that invade its nesting territory. It will only attack male fish, which display the red belly characteristic of the species. Why has natural selection favored this behavior?

choices.A: The behavior reduces competition between species, which gives the male stickleback access to more food.
choices.B: The behavior allows the male stickleback to attract females with its aggressive display.
choices.C: The behavior allows the male to establish a defined space for breeding with female sticklebacks.
choices.D: The behavior is a mechanism to reduce predation and resource competition.

questions.answer_text: The behavior allows the male to establish a defined space for breeding with female sticklebacks.

questions.stem: A vampire bat sharing blood with another bat that is not its kin is an example of ________.

choices.C: learned behavior
choices.D: agonistic behavior

questions.answer_text: reciprocal altruism

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of innate behaviors?

choices.A: Their expression is only weakly influenced by genes.
choices.B: They occur with or without environmental stimuli.
choices.C: They are expressed in most individuals in a population.
choices.D: They occur in invertebrates and some vertebrates but not mammals.

questions.answer_text: They are expressed in most individuals in a population.

questions.stem: According to Hamilton's rule,

choices.A: natural selection does not favor altruistic behavior that causes the death of the altruist.
choices.B: natural selection favors altruistic acts when the resulting benefit to the recipient, corrected for relatedness, exceeds the cost to the altruist.
choices.C: natural selection is more likely to favor altruistic behavior that benefits an offspring than altruistic behavior that benefits a sibling.
choices.D: the effects of kin selection are larger than the effects of direct natural selection on individuals.

questions.answer_text: natural selection favors altruistic acts when the resulting benefit to the recipient, corrected for relatedness, exceeds the cost to the altruist.

questions.stem: Female spotted sandpipers aggressively court males and, after mating, leave the clutch of young for the male to incubate. This sequence may be repeated several times with different males until no available males remain, forcing the female to incubate her last clutch. Which of the following terms best describes this behavior?

choices.C: promiscuity
choices.D: certainty of paternity

questions.answer_text: polyandry

questions.stem: A region of the canary forebrain shrinks during the nonbreeding season and enlarges when breeding season begins. This change is probably associated with the annual

choices.A: addition of new syllables to a canary's song repertoire.
choices.B: crystallization of subsong into adult songs.
choices.C: sensitive period in which canary parents imprint on new offspring.
choices.D: elimination of the memorized template for songs sung the previous year.

questions.answer_text: addition of new syllables to a canary's song repertoire.

questions.stem: Although many chimpanzees live in environments with oil palm nuts, members of only a few populations use stones to crack open the nuts. The likely explanation is that

choices.A: the behavioral difference is caused by genetic differences between populations.
choices.B: members of different populations have different nutritional requirements.
choices.C: the cultural tradition of using stones to crack nuts has arisen in only some populations.
choices.D: members of different populations differ in learning ability.

questions.answer_text: the cultural tradition of using stones to crack nuts has arisen in only some populations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not required for a behavioral trait to evolve by natural selection?

choices.A: In each individual, the form of the behavior is determined entirely by genes.
choices.C: An individual's reproductive success depends in part on how the behavior is performed.
choices.D: Some component of the behavior is genetically inherited.

questions.answer_text: In each individual, the form of the behavior is determined entirely by genes.

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: If an ecologist were studying the regional interactions among multiple populations of different species and how they influence the exchange of materials between their various environments, then this would be an example of which kind of research?

choices.C: global ecology
choices.D: ecosystem ecology

questions.answer_text: landscape ecology

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: What would happen to the seasons if Earth were tilted 35 degrees off its orbital plane instead of the usual 23.5 degrees?

choices.B: Winters and summers would be more severe.
choices.C: Winters and summers would be less severe.
choices.D: The seasons would be shorter.

questions.answer_text: Winters and summers would be more severe.

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: Which of the following causes seasons on Earth?

choices.A: the variation in proximity of the Earth to the sun at different times of the year
choices.B: the constant tilt of the Earth, combined with its orbit around the sun
choices.C: the distance between the Earth and the sun in winter versus in the summer
choices.D: the variation or wobble of Earth's tilt during the year

questions.answer_text: the constant tilt of the Earth, combined with its orbit around the sun

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: Which of the following might be an investigation of microclimate?

choices.A: the effect of ambient temperature on the onset of caribou migration
choices.B: the seasonal population fluctuation of nurse sharks in coral reef communities
choices.C: competitive interactions among various species of songbirds during spring migration
choices.D: how sunlight intensity affects plant community composition in the zone where a forest transitions into a meadow

questions.answer_text: how sunlight intensity affects plant community composition in the zone where a forest transitions into a meadow

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: In creating global climate patterns, which of the following factors is the primary cause of all of the other factors that are listed?

choices.A: precipitation differences between tropical and polar regions
choices.C: global wind patterns
choices.D: variation in the heating of Earth's surface

questions.answer_text: variation in the heating of Earth's surface

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: For mountain ranges that are subjected to prevailing winds, why is the climate drier on the leeward (downwind) side?

choices.A: Deserts create dry conditions on the leeward side of mountain ranges.
choices.B: The sun illuminates the leeward side of mountain ranges at a more direct angle, converting to heat energy, which evaporates most of the water present.
choices.C: Pushed by the prevailing winds on the windward side, air is forced to rise, cool, condense, and drop its precipitation, leaving drier air to descend the leeward side.
choices.D: Air masses pushed by the prevailing winds are stopped by mountain ranges and the moisture is used up in the stagnant air masses on the leeward side.

questions.answer_text: Pushed by the prevailing winds on the windward side, air is forced to rise, cool, condense, and drop its precipitation, leaving drier air to descend the leeward side.

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: What would be the effect on climate in the temperate latitudes if Earth were to slow its rate of rotation from a 24-hour period of rotation to a 48-hour period of rotation?

choices.A: Seasons would be longer and more distinct (colder winters and warmer summers).
choices.B: Large-scale weather events such as tornadoes and hurricanes would no longer be a part of regional climates.
choices.C: Winter seasons in both the northern and southern hemispheres would have more abundant and frequent precipitation events.
choices.D: There often would be a larger range between daytime high and nighttime low temperatures.

questions.answer_text: There often would be a larger range between daytime high and nighttime low temperatures.

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: Subtropical plants are commonplace in Land's End, England, whose latitude is the equivalent of Labrador in coastal Canada, where the local flora is instead subarctic. Which statement best explains why this apparent anomaly exists between North America and Europe?

choices.A: Labrador does not get enough rainfall to support the subtropical flora found in Land's End.
choices.B: Warm ocean currents interact with England, whereas cold ocean currents interact with Labrador.
choices.C: Rainfall fluctuates greatly in England; rainfall is consistently high in Labrador.
choices.D: Labrador receives sunlight of lower duration and intensity than does Land's End.

questions.answer_text: Warm ocean currents interact with England, whereas cold ocean currents interact with Labrador.

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: In mountainous areas of western North America, north-facing slopes would be expected to ________.

choices.A: receive more sunlight than similar southern exposures
choices.B: be warmer and drier than comparable southern-exposed slopes
choices.C: support biological communities similar to those found at lower elevations on similar south- facing slopes
choices.D: support biological communities similar to those found at higher elevations on similar south- facing slopes

questions.answer_text: support biological communities similar to those found at higher elevations on similar south- facing slopes

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: In the region of the Rocky Mountains, imagine that one local variety of Ponderosa pine (Pinus ponderosa) predominantly occurs between 5,000-8,500 feet in elevation, where it can best tolerate temperatures and precipitation. If future climate change in this region causes the temperature to increase and rainfall to decrease, then which of the following changes might an ecologist predict about the variety's range?

choices.A: that variety will occur at lower elevations
choices.B: that variety will occur at higher elevations
choices.C: that variety will occur at lower elevations and/or lower latitudes
choices.D: that variety will occur at higher elevations and/or higher latitudes

questions.answer_text: that variety will occur at higher elevations and/or higher latitudes

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: Imagine some cosmic catastrophe jolts Earth so that its axis is perpendicular to the orbital plane between Earth and the sun. The most obvious effect of this change would be ________.

choices.B: an increase in the length of a year
choices.C: a decrease in temperature at the equator
choices.D: the elimination of seasonal variation

questions.answer_text: the elimination of seasonal variation

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: The main reason polar regions are cooler than the equator is that ________.

choices.A: solar radiation strikes the poles at a lower angle and travels through more atmosphere
choices.B: the poles are farther from the sun than is the equator
choices.C: the polar atmosphere is thinner and contains fewer greenhouse gases
choices.D: the poles are permanently tilted away from the sun

questions.answer_text: solar radiation strikes the poles at a lower angle and travels through more atmosphere

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: The success of plants extending their range northward following glacial retreat is primarily determined by ________.

choices.A: whether there is simultaneous migration of herbivores
choices.C: their seed dispersal rate
choices.D: their tolerance to cooler temperatures

questions.answer_text: their seed dispersal rate

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: As climate changes because of global warming, plant species' ranges in the northern hemisphere may move northward. The trees that are most likely to avoid extinction in such an environment are those that ________.

choices.A: have larger, more contiguous established populations to begin with
choices.C: have seeds that become viable only after a forest fire
choices.D: disperse many seeds in close proximity to the parent tree

questions.answer_text: have larger, more contiguous established populations to begin with

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: Generalized global air circulation and precipitation patterns are caused by ________.

choices.A: solar radiation that warms moist air masses near the equator, which then cool and release precipitation as they rise, and then, at high altitude, move north or south of the tropics and sink back to the surface as dry air masses
choices.B: air masses that are dried and heated over continental areas, which then rise, cool aloft, and descend over oceanic areas, followed by a return flow of moist air from ocean to land, delivering high amounts of precipitation to coastal areas
choices.C: polar, cool, moist, high-pressure air masses from the poles that move along the surface, releasing precipitation along the way to the equator, where they are heated and dried
choices.D: solar radiation that warms dry air masses at the poles, causing them to sink toward the tropics, gain moisture, and then release it as precipitation.

questions.answer_text: solar radiation that warms moist air masses near the equator, which then cool and release precipitation as they rise, and then, at high altitude, move north or south of the tropics and sink back to the surface as dry air masses

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: At 15-30°N, air masses formed over the Pacific Ocean are moved by prevailing westerlies, where they encounter extensive north-south mountain ranges. Which statement best describes the outcome of this encounter between a landform and an air mass?

choices.A: The cool, moist Pacific air heats as it rises, releasing its precipitation as it passes the tops of the mountains. This now warm and dry air cools as it descends on the leeward side of the range.
choices.B: The warm, moist Pacific air rises and cools, releasing precipitation as it moves up the windward side of the range. This now cool and dry air mass heats up as it descends on the leeward side of the range.
choices.C: The cool, dry Pacific air heats up and picks up moisture from evaporation of the snowcapped peaks of the mountain range, releasing this moisture as precipitation when the air cools while descending on the leeward side of the range.
choices.D: These air masses are blocked by the mountain ranges, producing high annual amounts of precipitation on the windward sides of these mountain ranges.

questions.answer_text: The warm, moist Pacific air rises and cools, releasing precipitation as it moves up the windward side of the range. This now cool and dry air mass heats up as it descends on the leeward side of the range.

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: Coral reefs occur on the southeast coast of the United States but not at similar latitudes on the southwest coast. Differences in which of the following most likely account for this?

choices.C: water temperatures driven by ocean currents
choices.D: salinity differences

questions.answer_text: water temperatures driven by ocean currents

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: Which of the following investigations would shed the most light on the future distribution of organisms in temperate regions that are faced with climate change?

choices.A: Remove, to the mineral soil, all of the organisms from an experimental plot, and monitor the colonization of the area over time in terms of both species diversity and abundance.
choices.B: Look at the climatic changes that occurred since the last ice age and how species redistributed as glaciers melted, then make predictions on future distribution in species based on past trends.
choices.C: Compare and contrast the flora and fauna of warm/cold/dry/wet climates to shed light on how they evolved to be suited to their present-day environment.
choices.D: Quantify the impact of man's activities on present-day populations of threatened and endangered species to assess the rate of extirpation and extinction.

questions.answer_text: Look at the climatic changes that occurred since the last ice age and how species redistributed as glaciers melted, then make predictions on future distribution in species based on past trends.

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: Generally speaking, deserts are located in places where air masses are usually ________.

choices.C: at the start of trade winds
choices.D: descending

questions.answer_text: descending

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: When climbing a mountain, we can observe transitions in biological communities that are analogous to the changes ________.

choices.B: in a community through different seasons
choices.C: in an ecosystem as it evolves over time
choices.D: across the United States from east to west

questions.answer_text: in biomes at different latitudes

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: If the direction of Earth's rotation reversed, the most predictable effect would be ________.

choices.A: an elimination of deserts and increase in tropics
choices.B: winds blowing from west to east along the equator
choices.C: a loss of seasonal variation at high latitudes
choices.D: the elimination of ocean currents

questions.answer_text: winds blowing from west to east along the equator

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: Use the following figures to answer the question below. Based on the data in the figures, which of the following statements are correct? I) Area 1 would be considered a desert because of its high average temperature. II) Area 1 has more average precipitation than Area 2. III) Area 2 would be considered a desert because of its low average precipitation. IV) Area 2 has a larger annual temperature variation.

choices.C: only I, II, and IV
choices.D: only II, III, and IV

questions.answer_text: only II, III, and IV

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: Use the following figures to answer the question below. Based on the data in the figures, which of the following statements are correct? I) Area 1 has more average precipitation than Area 2. II) Area 1 has a higher average temperature than Area 2. III) Both areas have low variation in monthly precipitation. IV) Area 2 has a lower annual temperature variation compared to Area 1.

choices.C: only II, III, and IV
choices.D: only I, II, and III

questions.answer_text: only I, II, and III

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: Use the following figures to answer the question below. East of the Mississippi River, in Hopkinsville Kentucky, the mean annual precipitation is 130 cm. The mean annual temperature is 14.3°C. In the winter, the mean temperature is 7.3°C, while in summer it is 20.6°C. Using the climograph shown here, how would we classify the biome found in Hopkinsville?

choices.C: shrubland during the winter, temperate forest during the summer
choices.D: temperate forest during the winter, tropical seasonal forest during the summer
choices.E: Biomes are not defined by annual values. It really depends on what season you're in.

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: Which of the following biomes spans the largest annual mean temperature range, but the narrowest mean precipitation range?

choices.C: desert
choices.D: taiga

questions.answer_text: desert

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: If global warming continues at its present rate, which biomes will likely take the place of the coniferous forest (taiga)?

choices.C: tropical forest and savanna
choices.D: chaparral and temperate broadleaf forest

questions.answer_text: temperate broadleaf forest and grassland

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: If you conclude that vegetation at every point on Earth exactly resembles the predicted biome distribution in a climograph, then ________.

choices.A: you are ignoring human land use changes or impacts, which have highly altered many regions within biomes
choices.B: the biome spanning the smallest combined ranges in precipitation and temperature is the tundra
choices.C: the biome most sensitive (in danger) from global warming is the desert
choices.D: you are ignoring the fact that local differences in soil, elevation, or topography can result in considerably different plant communities that are embedded within named biomes

questions.answer_text: you are ignoring the fact that local differences in soil, elevation, or topography can result in considerably different plant communities that are embedded within named biomes

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the interaction between fire and ecosystems?

choices.A: The likelihood of a wildfire occurring in a given ecosystem is highly predictable over the short term.
choices.B: Many kinds of plants and plant communities have adapted to frequent fires.
choices.C: The suppression of forest fires by humans has prevented certain communities, such as grasslands, from reaching their climax stage.
choices.D: Chaparral communities have evolved to the extent that they rarely burn.

questions.answer_text: Many kinds of plants and plant communities have adapted to frequent fires.

choices.D: E

choices.C: D
choices.D: H

questions.answer_text: C

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: The eight climographs show yearly temperature (line graph and left vertical axis) and precipitation (bar graph and right vertical axis) averages for each month for some locations on Earth. choices.C: elevation
choices.D: rain shadow

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: In areas of permafrost, stands of black spruce are frequently observed in the landscape, while other tree species are noticeably absent. Often these stands are referred to as "drunken forests" because many of the black spruce often "lean over" (that is, they are displaced from their normal vertical alignment). What is the most likely explanation for the unusual growth of these forests in this marginal habitat?

choices.A: Branches are adapted to absorb more carbon dioxide with this displaced alignment.
choices.B: Taproot formation is impossible, so trees developed shallow root beds.
choices.C: Trees are tilted so snow prevents them from breaking or tipping over.
choices.D: Trees tip so that they do not compete with each other for sunlight.

questions.answer_text: Taproot formation is impossible, so trees developed shallow root beds.

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: Which of the following is an important feature of most terrestrial biomes?

choices.A: annual average rainfall in excess of 250 centimeters
choices.B: a distribution predicted almost entirely by rock and soil patterns
choices.C: clear boundaries between adjacent biomes
choices.D: vegetation demonstrating vertical layering

questions.answer_text: vegetation demonstrating vertical layering

chapter.title: An Introduction to Ecology and the Biosphere

questions.stem: Use the figure to answer the following question. The figure proposes a combination of a top-down and bottom-up model (a hypothesis) to describe the variable effects of biological control herbivores on the fitness (growth and reproduction) of an invasive, non-native plant, spotted knapweed (Centaurea stoebe). These herbivores include multiple insects that were first studied in the plant's native home range in eastern Europe, where the plant is not dominant in grassland communities and does not pose a problem to land managers and conservationists. Many insects there were found to consume the plant's tissues, including stems, leaves, and seeds, and some were very host specific and were not found to attack plants other than C. stoebe. Several insects were subsequently transported and released in an attempt to reduce densities of this non-native and problematic weed in the United States. The y-axis shows C. stoebe plant fitness, and the x-axis represents the intensity of herbivory by the insects, from low to high. As the vertical shaded bar is moved along the x-axis, the ultimate effect of herbivory (now A, B, and C) on plant fitness can change based on its intensity and also may depend on the other factors. The horizontal dashed line represents no predicted change in fitness under the effects of varying intensity of herbivory, plant competition, and soil resources available to the plant (such as nitrogen or water), while the three solid lines represent other possible outcomes. (D.G. Knochel and T.R. Seastedt. 2011. Reconciling contradictory findings of herbivore impacts on spotted knapweed (Centaurea stoebe) growth and reproduction. Ecological Applications 20(7):1903-1912. What portion of the model would be characterized as bottom-up?

choices.C: intensity of herbivory on the plant
choices.D: plant competition and fitness

questions.answer_text: resources available to the plant

questions.stem: Use the figure to answer the following question. The figure proposes a combination of a top-down and bottom-up model (a hypothesis) to describe the variable effects of biological control herbivores on the fitness (growth and reproduction) of an invasive, non-native plant, spotted knapweed (Centaurea stoebe). These herbivores include multiple insects that were first studied in the plant's native home range in eastern Europe, where the plant is not dominant in grassland communities and does not pose a problem to land managers and conservationists. Many insects there were found to consume the plant's tissues, including stems, leaves, and seeds, and some were very host specific and were not found to attack plants other than C. stoebe. Several insects were subsequently transported and released in an attempt to reduce densities of this non-native and problematic weed in the United States. The y-axis shows C. stoebe plant fitness, and the x-axis represents the intensity of herbivory by the insects, from low to high. As the vertical shaded bar is moved along the x-axis, the ultimate effect of herbivory (now A, B, and C) on plant fitness can change based on its intensity and also may depend on the other factors. The horizontal dashed line represents no predicted change in fitness under the effects of varying intensity of herbivory, plant competition, and soil resources available to the plant (such as nitrogen or water), while the three solid lines represent other possible outcomes. (D.G. Knochel and T.R. Seastedt. 2011. Reconciling contradictory findings of herbivore impacts on spotted knapweed (Centaurea stoebe) growth and reproduction. Ecological Applications 20(7):1903-1912. What is the model's prediction for C. stoebe plant fitness when growing under high soil resource conditions?

choices.A: Plant fitness decreases as a result of low intensity herbivory.
choices.B: Plant fitness increases under all levels of intensity of herbivory.
choices.C: Plant fitness decreases only if the intensity of herbivory is very high.
choices.D: Plant fitness does not change.

questions.answer_text: Plant fitness decreases only if the intensity of herbivory is very high.

questions.stem: Recall that Clements's view of biological communities is that of a highly predictable and interrelated structure, while Gleason's view of biological communities is that individual species operate independently. questions.answer_text: Different plankton communities will develop in all ponds.

questions.stem: According to the nonequilibrium model of community diversity, ________.

choices.A: community structure remains stable in the absence of interspecific competition
choices.B: communities are assemblages of closely linked species that are permanently changed by disturbance

questions.answer_text: communities are constantly changing after being influenced by disturbances

questions.stem: Why do moderate levels of disturbance result in an increase in community diversity?

choices.A: Habitats are opened up for less competitive species.
choices.B: Competitively dominant species infrequently exclude less competitive species after a moderate disturbance.

questions.stem: Based on the intermediate disturbance hypothesis, a community's species diversity is increased by ________.

questions.answer_text: moderate levels of disturbance

questions.stem: In a particular case of secondary succession, three species of wild grass all invaded a field. choices.C: inhibition

questions.stem: There are more species in tropical areas than in places more distant from the equator. This is probably a result of ________.

choices.B: more dispersed annual solar radiation compared to the poles

choices.D: a longer time frame without disturbances for evolution and speciation

questions.answer_text: a longer time frame without disturbances for evolution and speciation

questions.stem: Which of the following is a widely supported explanation for the tendency of tropical communities to have greater species diversity than temperate or polar communities?

choices.A: There are fewer parasites to negatively affect the health of tropical communities.
choices.B: Tropical communities are low in altitude, whereas temperate and polar communities are high in altitude.
choices.C: Tropical communities have higher sunlight and precipitation, and are generally older than temperate or polar communities.
choices.D: More competitive dominant species have evolved in temperate and polar communities.

questions.answer_text: Tropical communities have higher sunlight and precipitation, and are generally older than temperate or polar communities.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct statement about MacArthur and Wilson's island equilibrium model?

choices.A: As the number of species on an island increases, the emigration rate decreases.

choices.C: Small islands receive few new immigrant species.
choices.D: Islands closer to the mainland have higher extinction rates.

questions.answer_text: Small islands receive few new immigrant species.

questions.stem: Use the following diagram of five islands formed at around the same time near a particular mainland, as well as MacArthur and Wilson's island equilibrium model principles to answer the question. Which region would likely have the greatest species diversity?

choices.C: island D
choices.D: the mainland

questions.answer_text: the mainland

questions.stem: Use the following diagram of five islands formed at around the same time near a particular mainland, as well as MacArthur and Wilson's island equilibrium model principles to answer the question. choices.C: C

questions.stem: Use the following diagram of five islands formed at around the same time near a particular mainland, as well as MacArthur and Wilson's island equilibrium model principles to answer the question. Which island would likely have the lowest extinction rate?

choices.C: D

questions.stem: According to the island equilibrium model, species richness would be lowest on an island that is ________.

questions.stem: One plausible hypothesis to explain why species richness is higher in tropical than in temperate regions is that ________.

questions.answer_text: tropical regions generally have more available water and higher levels of solar radiation

questions.stem: Zoonotic disease ________.

choices.A: is caused by suborganismal pathogens such as viruses, viroids, and prions only

questions.answer_text: is caused by pathogens that are transferred from other animals to humans by direct contact or by means of a vector

questions.stem: Why is a pathogen generally more virulent in a new habitat?

choices.A: Intermediate host species are more motile and transport pathogens to new areas.
choices.B: Pathogens evolve more efficient forms of reproduction in new environments.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the consequences of white-band disease in Caribbean coral reefs?

questions.answer_text: Algal species take the place of the dead coral, and the fish community is dominated by herbivores.

questions.stem: Which of the following studies would shed light on the mechanism of spread of H5N1 virus from Asia to North America?

questions.stem: In terms of community ecology, why are pathogens often more virulent now than in the past?

questions.stem: Scientists interested in how populations interact within communities are attempting to determine the species diversity of an island under study. What kind of data would be most helpful to the scientists in determining diversity?

questions.stem: You own 300 acres of patchy temperate forest mixed with grassy meadows. Which one of the following actions would increase the net primary productivity of the area the most?

questions.stem: Suppose you are studying the nitrogen cycling between vegetation, sediments, and water in a pond ecosystem over the course of a month. questions.stem: If you applied a fungicide to a cornfield, what would you expect to happen to the rate of decomposition and net ecosystem production (NEP)?

questions.answer_text: Decomposition rate would decrease and NEP would increase.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an accurate statement regarding mineral nutrients in soils and their implication for primary productivity?

choices.A: Globally, phosphorous availability is most limiting to primary productivity.
choices.B: Adding a nonlimiting nutrient will stimulate primary productivity.

questions.answer_text: Phosphorous is sometimes unavailable to producers due to leaching.

questions.stem: What advantage would there be for an ecosystem ecologist to measure net ecosystem production (NEP) instead of net primary production (NPP)?

choices.B: NEP can be expressed in terms of carbon fixed by photosynthesis for an entire ecosystem, minus respiration by producers, allowing the measurement of net CO2 flux.

questions.stem: How is net ecosystem production (NEP) typically estimated in ecosystems?

questions.stem: Which of the following ecosystems would likely have the largest net primary productivity per hectare and why?

questions.stem: Why is it that satellites, using wavelength reflectance technology, detect variable levels of productivity across Earth's oceans, rather than an increase toward the equator?

questions.stem: How does inefficient transfer of energy among trophic levels result in the typically high endangerment status of many top-level predators?

questions.stem: Why does a vegetarian leave a smaller ecological footprint than an omnivore?
